The results of qualitative and quantitative scene and ablation experiments show that the proposed deep optical flow algorithm is superior to the existing methods in terms of optical flow estimation accuracy, structural edge preservation ability and low light adaptability, and shows excellent performance in sparse texture scenes and low signal-to-noise ratio environments. In addition, by performing modal frequency error evaluation and energy ratio analysis on the identification results, the effectiveness and stability of the proposed method in modal main frequency identification and high-order mode extraction are demonstrated, providing a high-precision solution for non-contact modal analysis.

title: Complex dynamics and targeted energy transfer of double-beam nonlinear energy sink with magnetic interactions
abstract: Nonlinear energy sinks (NESs) have garnered sustained attention in recent years as highly efficient broadband vibration suppression devices. However, achieving optimal vibration control within limited space through the design of compact NESs configurations remains a key issue hindering its engineering applications. To address this, the present paper proposes a novel compact double-beam nonlinear energy sink device with magnetic interactions. The device constructs a two-degree-of-freedom vibration unit by cutting an internal sub-beam within the main beam, and integrates magnet mass blocks at the ends of the inner and outer beams. It utilizes the magnetic repulsion effect to develop an adjustable nonlinear stiffness system. The dynamic model of the 3DOF coupled system is formulated using Lagrangian method, with approximate analytical solutions derived through the harmonic balance method. The study conducts a parameter sensitivity analysis to explore the impact of NES parameters on the frequency response characteristics and vibration suppression performance of the primary system. Finally, the transient vibration suppression performance of various damping devices under various initial energy excitations is assessed based on critical performance indicators, such as the energy dissipation ratio. The findings show that the proposed NES achieves remarkable energy dissipation efficiency and robust performance across a wide frequency excitation range. This research presents a novel solution and theoretical foundation for broadband vibration control in engineering structures.

title: Data imbalance fault diagnosis method based on an ensemble multi-scale convolutional attention network
abstract: In recent years, mechanical intelligence fault diagnosis methods based on deep learning are in the ascendant. However, the problem of noise interference and data imbalance is often faced in practical applications, so it is still a challenge to achieve high precision and reliable fault diagnosis. To solve the problem that traditional convolutional neural networks have poor anti-noise performance and are easy to ignore the minority class samples, this paper proposes a mechanical intelligence fault diagnosis method based on an ensemble multi-scale convolutional attention network (EMCAN). First, a multi-scale convolutional attention network is constructed as the base classifier, which is mainly composed of the multi-scale convolutional denoising module (MCDM) and the cooperative attention module (CAM). MCDM suppresses high-frequency noise and extracts multi-scale discriminant features. Differentiated CAMs adaptively focus on important features and increase the diversity of base classifiers. Second, an ensemble strategy based on improved weighted voting is proposed, and balanced training subsets are constructed for each base classifier by sampling with replacement to improve the robustness and generalization of the ensemble model. The proposed EMCAN is validated on a bearing open dataset and a gearbox experimental dataset. Compared with the state-of-the-art comparison method, the Gmean of the proposed EMCAN is 4.60% and 12.11% higher under the most imbalanced conditions, respectively, which proves the validity and superiority of EMCAN.

title: Bayesian FFT modal identification for multi-setup experimental modal analysis
abstract: In full-scale forced vibration tests, the demand often arises to capture high-spatial-resolution mode shapes with limited number of sensors and shakers. Multi-setup experimental modal analysis (EMA) addresses this challenge by roving sensors and shakers across multiple setups. To enable fast and accurate multi-setup EMA, this paper develops a Bayesian modal identification strategy by extending an existing single-setup algorithm. Specifically, a frequency-domain probabilistic model is first formulated using multiple sets of structural multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) vibration data. A constrained Laplace method is then employed for Bayesian posterior approximation, providing the maximum a posteriori estimates of modal parameters along with a posterior covariance matrix (PCM) for uncertainty quantification. Utilizing complex matrix calculus, analytical expressions are derived for parameter updates in the coordinate descent optimization, as well as for PCM computation, enhancing both coding simplicity and computational efficiency. The proposed algorithm is intensively validated by investigating empirical examples with synthetic and field data. It demonstrates that the proposed method yields highly consistent results compared to scenarios with adequate test equipment. The resulting high-fidelity MIMO model enables structural response prediction under future loading conditions and supports condition assessment.

title: Identification of non-conforming temporal patterns in mixed shock and vibration data with the Information Impulse Function
abstract: The Information Impulse Function (IIF) is an analysis technique that operates on time–frequency representations of a signal to detect non-conforming, transient patterns. Transient patterns can signify events of scientific and engineering interest but may be difficult to confidently identify against non-Gaussian backgrounds. IIF analysis highlights non-conforming patterns and diminishes conforming patterns, providing a high confidence discriminator between potential events of interest and the background. This is accomplished by first calculating the relative participation of the temporal principal shape vectors as a function of signal compression. The integral of the resulting surface represents both signal complexity and uniqueness per instance in time. To demonstrate the IIF operator, acceleration response data was collected on a complex aluminum structure excited by stationary random vibration while simultaneously impacted by three different modal hammers. The force output of each hammer was recorded to corroborate the impacts in time with IIF results. Detection efficacy of the IIF is benchmarked using the scale-averaged wavelet power and the local Hölder exponent representing changes in signal energy and continuity, respectively. Results show that IIF analysis is highly effective at detecting impacts. General behavior of the IIF is discussed with specific examples.

title: Transient mixed elastohydrodynamic performance of journal bearings in wind turbine gearbox during start-up considering multi-component elastic deformations
abstract: To improve the torque density of wind turbine gearboxes (WTG), planet gear roller bearings are being replaced by planet gear journal bearings (PGJBs). However, the low rotational speeds, wide load variations, and varying operating conditions during startup significant challenges to the performance of PGJB. In this paper, a transient mixed elastohydrodynamic (EHD) model of PGJBs during start-up is proposed, which comprehensively considers multi-component elastic deformations, misalignment, and intermediate oil return groove (IORG) characteristics. Specifically, the dynamic rotational speed, meshing force, and moment of the planet gear, extracted from the wind turbine drivetrain model, serve as inputs for the PGJB. The influence mechanism of the IORG, radial clearance, and modification parameters on the transient EHD performance of PGJB is investigated, followed by experimental validation. Results indicate that the IORG effectively mitigates misalignment in PGJBs while simultaneously inducing earlier contact and significantly increasing both film and contact pressures. This leads to a multi-regime lubrication distribution at the PGJB interface and further influences its contact characteristics. During startup, the primary load-bearing regions maintain hydrodynamic lubrication, whereas the IORG-affected zones transition from mixed lubrication during mid-startup to boundary lubrication under rated operating conditions. Contact occurs in the edge region of the PGJB when the modification depth is less than 30 μm, and shifts to the IORG region at greater depths.

title: Physics-preserved graph learning of differential equations for structural dynamics
abstract: Spatio-temporal differential equations are fundamental to understanding the world, describing the dynamic behavior of a structure/system under external stimuli. The equations are typically solved with numerical methods, such as the finite element method, which is computationally inefficient for complex structures, especially under multi-load case analysis requiring repeated calls to slow numerical solvers. Meanwhile, the emerging data-driven deep learning approaches heavily rely on extensive labeled datasets. Here we propose a physics-preserved neural network that seamlessly integrates physical knowledge towards accurate and rapid computation of dynamic characteristics for complex systems without relying on labeled data. A graph convolutional network is created for modal computation in space domain, where physical laws and constraints are inherently encoded within the network architecture (termed ‘hard-embedding’). A physics-informed neural network is then adopted for the dynamic response computation in time domain. This hard-embedding approach remarkably improves computational accuracy compared to the state-of-the-art soft-constraint methods based on loss functions. The proposed model also realizes end-to-end generalization computations under different loading and initial conditions, thereby improving computational speed by hundreds of times compared to the finite element method. This characteristic renders our approach a promising alternative for realizing real-time structural dynamic computations.

title: Tracking growth of crack-like defects in hollow cylindrical structures from the stepped-wavelength scattering of helical guided ultrasonic waves
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for tracking the growth of crack-like defects in thin-walled hollow cylindrical structures. The method, referred to as the stepped-wavelength scattering analysis, identifies the length of a crack-like defect based on its scattering of helical guided ultrasonic waves (HGUW). Specifically, it is based on the observation that the nature of wave scattering transitions from a ray-like interaction to a diffraction-dominated interaction when the wavelength-to-crack length ratio approaches or exceeds 1. First, a numerical model was used to (i) analyze the scattering of HGUW by crack-like defects and (ii) observe the change in the nature of scattering with increasing wavelengths. Then, based on the numerical results, the stepped-wavelength scattering analysis procedure was established to determine the length of the crack-like defect. Finally, this procedure was validated through both numerical simulations and experimental testing on a thin-walled steel pipe with a vertical notch. For numerical validation, three models with vertical notches of 12, 13, and 14 mm were developed. Scattered responses from each model were obtained to test the procedure’s ability to determine the respective notch’s length. The procedure accurately identified the notch length in each case. For experimental validation, tests were conducted on a thin-walled steel pipe with a 14 mm through-thickness vertical notch. Structural responses around the notch were obtained from 12 PZT discs and used to estimate the notch length. The notch length was predicted to be 14.28 mm, closely matching the actual length. These successful validations established the method as a viable option to monitor crack-like defects in hollow cylindrical structures. If extended to practical applications, this approach could enable real-time monitoring of crack growth in real-world hollow cylindrical structures. The article concludes by exploring the extension of this method for practical applications through circumferential measurements.

title: Research on the signal quantization method for in-line inspection of composite defects in pipeline welds using weak magnetic method
abstract: Welds represent critical weak points in long-distance oil and gas pipelines, where residual stresses, microstructural transformations, and crack initiation frequently converge to form composite defects. Weak magnetic in-line inspection (ILI) technology, as a promising non-contact and passive sensing approach, has been widely applied to real-time assessment of stress concentrations in the pipe body. However, when applied to pipeline welds, its effectiveness is significantly limited by the complexity of magnetic signals generated by composite defects. To address this challenge, we develop a weak magnetic signal analysis model grounded in atomic-scale magnetization mechanisms, stress-magnetization coupling, and magnetic charge induction theory to capture the magnetic signatures of these complex weld defects. The model introduces two diagnostic parameters—relative (m) and absolute (n) fluctuation coefficients—to quantify defect severity from measured magnetic signals. Results from simulations and validation experiments show that the weak magnetic signal of the composite defect in pipeline welds fluctuates significantly near the crack, with m and n sensitively capturing defect-induced signal variations. For example, the relative coefficient m exhibits a standard deviation of approximately 0.72 for composite weld defects—more than two orders of magnitude higher than that for base metal cracks. Additionally, stress-induced changes in the weld cause an approximately 30 % shift in the absolute coefficient n. This study provides both a theoretical foundation and practical method for distinguishing and quantifying composite weld defects using weak magnetic ILI, significantly improving the diagnostic resolution of weld inspections.

title: Novel nonlinear dynamic modeling method and analysis of Truss-Hinge Deployable Arm considering hinge contact behavior
abstract: Truss Hinge Deployable Arms (THDAs) are lightweight, high-precision structures made of cables and beams connected by hinges, ideal for deployable space applications. The contact stiffness of the hinges, influenced by cable preload, significantly affects the THDA’s stiffness and stability. However, dynamic models that neglect hinge contact characteristics fail to accurate capture dynamic behaviors of THDA, and the discontinuous nature of hinge contact complicates modeling. This paper proposes a continuous dynamic modeling approach based on Equivalent Material Layer (EML), accounting for contact and geometric nonlinearities. A relationship between EML material parameters and hinge contact stiffness is established using strain energy conservation and fractal contact theory. The THDA’s nonlinear dynamic model replaces hinge contact characteristics with the EML. Dynamic experiments on truss units confirm the theoretical model, with a maximum error of 14.59% and a minimum error of 6.2%. Experimental results show strong consistency in the variation trend with the theoretical values. The impact of material and structural parameters on THDA dynamics is analyzed, showing that material parameters exhibit a monotonic relationship with the natural frequency, while structural parameters, influenced by geometric nonlinearity, without a consistent trend. Furthermore, the influence trends of these parameters on frequency evolve as the number of truss units and cable preload change. This study provides insights into reveal the effect of contact and geometric nonlinearities on natural frequency, offering a foundation for precise modeling, parameter optimization, and vibration suppression of cable-beam hinged structures.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of main reducer based on parallel multi-attention and contrastive fusion multi-source domain adaption considering compound-fault
abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of the main reducer can effectively reduce maintenance costs and avoid catastrophic accidents. There are two limitations in existing research: 1) it is difficult to obtain sufficient source domain data when predicting cross working conditions, and 2) it’s challenging to improve prediction accuracy due to the significant distribution discrepancy between compound-fault modes and single-fault modes. To solve these issues, this paper proposes a RUL prediction method based on parallel multi-attention and contrastive fusion multi-source domain adaption (PMA-CFMSDA). First, a parallel multi-attention degradation feature extraction module is proposed, which is applicable to the representation of degradation information for both single-faults and compound-faults, effectively alleviating the problem of distribution discrepancy between single-faults and compound-faults. Secondly, a novel domain adaptation module based on contrastive fusion is proposed to improve the transferability and domain invariance of features, thereby enhancing the generalization of the prediction model. Finally, the proposed method is validated on real-world main reducer dataset. The contrastive analysis results indicate that the proposed method has superior prediction accuracy in multi-condition cross-domain prediction, especially in the case of transferring from a single-fault source domain to a compound-fault target domain.

title: Extracting bridge frequencies and damping ratios using damped vibrations of a non-moving vehicle
abstract: While increasing endeavors have been made to develop efficient bridge damage inspection methods using vehicles as conveniently deployable sensors, accurately identifying bridge frequencies and damping ratios from vehicle responses remains a challenging task. By using the damped vibration of the non-moving vehicle-bridge system excited by a vehicle passing through the bridge, this study proposes a novel method for indirectly extracting bridge frequencies and damping ratios from the response of a non-moving vehicle parked on the bridge. Theoretical analyses of the non-moving vehicle-bridge system reveal how bridge vibrations are reflected in the response of the non-moving vehicle, leading to the development of a signal processing algorithm for automatically extracting bridge frequencies and damping ratios. Several numerical studies are conducted to assess the applicability of the proposed method and provide insights for real-world implementations, which are further validated through laboratory experiments. The results indicate that the proposed method is more robust in extracting bridge frequencies and damping ratios from vehicle responses than existing counterparts. Notably, the proposed method does not require stringent testing conditions, such as precise vehicle properties, specific bridge conditions, or low measurement noise, making it highly promising for future real-world applications. However, it is advised to avoid “trapping locations” during testing and to use a non-moving vehicle with low damping for optimal results.

title: Out-of-domain generalization for remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery from a single source: An adversarial contrastive learning approach
abstract: With the extensive sensor data provided by the Industrial Internet of Things, data-driven remaining useful life (RUL) prediction methods are crucial for enhancing equipment reliability in industrial environments. To enhance prediction accuracy under unknown operating conditions (OCs), domain adaptation and domain generalization-based RUL prediction methods have emerged. However, when only a single-source domain is available, the lack of sample diversity, coupled with significant and unpredictable domain shifts (DSs) between the source and unknown target domains, hinders the model’s ability to generalize effectively to the unknown target domain. To address these challenges, a novel RUL prediction method based on adversarial contrastive learning for single-source domain generalization (ACL-SDG) under unknown OCs is proposed. First, a semantic embedding-based multi-pseudo-domain generation (SE-MPDG) module is designed, which generates diverse and valid pseudo-domain samples, guided by the developed subdomain-level supervised contrastive learning loss, subdomain continuity manifold regularization, and semantic consistency constraints to improve the model’s out-of-domain generalization capability. Subsequently, a domain-invariant feature-guided RUL prediction (DIF-RP) module is proposed to alleviate DS. This module compels the feature extractor to mine domain-invariant degradation features across different domains, constrained by label-level supervised contrastive learning loss. Finally, adversarial training is conducted between the SE-MPDG and DIF-RP modules to further enhance the diversity of pseudo-domains while ensuring the cross-domain invariance of degradation features. Extensive experimental validation of single-source cross-domain RUL prediction for one practical dataset and two public datasets, under unknown OCs, demonstrates the efficacy and superiority of the proposed method.

title: Modelling and analysis for friction induced steering brake squeal considering three-dimensional nonlinear contact characteristics
abstract: Steering brake squeal is an emerging brake squeal phenomenon that requires attention and resolution. In this paper, a novel three-dimensional disc-pad system dynamics model is proposed to investigate the squeal features and dynamic behaviors under steering braking conditions. The two-dimensional nonlinear planar-friction and three-dimensional nonlinear contact characteristics are incorporated into the model. The influence of steering on the model is divided into two parts: disc deflection angle α and caliper installation angle β. The system is divided into geodetic coordinate system and disc coordinate system. Through coordinate transformation, the mechanism of normal, tangential and radial contact characteristics of the system is modeled in relation to disc deflection. A vehicle road test is conducted to provide steering brake squeal occurrence conditions and validate the model accuracy. Results indicate that under the steering condition, the occurrence of friction squeal increases, because the system instability is affected by the newly introduced radial contact stiffness, deflection parameters and the nonlinear planar-friction. The system undergoes Hopf bifurcation with changes in friction coefficient, contact stiffness, working condition parameters, and deflection parameters. The dynamic behavior of system instability mainly evolves from decaying vibration to periodic stable limit-cycle and then to chaotic vibration, which aggravates the occurrence of unstable friction squeal. Based on this three-dimensional model, a new mechanism for steering brake squeal is proposed: with the introduction of three-dimensional contact condition, steering brake squeal is produced by the tangential-normal and radial-normal mode-couplings of the brake pad; the disc deflection caused by steering, working condition parameters, three-dimensional contact parameters and nonlinear planar-friction, can affect mode-coupling instability, and lead to stick–slip vibration of the system. This work provides theoretical guidance for the diagnosis and structural parameter optimization of vehicle steering brake squeal.

title: Stochastic simulation method for ground motions considering parameters uncertainty of evolutionary power spectral density model for structural reliability assessment
abstract: The deterministic parameters commonly employed in evolutionary power spectral density (EPSD) model are highly empirical and the stochastic ground motions simulated accordingly exhibit single engineering characteristic. In this paper, a novel simulation method for nonstationary ground motions that considers the parameters uncertainty of EPSD model is presented. First, an integrated identification method for EPSD model parameters is developed based on wavelet packet transform and a series of parameters are identified corresponding to measured ground motion records. Then, the optimal marginal probability distribution of the parameters is fitted and the correlation between the parameters is established through the Copula function. Finally, combined with the spectral representation method, a reduced dimensional model of nonstationary ground motions is established, and three sets of stochastic ground motions are generated by considering certainty, randomness and correlation of parameters, respectively. The engineering applicability of the model is verified by comparison with the response spectra of measured ground motions. In addition, the direct probability integral method is introduced to investigate the effect of parameters uncertainty for EPSD model on the structural dynamic reliability. The results suggest that the natural variability of nonstationary ground motions simulated by considering the parameters uncertainty can be more reasonably characterised. Furthermore, when the correlation of model parameters is ignored, the dynamic reliability of structures will be underestimated.

title: Study on signal enhancement methods for acoustic emission waves in acoustic black hole waveguide rod
abstract: Waveguide rod can be used for acoustic emission (AE) monitoring of broken wires in prestressed steel strands of bridges, however, the propagation and attenuation characteristics of AE waves in the waveguide rod lead to the need to arrange a larger number of sensors for structural monitoring to meet the monitoring requirements, which increases the economic cost of monitoring. For the reason, this paper proposes to embed acoustic black hole (ABH) in the traditional cylindrical waveguide rods to realize the enhancement of the damage signal of the AE source, which can increase the monitoring range of the structure, reduce the number of AE sensors used and the investment of monitoring costs. In this paper, the theory of AE wave propagation in ABH waveguide rod is established, and the geometric model of the ABH structure embedded in cylindrical waveguide rods is constructed. The propagation mechanism of the AE wave in the ABH waveguide rod is visualized by numerical simulation method, and the propagation models of the AE wave in the ABH structure are established. The optimal arrangement of AE sensors in the ABH position is determined by experimental studies, and the influence of the ABH geometric parameters on the enhancement efficiency of the AE wave signals of the damage source as well as waveforms is analyzed. The results show that the ABH waveguide structure can realize the AE signal enhancement, the AE wave will be reflected in a “counterclockwise” manner in the ABH with a truncation height, and the amplitude of the AE wave follows the power exponential function to increase when it propagates to the direction of the ABH truncation height. AE sensors are arranged in the end of the ABH to achieve the best signal enhancement effect, and the ABH length and power index are positively correlated with AE amplitude enhancement efficiency. The ABH waveguide rod has not produce significant changes to the main frequency range of the damage AE source. Therefore, the ABH waveguide rod method proposed in this paper can realize signal enhancement and provide a theoretical basis for the sensor arrangement method of acoustic emission technology (AET) in structural health monitoring.

title: On the experimental dynamics of a flexible free-clamped cylinder subjected to axial flow
abstract: An experiment was conducted in a closed circulatory type water tunnel with a 26 cm × 26 cm horizontal test-section and optical access on four sides. A short, free-clamped silicone rubber flexible cylinder with a streamlined end was subjected to on-coming axial flow at streamwise Reynolds numbers ranging from 1.73×104 to 5.58×105. It was noted that the cylinder oscillates at two different frequencies: the cylinder natural frequency in water, centered at ∼ 2.1 Hz, and the fluid dynamics frequency at ∼ 0.08 Hz. It was observed that a stochastic (dynamical) bifurcation occurs at a streamwise Reynolds number of 2.46×105 (Uc=0.4m/s), and it precedes static divergence at a streamwise Reynolds number of 5.58×105 (UD=0.8m/s). In addition to these observations, a method for characterizing the quadratic phase coupling (or nonlinear frequency interaction) as a function of streamwise Reynolds number was developed using wavelet-based higher order spectral analysis and the Hilbert transform.

title: Vibration signal analytical model and signature analysis for harmonic drive flexible bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Flexible thin-walled rolling bearings are key components in harmonic drives. As they cyclically undergo elastic deformations and alternating loads in operation, they are more susceptible to damage. Effective fault diagnosis of flexible bearings is essential to the reliable service of harmonic drives. However, the complex kinematics, elastic deformations and multi-point contact excitations of flexible bearings result in highly complex vibrations of multiple modulations and time variability nature, thus making vibration-based fault diagnosis highly challenging. In order to address this issue, the time-varying fault characteristic frequency equations of inner race, outer race and rolling element are derived, considering the effects of outer race deformation and rolling element contact angle on the kinematics of rolling elements. To elucidate the complex modulation mechanism of complex vibrations, vibration signal analytical models of localized fault are formulated, considering multiple modulations on resonance due to bearing fault, time-varying vibration transfer path, time-varying angle between fault impact and vibration sensor measurement axis, and load zone passing effect. To thoroughly understand the fault vibration time–frequency features and spectral characteristics, the explicit equations of time–frequency representation, time-varying amplitude demodulation spectrum, Fourier spectrum, and amplitude demodulation spectrum are derived, and thereby the vibration symptom of inner race, outer race and rolling element localized fault are analytically revealed. The above theoretical derivations are validated experimentally through vibration signal analysis of harmonic drive flexible thin-walled rolling bearings, and the localized faults of inner and outer races, and rolling element are successfully diagnosed.

title: Elastic wave manipulation in suspension helical spring: Mechanisms and control strategies for tire acoustic cavity resonance noise mitigation
abstract: Developing helical springs that effectively suppress road noise without compromising the vehicle dynamics, particularly handling stability and ride comfort, poses a critical engineering challenge. To address tire acoustic cavity resonance (TACR) noise, a primary peak contribution of structure-borne road noise (SBRN), minimal structural modification strategies to control SBRN with micro-amplitude vibration are proposed. This paper provides unique elastic wave propagation models for helically symmetric beams to support the physical insight into vibration response. Comparative analysis of wave behavior shows that low-order quasi-propagating waves with high negative group velocity (NGV) exhibit omnidirectional and localized propagation characteristics. The scattering attenuation of these waves, resulting from geometric folding in helical configurations, demonstrates pronounced parametric dependencies on key spring geometry. Specifically, reducing wire diameter and increasing helix radius can enhance the attenuation band and attenuation of NGV quasi-propagating waves, while optimizing spring inclination angle may expand the primary vibration zone, thereby reducing the end vibration output. The low-level resonance and high tunability of these waves have resonance sidebands with high matching with the TACR band. Furthermore, damping optimization strategies of widely applicable wave mode matching and spatially advantageous response matching significantly improve vibration suppression. Overall, this work establishes a comprehensive dynamic design framework for helical springs that integrates numerical methods, elastic wave manipulation mechanisms, vibration optimization strategies, and experimental verification, offering scientific guidance for medium–low frequency TACR noise mitigation.

title: Editorial Board
Research on stability control of flexible rotor system under complex fluid excitation
abstract: For fluid machinery, fluid excitation is one of the primary factors affecting the stability of the rotor system. In particular, the nonlinear behavior of partially liquid-filled flexible rotor systems is more complex, and flow-induced instability failures can lead to catastrophic accidents. To address the above issues, this study takes a partially liquid-filled centrifuge rotor-AMB system (PLCR-AMB system) as an example and uses active magnetic bearing (AMB) for vibration reduction and stability enhancement. An optimal disturbance rejection control method is employed to ensure the stable operation of the rotor under fluid excitation. A dynamic model of PLCR-AMB system is established and simplified into a low-order model through modal reduction. A linear quadratic regulator optimal control method based on an extended state observer (LQR-ESO) is proposed. First, a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) is used to increase the system damping. On this basis, a series generalized notch filter (S-GNF) is employed to suppress interference from synchronous and sub-synchronous frequency vibrations. An extended state observer (ESO) is introduced to compensate for the uncertainties of fluid pulsations in the rotor system and minimize the control current. Then, the effectiveness of the control method is validated through simulations. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed LQR-ESO control method can effectively suppress critical speed resonance and non-synchronous vibrations induced by fluid excitation, preventing control current saturation.

title: A stepwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation algorithm for stability improvement of active noise control systems
abstract: Simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) has been widely investigated in active noise control (ANC) due to its model-free nature, which eliminates the need for system model estimation. Despite extensive efforts to enhance its performance, SPSA may suffer from instability and convergence issues, particularly in challenging environments. In this paper, we propose a stepwise SPSA algorithm that applies perturbations separately rather than simultaneously, significantly improving stability while maintaining comparable performance to standard SPSA. A Lyapunov-based theoretical analysis proves the algorithm’s robust stability. A parameter optimization framework further enhances performance by guiding the selection of perturbation coefficients and step sizes. Numerical simulations and real-time DSP board implementation validate the improved stability and practical effectiveness for ANC applications.

title: Broadband vibration control in irregularly perforated composite hexagonal-prism frame via NiTi-ST-based nonlinear absorbers: Modeling, analysis, and experiments
abstract: A Nitinol steel wire rope-enhanced nonlinear vibration absorber (NiTi-ST-NVA) is developed to address variable-temperature broadband vibration-damping challenges in the composite laminate hexagonal-prism frame with irregular holes (CLHF-IH). A hole-compensated Rayleigh-Ritz method is proposed to address the dynamic issue caused by irregular perforations, validated through finite element simulations and hammer impact tests. A multidimensional nonlinear dynamic decoupling model is established, integrating Galerkin truncation, Runge-Kutta, and harmonic balance methods. Vibration tests achieve a maximum damping efficiency of 55.42 %, demonstrating effective vibration control across the entire frame. Aircraft typical temperature domain thermal experiments (−20 °C to 120 °C) confirm the temperature-adaptive damping performance. Parameter optimization identifies an optimal added mass range beyond which excessive mass degrades suppression efficiency and structural dynamics. These findings provide a validated framework for vibration control in perforated aerospace structures and the application of shape memory alloy devices.

title: Quantifying and locating grouting voids in prestressed tendon ducts based on second harmonics of longitudinal guided waves
abstract: Grouting defects have a serious influence on the durability of post-tensioned prestressed concrete structures; however, it is challenging to detect due to invisibility. This study proposes a novel method utilizing second harmonics of longitudinal guided waves (GWs) to detect grouting voids in the prestressed tendon ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete beams. Numerical simulation and experimental study were carried out on the post-tensioned prestressed concrete beam specimen with and without voids. The grouting voids were detected using two methods: pitch-catch and pulse-echo. The nonlinear parameter of the longitudinal GWs was used for void quantification, while the void location was achieved through frequency-wavenumber analysis. The results indicate that the presence of the void causes contact acoustic nonlinearity (CAN) which generates second harmonics, allowing for qualitative identification of grouting voids. The amplitude of the nonlinear parameter increases with the void length. Both the pitch-catch and pulse-echo methods can quantify and locate voids and do not require baseline data. However, compared with the pitch-catch method, the pulse-echo method is considered more suitable for quantifying and locating grouting voids. The absolute error of using the pulse-echo method to evaluate the void length is within 28 mm, and the relative error of void location evaluation is within 7 %, with high evaluation accuracy.

title: A spring-cantilever-beam-based piezoelectric-electromagnetic energy harvester for low-frequency excitation capture
abstract: In this paper, a spring-cantilever-beam-based piezoelectric-electromagnetic energy harvester is proposed and the prototype increases the vibration frequency by adopting a spring, which can capture the energy under low-frequency excitation. Simulation and experimental analysis show that energy can be captured efficiently under low-frequency excitation. At the same time, the use of magnetic coupling structure can also reduce the collision of the piezoelectric patch and increase the service life of the piezoelectric patch. The experimental results show that the prototype has optimal power output performance when the number of rotor contacts is 3, the wire diameter of the spring is 0.7 mm, the diameter of the magnets coupled is 20 mm, the spacing is 20 mm, the number of magnets cutting the coil is 3. The optimum output power after series connection of PEH and EMH is 2.01 mW when the resistance is 0.6 kΩ. Demonstration experiments successfully light 73 LEDs as well as powered four resistors with different resistance values, proving the feasibility of the prototype’s practical application. It provides a new solution for the study of piezoelectric-electromagnetic energy harvester systems.

title: Fundamental frequency optimization of variable stiffness Multi-Region composite panels in Presence of geometrical nonlinearity
abstract: Multi-region laminate optimization offers a comprehensive approach to enhance aerospace structures, making them efficient, safe, and cost-effective. Similarly, Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) processes optimize toolpaths and fiber deposition, reducing waste, saving time, and improving composite quality. Strategically placing fibers where needed, it boosts structural performance and allows for innovative composite designs. This study, first, focuses on optimizing the Fundamental Natural Frequency (FNF) of composite panels, which feature various Curvilinear Fiber Paths (CFP) mathematically modeled using bilinear interpolation distributed across different regions of the panel with comparisons drawn against the conventional Unidirectional (UD) fiber layup. Secondly, a study is conducted to explore the Fundamental Amplitude-dependent Nonlinear Frequencies (FANF) within the context of the optimized configuration featuring curved fiber layup. The modulation of stiffness in composite laminates is achieved through continuous adjustments of fiber angles, governed by the CFP function. A nonlinear structural model, grounded in the principles of virtual work, is employed for this analysis. The formulation incorporates Green’s nonlinear kinematic strain relations to accommodate geometric nonlinearities, and First-order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT) is applied to extend the analysis to moderately thick cylindrical panels, including transverse shear deformations. The principal aim of this investigation is to evaluate the impact of Variable Stiffness (VS) parameters across multiple regions on the linear and nonlinear free vibration characteristics of the panel. This research examines symmetric eight-layered composite panel incorporating three distinct design regions and two boundary condition sets. The Generalized Differential Quadrature (GDQ) method is employed to solve the nonlinear equations of motion governing these structures. The numerical findings show the impact of fiber angle paths and boundary conditions on the FNF of cylindrical panels.

title: On the normalisation and mapping of influence lines
abstract: Bridges are vital components of transportation infrastructure, necessitating effective management of structural conditions to ensure safety and cost-effectiveness. Structural health monitoring (SHM) systems, utilising sensor data, offer a promising approach to tracking structural condition changes. By exploiting the increasing availability of structural information as a result of this activity, population-based SHM (PBSHM) aims to enhance approaches for practically managing structures by utilising the similarities between structures within a population to permit knowledge transfer between different population members. Influence lines have proven insightful for bridge condition assessment but are typically limited to individual structures and often rely on pre-damage baselines, which are unavailable for structures not instrumented and tested before damage or deterioration occurs, a common scenario on older structures and even newer ones. To address these limitations, we propose a population-based bridge condition assessment methodology that utilises normalised influence lines, where the resulting non-dimensional functions permit comparisons across different bridges, alleviating the requirement for repeated load testing. The originality of this approach lies in the fact that normalised influence lines are independent of specific material and geometry properties, which enables the creation of transformed influence lines (via simple parametric maps) for comparing varying sensor locations and structural responses across bridges. For SHM researchers and practitioners alike, the significance of this approach lies in its potential to address a gap in current influence line work by systematically facilitating transfer learning between structures, thus providing the potential to unearth patterns that individual analyses may miss. Our method is validated using experimental case studies at both laboratory scale, with known damage states, and full scale, demonstrating its effectiveness in harmonising influence lines across diverse structures and test set-ups. This study demonstrates (i) an approach to normalising influence lines with straightforward interpretations; (ii) how these can map (and compare) influence lines between different set-ups, facilitating transfer learning; and (iii) the application of Bayesian model calibration to use influence lines for condition assessment between structures. By uncovering patterns in bridge behaviour across structures, this population-based approach advances current bridge condition assessment methods and offers a foundation for more robust, scalable infrastructure management techniques.

title: A novel maximum impulse amplitude deconvolution for rolling bearing weak fault identification enhanced by spectrum information guided VMD
abstract: The analysis of vibration signals constitutes a widely employed diagnostic methodology for detecting bearing faults. In real harsh operational environments, periodic fault-induced impulses, which represent a characteristic manifestation in vibration signal, pose significant challenges in feature extraction under the strong noise contamination, particularly for weak faults. Deconvolution methods are commonly used for weak feature extraction, but the existing classical methods still facing the problem of insufficient feature extraction capability under complex strong noise interference. Therefore, this paper proposes a new periodic impulse amplitude ratio (PIAR) index based deconvolution algorithm for improving this issue. To further enhance the weak feature and suppress noise, an improved VMD method based on spectral information (SIVMD) is further proposed to obtain the frequency band that contains the most fault information. Based on the full combination of SIVMD and MIAD, weak fault information can be effectively enhanced. To be specific, firstly, the penalty factors, decomposition numbers and initial center frequencies of VMD are adaptively optimized by the spectral trend and the nonlinear function, instead of using the traditional intelligent optimization method, to obtain the optimal frequency band. Secondly, the proposed MIAD is used to filter the noisy signal. Finally, the enhanced extraction of fault characteristics can be implemented through envelope analysis. The simulated and experimental signal analysis are utilized to verify the promising performance of proposed SIVMD-MIAD method compared with existing widely used methods.

title: An ANN, CGAN, and transform pair based framework to simulate seismic ground motions
abstract: The use of seismic ground motion records to carry out the time history analysis of structures, evaluate the fragility curve, and assess risk for structures subjected to earthquake loading is well known. The number of actual records in the seismic ground motion database is growing after each large seismic event. However, the stochastic records vary from event to event, and the available records matching a specified scenario seismic event defined by earthquake magnitude, source-to-site distance, and site condition may not be available. In the present study, we propose a new framework to simulate the seismic ground motions conditioned on the scenario event and site condition. The framework consists of three components: 1) the prediction of the duration, total power and the parameters of the marginal (Gaussian/Non-Gaussian) distribution function of the record; 2) the generation of an image (or matrix) of the power spectral density (PSD) function in the time-scale domain, and 3) the simulation of the record that matches the predicted and generated conditions. By considering the records from strike-slip fault earthquakes, we develop new predictive models for the duration, total power and marginal distribution of the ground motions by using the artificial neural network, and a new generative model for the image of the PSD function in the wavelet (i.e., time-scale) domain by using the conditional generative adversarial nets. Based on the predicted characteristics and generated image of the power distribution in the time-scale domain for the scenario seismic event, we propose the use of the iterative power and amplitude correction algorithm to simulate the nonstationary Gaussian/non-Gaussian ground motion record. A comparison of the characteristics of the sample records to those of actual records is presented to indicate the suitability and validity of the former.

title: Differentiable singular value decomposition (SVD)
abstract: Singular value decomposition (SVD) is widely used in modal analysis, such as proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and resolvent analysis, to extract key features from imaginary problems. SVD derivatives need to be computed efficiently to enable the large-scale design optimization. However, for a general imaginary matrix, no method can accurately compute this derivative to machine precision and remain scalable with respect to the number of design variables without requiring the all of the singular variables. We propose two algorithms to efficiently compute this derivative based on the adjoint method and reverse automatic differentiation (RAD) and RAD-based singular value derivative formula. Differentiation results for each method proposed were compared with FD results for one square and one tall rectangular matrix example and matched with the FD results to about 5–7 digits. Finally, we demonstrate the scalability of the proposed method by calculating the derivatives of singular values with respect to the snapshot matrix derived from the POD of a large dataset for a laminar–turbulent transitional flow over a flat plate, sourced from the John Hopkins turbulence database (JHTDB).

title: Dynamic modeling of cylindrical roller bearings considering raceway crack defects
abstract: When non-through crack defects occur in cylindrical roller bearings (CRBs), they can affect the vibration level and service life of the bearings and even the rotor system. When the roller rolls over the raceway with non-through crack defects, the time-varying stiffness (TVS) between the roller and the raceway will change. To explore this problem, this paper proposes a stiffness-equivalent model and incorporates it into the dynamic model of the CRB. Then a test bench was built to compare and analyze the experimental results with those in the theoretical model. The influence of the size and inclination angle of non-through crack defects on the vibration characteristics and TVS of the CRBs was investigated. The results indicate that the excitation amplitude of the TVS increases with the depth and length of the crack defect, whereas the inclination angle of the crack defect reduces the TVS excitation amplitude. Then non-through crack defects contribute to the vibration of the CRBs with the changes in TVS excitation amplitude. This research can provide a theoretical basis for the fault diagnosis of CRBs.

title: Identification of out-of-plane loads over multi-span Timoshenko beams
abstract: We consider a multi-span continuous beam made up elastic elements modeled by the Timoshenko equation occupying Ω=[0,L]⊂R. The supports of the structure are located at the nodes Pn, n=1,...NP. We prove that the loading of the form g(t)Ξ(x) that acts orthogonally to Ω, over the structural system, with known temporal function g:R+→R, g∈C1, g(0)≠0, and Ξ∈H−1(Ω∖∪n=1Njavax.xml.bind.JAXBElement@4f2cfa40Pn), can be identified if the displacement history is known over any segment of the system over an interval of time that is long enough.

title: Inverse design on customised absorption of acoustic metamaterials with high degrees of freedom by deep learning
abstract: On-demand design of acoustic metamaterials remains challenging due to iterative, resource-intensive trial-and-error processes. This study presents a novel conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN)-based inverse design method for metaporous materials with perforated plates (MMPP), enabling rapid and efficient generation of embedded inclusions within metaporous materials in a high-freedom design space. Leveraging prior acoustic knowledge, a custom dataset incorporating closed rigid and thin-walled inclusions is constructed to support broadband, low-frequency absorption. The CGAN learns the nonlinear mapping between target broadband absorption spectra and MMPP configurations, achieving high fidelity (mean squared error (MSE) = 5.03 × 10−3, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) = 6.39%) between the predicted absorption curves of inverse designs and the target absorption curves from the test set. Unlike conventional data-driven methods, this CGAN-based inverse design method integrates structural constraints and physics-guided post-processing to generate manufacturable, interpretable, and novel designs beyond the training data distribution. The generated patterns corresponding to different acoustic performances reveal underlying physical correlations: structures optimised for low-frequency absorption generally exhibit lower filling ratios and shallow-embedded inclusions, whereas those designed for high-frequency performance tend to feature higher filling ratios and deep-embedded inclusions. Furthermore, the method produces diverse structure candidates tailored to user-defined absorption targets. With a thickness of 51 mm, the inverse designs achieve effective sound absorption (α>0.5) across 360–3000 Hz. Multiple absorption peaks are induced through a combination of micro-perforation resonance, local resonance of embedded inclusions, and higher-order modal resonances coupled with acoustic wave interference. This work enables rapid, performance-driven inverse design and provides a new approach to exploring the structure-performance coupling mechanisms in acoustic metamaterials.

title: Experimental and simulation investigation of the nonlinear dynamic characteristics of a folding fin with free-play
abstract: Due to wear and manufacturing tolerances, the free-play will appear at the hinges of folding fins, which will seriously affect its vibration characteristics and then affect the flight control performance of the aircraft. In this paper, a nonlinear dynamic model of folding fin considering the contact nonlinearity of multiple parallel local connection interfaces is presented. Firstly, the improved fixed-interface modal synthesis method is used to reduce the degrees of freedom except the connecting interface, which can effectively improve the computational efficiency. Then, considering the preload in the folding mechanism, a nonlinear-equivalent connection stiffness model is proposed, where the parameters in the model can be obtained directly through contact theory. This model can not only well explain the nonlinear vibration characteristics of the folding fin with free-play in the test, but also transform the preload problem into a simpler problem without preload. Based on the above work, a reduced-order nonlinear dynamic model of the folding fin with free-play is further established. The model prediction results are in good agreement with the test results, indicating that the established mathematical model can reflect the nonlinear characteristics of the folding fin with preload and can be used for the flutter analysis of the folding fin. Furthermore, the parameter analysis of the nonlinear model is performed to determine the main parameters affecting the nonlinear vibration of the folding fin.

title: Parameter estimation of structural dynamics with neural operators enabled surrogate modeling
abstract: Parameter estimation in structural dynamics generally involves inferring the values of physical, geometric, or even customized parameters based on first principles or expert knowledge, which is challenging for complex structural systems. In this work, we present a unified deep learning-based framework for parameterization, forward modeling, and inverse modeling of structural dynamics. The parameterization is flexible and can be user-defined, including physical and/or non-physical (customized) parameters. In the forward modeling, we train a neural operator for response prediction -- forming a surrogate model, which leverages the defined system parameters and excitation forces as inputs to the model. The inverse modeling focuses on estimating system parameters. In particular, the learned forward surrogate model (which is differentiable) is utilized for preliminary parameter estimation via gradient-based optimization; to further boost the parameter estimation, we introduce a neural refinement method to mitigate ill-posed problems, which often occur in the former. The framework's effectiveness is verified numerically and experimentally, in both interpolation and extrapolation cases, indicating its capability to capture intrinsic dynamics of structural systems from both forward and inverse perspectives. Moreover, the framework's flexibility is expected to support a wide range of applications, including surrogate modeling, structural identification, damage detection, and inverse design of structural systems.

title: Development of an end-to-end deep learning model for spatial-temporal vehicle identification with measured vibration responses of bridges
abstract: This paper proposes a novel end-to-end deep learning model, MVIDetr, designed for real-time identification of the position, velocity, and mass of moving vehicles on bridges by using structural responses such as displacement and acceleration. MVIDetr employs a Transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture that eliminates the necessity for manually crafted parameters, such as anchor boxes and non-maximum suppression, thereby enabling direct predictions of vehicle-related information from time-series structural data. The network architecture consists of a feature extraction backbone, an encoder to capture global context, and a decoder to generate target-level predictions. Extensive numerical simulations were conducted on simply supported beams, continuous beam bridges, and a more complex half-car vehicle model to assess the model’s robustness across various vehicle and structural conditions. The results indicate that MVIDetr significantly outperforms the post-processing-dependent MVINet, especially in multi-vehicle scenarios, by achieving lower missed detection rates, higher intersection over union (IoU) scores, and reduced errors in velocity and mass predictions. Furthermore, this study examines the effects of sensor types, layout schemes, and labeling strategies on model performance, discovering that displacement responses yield higher identification accuracy than acceleration alone, especially for continuous beam bridges. Notably, dense sensor layouts offer limited additional benefits compared to optimized sparse configurations. The paper further explores the influence of modeling uncertainties by varying structural mass and stiffness, confirming the model’s robustness under realistic parameter variations. Finally, an investigation into the “truncation effect” of labeling strategies reveals both the advantages and limitations in terms of training performance and generalization.

title: A reinforcement learning-based optimized backstepping control approach for uncertain electro-hydraulic systems
abstract: The electro-hydraulic system (EHS) stands as important automation equipment, extensively utilized across various industries. Current control research efforts primarily concentrate on the steady-state and transient behaviors of the EHS, yet the question of how to achieve optimal control performance remains largely unaddressed and unexplored. In this study, to achieve the near-optimal control performance, an optimized backstepping control (OBC) approach is proposed for uncertain EHSs. Firstly, the EHS is segmented into three distinct subsystems: the position control loop, the velocity control loop, and the force control loop. Then, an approximate optimal controller is developed for each subsystem based on the reinforcement learning (RL) strategy, where the update laws for the actor–critic neural network weights are derived from a simple positive definite function rather than the square of the Bellman residual, which simplifies the controller structure also removes the excitation condition of RL. Based on the Lyapunov stability theory, it is proved that all error signals of the closed-loop system are semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, simulation and physical experiments demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach.

title: Graph-based meta learning to predict tool tip dynamics of multiple machine tools with few labeled data
abstract: In manufacturing enterprises, batch machining commonly entails the utilization of multiple identical-type machine tools. Owing to inherent variations among these machine tools, the distribution of tool tip dynamics data exhibits considerable discrepancies across different machines. Consequently, a dynamics predictive model developed for one machine tool may not be directly applicable to others. Instead, the model needs to be retrained for the target machine tool, but this process requires sufficient experiments to obtain labeled training samples. To address this challenge, a novel graph-based meta learning approach is proposed to predict tool tip dynamics of different machine tools with few labeled data. Initially, a limited number of key position-speed configurations are selected for each machine tool to carry out chatter tests to obtain labeled samples. Subsequently, a regularized graph-based method named graph attention auto-encoders network (GATAE) is presented for modelling position-speed related dynamics. GATAE model ingests and reconstructs node features by using the graph network with stacked encoder and decoder layers, effectively improving the predictive performance under few data scenarios. Furthermore, to enhance the model’s generalization capability, a model-agnostic meta-learning method (MAML) is introduced to GATAE model, empowering it to acquire the meta learning ability and swiftly adapt to new prediction tasks on target machine tools. Ultimately, two case studies are designed to verify the effectiveness, robustness, and generalization of the proposed method.

title: Quantitative stiffness evaluation and damage mechanism investigation in open-hole composites via multi-modal SHM data fusion
abstract: Accurate assessment of stiffness in composite laminates remains a critical challenge for structural integrity evaluation. This study develops a novel multi-modal structural health monitoring (SHM) framework that synergistically integrates ultrasonic guided wave (UGW) and acoustic emission (AE) technologies, capitalizing on their complementary strengths: UGW’s sensitivity to mechanical property variations and AE’s damage-mode classification capacity. The methodology proposes an UGW propagation characteristic-based numerical model to establish quantitative correlations between UGW phase velocity variation and stiffness reduction across distinct damage modes, with inputs derived from AE signal analysis. Initially, to acquire the damage ratios across different damage stages and understand the damage process, we perform clustering analysis on AE signal features, dividing the damage process into different stages and identifying primary mechanisms contributing to stiffness degradation. Additionally, the finite element method (FEM) simulation is conducted to further validate the damage mechanism, in conjunction with DIC results and fractographic analysis. Key findings reveal that abrupt stiffness reductions (quantified through UGW phase velocity shifts) exhibit a strong temporal correlation with high-energy AE events, indicating the feasibility and sensitivity of UGW-based stiffness monitoring. Finally, we employ AE events number as input for the UGW-based stiffness/velocity model, thereby integrating the complementary information from UGW and AE to establish a quantitative relationship between damage severity and actual stiffness variation. Comparative analysis demonstrates a < 2.3 % deviation between numerical predictions and experimental AE cumulative counts across all damage stages. This integrated approach provides a novel method in composite damage monitoring that enables quantitative mapping between non-destructive evaluation metrics and mechanical property evolution.

title: Parametric analysis and selection of Gabor-based phase motion estimation in structural identification
abstract: The phase-based motion estimation (PME) algorithm has become a powerful tool in the field of structural measurement due to its advantages of strong robustness and no surface preparation. Specifically, the Gabor wavelet is used to extract phase information from images in the PME algorithm. As a multi-parameter function, the Gabor wavelet transform requires predefined settings, while the choice of these parameters directly influences the performance of the PME. However, there is currently no systematic study on the influence of parameter selection and guidance in Gabor wavelet on PME algorithm. This paper conducts a detailed parametric study and provides guidance on applying PME algorithm. Numerical analysis is adopted to study the effects of the filter mask size, the spatial aspect ratio, the sinusoid wavelength and frequency bandwidth in Gabor wavelet on the PME algorithm. Then, the distribution characteristics of phase and application condition for PME algorithm are also investigated in this paper. The results demonstrate that the half-length of Gabor wavelet exceeds the approximate length of motion range in spatial domain to avoid phase unwrapping. Meanwhile, there is no negative frequency and direct component (DC) offset for Gabor wavelet in frequency domain. In addition, PME algorithm is only suitable for motion recognition of high-gradient changes in images, such as edges and textures. Finally, this paper validated the results of parameter analysis using a cantilever wooden beam experiments and the high robustness of the PME algorithm via changes the lighting environment in the laboratory.

title: From likelihood to limit state: A reliability-inspired framework for Bayesian evidence estimation and high-dimensional sampling
abstract: Bayesian analysis plays a crucial role in estimating distribution of unknown parameters for given data and model. Due to the curse of dimensionality, it becomes difficult for high-dimensional problems, especially when multiple modes exist. This paper introduces an efficient Bayesian posterior sampling algorithm, based on a new interpretation of evidence from the perspective of structural reliability estimation. That is, the evidence can be equivalently formulated as an integration of failure probabilities, by regarding the likelihood function as a limit state function. The evidence is then evaluated with subset simulation (SuS) algorithm. The posterior samples can be obtained following the principle of importance resampling as a postprocessing procedure. The estimation variance is derived to quantify the inherent uncertainty associated with the SuS estimator of evidence. The effective sample size is introduced to measure the quality of posterior sampling. Three benchmark examples are first considered to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm by comparing it with two state-of-art algorithms. It is then used for the finite element model updating, showing its applicability in practical engineering problems. The proposed SuS algorithm exhibits comparable or even better performance in evidence estimation and posterior sampling, compared to the aBUS and MULTINEST algorithms, especially when the dimension of unknown parameters is high.

title: Delamination detection in composite materials using laser-generated lamb waves with thickness-adaptive wavenumber filtering and broadband scale-adaptive 2D wavelet transform
abstract: Delamination is one of the most dangerous failure modes in composite materials and must be detected promptly to ensure safety and reliability. This paper proposes a novel method that utilizes laser-generated Lamb waves with thickness-adaptive wavenumber filtering and broadband scale-adaptive two-dimensional (2D) wavelet transform, enabling accurate depth localization and high-precision imaging of delamination in composite materials. On the one hand, considering the multi-layered anisotropic characteristics of composite materials, the proposed method constructs the thickness-adaptive wavenumber filters that match the directivity pattern of the wavefield to isolate the delamination-induced wavenumber components, and the delamination depth is accurately identified by calculating the image contrast coefficient of the filtered wavefield energy. On the other hand, considering the broadband characteristics of the laser-generated Lamb waves, the proposed method introduces a broadband scale-adaptive 2D wavelet imaging algorithm to quantitatively determine the optimal wavelet scale for corresponding frequency in the wavenumber-filtered wavefield, thereby achieving high-precision imaging of delamination defects. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through laser ultrasonic detection experiments on carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) plates with different layup configurations and delamination depths, and the applicability and limitations of the proposed method for detecting delaminations in practical applications is discussed. The research results can provide theoretical guidance and potential application for the high-precision nondestructive testing of delamination defects in composite materials.

title: Deep learning-based displacement identification and quantification for structures with surface features loss
abstract: Displacement is an important indicator for structural performance evaluation and its measurement accuracy directly affects the assessment of structural safety and service life. Although machine vision-based displacement measurement methods have exceptional advantages of long-distance shooting, non-contact operation, as well as time and labor efficiency, the surface features loss for monitoring target caused by the exposure to complex environmental conditions, such as illumination variations, fog, and surface occlusion, poses challenges for measurement accuracy in practical applications. In order to minimize the adverse effect of features loss, this paper proposes a novel deep learning-based displacement identification and quantification method with gradient correlation matching techniques. First, the end-to-end YOLOv8n algorithm is utilized to automatically extract calibration targets in complex scenarios, and exact position detection and reliable track could be realized even for mobile target under varying feature loss levels. Then, a gradient correlation matching technique based on machine vision is employed to analyze the correlation between image gradient vectors and corresponding pixels in overlapping regions. Finally, the actual displacement of structure is obtained through coordinate calculations. In laboratory experiments, the RMSE of displacement measured by this method does not exceed 0.03 mm and the results of outdoor experiment show high accuracy even the target exposed to illumination variations, heavy fog, and high occlusion rate; In-site bridge test further verifies its practicality and flexibility in engineering application.

title: The bio-inspired spider web dynamic vibration absorber applied to the transverse-torsional-axial vibration in rotor systems
abstract: In rotor systems, traditional vibration absorbers are capable only to suppress transverse vibrations or torsional vibrations or axial vibrations. For the simultaneous suppression of all three types of vibration in a rotor system, it is necessary to install three corresponding vibration absorbers at the same time. Firstly, inspired by the structure of the spider web, the bio-inspired spider web dynamic vibration absorber (SDVA) is designed in this study. The SDVA meets the above vibration suppression requirements while significantly reducing the size, mass and number of vibration absorbers. The SDVA consists of a center assembly ring, an inertial mass ring and multiple springs. Its structure is simple and easy to manufacture, install and maintain. Secondly, in order to obtain the dynamic stiffness of the SDVA accurately, the accurate expression for the spring bending stiffness is given for the first time. This expression is also important for the application of the spring in other scenarios. Thirdly, the dynamical equations are developed for transverse-torsional-axial vibration of the rotor system containing the SDVA and the general boundary conditions. In order to satisfy the general boundary conditions of this system, the dynamical equations of the system are constructed using the improved Fourier series method. After modal analysis and excluding the modal frequencies of SDVA, it is discovered that SDVA has little effect on the low-order transverse modal frequencies of the rotating shaft system. Fourthly, as revealed by analyzing the dynamics, the SDVA is effective in reducing transverse, torsional and axial vibrations for the rotor system. The time taken for the system to return to a stable operating state after a shock is shortened. Experimental comparisons show that the vibration suppression effect of SDVA on the rotor system is about 30%. To sum up, the SDVA can serve the purpose of the original design.

title: Deformation-driven membrane-type acoustic metamaterials for tunable sound absorption: A combined experimental and numerical study
abstract: In recent years, membrane-type acoustic metamaterials (MAMs) have demonstrated considerable potential for low-frequency noise control. Nevertheless, their practical application in dynamic environments with time-varying noise frequencies remains constrained by limited tunability. Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms governing the acoustic behavior and tunability of MAMs are not yet fully understood, hindering the formulation of robust design methodologies. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a tunable MAM featuring a simple yet effective adjustment strategy. The proposed design comprises a membrane with embedded mass blocks, a centrally positioned retractable rod, and a back cavity. By controllably inducing out-of-plane deformation in the membrane via the retractable rod, the system enables adjustment of membrane prestress, thereby achieving tunable sound absorption performance. To elucidate the working principle of such a practical adjustment strategy, a tailored finite element (FE) analysis framework is established, integrating coupled structural–acoustic domains and accounting for geometric nonlinearity in acoustic response. The validity of this framework is rigorously confirmed through impedance tube experiments. The analysis reveals that at the frequencies where sound absorption peaks, the surface impedance of the MAM matches the characteristic impedance of air. This results in the acoustic siphon phenomenon, enabling efficient conversion of sound energy into the system’s elastic strain energy. Leveraging this high-fidelity model, parametric investigation is further conducted to elucidate the effect of key factors on sound absorption performance, offering new insights for the design and analysis of tunable MAMs.

title: A new strategy for monitoring 3D internal deformation in dams based on the simplified inverse absolute nodal coordinate formulation (iANCF S3D)
abstract: Internal deformation monitoring is an essential component of dam health assessment. This study proposes a novel three-dimensional, distributed, and large-range deformation monitoring strategy to address the challenge of long-distance internal deformation monitoring in high dams. Firstly, the simplified three-dimensional inverse absolute nodal coordinate formulation (iANCF S3D) is developed based on the characteristics of internal deformation monitoring in dams. This method exhibits excellent robustness, high accuracy, and suitability for large deformation reconstruction. Finite element analysis is conducted to validate its advantages in terms of reconstruction accuracy for large deformations, element convergence, and computational efficiency, with an error percentage below 0.3 %. Additionally, the Number of Spacing Elements (NSE) is introduced, and an optimal NSE value of two is determined for inverse beam element division. Furthermore, a fiber optic based sensor is developed for long-distance, three-dimensional, distributed deformation monitoring within dams. Experimental validation through long-distance deformation tests demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed monitoring strategy, with a relative error of less than 1.5 %. This study provides a novel approach to internal deformation monitoring in high dams.

title: Corrigendum to “Physics-preserved graph learning of differential equations for structural dynamics” [Mech. Syst. Signal Process. 236 (2025) 112956]
Vibration-based damage detection of offshore wind turbine foundations under environmental and operational variations
abstract: Environmental and operational variations (EOVs) can alter dynamic responses of structures and hence mask subtle changes caused by damage, leading to unreliable structural health monitoring systems. Removing the EOV effects is one of the biggest challenges in structural health monitoring, especially for offshore wind turbines (OWTs) which are subjected to a variety of EOVs. In this paper, a new approach to remove the EOV effects for OWTs is proposed. It takes advantage of the fact that OWTs are built in groups and thus subjected to similar EOVs at the same time. When the monitored features are viewed relative to those of adjacent turbines, the complex EOV effects are likely to be cancelled out. Specifically, the relationships between the features of adjacent OWTs are modelled using Gaussian process regression. The obtained regression models are then used for predictive purposes, and the prediction residuals are monitored in a control chart for damage detection. The method is demonstrated on a wind farm with three OWTs affected by scour damage, and the results show that it can detect the damage and localise the damage to a specific OWT.

title: Simultaneous viscoelastic characterization of soft tissues based on shear wave ultrasound dispersion and multi-scale wavelet cross-correlation analysis
abstract: Ultrasound shear waves offer a non-destructive testing approach to assess the biomechanical properties of biological soft tissues. This paper presents a method based on the dispersion relations of ultrasound shear waves to inversely derive the viscoelastic properties of soft tissues. In the proposed method, dispersion relations are extracted from shear wave signals based on the multi-scale wavelet correlation analysis. Here, the continuous wavelet transform is employed to convert shear wave signals into various frequencies. The cross-correlation method is utilized to obtain the phase velocity of the shear waves.
