A novel dynamic response characterization modeling method for truss structures is proposed, integrating the finite element method and the transfer matrix method. First, the basic assumptions and boundary conditions for modeling are determined using the typical truss structure as the research object. Secondly, the transfer matrix is obtained through discretization and derivation, and the truss elements modeling is derived through the connection conditions. In addition, the modeling of the space truss structure system for dynamic response characterization is developed, incorporating connection attachments. Finally, the prototype was fabricated and the experimental system was constructed. The correctness of the proposed modeling method is verified by a comprehensive comparison of FEM simulations, proposed modeling computations and experimental measurements. The comprehensive comparison includes the frequency response, data analysis, correlation comparison and relative error comparison. The results demonstrate that the proposed method offers significant advantages in terms of both computational accuracy and efficiency, and it holds great potential for the dynamic characterization of complex space structures.

title: A novel bearing faults diagnosis of rotor-bearing systems based on vibration responses and convolutional neural network
abstract: Bearing faults, particularly outer race defects and angular misalignment, critically affect the performance and reliability of rotating machinery, leading to increased vibration, instability, and potential system failures. This study investigates the vibration characteristics of a rotor-bearing system under these defects, with a specific focus on applications in the sugar industry. An experimental test setup is designed to replicate these faults, and a mathematical model based on dimensional theory is developed to analyze the bearing force response under angular misalignment. The study integrates experimental and simulation-based approaches to validate the model and examine the influence of misalignment on rotor-bearing vibration responses. Additionally, the effects of outer race defects are analyzed under varying operating conditions. To enhance fault detection accuracy, a hybrid defect detection approach is proposed, combining expert knowledge with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) model. This deep learning-based framework enables automated feature extraction and fault classification, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering. The results indicate that angular misalignment amplifies variable compliance excitation, increasing vibration acceleration and directional instability, while also influencing spectral characteristics by reducing rotational frequency amplitude. The proposed 1D-CNN model achieves a fault classification accuracy of 98.67%, demonstrating its effectiveness for real-time bearing health monitoring. These findings offer valuable insights into mitigating misalignment and outer race defects, ultimately enhancing the operational stability of rotating machinery.

title: Trajectory pre-filtering-based cooperative tool servo diamond turning of complex-shaped optics
abstract: Traditional single slow slide servo (SSS) and fast tool servo (FTS) diamond turning processes face limitations due to the trade-off between stroke and bandwidth, which hinders high-precision and high-speed machining of complex-shaped optics with large depths. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel trajectory pre-filtering-based cooperative tool servo (TP-CTS) diamond turning process. The TP-CTS process utilizes a dual-stage feed drive system coordinated through a master–slave strategy, wherein the machine tool axis serves as the master servo and the fast tool axis as the slave servo. Tool trajectories are pre-filtered and assigned to the master servo, while the slave servo compensates in real time for deviations from the reference trajectory. The pre-filtering approach effectively bypasses the kinematic and dynamic constraints of the master servo, enabling full utilization of the dynamic capabilities of both servos. To further enhance system performance, an online data-driven control strategy is developed for the slave servo, integrating a Koopman operator-based feedforward controller with a high-bandwidth feedback controller to achieve near-zero phase-lag tracking. Experimental validation on a commercial lathe with a self-developed fast tool axis demonstrates that the TP-CTS process significantly improves machining efficiency while maintaining accuracy compared to the existing CTS method. The results highlight the substantial improvements offered by the proposed process, emphasizing its potential for high-precision, high-speed manufacturing of complex-shaped optics in industrial applications.

title: Wave-structure conversion and rainbow trapping effect in complex cross-sectional structures
abstract: The straight switch rail of the turnout is an engineering structure with variable cross-sections and special-shaped cross-sections. The propagation characteristics of guided waves in it are very complicated. Even for the guided waves of a single mode, the distribution of wave amplitudes varies greatly at different cross-sections of the straight rail. Therefore, this paper innovatively proposes a wave-structure conversion algorithm for variable cross-section structures. Employing this algorithm enables us to discern the pattern of wave amplitude distribution and the evolution of dispersion characteristics as a single mode traverses a straight switch rail. This paper also established a transient finite element model of the straight switch rail. Through the comb-like excitation method based on the principle of group velocity, the propagation of a single guided wave mode in the straight switch rail was simulated, thereby verifying the correctness of the wave-structure conversion algorithm for variable cross-section structures. Meanwhile, the dispersion information of modes in different key cross-sections is obtained based on the algorithm in this paper, and the rainbow trapping effect in straight switch rails is found for the first time. Eventually, the theoretical analysis results and the rainbow trapping phenomenon in the straight switch rail were verified through experiments. The main conclusions obtained are as follows: Under the excitation of specific center frequencies, some modes will exhibit the rainbow trapping effect, which will cease to propagate forward in the healthy straight switch rail and generate a completely reflected echo.

title: Multi-objective optimization for vibration suppression and weight reduction in composite sandwich shallow-spherical shells with functionally graded coating
abstract: This study is the first to integrate the composite sandwich shallow spherical shell (CSSS) with functionally graded coating (FGC) and an improved meta-heuristic algorithm, and optimize the vibration suppression and lightweight performance. Initially, using the mixing principle, high-order displacement field theory, complex modulus method, Lagrange equation and Newmark-β method, a theoretical model of the FGC-CSSS subjected to base excitation is established to analyze the free and forced vibrations of the structure. Then, the vibration suppression, stiffness and lightweight performance of the FGC-CSSS are optimized by a multi-objective approach utilizing the improved walrus optimization algorithm (IWOA). The minimum of the first resonant response amplitude, the minimum of the equivalent overall mass of the FGC-CSSS and the minimum of the reciprocal of the sum of natural frequencies are taken as objective functions, respectively. Also, the core thickness ratio, the coating thickness ratio, and the honeycomb cell thickness are selected as design variables. The effectiveness of the IWOA is validated through an example of engineering, and the data obtained from the theoretical model are compared with the literature and experimental results to ensure robust validation. Finally, an optimization method of the FGC-CSSS is conducted, and the landmark optimization results and corresponding variations on pareto front are displayed. These results demonstrate that the IWOA has better multi-objective optimization capability than NSGA-Ⅱ, and design variables C1 and C2 can improve vibration suppression, lightness, and structural stiffness performance by 85.5%, 43.5%, and 8.7%, respectively.

title: Higher-order sinusoidal input describing functions for open-loop and closed-loop reset control with application to mechatronics systems
abstract: Reset control enhances the performance of high-precision mechatronics systems. This paper introduces a generalized reset feedback control structure that integrates a single reset-state reset controller, a shaping filter for tuning reset actions, and linear compensators arranged in series and parallel configurations with the reset controller. This structure offers greater tuning flexibility to optimize reset control performance. However, frequency-domain analysis for such systems remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, this study makes three key contributions: (1) developing Higher-Order Sinusoidal Input Describing Functions (HOSIDFs) for open-loop reset control systems; (2) deriving HOSIDFs for closed-loop reset control systems and establishing a connection with open-loop analysis; and (3) creating a MATLAB-based App to implement these methods, providing mechatronics engineers with a practical tool for reset control system design and analysis. The accuracy of the proposed methods is validated through simulations and experiments. Finally, the utility of the proposed methods is demonstrated through case studies that analyze and compare the performance of three controllers: a PID controller, a reset controller, and a shaped reset controller on a precision motion stage. Both analytical and experimental results demonstrate that the shaped reset controller provides higher tracking precision while reducing actuation forces, outperforming both the reset and PID controllers. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed frequency-domain methods in analyzing and optimizing the performance of reset-controlled mechatronics systems. • Proposed HOSIDFs for open-loop and closed-loop reset control systems in a generalized structure. • Validated through simulations and experiments. • Established a connection between open-loop and closed-loop frequency response analysis. • Developed a MATLAB app for frequency response analysis of reset control systems. • Case studies demonstrate the MATLAB app’s application.

title: Reliability sensitivity analysis combining the two-stage Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods
abstract: The Reliability Sensitivity Index (RSI) based on Safety/failure Classification of model output (StarComp) quantifies the impact of uncertain model inputs on the failure of engineering structures. StarComp compares the prior Probability Density Function (PDF) of model inputs to their failure-conditional PDF. The recent two-stage Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm provides an efficient way to estimate the failure-conditional PDF and subsequently estimate the StarComp RSI. However, the original two-stage MCMC algorithm is limited to problems involving a single failure domain. In this work, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), a powerful MCMC algorithm based on Hamiltonian dynamics, is adopted and modified to sample the failure-conditional PDF effectively. By combining the barrier bouncing strategy with the dynamic exploration of HMC, the proposed algorithm is capable of generating Markov chains that traverse multiple failure domains, leading to a more accurate estimation of the StarComp RSI in cases with multiple failure domains. In the test examples with multiple failure domains, the proposed algorithm demonstrates superior effectiveness compared to existing algorithms.

title: About the theoretical basis of using pseudo-velocity as shock severity metric
abstract: Pseudo velocity shock response spectrum has been increasingly adopted in engineering sectors to measure the severity of shock environment. The justification of using pseudo velocity as shock severity metric is frequently referred to the relationship between structure’s maximum modal stress and velocity, which is inadequate. This research note clarifies the above misunderstanding and provides the theoretical underpinning for the use of pseudo velocity as a shock severity metric based on the lower damage bound concept.

title: Design and control of a magneto-electric hybrid low-frequency active vibration isolation system using smooth discrete model predictive control considering actuator saturation
abstract: Purpose of study Aiming to achieve high-performance low-frequency maglev vibration isolation, this study designs a magneto-electric hybrid low-frequency isolation system based on performance-balanced maglev isolation unit (MIU). An optimized model predictive control algorithm (MPC) strategy is designed to improve the active vibration control calculation speed and reduce the sensitivity of the light damping system to actuator saturation. Describe methods By employing a parallel connection of positive and negative stiffness, the compromise between low stiffness and high load capacity in the isolation unit can be effectively addressed, the use of reverse magnetic poles enhances the static magnetic force to support the load. This paper proposes a smooth discrete model predictive control (SDMPC) method, which is based on the Laguerre polynomials design and reduces online computational complexity. Meanwhile, the hyperbolic tangent function effectively passivates the “sharp corner” effect of the control signal when the actuator is saturated, eliminating the high-frequency response caused by this phenomenon. Results The six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) natural frequencies of the designed isolation system are all below 1.5 Hz, and the transmissibility of the system at the natural frequencies is below −4 dB. Compared to traditional control methods, the computation time of the controller has been reduced by 90 %, and the saturation time has been reduced by more than 70 %. These improvements significantly mitigate the adverse effects of actuator saturation on system performance. Conclusions/Discussion The magneto-electric hybrid isolation system designed in this paper achieves a well-balance in various performance indicators. The proposed SDMPC method notably enhances the light damping system’s resistance to actuator saturation, and improves the isolation effectiveness in the low-frequency range.

title: Experimental study on condition indicators for severity estimation of growing spalls in bearings
abstract: Rolling element bearings play a crucial role in various mechanical systems. One of the primary challenges in this domain is accurately estimating the severity of spalls. This research aims to investigate and characterize the impact of spall propagation on acceleration signatures to identify spall severity. Experiments were conducted to collect data from endurance tests featuring progressively growing faults on the outer ring of cylindrical roller bearings. First, a spall size estimate derived from load cell signals is utilized and validated through visual inspections. While load cells may not be available in practical applications, they serve as a ’ground truth’ to validate the acceleration-based algorithms. A novel condition indicator for classifying spall severity is introduced, derived from the analysis of condition indicator trends extracted from order domain signatures. These new condition indicators facilitate the identification of several stages of spall propagation before reaching a critical size where continued asset operation becomes unacceptable. The efficacy of this new condition indicator is demonstrated through three different endurance tests.

title: Visual vibration displacement measurement of rotating body based on angle-category mapping
abstract: The vibration displacement measurement technique utilizing vision has evolved into an advanced measurement method. However, current visual measurement approaches for rotating bodies often fail to fully exploit the flexible arrangement of vision sensors, typically conducting vibration measurements in a single direction from a fixed shooting angle. Therefore, several specific shooting angles were selected, and the rotating body was categorized into different segmentation categories based on these angles. An angle-category mapping method was proposed for measuring the tilted viewing angle of the rotating body, aiming to achieve vibration displacement measurement in both in-plane and out-plane directions. The proposed method incorporates a semantic segmentation algorithm designed for multi-resolution feature fusion tailored to rotor vibration images. Rotors captured at camera angles of 45°, 60°, and 75°served as the targets for segmentation and classification training. The measurement accuracy of the algorithm was enhanced through ablation experiments, and its feasibility was validated through comparative experiments with various networks. Finally, the performance evaluation is conducted by comparing the vibration displacement curve generated by the algorithm with the one collected by the eddy current sensor, utilizing the root mean square error (RMSE) to validate the reliability of the proposed method. The research results show that, for the existing visual vibration measurements with insufficient accuracy in multi-view scenarios, the proposed vibration displacement measurement method with “angle-category” mapping can effectively extract the vibration displacement of rotating bodies in the in-plane and out-of-plane directions from multiple shooting angles, which provides an effective non-contact measurement method for the visual vibration monitoring of high-speed rotating machines. It provides an effective non-contact measurement method for visual vibration monitoring of high-speed rotating machines.

title: Kurtosis transfer in MDOF systems under amplitude-modulated Non-Stationary Non-Gaussian Excitations: A Frequency-Domain decomposition approach
abstract: Non-stationary non-Gaussian random vibrations, frequently encountered in aerospace, mechanical, and civil systems, often induce transient structural responses with complex and unpredictable dynamics. Kurtosis, a key statistical measure of signal impulsiveness, plays a dual role in characterizing such transient behaviors and assessing vibration fatigue damage. This study develops a kurtosis transfer model for multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) systems under amplitude-modulated non-stationary non-Gaussian excitations, assuming the excitation spectrum sufficiently covers the system’s modal frequencies to induce resonance-dominated responses. The proposed framework reveals how kurtosis is selectively transmitted through specific modal pathways by establishing a mathematical relationship between frequency-domain excitation substructures and the resulting response kurtosis. In addition, a phase modulation strategy is introduced to adjust the non-Gaussian properties of decomposed excitation signals, thereby enabling active control of the system’s response kurtosis. Numerical simulations and experimental validations confirm the model’s predictive accuracy. The resulting methodology offers a physically interpretable and computationally efficient framework for known vibration systems, supporting both dynamic analysis and the design of excitation signals with targeted kurtosis levels for accelerated vibration fatigue testing.

title: A comprehensive review and evaluation framework for data-driven prognostics: Uncertainty, robustness, interpretability, and feasibility
abstract: Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) is critical for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of systems, a key enabler of Predictive Maintenance (PdM). This paper reviews state-of-the-art data-driven prognostic models, emphasizing four essential characteristics: uncertainty, robustness, interpretability, and feasibility. While traditional research has focused on enhancing RUL prediction accuracy, this review argues that these additional characteristics are equally vital for addressing the demands of PHM applications. The review examines Machine Learning (ML) techniques, stochastic models , and Bayesian filters (BFs), analyzing their strengths, limitations, and trade-offs. ML models excel in accuracy but often lack robust uncertainty quantification and adaptability across varying operational conditions. Stochastic models demonstrate greater robustness and feasibility, performing reliably with limited or variable data. Bayesian filters provide high interpretability and do not require run-to-failure data but face challenges in adapting to diverse environments. To bridge these gaps, this paper proposes a structured Model Evaluation Framework that integrates users’ specific needs with key model characteristics identified in the review. By quantifying the importance of the four characteristics, the framework enables systematic evaluation and selection of prognostic models. The findings underscore the need for advancements in uncertainty quantification, adaptive methods to improve robustness, and enhanced interpretability to meet practical and regulatory requirements. While current models offer valuable insights, further improvements are necessary to unlock their full potential for PHM and PdM applications, ensuring more reliable and actionable predictions.

title: Band gap characteristics of coupled periodic cable-beam structures
abstract: This paper focuses on periodic cable-beam coupled structures, deriving the motion control equations for cable elements and the spectral element dynamic equations. By incorporating the tensile, compressive, bending, and torsional characteristics of spatial beams and using an improved stiffness assembly method, we develop a general stiffness matrix and spectral element equations for periodic cable-beam coupled structures. Furthermore, using the ADAM deployable boom as an example, we investigate the influence of design parameters such as material properties, structural dimensions, and the number of elements on the band gap of cable-included frame structures, and study the effects of different defect modes on the band gap of frame structures.

title: Gtm-based spherical harmonics beamforming for train interior sound source identification
abstract: Spherical Harmonics Beamforming (SHB), which is a commonly utilized algorithm for spherical arrays, is recognized for its high spatial resolution and accurate sound imaging, making it a valuable technique for panoramic sound source identification. In conventional SHB methods for train interior sound source detection, fix-sized spherical grids are typically employed for sound source calculations. However, the identification accuracy is often affected due to the train’s interior not conforming to a standard spherical geometry. To address this limitation, a Geometric Topological Mapping-based Spherical Harmonics Beamforming algorithm (GTM-SHB) is proposed. The GTM-SHB algorithm transforms the conventional spherical computational grid into a cuboid grid that closely matches the train’s interior dimensions (length, width, and height), based on the spherical array’s specific location within the train. Using this cuboid grid model, the radial function is calculated precisely, with SHB incorporated and a correction factor introduced to normalize the output amplitude to the sound pressure level at one meter from the sound source. The results from numerical simulations and real-train experiments indicate that GTM-SHB accurately localize sound sources, both in the location and magnitude of sound sources. By adjusting the lengthwise dimension of the mapping grid, GTM-SHB effectively pinpoints the location and amplitude of sound sources in the target regions.

title: Data-driven system identification, model transfer, and forecasting of battery capacity with impedance measurements
abstract: Accurate estimation and forecasting of lithium-ion battery capacity are critical challenges that can limit their application and reliability. Popular solutions, such as equivalent circuit models (ECM) and physical methods, can explain internal battery changes but rely on accurate parameter estimation and modeling, which may limit their implementation. Machine learning methods show promise but are black-box in nature and not transparent. This paper proposes an efficient and transparent data-driven system identification approach using the Zero-Pole-Gain (ZPG) model to analyze Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) data for battery capacity estimation and multi-cycle forecasting. Using ZPG model poles as features and a simple polynomial relationship, the method outperforms the existing Gaussian Process Machine Learning (GPML) method on 10 out of 12 batteries. Further, this paper employs the Auto-Regressive eXogenous (ARX) technique for self-model capacity forecasting on the same battery and cross-battery model-transfer forecasting for unseen batteries under varying temperatures. Results from 12 batteries and over 20,000 EIS measurements show a low Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.08 mAh for self-model forecasting and 0.19 mAh for model-transfer forecasting, with a forecasting horizon of 30\% battery lifecycle. Comprehensive results demonstrate the value of the proposed method for capacity estimation and forecasting in battery management systems.

title: Spatial projection regularization based on double generalized cross-validation in acoustic calculation
abstract: This study investigates the error generation mechanisms in inverse problems, revealing that the computational accuracy of regularization methods is intrinsically related to the projection amplitude of measurement information in vector spaces. When the projection amplitude of measurement information in specific vector spaces is relatively small, the measurement information becomes susceptible to noise contamination, where noise components within these spaces significantly interfere with the solving process. Conventional regularization methods (e.g., Tikhonov regularization and Truncated Singular Value Decomposition (TSVD)) primarily target noise components associated with small singular values while neglecting noise interference in vector spaces corresponding to large singular values, thereby limiting their denoising effectiveness. To address this limitation, we propose a Spatial Projection Regularization (SPR) algorithm. Unlike traditional singular-value-amplitude-based filtering approaches, the SPR algorithm implements spatial truncation based on the projection amplitude of measurement information in vector spaces, achieving optimal balance between measurement information preservation and noise suppression. For automated computation, a Double Generalized Cross-Validation (D-GCV) method was developed by leveraging the parameter self-selection characteristics of SPR. Furthermore, the algorithm mechanism was thoroughly analyzed based on the physical properties of acoustic inverse problems. Theoretical investigations demonstrate that the projection-amplitude-based spatial truncation strategy better aligns with the computational characteristics of acoustic inverse problem. Numerical simulations using the equivalent source method were conducted for monopole, dipole, quadrupole, and asymmetric sound sources. Results demonstrate that compared with Tikhonov and TSVD methods, the SPR algorithm achieves superior noise suppression while preserving detailed acoustic field characteristics. Within the 100 ∼ 2000 Hz frequency range, the D-GCV method automatically selects optimal parameters, enabling SPR to significantly outperform conventional methods in computational accuracy. The dual-piston sound source embedded in a rigid enclosure has also verified the superiority of the SPR algorithm under varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Additional dual-source localization experiments further validate the algorithm’s engineering practicality and effectiveness.

title: Effective thickness mapping for composite laminates based on full wavefield guided wave analysis
abstract: Local wavenumber estimation has emerged as a robust tool for damage detection, localization, and thickness estimation in composite structures. However, its practical application faces challenges, particularly in selecting suitable excitation frequencies and addressing the narrowband limitations inherent in conventional local wavenumber estimation techniques. To overcome these constraints, this study introduces a novel method that leverages broadband excitation to enhance thickness estimation by exploiting local variations in dispersion curves. In the proposed approach, broadband guided waves are generated using piezoelectric actuators and recorded with a scanning laser Doppler vibrometer over a densely sampled inspection grid. Initially, fundamental anti-symmetric (A0) mode is extracted through filtering in the wavenumber-wavenumber-frequency domain. Subsequently, a three-dimensional circular tube-like filter is applied to filter a narrowband dataset within the A0 mode by effectively removing most components of the A0 mode. The filtered data is then transformed from the wavenumber-wavenumber-frequency domain to the spatial frequency domain. A frequency shift index is introduced for each point in the wavefield spectrum to quantify its correlation with the local effective thickness. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method were validated through experimental measurements conducted on an omega-stiffened glass fiber-reinforced polymer aerospace panel.

title: Dynamic modeling and control of hard-magneto-viscoelastic plates
abstract: Hard-magnetic soft materials can rapidly respond to remote magnetic fields, offering great potential for soft robotics and biomedical applications. Herein, this study proposes a systematic computational framework for dynamic modeling and control of hard-magneto-viscoelastic (HMVE) plates actuated by magnetic fields. The dynamic model of the hard-magneto-viscoelastic plate is developed using the absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF) to accurately capture its dynamic responses with geometric nonlinearity. The constitutive model of ideal hard-magnetic soft materials, incorporating the Kelvin-Voigt dissipation, is embedded into a four-point fully parametrized ANCF plate element. The element internal forces and their Jacobians are derived. Then the dynamic equations of the HMVE plate system are constructed and numerically solved by the implicit generalized-α time integration. Furthermore, a novel strategy of dynamic feedforward control for the plate system is proposed. The inverse dynamic solver is constructed to establish the relation between the configuration with target coordinates and the applied magnetic field. This solver fully accounts for the inertial effects within the implicit time integration, maintaining the same level of accuracy as the forward solver of dynamic modeling. Finally, numerical simulations and corresponding experimental validations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dynamic modeling and control methods for HMVE plates. Moreover, a novel particle transport application is explored through the HMVE plate control in the case studies. This work may inspire further advances in precise prediction, dynamic control, and applications of soft robots composed of actively deformed plates.

title: An innovative three-dimensional QZS vibration isolator and multi-stage vibration isolation platform design
abstract: High-precision scientific instruments and equipments have extremely high requirements for vibration control in experimental environments. Traditional vibration isolation technology has bottlenecks in low-frequency vibration suppression, long-term stability and adaptability to complex environments, which makes it difficult to meet the needs of high-end scientific research. The quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) vibration isolation technology provides a new way of thinking to solve this problem through the special non-linear stiffness design, which can effectively isolate the low-frequency vibration while guaranteeing the high bearing capacity. This project focuses on three-dimensional QZS vibration isolation isolator and multi-stage QZS vibration isolation platform to realize more accurate and stable vibration control. The research firstly designs a new type of three-dimensional QZS isolator, combining negative stiffness pre-compression springs and positive stiffness coil springs, and optimizes the structural layout so that it has high-static-low-dynamic stiffness characteristics in different directions. Subsequently, based on the nonlinear dynamics method, the amplitude-frequency characteristic and phase-frequency characteristic equations of the system are derived, and the vibration transmission characteristics of the isolator are analyzed. Further, the correctness of the theoretical study on the dynamic characteristics of the three-dimensional QZS isolator and the isolation performance are verified by shaking table experiments. Finally, a multistage QZS vibration isolation platform is constructed based on the proposed isolator, which integrates the air spring QZS system and vibration isolation grooves, in order to improve the overall vibration isolation performance and engineering applicability. This study aims to break through the technical bottleneck of low-frequency vibration control, provide efficient and stable vibration control solutions for scientific instruments in the fields of high-precision measurement, ultra-precision manufacturing, aerospace and other fields, and help the technological upgrading of high-end scientific research equipment.

title: Optimization of spatial resolution for improving distributed optical fiber vibration sensing performance in dam dynamic structural analysis
abstract: Traditional point-based vibration monitoring systems suffer from limited measurement density. DVS offers a promising alternative by enabling continuous strain measurement, improving spatial coverage and data richness. However, Existing studies on distributed vibration sensing (DVS) primarily focus on improving individual performance indicators, such as spatial resolution, strain resolution, or sensing range, while often overlooking the interdependencies among these indicators and their combined effect on measurement accuracy. In fact, spatial resolution directly influences both the measurement noise and the effective strain output, thereby impacting the signal quality and reliability of structural assessments. This study establishes a theoretical model to evaluate the effects of spatial resolution on strain resolution, measurement noise, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). A multi-point SNR optimization method is then proposed to determine the optimal spatial resolution for concrete dam monitoring. Experimental validation using cantilever beam tests and numerical simulations of dam sections confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Results show that optimizing spatial resolution significantly enhances measurement accuracy by balancing strain resolution and noise levels. The proposed method effectively improves SNR across multiple measurement points, offering a systematic approach for parameter selection in practical applications. This study provides theoretical insights and practical guidance for improving DVS in structural health monitoring.

title: Layered event-triggered robust switching cooperative strategy for dual-motor steer-by-wire vehicles under communication delays and interruptions
abstract: The increasing complexity of dual-motor steer-by-wire (DMSBW) system introduces significant challenges due to communication delays and interruptions, which deteriorate control signal consistency and compromise vehicle stability. To address this issue, this paper develops a layered event-triggered robust switching cooperative strategy by integrating switching signal processing with robust control techniques. First, the DMSBW switching control model is established based on the reception status of control signals at the steering motors. A novel robust exponential Hinf (REHinf) switching controller is then designed as the lower-layer controller to minimize tracking errors and ensure robust exponential stability via Lyapunov theory and the admissible edge-dependent average dwell time (AED-ADT) method. At the upper control layer, an event-triggered integral super-twisting sliding mode controller (ETISSMC) is developed to suppress adverse effects of communication delays and switching disturbances on vehicle stability while effectively reducing CAN communication resources. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments, demonstrating significant improvements in signal processing robustness, steering tracking accuracy, and vehicle yaw stability under practical communication constraints.

title: Frequency shifting: the key to approaching rolling element bearing prognosis to the first day, (conceptual framework)
abstract: Estimating Rolling Element Bearing (REB) life with its vibration signal, from the inception of its operation is an appetency in the prognostic field. To achieve this goal, a novel feature that shows the degradation process from the first day, is presented herein. In the current literature, the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is estimated based on the foundational assumption: “the vibration severity correlates with the level of degradation” and also by using features such as acceleration Root Mean Square (RMS) which is related only to the vibration amplitude. In these methods, the RUL is just estimated after the First Prediction Time (FPT) at the last step of the REB lifespan. This paper illustrates that the vibration frequencies, at first, formed in high frequencies (including REB natural frequency) and then shifted down in the frequency spectrum. This frequency shift is correlated to the REB degradation. Consequently, this frequency shift can be the foundational assumption for the REB life estimation. In this article, for the first time, Frequency Center (FC) feature is proposed to capture the time-dependency of the frequency shift; and the FC special graph shows the degradation process over time even from the first day. FC is an early indicator of degradation and eliminates the need for FPT determination. This innovative approach offers a more comprehensive understanding of the degradation process, paves the way for the REB early life estimation, and can revolutionize the REB prognostic field. In order to validate and observe the repeatability of the frequency shift phenomenon as well as the applicability of the FC feature, in addition to collecting experimental data from a new test rig, seven Accelerated Life Tests (ALTs) have been used from three separate test rigs.

title: Super-resolution imaging of multiple defects in metal thin plates using phased array ultrasonic Lamb waves
abstract: Metal thin plates are commonly used in advanced equipment such as aerospace and high-speed rail. Due to the coupling effects of material properties, manufacturing processes, and environmental factors, metal thin plates are prone to developing multiple defect damage patterns. The combination of ultrasonic Lamb wave inspection technology and phased array ultrasonic technology enables rapid long-distance, quantitative defect detection/monitoring of defect in large areas of metal thin plates. However, the imaging accuracy and resolution for multiple defects are limited by Lamb wave dispersion, mode conversion, and the inherent resolution threshold of phased array systems, which may prevent accurate identification of closely spaced defects. This work suggests a phased array ultrasonic Lamb wave imaging approach based on time-reversal and Modified Delay-Multiply-and-Sum (TR-MDMAS). The time-reversal technique is employed to focus defect-scattered signals and suppress the impact of Lamb wave dispersion on lateral resolution. On this basis, Correlation Coefficients (CC) and Coherence Factor (CF) of signal pairs are introduced into the beamforming process to adaptively multiply the primary contributing signal pairs, thereby reducing noise interference, suppressing low-coherence signals, and improving imaging contrast and resolution. The experimental results reveal that when the defect spacing exceeds the imaging resolution threshold, the TR-MDMAS method outperforms Delay-and-Sum (DAS), time-reversal and Delay- and-Sum (TR-DAS), and Delay-Multiply-and-Sum (DMAS) in terms of Contrast Ratio (CR), Contrast-to-Noise Ratio (CNR), and Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM). More importantly, when the defect spacing is less than the resolution threshold, DAS, TR-DAS, and DMAS fail to accurately distinguish multiple defects, whereas TR-MDMAS still enables accurate defects identification, achieving super-resolution imaging.

title: Investigation on the ballistic impact response and energy absorption characteristics of CFRP/aluminum honeycomb sandwich panel multi-layer structures
abstract: This paper models the space debris target plate as a multi-layer structure of CFRP/aluminum honeycomb sandwich panels. The harpoon capture of space debris was investigated through ground experiments and numerical simulations. Ballistic tests were conducted to determine the damage modes and ballistic limit velocities of both contacted and spaced CFRP/aluminum honeycomb sandwich panels. The results indicate that, due to differences in stress wave propagation, reflection, and energy dissipation mechanisms across multi-layer structures, the ballistic limit velocity of the contacted target plate was 4.7 % higher than that of the spaced target plate. Subsequently, a finite element model of the multi-layer structure target plate was developed using a user-defined VUMAT subroutine in ABAQUS to simulate in detail the impact response, damage evolution, and energy absorption processes of the target plate. The results indicate that the impact point location of the harpoon has a limited effect on velocity decay and energy absorption. Additionally, the front and rear sides of the target plate exhibit distinctly different damage characteristics: regular hole expansion on the front side and fiber tearing with delamination on the rear side. Regarding energy absorption, variations in impact velocity have a minimal effect on the total energy absorption. The contacted target plate absorbs significantly more energy than the spaced target plate, with over 85% of the energy absorption occurring during the penetration of the Al2024 aluminum alloy sheet by the harpoon. The proportion of energy absorption in different phases remained stable, with changes in impact velocity having little effect on the energy absorption ratio in each phase.

title: Semi-supervised dynamic generalization network with dual feature enhancement strategy for machinery fault diagnosis under unseen working conditions
abstract: Domain generalization (DG)-based fault diagnosis aims to leverage the knowledge of trainable dataset to enable the trained model to exhibit the excellent performance for the diagnostic task under unseen working condition. Nevertheless, existing DG diagnosis methods primarily focus on learning domain-invariant features with a static model, i.e., the parameters of their feature extractors are frozen once the training work is finished. Not taking into account the individual difference of the input samples, the generalization of DG method with the static model will be degraded for the significant distribution discrepancy between training dataset and testing dataset under varying working conditions. Besides, various studies presume extensively annotated data in training stage, which are difficult to be achieved in industrial scenarios. To address these issues, a novel framework named semi-supervised dynamic generalization network with dual feature enhancement strategy (SDGN-DFES) is proposed for machinery fault diagnosis under unseen working condition. In the SDGN-DFES, a dynamic feature extractor (DFE) is constructed for extracting coarse-grained features and fine-grained features by the static and dynamic modules. Whether the training stage or testing stage of the SDGN-DFES, the parameters of DFE can be dynamically updated according to individual samples. Moreover, motivated by the characteristic of the dynamic coefficients hidden in DFE, a dual feature enhancement strategy is present for further ensuring the reliability of the extracted domain-invariant features. Extensive experimental analysis and detailed discussions qualitatively and quantitatively demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method over some advanced methods.

title: R3PTL: refine, reuse, and remix – an innovative partial transfer learning framework for intelligent machinery fault diagnosis with sample scarcity
abstract: Over the past few years, deep learning-based approaches have been extensively employed in machinery fault diagnosis, achieving remarkable outcomes in the case of unknown target domain data labels. However, current methods still face unresolved issues, such as fault diagnosis in cases of partial domain transfer and sample scarcity. Thus, a novel framework for intelligent rotating machinery fault diagnosis is introduced to address the issue of sample scarcity in partial transfer learning. Firstly, an effective “Refine” module is proposed, which automatically filters out unrelated source samples to avoid overfitting. Secondly, the “Reuse” module generates soft-pseudo labels for target domain samples without labels, allowing for cross-domain mixing of data. Then, the “Remix” module mixes the data from different domains, constructing multiple mixed samples that can be used for both supervised learning classification and domain adaptation. In addition, a domain discriminator is used to continuously reduce the distinctions in sample features between different domains, thereby achieving transfer learning. Finally, the introduced R3PTL framework is verified by setting partial transfer tasks on two fault diagnosis datasets using episodic training and episodic testing. The outcomes of the experiment suggest that when compared to the mainstream cutting-edge framework, R3PTL achieved higher accuracy in fault diagnosis with sample scarcity, which further extends transfer learning to more practical production conditions.

title: Tunable quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolators with electromagnetic damping for low-frequency vibration isolation enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolator with electromagnetic shunt damping (QVI-EMSD) based on an array of permanent magnets for low-frequency broadband vibration isolation. The compact magnetic stiffness configuration is achieved through an array magnet arrangement, while EMSD is implemented via coil connections. A model for the permanent magnetic force of the array magnet system is established, and the magnetic induction intensity at any point in space is derived and validated. Two types of EMSD under different coil connection configurations in a 2 × 3 array of magnets are analyzed. The effects of the magnet size and array dimensions on the electromagnetic damping coefficient and stiffness are examined. The harmonic balance method (HBM) is employed to derive the amplitude-frequency response of the QVI with quadratic and cubic EMSD (QEMSD/CEMSD). The analytical solutions are numerically validated. The effects of the linear spring stiffness and excitation amplitude on vibration isolation performance are analyzed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed QVI-EMSD effectively suppresses nonlinear jumps, and reduces peak responses in the resonance region compared to conventional QVIs. Additionally, the design allows for adjustable positive and negative stiffness, providing adaptability to varying loads. This study provides a valuable guidance for the design of compact QZS vibration isolators with nonlinear damping.

title: Curved micro-perforated panel liners for noise reduction in small ducted unmanned aerial vehicles: design, performance, and experiment
abstract: Ducted unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), featuring encased propellers, offer enhanced aerodynamic efficiency and reduced noise compared to conventional rotorcraft. However, addressing the noise issue of small ducted UAVs remains a critical challenge due to compact size and weight constraints. This study proposes an innovative noise reduction solution using a curved micro-perforated panel (MPP) liner. The acoustic characteristics of the curved MPP, influenced by its curvature depth and offset distance, were systematically investigated through finite element modeling and experimental testing. A parametric study via finite element modeling revealed that increasing curvature depth enhances mid-to-high frequency sound absorption by extending interaction lengths, while optimal offset distance alignment with the propeller’s horizontal plane reduces sound pressure levels by 2.1 dB on average. A composite liner integrating curved MPP with polyester fibers further improved noise reduction compared to curved MPP liner without the composite, achieving up to 3.1 dB attenuation, whereas duck feather fiber integration demonstrated superior performance (4.2 dB reduction) at high rotational speeds. Aerodynamic evaluations showed that the curved MPP liner not only reduced noise but also enhanced thrust by 30 g at 5000 rpm compared to rigid ducts. The liner demonstrated effective performance with various propeller designs, with toroidal propellers achieving the highest noise reduction (3.7 dB) due to the stabilized airflow. Experimental validation confirmed the curved MPP liner’s effectiveness across 100–3000 Hz, emphasizing its dual benefit of noise suppression and aerodynamic efficiency. This work provides a practical framework for balancing acoustic performance, structural compactness, and aerodynamic demands in UAV applications, advancing environmentally compliant UAV design.

title: Design of improved viscoelastic dampers exploring 3D printing technology
abstract: Vibration attenuation based on viscoelastic dampers have long been used to cope with a variety of industrial problems. Nonetheless, the quest for improving the effectiveness of those dampers is still an active research topic. Very often, technical and economical constraints involved in traditional manufacturing processes of more complex damping devices must be dealt with. The emergence and development of additive manufacturing technology have opened promising opportunities for innovative solutions. Among the existing technologies, PolyJetTM is an additive manufacturing technique in which an object is built in successive layers by jetting drops of ultraviolet curable liquid photopolymers, thus enabling to create complex, non-homogenous parts, with high geometric accuracy and finishing quality. This paper intends to fulfil some research needs by reporting investigations conducted to assess the damping performance of a novel design of viscoelastic surface treatment, named herein “lamellar damper”, which offers the possibility of achieving vibration mitigation goals by setting the design parameters. The research work involves both numerical modelling and experimental testing. For the later, PolyJetTM is used to manufacture prototypes of the lamellar damper. Confined to beam-like structures, the study comprises: 1) the development of low- and high-fidelity finite element models intended to predict the damping levels provided by the dampers considered, in comparison with conventional constrained layer dampers; 2) the realization of vibration tests on a beam to which 3D-printed lamellar dampers are applied, aiming at obtaining a set of frequency response functions and quantifying the associated natural frequencies and modal damping ratios. In addition, simulations are performed to assess the influence of relevant design parameters on the damping performance of lamellar dampers. The conclusions of the investigation indicate that the lamellar damper can provide improved damping performance and that PolyJetTM can be a viable and efficient process for the manufacturing of those dampers for practical applications.

title: A novel frequency estimation strategy and filter based on the gearbox response mechanism model
abstract: In the gearbox response signal, numerous sideband components generated by different fault characteristic frequencies are interleaved. Coupled with the noise interference, this makes health monitoring based on spectral analysis highly challenging. Traditional filtering methods, such as low-pass, high-pass and band-pass filters, and mode decomposition methods, exhibit limitations in filtering out interference signals over the entire frequency spectrum. Moreover, the absence of speed information complicates the determination of appropriate passbands. Most critically, noise within the passband is entirely retained. To address these issues, this paper proposes a methodology for estimating characteristic frequencies and filtering interference signals based on a novel response mechanism model (RMM) of gearbox. The proposed RMM model takes into account the structural attributes and vibration response mechanism of the gearbox, describing the modulation phenomena of fault characteristic frequencies on the meshing frequency and its harmonics. The proposed model-based frequency estimation (MFE) strategy accurately computes characteristic frequencies even in the absence of speed information. Additionally, the proposed model-based filter (MF) can perform accurate filtering over the entire frequency spectrum or within specified gear train vibration responses. Numerical simulations and experimental data validate the viability and effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian calibration of Bouc–Wen hysteretic models with applications to seismic isolators
abstract: Harnessing the potential of base-isolation devices requires both experimental testing campaigns to observe their behavior as well as properly calibrated hysteretic models to predict their response for future hazards. However, calibrating a nonlinear hysteretic model based on a single experimental test might omit critical behaviors observed in other tests. This study performs hierarchical Bayesian calibrations for a series of bi-axial hysteretic models from the Bouc–Wen family that attempt to capture the restoring force behavior observed in two steel yielding damper pairs during a full-scale testing campaign at E-Defense. Critically, the hierarchical approaches incorporate data from numerous tests featuring different ground motions into calibration. Two different treatments of the prediction error variance are explored to cover both non-informative assumptions as well as probabilistic models for the error variance. The results demonstrate that the two different approaches yield fairly comparable measures of parametric uncertainty, e.g., posterior distributions, for a given device, but the different devices actually produce different degrees of uncertainty in the hysteretic shape parameters. Further, the impact of the two different approaches is minimal in terms of the prediction error variance for observed data, but the probabilistic model is much better suited to unobserved data. A joint calibration considering data from both devices also reveals that adding data from a second device does not necessarily result in a reduction in the overall uncertainty of model parameters or response predictions.

title: Dynamic behavior of shear-thickening fluids under harmonic excitation: An experimental investigation
abstract: Shear-thickening fluids (STFs) become more viscous under shear stress, which makes them useful for many engineering and scientific applications. However, their behavior under normal forces, especially when these forces are applied harmonically, is less understood. Here, we examine the dynamic response of STFs under harmonic excitation. Our experimental setup features an unbalanced rotor attached to a vibrating plate submerged in an STF-filled container. We monitored the rotor’s speed, the system’s displacement, and the STF force. Data from experiments without STF were used to identify system parameters, and measurements of the STF force revealed the dynamic nature of the STF force. By comparing responses with and without STF, we identified three regions of behavior: in the pre-resonance region, the STF force is negligible; at resonance, it acts as a significant damping force; and in the post-resonance region, it behaves like an on-off force. Overall, the STF effectively reduces resonance amplitudes. These results can inform the design of complex structures incorporating STFs.

title: A novel compliant mechanism-based large range 3-DOF micropositioning stage: Design, modeling, and experimental validation
abstract: This paper presents a novel high-precision compliant mechanism-based 3-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) micropositioning stage with a large range and planar layout. The proposed stage comprises three identical kinematic chains arranged in a parallel and symmetric configuration. Each chain includes a cartwheel revolute flexure hinge paired with compound basic parallelogram (CBP) prismatic flexure modules, together forming a PPR-kinematic chain. A comprehensive kinematic, compliance, and dynamic model is established and validated computationally. To mitigate the high parasitic motion and cross-coupling effects inherent in higher-DOF parallel mechanisms, an optimized flexure configuration and a robust control strategy are employed. An extended state observer (ESO)-based super-twisting sliding mode controller (STSMC) is implemented to enhance trajectory tracking while accommodating disturbances with reasonable control effort. A high-resolution laser interferometer-based experimental setup is established to validate the stage’s motion performance. Experimental results confirm the manipulator’s capability to perform large range micropositioning and micromanipulation tasks while maintaining high dynamic performance.

title: Mechanism-driven data model for tool condition monitoring
abstract: Efficient and accurate prediction of tool wear state and remaining useful life (RUL) is crucial for enhancing machining reliability, operational safety, and sustainable manufacturing. The currently common models for tool condition monitoring (TCM) can be classified into physics-based models and data-driven models. Physics-based models are primarily based on empirical formulas, failing to account for the dynamic variations in milling conditions and parameters. Data-driven models, on the other hand, are often influenced by the extracted features, leading to physical inconsistencies and posing the risk of overfitting during model training. To overcome the aforementioned issues, a mechanism-driven data (MDD) model that integrates physics-based and data-driven approaches is proposed. This model first leverages a physics-based approach to mitigate the issue of limited labeled data, constructing a labeled dataset guided by physical models, which is subsequently employed to train the data model. Then, based on the principles of Bayesian filtering, this model integrates the predictions from the physics-based model with those from the data-driven model using Particle filtering techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to standalone physics-based or data-driven models, the proposed model achieves higher accuracy and better physical consistency. Additionally, it can quickly correct the prediction results from small sample data, improving accuracy by 47.2%, thus enabling efficient and accurate prediction of tool conditions. By enabling more reliable tool condition prediction, the proposed method contributes to extending tool life, reducing material waste, and supporting sustainable industrial practices.

title: An evolutionary power spectral density model for typical pulse-like ground motions in structural random vibration analysis
abstract: Power spectral density (PSD) models are widely utilized for stochastic ground motion and have evolved into evolutionary power spectral density (EPSD) models to capture the inherent non-stationarity. However, an EPSD model specifically for near-fault pulse-like ground motions (PLGMs) remains undeveloped. This absence has hindered the advancement of random vibration analysis methods for structures subjected to PLGMs, as classical approaches rely on PSD-based formulations. Addressing this gap is crucial for improving the seismic resilience of structures in near-fault regions. In response, this study introduces a comprehensive EPSD modeling framework for PLGMs. First, the theoretical foundation and a database of typical PLGMs are established. Next, the framework for developing the EPSD model for PLGMs is elaborated. Finally, a comprehensive numerical implementation and application of the proposed EPSD modeling approach is presented. The numerical examples demonstrate the model’s capability to capture the pulse-like characteristics of ground motions and its effectiveness in structural random vibration analysis.

title: On chatter stability in micro milling considering multiple delays from cutter runout and tool deflections
abstract: The existing body of research on multiple delays in micro milling has primarily focused on analyzing the effects induced by tool runout. However, under varying machining parameters, the variations in static tool deflections caused by different cutting forces from tool runout will further influence the distribution range of multiple delay periods, thereby introducing additional complexities to the stability analysis of the machining process. This article proposes a dynamic model to characterize the chatter stability of micro milling with the consideration of the coupled effects of cutter runout and tool deflections, emphasizing the advantage of taking account into multiple delays caused by both factors. Based on Timoshenko beam theory and the radial runout model, an iterative algorithm is constructed to calculate the tool’s actual effective radii under deflections. Subsequently, instantaneous directional factors involved in the dynamic model are reconstructed with the aid of the obtained multiple delays and actual tool’s radii. Finally, a numerical algorithm aiming at efficiently solving the stability lobe diagrams (SLDs) is constructed based on Newton–Raphson method, greatly reducing the computation time required by the traditional semi-discretization method. A series of micro milling experiments verify the proposed model.

title: Random vibration analysis of linear structures under time-varying coherent nonstationary excitations: An enhanced evolutionary spectral method
abstract: The classic evolutionary spectral method for the nonstationary random vibration analysis of linear structures is generally based on the assumption of time invariant coherence function. For the need of refined random vibration analysis, an enhanced evolutionary spectral method is proposed for the random vibration analysis of structures subjected to time-varying coherent nonstationary excitations. First, the enhanced evolutionary spectral analysis framework is established based on the Cholesky decomposition of the evolutionary power spectral density matrix of time-varying coherent nonstationary excitations. Further, a fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based algorithm is proposed to expedite the computation of this framework with the aid of the diagonal proper orthogonal decomposition interpolation technique. The proposed method possesses a rigorous mathematical derivation that can degenerate into the classic evolutionary spectral method. It demonstrates exceptional efficiency because it replaces numerous time history analyses with FFT operations and executes Cholesky decomposition only at sparse interpolation points. Additionally, it can selectively solve the responses of specific degrees of freedom according to requirements to obtain a higher efficiency. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and high efficiency of the proposed method through comparison with the results obtained from Monte Carlo simulation.

title: Self-tuning vibration absorber based on model reference adaptive control
abstract: The performance of a tuned vibration absorber (TVA) is highly sensitive to its structural parameters, and even slight mistuning can significantly degrade its vibration suppression performance. However, structural parameter uncertainties caused by manufacturing tolerances, along with time-varying features such as parameter drift or abrupt changes due to aging or environmental variations, often result in TVA mistuning and degraded performance. Therefore, developing precise tuning strategies for TVAs with uncertain and time-varying structural parameters is of great importance, and further research is urgently needed in this area. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a self-tuning vibration absorber based on model reference adaptive control (MR-STVA), which possesses the ability to compensate for structural parameter uncertainty, drift, and abrupt changes − a capability we define as structural parameter adaptive compensation. First, an adaptive control law is developed using Lyapunov stability theory to ensure system stability. Then, a fixed Lyapunov matrix is constructed by leveraging the specific structure of the TVA, allowing MR-STVA to track dynamic reference models and maintain effective suppression of time-varying disturbances. Moreover, a non-uniform gain scaling strategy is proposed to suppress undesired variations in the adaptive control law and reduce energy consumption. A series of experiments are conducted on a custom-built platform, including: (1) self-tuning under structural parameter uncertainty, (2) self-tuning under abrupt stiffness changes, (3) adaptive vibration absorption under time-varying excitations, and (4) convergence performance evaluation. Results verify the effectiveness and practical feasibility of MR-STVA under complex and variable operating conditions.

title: Improved operational modal analysis by modified data-driven stochastic subspace identification featuring visualization
abstract: Operational modal analysis is beneficial to structural health monitoring and design. Data-driven stochastic subspace identification, in particular, is one of the commonly accepted system identification methods in operational modal analysis due to stability, accuracy, and efficiency. This parametric method requires appropriate estimation of the model order for extracting accurate modal parameters. A stabilization diagram is an alternative approach to address this challenge. Still, establishing this tool is computationally expensive and highly dependent on the experience of users. An improved modal parameter estimation framework is therefore developed in this study by modifying the data-driven stochastic subspace identification to effectively identify accurate structural modes, while not compromising the ease of usage. In this framework, due to the application of singular value decomposition to the projection matrix, the observability matrix is sorted into interpretable components. These components are paired based on vector direction similarity on the basis of modal energy, wherein resulting pairs are separately utilized for modal parameter estimation, allowing for the sequential identification of modes. Additionally, a mode validation algorithm is developed to eliminate spurious modes. A numerical study is carried out to demonstrate the proposed framework, and two experimental examples are conducted to investigate the performance. The row size of the Hankel matrix, as a user-defined parameter, is found to influence the precision of estimates and mode identifiability, where non-identification can be mitigated through adjustment without overestimation. Results further verify the reliance of the proposed framework on the modal energy of structural modes, its accuracy for lightly damped systems, and its reduced computational cost through its operations on smaller matrices at a single model order only. Moreover, numerical and experimental studies illustrate its ease of usage through the sequential mode selection process, which required minimal expert intervention, and through verifiable outcomes via visualization of the modal responses.

title: Multiscale thermal-fluid-solid coupled dynamic modeling of multi-type bearing-supported rotor system with misalignment faults
abstract: The multi-type bearing-supported rotor (MBR) system serves as the primary power transmission assembly in heavy machinery with long-term continuous operation due to its exceptional load capacity and stability. The interplay of assembly-induced misalignment faults, lubrication interfaces, thermal characteristics, and mechanical properties in MBR systems progressively amplifies system degradation. In this regard, this study develops a thermal-fluid-solid coupled method for flexible MBR systems with various misalignment faults. The transient coupling effects of heat generation and lubrication degradation are characterized by the lubricant rheological properties and the internal microscopic contact profiles. The thermal-fluid-solid coupling analytical stiffness of multi-type bearings is derived based on the chain rule and implicit function differentiation. The multiscale coupling in MBR systems is comprehensively addressed through an interactive iterative co-development of solid, fluid, and thermal submodules. The multi-physics characterization capability of the developed approach is validated by an established experimental platform. The spatio-temporal evolution mechanisms of the MBR system’s structural dimensions, lubricant film, and temperature are investigated. Numerical analysis demonstrates the energy allocation mechanism of the bearing initial clearance within the MBR system. Additionally, a reasonable initial clearance design range is provided for both healthy and misaligned MBR systems from the perspectives of energy allocation and vibration control.

title: Accurate phase-based 3D positioning for machine calibration using perspective-aligned gabor filter and monocular vision
abstract: Inspired by recent advancements in phase-based motion estimation techniques, which have achieved an accuracy of 0.003 pxl, reaching the theoretical limit of an 8-bit image (1/255 pxl), this study extends phase-based methods to the field of 3D positioning by leveraging the unique properties of image phase. Using a multi-grid square-dot board and a novel perspective-aligned Gabor filter, the 3D position of the board center is accurately measured with a single camera, achieving a total mean absolute error of approximately 0.01 mm at a capturing distance of 1 m under daylight conditions. The approach first detects the centers of square-dot markers in the image domain, which are then used to compute the homography matrix that maps the board coordinates to the image plane. The relative 3D position is subsequently determined by decomposing the homography matrix in conjunction with the camera intrinsic parameters. This study provides a derivation of the phase-based marker center detection process in both non-perspective and perspective views, demonstrating that the marker center can be precisely located using phase zero-crossing. Additionally, it is shown that linear phase extraction under perspective distortion requires a spatially varying Gabor filter, which must be perspective-aligned according to the convolution overlap position. To validate the accuracy of the proposed technique, numerical simulations are performed for both phase-based marker center detection and 3D positioning. Further experimental validation is conducted on a parallel kinematic machine tool, where the end effector movement is tracked using the proposed technique and compared against measurements from a laser tracker. The results confirm the accuracy of the proposed 3D positioning approach and its potential for precise machine tool calibration tasks.

title: Experimental and numerical study on dynamic behavior evolution of cracked blade-disc
abstract: Cracks in blade-disc structures of aircraft engines seriously threaten flight safety. This study conducts vibration-based crack propagation experiments on both intact and pre-cracked blade-discs. The characteristics of crack propagation at various stages are analyzed, and the experimentally obtained crack paths are incorporated into a dynamic model to simulate vibration evolution during propagation. The model is verified through experiments and numerical simulations. Furthermore, predictive models are established to characterize the relationships among crack length, resonance frequency, and load cycles, including a direct mapping between resonance frequency and crack length. Results indicate that cracks in the intact blade-disc propagate radially, with the resonance frequency decreasing gradually at first, then more rapidly. For pre-cracked blade-discs, the crack initially propagates along the pre-crack direction and then transitions to radial propagation, accompanied by a resonance frequency decline rate shifting from rapid to stable. The proposed dynamic model and findings can provide theoretical support for life prediction and crack fault diagnosis of blade-disc.

title: Common distribution discrepancy knowledge distilling: A new out-of-distribution generalization framework for machinery RUL prediction
abstract: Plenty of remaining useful life (RUL) transfer prediction methods have been developed to tackle with distribution shift and knowledge migration. However, most of them completely rely on the presupposition that the testing target-domain data sample can be accessible in advance during the training process, which cannot satisfy the real-time requirement in some engineering scenarios. To this end, a new out-of-distribution generalization framework named common distribution discrepancy knowledge distilling (CDDKD) is proposed, which can implicitly achieve the distribution alignment between source and unseen target domains via mining the common discrepancy knowledges embedded in the heterogenous mechanical equipment. In the CDDKD framework, an information decoupling network (IDA) model is constructed to eliminate the negative influence caused by the interfering noise, thereby extracting the inherent degradation trend features. Furthermore, a new vibration characteristic-based high-order moment distance (HMD) is proposed to boost the discrepancy representation ability in both original sample feature space and high-dimensional Hilbert space. An asynchronous hierarchical update strategy is designed to ensure the effectiveness of IDA model. Ultimately, the experimental results on gear and XJTU-bearing life cycle datasets validate the advantages of proposed CDDKD compared with other typical and state-of-the-art RUL transfer prediction methods.

title: Arrival time detection of AE signals using multi-threshold wavelet denoising and improved AIC for composites damage localization
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) technology, with its exceptional high-frequency, high-sensitivity, and real-time monitoring capabilities, is increasingly recognized as a promising solution for structural health monitoring of composites. However, accurately locating damage sources in composite structures under high-noise conditions remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the difficulty in precisely detecting the time of arrival (ToA) of low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) signals. To address this issue, this study proposes an enhanced AE signal ToA picking method that ingeniously integrates the advantages of multi-threshold wavelet denoising and the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The performance of the proposed method is systematically benchmarked against state-of-the-art methods based on Manhattan distance statistics, higher-order statistical kurtosis measures, and characteristic function surrogate entropy variance model. Compared with the other methods, the proposed method demonstrates superior accuracy while maintaining high computational efficiency. Localization experiments conducted on carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) plate show that, compared with ToA detection based on manual identification, the new method not only maintains a higher localization success rate but also exhibits a similar error distribution. The results indicate that this method provides significant advantages in detecting the ToA of low-SNR AE signals propagating within composites, and offering a more reliable and efficient technological support for structural health monitoring, thereby advancing the technological development and practical application of this field.

title: Vibration suppression of high-load flexible rotor system using AMB with low current cost
abstract: High-load flexible rotor system experiences a sharp increase in vibration when crossing the critical speed. During active vibration control using an active magnetic bearing (AMB), current saturation increases the risk of rub-impact faults. To address the above issues, a control method based on variable-speed fast online balance compensation for H∞ (VSFOB-H∞) is proposed, which realizes the vibration control with low current cost and effectively improves the stability of high-load flexible rotor systems. Due to unbalanced centrifugal inertial forces and complex fluid excitations, the centrifuge exhibits a significant amplification of critical vibrations, characterizing it as a typical high-load system. This paper focuses on the centrifuge and develops a reduced-order model of the centrifuge rotor-AMB system. First, the VSFOB method is used to reduce the unbalanced vibration. Then, the H∞ control strategy is applied to specifically suppress critical resonance. The simulation verifies the effectiveness of this method in controlling asynchronous vibrations under fluid excitation. Finally, the VSFOB-H∞ control method is implemented in real centrifuge. The vibration was reduced by 51 % at the operating speed and by 65 % at the critical speed. The experimental results show that VSFOB-H∞ control method can significantly suppress vibration of centrifuge with low current cost.

title: Simulation and experimental study of a high-compact circular Halbach-array magnetic coupling for enhanced torsional vibration isolation in rotating machinery
abstract: Torsional vibrations can pose significant harm to rotating machinery, leading to large shear stresses within the shafts and undesired impact forces. Therefore, the torsional vibration control is a critical concern in the design and operation of rotating machinery. In this paper, a high-compact circular Halbach-array magnetic coupling (CHMC) is designed for enhanced torsional vibration isolation. In contrast to traditional array magnetic coupling, this paper presents a design that leverages the unique magnetic properties of the Halbach-array. The Halbach-array, which consists of permanently magnetized elements arranged in a specific configuration, amplifies the magnetic field, enhancing the performance of the CHMC.
