Therefore, a modified index is proposed, by employing the Guyan reduced (statically condensed) stiffness matrix which takes the DOFs measured by the sensors as the masters. The proposed index proves to be effective not only in identifying DOFs with higher strain energy but also in identifying optimal master DOFs for Guyan reduction that best preserves the original eigenvalues (frequencies) and mode shapes. Furthermore, error estimators for the eigenvalues and mode shapes in Guyan reduction are formulated which effectively explain the relationship between strain energy content and Guyan reduction error. A comprehensive case study is conducted to showcase the advantages of using the proposed strain energy index in BSSP from both perspectives of strain energy capture and Guyan reduction performance.

title: Mapping analysis of sliding bifurcation of a class of single-sided constrained oscillators
abstract: The three-dimensional mapping method is introduced to analyze the non-smooth boundaries of a single-sided constrained oscillator system in detail. We obtained the switching mechanisms and the possible local mappings on the non-smooth boundaries. Under the guidance of theoretical analysis, the occurrence of sliding bifurcations is verified by simulation. The motion switching of the intersecting points on the dynamic sticky boundary lines is analyzed for the first time, and the complete periodic motions are constructed by the local mappings derived from theoretical analysis. The characteristic of this research is that, on the one hand, it provides a new research route for the study of oscillator systems; on the other hand, the extension of the three-dimensional mapping method in oscillator systems reflects the characteristics of the dynamic sticky boundaries, which makes all the sticky boundary lines need to be classified for discussion and increases the difficulty of calculation, but two new bifurcation phenomena are obtained: the boundary surface grazing bifurcation and the second type of boundary-intersection crossing bifurcation.

title: Deformation sensing of fixture structure and double-curved skin surface in aircraft assembly using strain data
abstract: Fixture is widely used for locating the aircraft parts and ensuring the skin shape of aviation product in assembly. This research proposes an approach that determines the deformations of both fixture structure and skin using strain data gauged by fiber Bragg gratings to monitor their assembly status. The strain data of skin are transferred to curvatures and multiple curves are reconstructed. The skin surface is formed by the curves and its posture is registered to the fixture by location reference. An improved curvature interpolation method that considers the spatial lengths of gratings is proposed to enhance the shape accuracy of skin. On the purpose of adaptation to the bidirectional bending surface with variance of convexity, curve reconstruction and coordinate transformation algorithms are proposed. A mapping model from strain to displacement is established for the fixture structure by modal superposition. The orientations of multiple sensors on the structure are optimized to minimize the conversion error. The algorithms for deformation sensing are integrated into a developed monitoring software and undergo experiment tests. The results show that the maximum relative errors in skin displacement are 8.28 % and 1.94 % for traditional and improved curvature interpolations, respectively. The maximum error of board deformation is 6.13 %, which validates the efficiencies of the proposed methods. Verification of the software demonstrates that it can provide accurate and instant sensing of the deformations in aircraft assembly application.

title: Deconvolution of acoustic beamforming maps in interference environments with mean-reverting stochastic differential equations
abstract: Accurate identification of noise sources is the key technology for low noise design of products. Acoustic measurements are not always performed in the anechoic chamber due to practical constraints, and the signals measured by the microphone arrays may be contaminated by background interference. The results of acoustic imaging are blurred by background interference, making it difficult to identify the noise sources. A grid-based high-resolution acoustic deconvolution method via the score-based generative model (SGM) is proposed. The multi-step forward and reverse processes in the SGM are expected to alleviate the difficulty of predicting the real sound source distribution underlying the contaminated data through the neural network in a single step. In this research, the forward and reverse processes of the SGM following mean-reverting stochastic differential equations are utilized to relate the real source distribution to the output of conventional beamforming. The proposed deconvolution method is capable of accurately identifying the target sound source and suppressing the interference in numerical simulations of Gaussian and reverberant interference, as well as the closed test section wind tunnel experiment.

title: Optimal sensor placement method for system equivalent model mixing using correction forces
abstract: In the domain of dynamic substructuring for complex mechanical systems, the precision of frequency-based substructuring (FBS) crucially depends on accurate measurements of the driving point frequency response functions (FRFs) at the coupling points, including both translational and rotational degrees of freedom. System equivalent model mixing (SEMM) addresses existing challenges by combining numerical and experimental models to increase the accuracy of system dynamic predictions. However, the effectiveness of SEMM is highly sensitive to sensor placement, necessitating a robust method for optimal sensor selection. Accordingly, this study introduces an optimal sensor placement (OSP) strategy specifically designed for SEMM. The proposed correction force-based SEMM (C-SEMM) method integrates numerical and experimental models by applying correction forces, thereby allowing the pre-experimental optimal sensor and excitation locations to be selected using numerical models. Validations were conducted using a vehicle suspension subframe. The results demonstrated that the sensor sets obtained via the proposed OSP method tended to have higher accuracies, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Time-frequency weighted spectral amplitude modulation and its applications in fault diagnosis of rolling bearings
abstract: Spectral amplitude modulation (SAM), as a complement to the narrowband amplitude demodulation techniques, has recently garnered significant attention in the field of rolling bearing fault diagnosis. However, two major drawbacks limit its applications. First, due to the average effect of Fourier transform (FT), significant errors will arise in the edited amplitude, which subsequently affects its performance. Second, the resonance frequency band excited by defects is relatively narrow, while SAM applies the same magnitude order (MO) across the entire magnitude spectrum, which implies the energy of some invalid components will inevitably be amplified, potentially obscuring the characteristic frequencies. This phenomenon becomes particularly pronounced when the amplitude of the fault signal is comparable to that of the interference noise, as both are synchronously amplified or attenuated. In this paper, a time–frequency weighted spectral amplitude modulation (TFWSAM) method is proposed. In TFWSAM, Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) is employed to replace FT since it can capture time-varying amplitude and phase information. Besides, the TFWSAM method operates through differential weighting in the time–frequency domain. Specifically, it enhances the fault feature by assigning higher weighting coefficients, while suppressing interference noise through the reduction of these weighting factors. Due to the aforementioned improvements, the TFWSAM effectively addresses the issue where SAM struggles to reliably extract bearing fault features under strong background noise. Simulated and experimental analysis results demonstrate that TFWSAM exhibits superior performance, compared with SAM and other state-of-the-art signal processing methods.

title: Semi-active control architecture for MRE-based structure vibration isolation systems via combined Long–Short-Term-Memory and predictive control
abstract: Semi-active vibration control of Magneto-Rheological Elastomers (MREs) based isolators plays a crucial role in protecting structure from ground vibrations. Different hierarchical and modular control architectures have been proposed in the technical literature and several methods have been enacted for deriving the best suitable inverse nonlinear MRE model to be embedded into the vibration isolation control systems. In this direction, the prediction of the MRE magnetization current may be more accurate when leveraging the Long–Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks as they are able to capture long-term dependencies and complex temporal patterns in sequential data. Thus, vibration isolation performance of structures could be further improved. Accordingly, this work aims at proposing a novel hierarchical control architecture which exploits the combined advantages of MPC approaches at higher layer and the predictive ones of the LSTM at lower layer. In doing so, the proposed solution is able to compute the proper control force to be imposed to the structure, also adapting its value to the effective varying external conditions, while supplying the isolation system with the more appropriate magnetization current thanks to the improved prediction capabilities of LSTM network. The effectiveness of the proposed semi-active control system in guaranteeing structure vibration isolation is experimentally evaluated by considering an own developed test rig which consists of a vibrating structure base, a MRE plus Ball Transfer Units (BTUs) isolation systems and a flexible beam with two masses. Experiments, carried out in different scenarios and several operative conditions, confirm and disclose the efficacy and the advantages of the proposed approach.

title: Experiment and simulation research on the vibration reduction of a dual-beam system equipped with a wire-type coupling nonlinear energy sink
abstract: Coupling beam systems are widely employed in various fields, and some classical engineering structures can be simplified as coupling beam systems. In engineering practice, engineers hope to introduce fewer auxiliary devices to reduce the vibration of each substructure belonging to the coupling beam systems. As an improvement of nonlinear energy sinks (NESs), coupling NESs are attempted to synchronously reduce the modal resonance of each substructure belonging to the coupling beam systems. However, the existing references are mainly limited to theoretical studies, limiting the engineering application of coupling NESs. Against this background, this research carries out the experiment and simulation work on the vibration reduction of a dual-beam system by designing a wire-type coupling nonlinear energy sink, where a wire-type coupling NES is designed, manufactured, and tested. Through the whole research, it can be determined that the proposed wire-type coupling NES can be correctly realized by using common engineering units, proving the correctness of the coupling NES design principle. The wire-type coupling NES is not a pure vibration-reduction element. The vibration reduction states of the coupling NES are divided into linear and nonlinear states according to the dual-beam system’s nonlinear phenomena. Within an appropriate adjustment range, the dual-beam system’s vibration reduction effect can be enhanced by adjusting the nonlinear stiffness of each substructure belonging to the coupling NES independently or synchronously. Importantly, the experiment related to the dual-beam system with a wire-type coupling NES fully verifies the vibration reduction characteristic of the coupling NES made in the theoretical analysis. Overall, this research proposes and manufactures a novel wire-type coupling NES, providing a possible solution to synchronously reduce the vibration of each substructure of coupling beam systems in engineering.

title: Nonlinear model updating for dynamics of riveted joints
abstract: Joints are difficult to model because of various small-scale and nonlinear features, such as local geometry, preload, friction and contact. These features cause a local change in stiffness and energy dissipation which result in changes in the effective natural frequency and damping of the whole structure. Past studies have modeled bolted joints by constraining the nodes near a joint to a single pair of nodes and then using a nonlinear Iwan Element to capture the energy dissipation and stiffness loss in the joints. In this paper, a similar approach is proposed for modeling riveted joints, which seeks to capture the vibrational response of a test structure including changes in the effective modal frequency and damping with vibration amplitude. A four parameter, nonlinear Iwan element is used to model each rivet joint in the test structure. The rest of the structure is modeled using a linear finite element model (FEM), which is reduced using interface spiders and the Hurty/Craig–Bampton method to speed up simulations. Various modeling practices, including how the geometry is approximated, element types and constraint types, are explored to find which options produce the best results. The Quasi-Static Modal Analysis (QSMA) approach is used to find the effective modal natural frequencies, damping ratios, and mode shapes as a function of vibration amplitude. Optimization is used to find the parameters of the Iwan elements that brings the nonlinear behavior of the first mode into agreement with measurements. The same Iwan parameters are then used to predict the nonlinearity in the other modes of the assembly.

title: Time–frequency balanced data reconstruction for SHM based on wavelet-enhanced multi-scale residual convolutional block and frequency distribution loss
abstract: The reconstruction of structural dynamic data is critically imperative for the effective operation of structural health monitoring systems, owing to the unavoidable data loss or degradation encountered during in-service operations. Existing research predominantly emphasizes the evaluation of reconstruction efficacy within the time domain, with insufficient deliberate efforts allocated to fitting within the frequency domain. This oversight leads to suboptimal alignment between the reconstructed and actual data in high-frequency ranges, a typical phenomenon of spectral bias of neural networks. This study introduces an advanced model for the reconstruction of structural dynamic data, leveraging a combination of a wavelet-enhanced multi-scale residual convolutional (WE-MRC) block and an innovative frequency-domain-targeted loss function (FDL). The proposed model incorporates a long short-term memory network (LSTM) for its proficiency in capturing temporal correlations and a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract hierarchical features, which is advantageous for integrating features from the frequency domain perspective. Two numerical studies and one practical study are conducted to validate the superiority of the proposed model over existing ones. The results demonstrate that the incorporation of the WE-MRC block and FDL effectively captures features conducive to producing time–frequency balanced output data, with promising implications for real-world data recovery and damage detection.

title: A multi-expert diffusion model for surface defect detection of valve cores in special control valve equipment systems
abstract: The valve core is a critical mechanical component of control valves, and accurate surface defect detection is essential for ensuring the reliable operation of special control valve systems. However, current methods often suffer from unsatisfactory detection accuracy due to the uncertain defect size and the strong interference of background grayscale. Additionally, many existing techniques depend on heuristic object priors (e.g., anchor boxes and reference points), reducing adaptability to complex environments. To tackle the above issues, a Multi-Expert Diffusion Model is proposed, integrating a Multi-Expert Feature Extraction (MFE) module, a Low-Pass Guided Feature Aggregation (LGFA) module, and a Heterogeneous Diffusion Detection (HDD) mechanism. Specifically, at the feature level, MFE explores the large kernel convolution and multi-expert selection mechanism, which ensures the model can dynamically adjust larger spatial receptive fields and better extract representative features of multi-scale defects from complex backgrounds. LGFA predicts spatial changes through a low-pass filter, reducing intra-class differences in the multi-scale feature fusion process and providing a complete feature basis for decision-making. At the decision level, HDD transforms defect detection into a denoising process that generates category distributions and bounding boxes, which weakens the model’s reliance on heuristic object priors and ensures its scalability in detecting miscellaneous defects. Overall, the proposed method achieves high-accuracy surface defect detection from a novel generative perspective. Experiments on a real control valve platform show a 6.1% detection accuracy gain over special methods, providing a solid guarantee for the safe operation of electromechanical equipment.

title: Using fast Fourier transform analysis for the rapid evaluation of the diffraction fringes of optical components produced through ultraprecision single-point diamond turning
abstract: High-end optical molds are essential for mass-producing precision optical components used in biomedical, defense, and automotive manufacturing applications. These components are often produced through single-point diamond turning (SPDT), and their optical performance depends on their surface quality and shape accuracy. On mirror-grade surfaces, periodic microstructures caused by feed rate variations and tool wear can induce diffraction, leading to visible rainbow diffraction fringes that degrade optical performance. In traditional surface metrology, inspections of diffraction fringes require visual or laser-based methods, which are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and heavily reliant on human judgment and experience. To improve the efficiency of quality inspection, this study developed a fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based method to assess diffraction intensity. A full-factorial experiment was performed to analyze the effects of feed rate and tool wear on diffraction intensity, with the FFT employed to extract surface periodic features. The experimental results indicated that greater tool wear led to higher diffraction intensity, with the second harmonic of the FFT response being strongly correlated with diffraction intensity (K > 0.89) under 650-nm laser illumination. Analysis of the theoretical diffraction angle confirmed that the second harmonic was the main cause of diffraction, with the positional accuracy of theoretical diffraction spots exceeding 90 %. When the second harmonic response exceeded the surface roughness threshold, imaging quality was negatively affected. The proposed innovative FFT-based approach enabled rapid diffraction assessment, assists in tool wear monitoring and reducing quality inspection time by 65 % compared with traditional laser-based inspection methods. Thus, this method has high potential for application in quality inspections in SPDT.

title: Optimization of suspension bushing stiffness in early development stages using blocked force and energy index
abstract: Enhancing the noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) performance of a vehicle requires optimizing the stiffness of suspension bushings, as this stiffness directly influences these characteristics. However, accurately predicting vibrations or noise perceived by passengers in the early development stages is complex due to undefined vehicle attributes, thus requiring the creation of appropriate surrogate indices. This study presents a methodology to optimize bushing stiffness in the initial design phase of the suspension system, employing force and energy indices. This approach calculates objective functions based on variations in bushing stiffness within a suspension system mounted on a rigid rig and identifies optimal stiffness combinations through injection-based substructuring. Validation with a half-car model showed substantial reductions in kinetic energy and acceleration across various design parameters. Further optimizations were conducted on a MacPherson strut suspension system, incorporating strategies to minimize the effects of measurement errors. Focusing solely on NVH performance resulted in bushing stiffness converging towards the lower limit, which may adversely affect ride and handling (R&H) performance. In contrast, a multi-objective optimization strategy effectively identified stiffness combinations that balanced NVH and R&H performances. The energy index provided greater optimization flexibility than the force index, offering more local minima and enhanced fine-tuning capabilities.

title: Dynamic external excitation identification of electromagnetic vibration energy harvesting systems based on improved augmented unscented Kalman smoother method
abstract: In this paper, an improved augmented unscented Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother is proposed for identifying the external excitation of the electromagnetic vibration energy harvester in the time-domain. To reduce the drift in external excitation estimation, unscented Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother is incorporated into unscented Kalman filter to improve the accuracy of the estimation process. Given the poor accuracy and stability in inappropriate noise covariance, an improved URTSS approach with the symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) indicator is introduced. By applying the SMAPE indicator within the L-curve approach, the augmented state of process noise covariance can be effectively estimated, which improves the identification accuracy. Moreover, the proposed approach can facilitate the precise determination of the point of maximum curvature automatically, outperforming the traditional second-norm indicator in the accuracy. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, numerical simulations are conducted for two electromagnetic vibration energy harvesting systems exhibiting strong nonlinear stiffness and electrical parameters, verifying the method’s effectiveness under both harmonic and random excitations. Additionally, an experimental example is conducted under similar excitations, and the results further validate the applicability of the proposed method for practical cantilever beam-based electromagnetic vibration energy harvester. Results from the simulation and experimental studies demonstrate that the proposed method is valid even under 9.1% model uncertainty and does not rely on unknown external excitation statistics. This approach provides a solid theoretical foundation for identifying external excitation in harvesters and offers a viable solution for the miniaturization and compactness of wireless monitoring devices.

title: A conditional diffusion model-based data augmentation method for structural health monitoring of composites
abstract: To address the data scarcity in structural health monitoring (SHM), this study proposes a health index (HI) prediction framework based on a feature-transfer-based conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (Conditional DDPM) for data augmentation. Specifically, guided wave signals from piezoelectric (PZT) sensors are first processed using the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) to extract two-dimensional feature maps. Subsequently, a novel HI construction method based on the inverse Weibull distribution function is proposed as the condition for data generation in the Conditional DDPM. A two-stage training strategy is then implemented, where the model is pretrained on normalized feature maps to comprehensively learn data distribution patterns, followed by transfer learning on raw feature maps to leverage pretrained knowledge for generating high-quality augmented data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significantly improved HI prediction performance compared to traditional augmentation techniques and other intelligent generative models such as conditional variational autoencoders (VAEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs). Cross-validation experiments on a compression-compression fatigue dataset show a 25.5% reduction in root mean square error (RMSE). Furthermore, a generalization test on a tension–tension fatigue dataset indicates the method's potential effectiveness across different datasets. The work provides a novel and efficient data augmentation strategy for SHM of composite structures, showing promising potential to improve structural performance and reliability.

title: Research on adaptive denoising for oil and gas pipeline detection signals based on generative diffusion probabilistic framework
abstract: Oil and gas pipelines are critical to energy transport, and reliable defect detection is essential for operational safety. However, field detection signals are often contaminated by random noise, distorting defect features. Traditional denoising methods exhibit limited stability and adaptability under complex noise conditions. While probabilistic diffusion offers a promising multi-step Markov framework for noisy signal processing, conventional fixed diffusion strategy lack flexibility across varying noise levels. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an Adaptive Fuzzy Diffusion Denoising Method (AFDM) for complex noisy pipeline signals. AFDM combines a multi-modal predictive model with a fuzzy diffusion criterion, enabling dynamic adjustment of diffusion scale and diffusion step based on the noise state during the Markov process. Validation on both simulated and field data demonstrates the superior adaptive denoising performance of AFDM, achieving average SNR improvements of 10.12 dB and 8.94 dB, respectively. Compared to advanced methods (RLMD, NA-MVMD, ICEEMDAN, CleanUNet, EEGDnet, and TSMixer), AFDM yields 13.82 % higher SNR, 32.31 % lower MAE, and improvements of 2.33 % in SSIM and 2.00 % in CC on average. These results highlight the enhanced stability and adaptability of AFDM, effectively improving the representation and integrity of defect features in oil and gas pipeline detection signals.

title: Predictive control algorithm for the Adaptive Tuned Particle Impact Damper
abstract: This paper presents a novel predictive control strategy for the Adaptive Tuned Particle Impact Damper (ATPID), aimed at improving vibration suppression in systems with limited available information. The proposed control algorithm, called the Predictive Control Algorithm (PCA), is based on the prediction and optimization of system dynamics and operates effectively even when system parameters and external excitations are unknown. The only available input for the control process is the measured vibration response of the system. Under this constraint, the PCA accurately estimates the optimal height of the damper in real time, achieving vibration reduction of up to 75%. The algorithm also exhibits a second operational mode: when a theoretical model of the mechanical system is available, the PCA can incorporate this additional knowledge to further enhance control accuracy and performance. The algorithm’s two operating approaches enable its application in a wide range of engineering environments. The robustness of the approach is further validated through sensitivity analyses investigating the impact of variations in particle mass, excitation amplitude, and gravitational conditions. The results obtained from the PCA algorithm show that the height prediction error remains below 10%, with accuracy increasing in conditions of higher excitation and particle mass. The main novelty of this work is the development of a versatile and fully adaptive predictive control algorithm for ATPID systems, capable of optimizing damper parameters based solely on vibration feedback but also leveraging mathematical system models when available. The proposed control algorithm represents important progress in the development of adaptive mechanical structures employing particle impact damping technology.

title: Synchronous response of a large-scale rotor–stator model with multi rolling bearings based on high-accuracy FRF-based harmonic balance method: Simulation and experiment
abstract: A high-accuracy and computationally efficient method is proposed to predict nonlinear responses of the rotor–stator system in frequency domain. A modified harmonic balance method with accurate FRFs is proposed. A practical hierarchical computing strategy to define sub-system’s FRFs is developed and standardized for engineering application. This method offers significant advantages over popular variety of modal synthesis methods and can be applied with high-dimensional finite element model for nonlinear rotor dynamic analysis. The superior qualities of proposed method are validated by high correlation between the measured and predicted 1X responses of a practical rotor–stator test rig. The responses show the stiffness hardening characteristic of the Hertz contact in bearings, as well as the backward whirl and split resonance caused by the anisotropic stiffness. By analyzing the contact force of bearings it is confirmed that gravity and radial clearance are main causes of backward whirl and split resonance in this test rig. It indicates the potential of practical applications in engineering.

title: A new guided wave array-summated gradient product index (SGPI) for monitoring invisible hole-edge crack in the aircraft attachment lug under time-varying conditions
abstract: The attachment structure is the critical load-bearing component that ensures structural integrity. Due to its extreme service environment, it is prone to initiate hole-edge crack, resulting in a decrease in structural integrity and endangering aircraft safety. Attachment structures are often located in narrow and inaccessible areas, and have complex connections such as screws and bolts. It is difficult to detect timely that the crack initiated on the attachment structure surface is covered and invisible. Therefore, the monitoring for invisible hole-edge crack is crucial and poses a persistent challenge. The guided wave-structural health monitoring (GW-SHM) can monitor crack in invisible areas, but the varying environmental and operational conditions (EOCs) caused by bolt connection lead to poor monitoring reliability. Aiming at this problem, a new guided wave array-summated gradient product index (SGPI) is proposed in this paper. A two-level EOC suppression mechanism included GW signal processing level and damage feature extraction level is established to enhance the accuracy and reliability of monitoring for invisible hole-edge crack. At the GW signal processing level, the effective feature in GW array is obtained by eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) to use for preliminary suppression. At damage feature extraction level, the time-invariant damage feature SGPI is extracted by innovative quantification-enhancement processing to achieve further suppression. Finally, a reliable damage alarm method-based SGPI is established to improve monitoring result. The proposed method is verified by a monitoring experiment of invisible hole-edge crack propagation in the aircraft attachment lug with bolted connection. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

title: A novel rubbing force model for blade-coating-casing of aero-engine considering friction-induced thermal and wear effects
abstract: The rubbing fault between the blade and coated casing threatens the safe operation of aircraft engines, because this causes excessive vibration and fatigue damage. To enhance the accuracy of rubbing force prediction, this study incorporates both thermal and wear effects. Firstly, based on one-dimensional unsteady-state heat conduction theory and linear thermal expansion theory, the temperature rise and deformation of the blade and casing are calculated. The calculation expressions of thermal effects are validated against results from existing literature. Considering the effects of coating stiffness, thermal, and wear on the rubbing force, a new normal rubbing force model is established and validated using the measured rubbing forces. Finally, the influence of thermal effects, wear effects, and coating stiffness on the normal rubbing force is analyzed. The results indicate that under low equivalent stiffness due to the coated casing, the contact force between the blade and casing increases linearly with penetration depth. An instantaneous temperature rise from the ambient temperature to 600 °C and blade tip expansion can be found. Additionally, casing ellipticity significantly affects both temperature rise and thermal deformation. The research offers a refined model for calculating the rubbing-induced dynamic response and contributes to fault diagnosis.

title: Reference-periodic-similarity based reweighted singular value decomposition signal denoising scheme and its application for weak fault feature diagnosis in industrial rotating machinery
abstract: Reweighted singular value decomposition (RSVD) has demonstrated its effectiveness for signal denoising and fault feature diagnosis for rotating machinery in recent years. Different from traditional energy-based SVD denoising approaches which usually retain singular components (SCs) with higher singular values, RSVD leverages various indicators such as periodic modulation intensity (PMI) and Gini index (Gini) to selectively pick SCs that contain richer fault-related information. However, it is shown that PMI-based RSVD and Gini-based RSVD are not as effective in some weak fault feature scenarios. To overcome this issue, a reference-periodic-similarity (RPS) based RSVD scheme, which leverages fault period T as prior knowledge, is proposed for signal denoising and weak feature diagnosis. A new indicator, namely RPS, is introduced to select the most suitable SCs by evaluating the periodic similarity with a pre-defined reference signal. Using RPS, interferences from non-fault related signal components become less influential and SCs with very weak fault signature can still be selected for signal reconstruction. The advantages of RPS-based RSVD are verified by both simulated analysis and real experimental signals. The results show that the proposed method is powerful in signal denoising even when fault features are very weak.

title: Online tool condition monitoring based on optimized multi-sensor acoustic features for robotic abrasive belt grinding
abstract: This study presents a neural network-based approach for abrasive belt wear monitoring using enhanced acoustic features. By integrating Bessel curve-based nonlinear scaling with conventional Mel features extraction framework, we developed six distinctive acoustic descriptors. Three neural network architectures – 1DCNN, LSTM, and their hybrid – were employed for classification, with TOPSIS optimization determining the optimal feature-model combinations. Experimental results demonstrate average accuracy, precision, recall and f1 score of 92.46 %, 91.90 %, 91.67 %, and 0.914, respectively, with remarkably short processing times of 57.01 s for training and 11.11 ms for inference. The TOPSIS-optimized configurations achieved over 95 % accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency (training < 56 s, inference < 13.5 ms). This high-performance solution enables real-time industrial monitoring, offering significant improvements for intelligent maintenance in automated robotic grinding systems.

title: Metastructure-enhanced single-sensor method for improving UAV propeller fault localization
abstract: Propeller fault localization in multirotor UAVs is essential for flight safety, especially under limited sensor resources and complex environmental conditions. However, traditional single-sensor strategies often fail to distinguish fault-induced vibration features that are highly similar due to the structural symmetry of multirotor UAVs, thereby limiting fault localization accuracy. To address this limitation, this study proposes a single-sensor propeller fault localization method enhanced by metastructure racks. These racks are optimally designed using an effective mass random distribution strategy to modulate vibration transmission and improve feature distinguishability. Theoretical analysis, numerical simulations, and comparative experiments confirm that the metastructure racks substantially reduce the cross-correlation of vibration responses. The t-SNE visualization further presents good distinguishability in signal feature space. In single-sensor fault localization experiments involving both single-type and multi-type damage datasets, the Meta-group equipped with metastructure racks achieves average localization accuracies exceeding 98% in both single- and dual-propeller damage scenarios. These results are obtained with a lightweight Single-Layer Perceptron model requiring approximately 30 to 60 s of training and represent improvements of up to 23.95% over the Ctrl-group. Furthermore, even under data sparsity or noise interference, the proposed method maintains at least 90% localization accuracy, demonstrating excellent robustness and adaptability. This study offers a promising structure–algorithm co-design paradigm for achieving high-precision, low-power, and interference-resilient UAV fault localization.

title: A zero-shot bearing fault diagnosis framework utilizing spatial relationships among primary features under variable working conditions
abstract: Under variable working conditions, new types of faults are likely to emerge in bearings, and obtaining samples of all fault types in real industrial environments remains a significant challenge. Although zero-shot learning enables intelligent fault diagnosis in the complete absence of target fault samples, the hidden spatial relationships among primary features are often overlooked during the fault feature inference process, which can lead to diminished diagnostic accuracy. Therefore, a zero-shot bearing fault diagnosis framework utilizing spatial relationships among primary features under variable working conditions is proposed in this study. The framework mainly consists of three modules. The input is compressed into deep abstract features by the fault feature extraction module for seen categories through multi-level convolution, multi-scale residual fusion, and a spatio-channel cooperative attention mechanism. The symmetric primary feature dot attribute generation module is responsible for providing discriminative and geometrically semantic information as attribute representations of fault types. The fault feature inference module for unseen categories is employed to align the mapping relationship between fault features and the symmetric primary feature dot attributes. Compared with four recently published similar methods, the proposed framework achieves average improvements of approximately 6.25% and 3.09% in diagnostic accuracy on the two datasets, respectively, and exhibits better inference performance for unseen fault features.

title: Multi-projection support matrix regression for remaining useful life prediction of roller bearing
abstract: Support vector regression (SVR) benefits from strong statistical foundations for roller bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, but it requires disrupting the data structure for feature extraction. Support matrix regression (SMR) is a novel data regression method that preserves the global features of the matrix-form data but ignores local structural state information. To addressing the aforementioned structural limitation, a matrix-form regression model is proposed, termed multi-projection support matrix regression (MPSMR). In MPSMR, a novel multiple projection modeling mechanism is designed to capture local manifold geometric properties, which can preserve the intrinsic data structure while effectively capturing potential inter dimensional correlations. Meanwhile, in the multi-hyperplane regression model ensemble, an innovative dynamic weighting allocation criterion is proposed to enhance the flexibility and adaptability, making the model more accurate in predicting data under different operating conditions. Experimental validation on two accelerated degradation roller bearing datasets conclusively establishes the superior performance.

title: Primary and secondary resonance characteristics of electro-thermo-mechanically loaded GNP-Reinforced MEMS beams: A microstructurally informed approach
abstract: Electro-thermo-mechanically loaded GNP-reinforced MEMS offer significant potential for advanced applications in sensing, actuation, and energy harvesting systems, especially when mechanical strength, thermal stability, and electrical conductivity is important for reliable, multifunctional micro-scale devices. This study investigates the nonlinear dynamic response of a fully clamped micro-scale composite beam reinforced with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs), simultaneously subjected to a uniform temperature increase and an external electric force within a viscous medium. The beam is modeled based on Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, considering a polymer matrix embedded with graphene inclusions to achieve a structure exhibiting excellent tensile strength as well as superior thermal, electrical, and mechanical conductivity. Geometric nonlinearity is accounted for using von Karman strain theory, while the modified couple stress theory is employed to incorporate size-dependent effects into the governing equations. These nonlinear partial differential equations are reduced to a single-degree-of-freedom system via the Galerkin method and further analyzed using the method of multiple time scales to investigate forced vibrations under both primary and secondary resonance conditions. A comprehensive parametric study is conducted to explore the effects of various parameters, including boundary constraints, material length scale, GNP content and distribution pattern, initial electrode gap, and applied AC/DC voltages on the system's dynamic behavior.

title: Ultrasonic identification of CFST debonding via A novel Bayesian Optimized-LSTM network
abstract: Debonding in concrete-filled steel tube (CFST) arch bridges can significantly reduce their bearing capacity and service life. Traditional methods for detecting this debonding largely depend on the subjective judgment of inspectors, which can be unreliable. This paper introduces a nondestructive testing method utilizing ultrasonic waves to monitor debonding defects in CFST. Nine steel tube concretes with varying debonding defects were monitored using the radial-pair measurement method. To classify these defects, we developed a defect recognition model called BO-LSTM, which combines Bayesian optimization (BO) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, based on the traditional ultrasonic testing principles for CFST. This algorithm addresses the inherent parameter tuning challenges of traditional methods and can effectively capture the characteristic information of ultrasonic defects in CFST. The BO-LSTM model is compared with three conventional classification algorithms including random forest (RF), gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Experimental results demonstrate that the BO-LSTM model achieves optimal performance with prediction accuracies of 100%, 99.3%, and 99.3% for CFST specimens of three degrees of debonding, respectively. To enhance model interpretability, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was employed to quantify the contribution of each input feature, providing transparent insights into the model’s decision-making process. Consequently, this method holds promise for enhancing the application of ultrasonic inspection technology in the real-world evaluation of arch bridges, thereby improving the quality of arch bridge construction.

title: Research of propagation characterization of ultrasonic guided waves in complex gas–liquid two-phase flow pipes
abstract: Gas-liquid two-phase flow pipelines are common in the petroleum, chemical, and energy industries, rather than hollow or fully liquid-filled pipelines. The behavior of gas and liquid significantly affects the propagation characteristics of the guided waves. In this paper, the bandgap phenomenon of ultrasonic guided waves caused by a typical flow pattern of stratified flow is analyzed in detail and experimentally verified. The results show that in the non-axisymmetric structure of gas–liquid two-phase flow pipeline, bandgap phenomenon occurs at the frequency where the phase velocities of the higher-order flexural mode and the lower-order L(0,1) mode are equal, resulting in distortion of the reflection echo. A method for enhancing the detection precision of gas–liquid two-phase flow pipelines has been proposed, based on a meticulous analysis of propagation modes within bandgap and non-bandgap regions to identify the optimal excitation frequency. The maximum error of end reflection positioning accuracy is 1.06 %.

title: Adaptive fuzzy output-feedback finite-time control of vehicle suspension systems: An accelerated observation approach
abstract: In this paper, a fuzzy adaptive output feedback finite-time control method for the active suspension systems (ASSs) is investigated. To improve the observation capability (including the observation speed and accuracy), we propose a novel accelerated observation control scheme by employing a rate function in the observer design. Meanwhile, we introduce a new kind of barrier function, referred to as the finite-time tan-type Barrier Lyapunov function (FTTBLF). By designing the FTTBLF-based control method, the vertical displacement of the body can be converged in a finite time while ensuring that it does not exceed the safety constraint bounds. Furthermore, the fuzzy logic systems are employed to handle the unknown nonlinear dynamics, and estimate the unknown external disturbances using the nonlinear disturbance observer. Then, it is proven by using Lyapunov stability theory that the all signals in the closed-loop ASSs are bounded. Finally, simulation results under two different road conditions validate the rationality of the developed approach.

title: Investigation of the influence mechanism of intake blockage on the thrust characteristics of a water jet propulsion pump based on model experiments and the Time-FFT-Bis data analysis system
abstract: To study the effect of intake blockage in water jet propulsion pumps operating in open waters, this study conducted model experiments using a direct thrust measurement system under different blockage conditions, thereby accurately obtaining instantaneous thrust data. After denoising, a Time-FFT-Bis analysis framework combining time–frequency analysis, cosine similarity, and dual spectrum analysis was established. The results indicate that small blockages have limited impact on the periodicity and average performance of thrust, while large blockages significantly disrupt the thrust pattern and reduce performance. The blockage near the inlet lip significantly affect the intensity of thrust pulsation. Under different blockage conditions, the instantaneous thrust pulsation frequency remains around 8–9 Hz, but blockage at key positions in the pump inlet passage can cause the secondary dominant frequency to shift from 11-12 Hz to 4–5 Hz. In addition, blockage at key positions in the pump inlet can significantly affect the thrust frequency distribution and frequency coupling, resulting in suppression of frequency coupling near 4 Hz or 12 Hz. When the blockage area reaches 50 % of the intake area, the blockage will seriously deteriorate the intake conditions and destroy the frequency coupling characteristics of instantaneous thrust pulsation. Therefore, to ensure the safe and stable operation of water jet propulsion pumps, it is imperative to minimize blockages at critical intake locations and avoid large-scale obstructions.

title: Network-optimized sparse deconvolution with statistical-temporal constraints: A robust blind framework for repetitive fault extraction in rolling bearings
abstract: Blind deconvolution methods have shown great effectiveness in extracting periodic fault impulses, which provides crucial technical support for enhancing the reliability of rotating machinery. However, existing methods are constrained by their dependence on prior knowledge of fault periods and susceptibility to strong background noise or non-periodic impulse interference. To address these limitations, a novel network-optimized sparse deconvolution with statistical-temporal constraints (NOSD-STC) framework is proposed. Initially, a lightweight network architecture is constructed to optimize the inverse filter weight. Besides, a robust sparse kurtosis-temporal window regularization (RSK-TWR) objective is formulated to balance periodic impulse amplification and impulse noise suppression. Specifically, the RSK-TWR integrates a statistical metric to enhance sparse periodic fault sensitivity while penalizing abrupt temporal variations in filtered outputs through adjacent-step constraints, which effectively suppresses the influence of random impulse noise and ensures robust convergence during weight optimization. Furthermore, a weight correction module is constructed to adjust filter parameters by penalizing unstable weight updates caused by weight initialization. This adjustment enables the weights of any channel to directly serve as deconvolution filters for signal processing without requiring additional dimensionality reduction methods. The proposed framework eliminates the requirement for prior knowledge of fault periods, with its deep network architecture improving robustness against high-intensity background noise. The ability of the NOSD-STC algorithm in extracting periodic impulse components has been confirmed through both simulated and experimental signals, which also has advantages compared with some cutting-edge methods.

title: HVA-YOLO: A real-time instance segmentation method under Hybrid Visual Attention applied to steel plate surface defect detection
abstract: End-to-end real-time industrial surface defect detection is a crucial aspect of the production process for mechanical systems. Numerous studies have employed computer vision methods in defect signal processing tasks. Defects on the surface of industrial products often have large feature scale spans, diverse features and randomization, resulting in a single horizontal target detection frame that does not represent the defects well. The instance segmentation method can represent the defect region pixel by pixel, which is also helpful for subsequent monitoring and process control. This study further optimizes the feature condition self-recognition module based on the YOLO network. Multi-head self-attention is utilized to constitute an efficient visual self-attention mechanism to capture further the contours and detailed information of defects for feature learning with hybrid visual attention. Hybrid pooling and depthwise separable convolution for spatial channel down-sampling module are proposed for the first time and applied to the backbone and neck stages. The module can further enhance the ability of neural networks to extract high-level semantic information and effectively reduce computational resources. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve significant detection accuracy and speed improvement in steel plate surface defect recognition. Meanwhile, the real-time instance segmentation method not only empowers intelligent manufacturing, but also the segmented defect regions can help the subsequent improvement of the production process to realize the intelligence of the mechanical manufacturing system.

title: Identification and influence of cubic nonlinear damping of vertical track nonlinear energy sinks
abstract: Nonlinear Energy Sinks (NESs) are effective for broadband vibration reduction. Nonlinear damping plays a key role in NESs performance. However, the research on the identification and influence of NESs nonlinear damping is still relatively scarce. This paper experimentally identifies the damping of vertical track NES (VTNES) by appropriately using the restoring force surface method, which is the first reported. The Complexification-Average (CxA) method is developed to analyze nonlinear damping impact on vibration reduction performance. Results reveal that VTNES exhibits significant cubic nonlinear damping, measurable via the restoring force surface method. Nonlinear damping can effectively suppress saddle-node bifurcations. Furthermore, as VTNES nonlinear damping increases, the saddle-node bifurcation region, including the frequency island, shrinks until it vanishes. Increasing nonlinear damping can significantly enhance the vibration reduction efficiency of the VTNES across various excitation amplitudes. When the excitation amplitude is high enough to generate a frequency island, the vibration reduction efficiency becomes highly sensitive to the nonlinear damping. Therefore, the in-depth study in this paper provides valuable insights into the VTNES damping forms in practical applications and highlights the significant impact of nonlinear damping on the vibration reduction performance of NESs.

title: DDPM-LFR: an enhanced local feature refinement diffusion model for helicopter tail drive system fault diagnosis
abstract: Fault diagnosis of the helicopter tail drive system is crucial to flight safety. However, the scarcity of fault data leads to severe class imbalance, which significantly reduces diagnostic accuracy. To address this challenge, an enhanced local feature refinement diffusion model (DDPM-LFR) is proposed to generate high-quality fault samples and mitigate class imbalance. Unlike Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which rely on adversarial training, diffusion models like DDPM-LFR are based on a Markov diffusion process that adds noise to data progressively and then learns to reverse the process to generate realistic samples. Specifically, a Local Feature Refinement (LFR) block is designed to extract global discriminative features and refine local key features, improving the fidelity of the generated samples. Additionally, classifier-free guidance (CFG) is integrated to enhance sample diversity without requiring an additional classifier. Furthermore, a dynamic weighted exponential moving average (DWEMA) strategy is introduced to stabilize model training further improving the sample quality. Extensive experiments were constructed on the helicopter tail drive dataset. The results demonstrate that DDPM-LFR outperforms GAN-based methods in generating realistic and diverse fault samples. Moreover, experiments on the CWRU bearing dataset confirm the generalizability of DDPM-LFR in different fault diagnosis scenarios. The proposed DDPM-LFR significantly improves the accuracy of the downstream classifiers, providing a new approach for real-world imbalance fault diagnosis applications.

title: On the issue of global variability in long-term SHM: damage detection using SSA-KPCA-enhanced MSPC
abstract: Long-term structural health monitoring (SHM) is a crucial technology for the life-cycle management and maintenance of infrastructure. However, global variability—arising from identification uncertainty (IU) and environmental and operational variations (EOVs)—obscures damage effects and limits the practical implementation of long-term SHM in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, this study leverages the temporal-spatial structure of damage-sensitive features (DSFs) and introduces singular spectrum analysis (SSA) as a preprocessing step for kernel principal component analysis (KPCA), which effectively mitigates the interference caused by IU and EOVs in long-term SHM. Associating with the long-term SHM of the Z24 Bridge benchmark, an SSA-KPCA-enhanced multivariate statistical process control (MSPC) method is proposed and validated to address the impact of global variability. Specifically, SSA is employed for long-term trend extraction and noise filtering based on the temporal structure of DSFs, while KPCA is utilized to achieve nonlinear separation of EOVs effects in the principal subspace and damage effects in the residual subspace. Additionally, an optimal kernel parameter selection method is proposed to enhance performance. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms conventional methods, leading to a substantial improvement in damage detection within long-term SHM applications.

title: Editorial Board
Uncertainty propagation and subspace identification of isotropic wind turbines with the PO-MOESP algorithm
abstract: The estimation of modal parameters of an operating wind turbine is an important task, that can be carried out using subspace algorithms. The PO-MOESP is one of the subspace algorithms suitable for this task, since it can model the atmospheric turbulence as a process noise. Besides the point estimates available through the subspace identification, the knowledge of the related uncertainty bounds is fundamental for structural monitoring. While the methodology for uncertainty quantification is well-established for many subspace algorithms, the dedicated uncertainty propagation for MOESP-type of methods is missing. The aim of this work is to close this gap and develop an uncertainty quantification scheme suited for PO-MOESP. The method is validated by Monte Carlo simulations of the IEA 10 MW reference turbine in turbulent wind, proving its accuracy with a difference of less than 10 % between the target and the estimated modal parameter covariances. The application to a dataset recorded on the Aventa AV-7 turbine confirms the accuracy of the developed approach.

title: Towards an improved experimental joint identification in frequency-based substructuring
abstract: The dynamic behavior of assembled structures is strongly influenced by the dynamic properties of connections between the individual substructures, commonly referred to as joints. Accurately predicting assembly dynamics relies on identifying joint properties, which are influenced by factors such as preload, temperature, and vibration amplitude. These interactions make analytical and numerical modeling challenging, necessitating an experimental modeling approach. This study presents a joint identification framework inspired by the Lagrange multiplier frequency-based substructuring, along with four mutually independent modifications to the identification approach. These modifications comprise sparse regression, rigid-body mode constraints, excitation direction updating, and indirect parametrization. A parametrization-based approach is employed for estimating the mass, damping, and stiffness properties of the joint. The numerical and experimental results highlight the benefits of each modification and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for robust joint property estimation. • A reformulated parametrization-based joint identification approach is presented, inspired by the LM-FBS methodology. • Indirect parametrization and LASSO are explored as alternatives to direct parametrization and least squares. • Joint identification is enhanced by excitation direction updating and rigid-body mode constraints.

title: Enhancing motion smoothness and load capacity of stick-slip piezoelectric actuator through asynchronous driving method with preload coordination
abstract: Addressing the limitations of poor motion smoothness and low load capacity in existing stick-slip piezoelectric actuators, an asynchronous driving method with preload coordination (ADPC method) and the corresponding rotary piezoelectric actuator are proposed. The actuator is driven asynchronously by two driving units, each comprising a driving module and a preload module, achieving performance breakthroughs by synergistically controlling the preload during the driving process. A dynamic model is established to analyse the impact of initial preload and friction coefficient variations on motion smoothness. The actuator is fabricated, and the driving performance of the stick-slip, asynchronous driving, and ADPC methods is tested. The experimental results demonstrate that the ADPC method can completely suppress backward motion in both forward and reverse directions, as well as maintain high linearity at different driving voltages and high bandwidth of driving frequencies. Under high-frequency and large-stroke motion conditions, the ADPC method achieves displacement linearity close to 1, with 48.6 % improvement in speed smoothness compared to the stick-slip driving method, and reaches a maximum speed of 474.46°/s at a driving frequency of 3000 Hz. Load capacity tests show that the stepping angle of the ADPC method remains highly stable under a vertical load of 10 kg. The maximum output torque of the ADPC method reaches 95 N · mm, which is a 12.5 times improvement compared to the stick-slip driving method.

title: Combined improved U-Net network and electromagnetic ultrasonic circular array imaging methods for crack characterization
abstract: Electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) is widely used in defect characterization but face challenges such as low energy coupling efficiency and limited space, leading to low-resolution defect imaging. To overcome this limitation, an enhanced U-Net deep convolutional neural network denoising method, combined with an improved imaging method based on virtual element signal reproduction (VESR) for crack characterization, is proposed. This approach learns from two-dimensional time–frequency domain segments for denoising and utilizes crack scattering information along with VESR method for imaging, circumventing the limitations of the 2λ criterion. The experimental results indicate that the minimum crack localization error is 1.12 mm, while the minimum angular error is 1.33°. These results highlight the enhanced clarity and reliability of the proposed method for crack characterization, even in noisy conditions. The proposed method successfully characterizes crack with sub-λ dimension. Furthermore, the denoising method provides an effective solution for various acoustic frequency band denoising tasks.

title: High resolution ultrasonic imaging in stiffened composite panels by robust data-driven matched-field processing
abstract: Ultrasonic imaging techniques for waveguide structures are commonly deployed using sparse piezoelectric transducer arrays operated under basic wave beamforming such as Delay-and-Sum (DAS) or MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) methods. In the case of complex aerospace structures such as stiffened composite panels, attenuation, reflection, refraction and dispersion effects significantly complicate the beamforming process. This complexity limits the effectiveness of traditional time reversal imaging techniques, which rely on simplified assumptions of wave propagation. To address these challenges, the complexity of the wave propagation can be best leveraged by using data-driven Matched Field Processing (MFP) techniques. These methods, which utilize experimental or simulated data as virtual back-propagators, are predominantly employed within the Reverse Time Migration (RTM) linear beamforming framework, and yet remain underutilized in advanced non-linear array signal processing applications. This work introduces optimum virtual time reversal within the data-driven MFP framework using a sparse array of ultrasonic piezoelectric transducers applied to a stiffened composite aerospace panel representative of modern aircraft construction. Specifically, we implement the broadband Coherent White Noise Constraint (C-WNC) beamformer, which offers enhanced resolution and contrast by adaptively optimizing the virtual back-propagation models to the measured cross-frequency covariance structure of the array. Unlike traditional RTM, this approach minimizes the output variance to achieve MUSIC-like super-resolution, while maintaining robustness to model mismatch. This study also addresses the challenge of highlighting the secondary wave source corresponding to the damage, which is generally much weaker than the primary wave excitation source. The passive reconstruction of inter-element transfer functions using the Normalized Cross-Power Spectrum (NCPS) eliminates the need for active transmitters or pre-calibrated baselines. By passively “listening” to a limited number of uncontrolled hammer impacts, an effective Full Matrix Capture (FMC) active transfer matrix is reconstructed. This enables the application of the C-WNC algorithm to successfully image simulated damage in the stiffened composite panel, while effectively suppressing “louder” excitation sources. This result validates the proposed framework’s potential to achieve high-resolution, high-contrast defect imaging in low SNR complex waveguide structures using sparse and low-cost receiver arrays, and establishes a path forward for passive structural health monitoring.

title: Spectrum forming and its high-performance implementations for the blade tip timing signal processing
abstract: Blade Tip Timing (BTT) is a critical non-contact technique for monitoring rotating blade vibrations, yet its effectiveness is hindered by under-sampled signals that violate the Nyquist criterion. Traditional methods for BTT signal processing often rely on prior information or specific operational conditions, limiting their applicability. This paper introduces Spectrum Forming (SF), a novel framework tailored for BTT signal analysis, to address spectral aliasing and enhance vibration feature extraction. SF redefines “beamforming” concepts in BTT contexts, interpreting “beam” as vibrational energy at specific frequencies and “forming” as phase synchronization across probes. Building on SF, advanced methods—including non-negative least squares (De-NNLS), non-convex optimization with generalized mini–max concave penalty (De-GMCP), CLEAN based on frequency coherence (CLEAN-FC), and functional spectrum forming (FSF)—are developed to suppress aliasing and improve resolution. Numerical simulations and experimental studies on rotating blade disks and compressor rotors validate the efficacy of these methods. Results demonstrate that CLEAN-FC achieves superior aliasing suppression and target frequency detection at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), while De-GMCP excels in amplitude accuracy. The proposed SF framework and its extensions offer robust, high-performance solutions for under-sampled BTT signal processing. The Python code to implement part of the numerical simulation can be downloaded from https://github.com/zhang19980521/sf_mssp.git.

title: Piezoelectric, tapered acoustic emission transducer design and modeling method for high-precision damage detection in mechanical structures
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) technology is suitable for early damage detection and location of mechanical structures owing to its high-frequency and high-sensitivity characteristics. However, as the core component for signal sensing, common cylindrical AE transducers have a large contact area, which makes the signal time of arrival (ToA) to exhibit a systematic deviation, thereby reducing the damage location accuracy. Further, a complete model of tapered AE transducers with a small contact area is lacking, and there is no study on a design theory for tapered matching layers considering wave attenuation. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper proposes a piezoelectric, tapered AE transducer design and modeling method. First, based on the structural features of tapered AE transducers, an energy radiation model and a thickness design model considering wave attenuation of the tapered matching layer were established, with the optimum thickness of matching layer determined. Second, a dimensional model considering aperture effects and an electromechanical coupling model of piezoelectric ceramics were established. On this basis, a complete dynamic simulation model for the electroacoustic characteristics of tapered AE transducers was developed. The multiphysical field coupling and transmission process of AE waves was resolved, and the correctness of above models was verified. Tapered AE transducers with different matching layer thicknesses were tailored. The correctness of the tapered matching layer design model and the accuracy of signal ToA for tapered AE transducers were verified by lead-breaking tests, where the tapered transducers exhibited better ToA accuracy than cylindrical ones. Finally, tomography and bearing damage tests were conducted to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the tapered AE transducer in damage detection and location. The proposed method can provide a valuable theoretical framework for transducer design in structural health monitoring in complex environments.

title: Structured Bayesian framework for distributed dynamic load identification: Exploiting joint sparsity and spatial correlation priors
abstract: Distributed dynamic load (DDL) identification is a challenging inverse problem, particularly under limited measurements. To address the inherent ill-posedness, a structured Bayesian framework integrating joint sparsity and spatial correlation priors is proposed in this paper. The DDL is discretized into multiple concentrated forces, which are assumed to share common spectral support and exhibit spatial correlation due to physical continuity and shared excitation sources. The strain-load equation is derived using Duhamel’s integral and strain modes. The joint sparsity is introduced through an extended spike-and-slab prior, effectively reducing the dimensionality of solution space. A kernel-based similarity matrix is employed to account for the spatial correlation among discretized forces, enhancing the stability of the solution. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is solved using the simultaneous adaptive sparsity matching pursuit (SASMP) algorithm, which efficiently identifies non-zero spectral components without requiring prior knowledge of sparsity levels while dynamically updating prior parameters. The identified discretized loads are then used to reconstruct the continuous load distribution via orthogonal polynomial fitting and equivalent nodal force calculation. The proposed method’s effectiveness and robustness are validated through numerical tests involving diverse load scenarios. Even under significant noise conditions, complex spatiotemporally coupled distributed loads can be accurately identified. In addition, a wave flume experiment is conducted to further validate the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed method. The results validate its capability to accurately identify wave loads.

title: Research on three-dimensional vibration displacement measurement of rotating disc based on monocular vision
abstract: Rotating discs are prone to generating three-dimensional (3D) vibrations during operation. Existing studies on visual vibration displacement measurement generally focus only on the in-plane radial vibration, while ignoring the out-of-plane yaw vibration. To obtain three-dimensional vibration displacement signal of a rotating disc, this paper proposes a three-dimensional vibration displacement measurement method based on monocular vision. This method utilizes the vibration video of a rotating disc collected by a single high-speed camera as input, and applies semantic segmentation and depth estimation algorithms to achieve simultaneous measurement of the in-plane and out-of-plane vibrations. When measuring the in-plane vibration, this paper adds a location feature information embedding mechanism (LFIE) and a context information acquisition module (CIA) to the semantic segmentation algorithm, which greatly improves the detection accuracy of the dynamic displacement of the rotating disc. The out-of-plane vibration is predicted by a monocular depth estimation algorithm. In order to accurately obtain the out-of-plane vibration in the depth map, this paper designs a coordinate extraction module to determine the pixel points for depth information extraction. This paper produces in-plane and out-of-plane rotating disc datasets, and develops a set of time domain and frequency domain indicators to evaluate the performance of vibration displacement measurement. Through ablation experiments and comprehensive comparative experiments, the performance of the proposed method in three-dimensional vibration displacement measurement in a dynamic environment of a rotating disc is verified.

title: Signal recovery in structural health monitoring via dual-domain transformer-GAN with dynamic masking
abstract: Recovering missing signals in structural health monitoring (SHM) under complex scenarios, such as diverse missing patterns and the need for high time–frequency fidelity, remains a significant challenge for existing methods. Therefore, this paper proposes an automated signal recovery framework based on a Symmetric Transformer-GAN for Adaptive signal Recovery, named the STAR-Net. First, the generator of the STAR-Net utilizes a symmetric encoder-decoder Transformer combined with positional encoding and residual connections for long sequence modelling. The generated signal is input into a time–frequency dual-domain discriminator to ensure the fidelity of its time–frequency spectrum. The dynamic mask mechanism simulates various missing scenarios, enabling the STAR-Net to handle a wide range of missing conditions without the need to know the missing patterns in advance. The study utilized measured acceleration signals from the stay cables of the typical bridge. It validated the effectiveness and robustness of the STAR-Net across four different missing scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that in the mixed missing scenario, the time domain correlation of the signals recovered by the STAR-Net reached a value of 0.9978, while the multi-scale spectral loss was 1.4710. The STAR-Net was compared with four models: the k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), the Generative Adversarial Imputation Nets (GAIN), the STAR-Net-pruning variant (STAR-Net-PV), and the STAR-Net-time domain variant (STAR-Net-TDV). The results demonstrate the high accuracy of the STAR-Net, as well as the effectiveness of the STAR-Net-PV in scenarios with limited computational resources. The suitability of the proposed approach for SHM related tasks is validated by stochastic subspace identification (SSI) and short-time Fourier transform (STFT). The natural frequencies in the recovered signals and the real signals are identical, and the time–frequency correlation coefficient reached 99.83%. The direct transfer experiment results confirmed the STAR-Net’s ability to generalize across various bridge structures. This study provides an effective and robust solution for the automated repair of SHM signals in complex scenarios.

title: Electromechanical-coupled dynamic modeling method for in-plane vibration of multiple-input piezoelectric composite plates
abstract: Broadband vibration suppression in aerospace and marine systems faces complex-condition challenges. Piezoelectric smart structures offer active control potential through electromechanical coupling. For multiple-input piezoelectric composite plates, accurate in-plane vibration characterization is critical for energy transfer and multi-mode control. However, existing models fail to resolve two-dimensional electromechanical coupling under arbitrary boundaries. This work proposes a transfer matrix method-based dynamic modeling method for describing the in-plane vibrations of rectangular piezoelectric composite plates (RPCP), establishing a theoretical foundation for plate vibration control. First, the RPCPs are discretized into lattice systems composed of piezoelectric composite beam elements with orthogonal connection, converting the electromechanical-coupled dynamic problem from two-dimensional to one-dimensional systems. Then, an electromechanical-coupled dynamic modeling method for the single-input RPCPs is developed by establishing transfer equations and orthogonal transfer conditions of the piezoelectric composite beam elements. Subsequently, an electromechanical-coupled dynamic modeling method for the multiple-input RPCPs is constructed by defining two-dimensional transfer conditions between the single-input models. Finally, a nine-input RPCP is designed and modeled using the proposed method. Validation via the finite element method and experiments confirm close agreement between model predictions and measured/simulated results, demonstrating accurate prediction for electromechanical-coupled vibrations of RPCPs under arbitrary boundaries. The method offers a simple modeling process and high computational efficiency, providing an efficient theoretical tool for active vibration control.

title: A versatile filter model for the approximation of stationary stochastic processes with power spectral density functions in the form of non-rational functions
abstract: In engineering problems, the uncertainty of excitations must be addressed through appropriate stochastic modeling and simulation methods. One of the widely used approaches is to approximate the power spectral density (PSD) of a stationary excitation using an analog filter system, which usually makes the problem more analytically tractable. Along this line, this paper proposed a versatile linear analog filter system capable of simulating commonly used load PSDs in engineering in the form of non-rational functions, such as wave spectra, fluctuating wind speed spectra, and track irregularity spectra. By adjusting the excitation transfer relationships and system parameters, the model can achieve accurate approximations for PSDs with complex characteristics involving non-rational functions or even piecewise differentiable functions. To demonstrate its effectiveness and accuracy, the proposed filter system is applied to two representative PSD functions commonly used in engineering: the track irregularity spectra in vehicle-track coupled dynamics and the fluctuating wind speed spectra in wind engineering. A multi-segment filter model is generated for the piecewise PSDs of the Chinese high-speed railway track irregularity. On the other hand, the filter model is extended into a fractional-order system by incorporating the fractional derivatives to approximate the Davenport spectrum and the Kaimal spectrum of fluctuating wind speed. Parameter conversion formulas are also proposed, enabling the method to be conveniently applied to different target spectra with satisfactory accuracy. The proposed filter model provides an efficient approach for simulating engineering excitations. Furthermore, it has the potential to support stochastic response analysis and reliability analysis of systems on the probability density level.

title: A computational-efficient adaptive algorithm based on frequency point selection in multichannel active noise control systems
