abstract: Multichannel filtered-reference least mean square (FxLMS) algorithms encounter critical implementation challenges in practical active noise control systems, particularly when expanding quiet zones in complex acoustic environments. Integration of multiple input and output signals compromises convergence rates and elevates computational complexity. Conventional normalization strategies accelerate convergence speed but incur higher computational burdens on digital signal processors. Although frequency domain processing and partial updates can alleviate these issues, they deteriorate the real-time and steady-state performance of the system. This paper proposed a computational-efficient method based on frequency point selection. The inverse contribution factors for filter updates are obtained offline to assess the coupling degree of the secondary paths using their power spectral density ratios. Upon system activation, frequency-point-selective updates guided by these factors optimize computational resources, with subsequent time-domain conversion enabling real-time filtering. The proposed algorithm achieves comparable convergence speed and steady-state performance to centralized algorithms with reduced computational complexity and maintained system robustness. Simulation results indicate average noise reductions of 6.2 dBA and 5.0 dBA for the headrest and door systems, respectively, while experimental measurements reveal reductions of 4.8 dBA and 4.0 dBA. Furthermore, in low secondary path coupling scenarios, this algorithm can achieve faster convergence than its centralized counterparts.

title: Analysis and experiment of a novel three-directional vibration isolator with variable damping and stiffness
abstract: Vibration isolation is an effective strategy for reducing the transmission of ambient vibrations through the structure to the equipment. Traditional vibration isolation devices can only reduce the response of the equipment in the vertical direction. However, vibrations are typically multi-directional in most situations. In this study, a novel variable damping and variable stiffness three-directional (3D) vibration isolator was proposed to control vibrations under complex multi-directional vibration conditions. The triaxial stiffness and damping nonlinearity of the 3D vibration isolator (3DVI) were realized by a friction-extrusion coupling mechanism using curved rubber blocks, which is cheap and easy to fabricate. A static mathematical model of the 3DVI was established, and the vertical and horizontal dynamic equations of the 3DVI under harmonic excitation were deduced. The absolute acceleration transmissibility function was obtained using the harmonic balance method. The theoretical analysis results showed that the 3DVI exhibited low stiffness and damping under small loads in both the vertical and horizontal directions, which can improve the vibration isolation efficiency during high-frequency vibrations. At large vibration amplitudes, the stiffness and damping of the 3DVI increased owing to the rubber extrusion pressure and increased corresponding friction, thus effectively suppressing the resonance. The pseudo-static test and theoretical results were found to be in good agreement. The shaking table frequency sweep test reveals that in the vertical and horizontal directions of 3DVI, the resonance peak frequency of the isolator is low, the resonance amplification is small, and the vibration isolation efficiency in the effective vibration isolation area is relatively good.

title: Directionality effects in tuned liquid column dampers
abstract: Structural vibrations in the real world are multidimensional and multidirectional. The directionality effects of tuned liquid column dampers (TLCDs) significantly influences their dynamic characteristics and vibration control effectiveness. This study presents computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based numerical analyses for four types of dampers: (1) conventional TLCD, (2) toroidal TLCD, (3) star-shaped TLCD, and (4) polygonal TLCD, with a particular focus on the directionality effects of these damping devices. During the numerical simulations, to ensure a fair comparison, all types of TLCDs are designed with the same liquid mass, the same liquid oscillation frequency, and the same container footprint. A quantitative analysis and comparison is conducted on the dynamic properties and vibration reduction characteristics of these dampers under unidirectional excitation at various directions, as well as under bidirectional excitation scenarios involving two mutually orthogonal directions. The research findings not only provide deep insights into the direction-related dynamic characteristics of TLCD-type devices but also offer important guidance for the selection and design of TLCDs in engineering practice.

title: Methodology for health indicators design based on distributions’ distance measures applied to robust CSC maps. Application to non-Gaussian vibration-based fault detection
abstract: We address the problem of vibration-based local damage detection in rolling element bearing in the presence of non-Gaussian noise. The main challenge is to design a health indicator (HI) that efficiently detects damage at an early stage. Classical time domain statistical approaches, such as kurtosis or second order cyclostationarity-based health indicators, often fail due to the presence of large, non-cyclic outliers. Our methodology is based on cyclostationary analysis using the cyclic spectral coherence (CSC) map. Due to presence of non-Gaussian noise, recently developed robust CSC maps are considered (trimmed covariance- and Spearman correlation-based estimators). The empirical distributions of the samples from informative and non-informative parts of the maps are calculated and distance between such distributions is estimated. This distance could be interpreted as “difference” between distributions, and the progressing fault should increase this distance. Two scenarios for distributions’ distance calculations are proposed. They are based on the empirical distribution function and kernel density estimator. In the first scenario, we apply the Kolmogorov–Smirnov and Cramer test statistics while in the second one, the Hellinger and the Jeffreys distances. To validate the results, the monotonicity, the trendability, and the prognosability criteria are used for simulated data. For real data, when only one HI curve is available, we proposed a method that focuses on the separability (between healthy and faulty conditions) evaluated using the Fisher criterion. For the second real dataset, where only signals from healthy and faulty states were available, we proposed comparing the ratio between HIs derived for these two states. Our results outperform raw signal-based and classical CSC-based HIs. • New methodology for health indicators design is proposed. • Robust CSC maps are utilized. • Distribution of samples from CSC map are derived. • Distributions’ distance measures are proposed as a new HI. • Simulated and real data are used for validation.

title: Graph Laplacian-regularized pseudo-force sparse reconstruction imaging for damage in complex composite structures
abstract: Guided waves are promising tools for damage detection in composites due to their efficiency, large coverage, and sensitivity to various defects. However, imaging anomalies in composites with complex geometries, such as stiffened composite plates, is still challenging because of anisotropy and complex boundaries. This paper proposes a graph Laplacian-regularized pseudo-force sparse reconstruction (GL-PFSR) method for damage imaging in complex structures. Based on the first-order shear deformation theory (FSDT), it states that the scattered wave field produced by defects in a damaged composite structure is equivalent to that induced by pseudo-forces applied at the corresponding region of the intact structure. Thus, the damage imaging problem can be transformed into a force identification problem, in this paper, it is solved by optimizing a graph Laplacian regularized group LASSO problem. By adding a graph Laplacian regularization term, the inherent spatial continuity information can be leveraged, making the method better quantitatively evaluate defects. The method is validated on carbon fiber-reinforced plastics (CFRP) with omega stringers, and the results show that the method can image both simulated damage and real delamination induced by an impact. The results show that the method can not only localize damage but also evaluate the extent of the defects.

title: Improved mode decomposition method for vibration signal denoising of aero-engine shaft bearing
abstract: Aero-engine main shaft bearing vibration signals are critical for diagnosing bearing fault types. However, traditional mode decomposition methods often suffer from inadequate noise reduction or unintended removal of essential signal information. When processing complex signals, it also becomes difficult to distinguish between noise modes and signal modes, often requiring multiple criteria for mode selection. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved mode decomposition denoising method. In this method, Quantile-Based Noise Estimation (QBNE) is applied to each Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) obtained from Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN). This method can effectively remove noise while preserving as much signal information as possible, without the need for multiple mode selection criteria. Three simulated signals with non-stationary, impulse, and periodic noise, along with real aero-engine main shaft bearing vibration signals, are used as data examples. The performance of the method is evaluated against Variational Mode Decomposition combined with Wavelet Transform (VMD-WT), Moving Average Filtering (MAF), and Traditional CEEMDAN denoising method (Traditional CEEMDAN), demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness.

title: Development and evaluation of a laboratory-scale test rig prototype for full characterization of wind turbine main bearing dynamics and condition monitoring
abstract: Effective condition monitoring of the main bearing is essential for preventing unexpected wind turbine failures. However, the massive size of real-life main bearings poses challenges for laboratory monitoring. To address this, a laboratory-scale test rig prototype was developed for the full characterization of wind turbine main bearing dynamics and condition monitoring. Turbine scaling laws were employed to estimate the parameters of a full-scale wind turbine rotor on a smaller scale, enabling the accurate simulation of real-world conditions in a controlled environment. The scaled wind turbine parameters yielded a test rig with a main shaft diameter of 30 mm, a shaft speed range of 100–300 RPM, a maximum aerodynamic thrust of 1500 N. Three spherical roller bearings were used as test specimens, each artificially induced with 1 mm-deep and 1 mm-wide cracks on the inner race, outer race, and rolling elements. Vibration data were then collected from the rig for analysis. Preliminary evaluation using one-way ANOVA (F = 35.8, p = 0.00001) confirmed significant variations in key statistical characteristics of the vibration signals across bearing health states, indicating that the data collected from the rig were discriminative. A Bayesian-optimized LSTM model was then developed for main bearing fault diagnosis. Results from this investigation demonstrated that Bayesian optimization improved main bearing fault classification accuracy by an average of 3.49 %, while also reducing potential false alarms by 50 %. Additional evaluation metrics indicated a precision of 97.6 %, a recall of 97.8 %, an F1-score of 97.7 %, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98. These findings underscore the effectiveness of the proposed test rig as a valuable research tool for advancing the understanding of wind turbine main bearing behaviour and condition monitoring. Moreover, insights from this research methodology may be extended to other wind turbine bearings, thereby contributing to advancements in wind turbine predictive maintenance.

title: Real-time estimation and compensation of random drift in MEMS gyroscopes using cubature Kalman filter based on adaptive differencing Elman neural network
abstract: The random drift of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) gyroscopes leads to significant error accumulation in pose calculation, limiting their further applications in surveying, navigation, and positioning. This paper proposes a novel adaptive differencing Elman neural network (ADENN) and integrates it into the cubature Kalman filter (CKF) framework to accurately estimate and compensate for the random drift of MEMS gyroscopes in real time. In the proposed method, the random drift is modeled as a nonlinear autoregressive integrated moving average process, with its optimal predictor achieved using the ADENN. Notably, a straight-through estimator is introduced into the ADENN to enable gradient propagation in the adaptive differencing process. Additionally, a batch propagation strategy for cubature points is proposed to guarantee the valid integration of the ADENN with the CKF. Comparative experiments conducted on a customized gyroscope demonstrate that, compared to four other methods, the proposed method significantly reduces both autocorrelation and bias instability of the gyroscope output, validating its effectiveness and superiority.

title: Nonlinear dynamics of two-stage planetary transmission system
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic response and primary resonance behavior of a two-stage planetary gear transmission system. A translational-torsional coupled dynamic model is developed, incorporating factors such as gear backlash meshing and shaping, vibration friction under lubrication conditions, and transmission errors. Firstly, comprehensively consider the time-varying mesh stiffness under the coupling of various factors and conduct finite element verification. Secondly, establish a set of nonlinear dynamic equations based on the model. When applying the Runge-Kutta method to solve systems of equations, it is necessary to set parameters for the integrator to prevent issues such as pseudo-periodic solutions. Key behaviors on the meshing lines are presented through time history plots, FFT spectrum, phase trajectories, Poincaré sections, and time–frequency distributions, while bifurcation diagrams and largest Lyapunov exponent plots are utilized to explore global dynamics. Additionally, 3D phase diagrams and FFT analyses confirm these findings. Using the multiscale method, the study examines primary resonance characteristics at both the input and output stages, analyzing the effects of meshing stiffness, damping coefficients, and external loading conditions on resonance amplitude and system stability. Results reveal that the system’s vibration response changes synchronously with variations in external excitation frequency. Furthermore, when considering inter-stage coupling stiffness and other factors, the gear mesh pairs on the first and second stages exhibit similar dynamic behavior, with only differences in vibration amplitude, which can lead to resonance phenomena. Appropriately increasing support stiffness and damping, while minimizing fluctuations in external loads, can help mitigate the adverse effects of resonance on the system, providing theoretical basis for engineering design.

title: An adaptive multitask deep learning model for reliability analysis of vehicle-bridge stochastic vibration systems
abstract: The reliability assessment of vehicle-bridge interaction (VBI) system is crucial for ensuring the operational safety of trains on bridges. While deep learning models have been applied to predict VBI system dynamic responses, most models focus on either vehicle or bridge responses alone. Given the strong coupling and interaction between vehicles and bridges, single-response prediction fails to fully capture the dynamic behavior of bridges under moving vehicles. For this, an adaptive multi-task learning model (AMLM) is proposed, which integrates an optimization algorithm, a shared convolutional neural network (CNN), and two improved long short-term memory networks (LSTM), to simultaneously forecast the responses of both vehicles and bridges. An adaptive loss modulation strategy based on homoscedastic uncertainty is proposed to dynamically balances the loss contributions of different tasks. Furthermore, the probability density evolution method (PDEM) is employed for VBI system reliability analysis. The performance of the AMLM − PDEM framework is compared with the conventional PDEM, and the impacts of vehicle speed and noise levels on prediction accuracy are investigated. The results demonstrate that the devised framework can precisely and effectively predict vehicle and bridge dynamic responses simultaneously. Under the principle of three times standard deviation, the vertical acceleration reliability for the train and bridge are 0.9923 and 0.9977, respectively.

title: Characterization of high-frequency ultrasonic transducers using S-parameters: Separation of electrical and acoustic responses
abstract: Ultrasound based measurement and sensing systems are widely used in NDT, healthcare and process industries. To generate and receive ultrasound, a typical system comprises a pulse generator, a transducer, and a receiver unit that includes amplifiers, an analog filter, and an analog-to-digital converter (ADC), where the transducer is coupling the electrical and the acoustic domains. In many applications, improvements in the measurement properties require optimization of the transducers and hence characterization of their properties, i.e. electrical impedance for efficient system integration or acoustic bandwidth, which is typically done by looking into the measurement signal under certain conditions or for specific objects. However, an isolated characterization of the transducers is currently not possible since the recorded system response is superimposed by the electrical system response and possible acoustic wave propagation effects. This problem is even more pronounced for high-frequency applications, since RF phenomena, e.g., electrical reflections interfering with the measurement signals, are relevant.In this paper we introduce scattering parameter (S-parameter) measurements using a vector network analyzer in combination with time-frequency analysis for high frequency transducer characterization. It allows to separate the electrical and acoustic domains and isolated transducer characterization independently from the transceiver system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through the example of scanning acoustic microscopy, a standard NDT technique in microelectronics. We present transducer measurements, illustrating the separation of electrical impedance across a broad frequency range up to 4.5 GHz and the extraction of acoustic signals for detailed characterization of the transducer's acoustic properties.

title: Observability of nonlinear discrete-time systems with unmeasured inputs
abstract: The observability analysis of a dynamic system for a given sensor setup offers useful insights on the ability to estimate its states and parameters. Recent works have further extended the concept of observability to systems under unmeasured inputs, while efficient algorithms have allowed the study of realistic dynamic systems which typically involve multiple degrees of freedom and parameters to be identified. Observability algorithms however typically rely on the assumption that the measurements are obtained continuously in time. While the results obtained from this assumption are still useful, some of the observations from the observability analysis, e.g., the derivatives of the measurements needed for the system to become observable, are hard to link to system identification algorithms. Such algorithms use measurements that have been logged at some finite sampling frequency, while the inputs are often represented using a discretization in time. In this work, the concept of (state, parameter and input) observability under the presence of unmeasured inputs is extended to discrete-time systems. This allows accounting for the measurements and inputs being sampled at some finite frequency. The outcomes of the observability analysis are extended to include the number of measurements needed for a state, parameter or input to become observable. The work will discuss how this property is especially important in the case of unmeasured inputs. An efficient algorithm to calculate the observability of discrete systems under the presence of unmeasured inputs is introduced. An efficient numerical implementation of the algorithm is introduced using stabilization of the results across different numerical precisions. The algorithm is then used for dynamic systems which are discretized by methods of different order, and the effect of this process on the observability properties of the system is discussed. Suitable examples demonstrate how the observability of discrete-time systems with unmeasured inputs can guide significant decisions in terms of sensor placement and the modelling of the system.

title: A compact 3D bandgap multi-material metamaterial design for vibration testing
abstract: The use of metamaterials is an established approach in the field of vibration isolation, leveraging their exceptional tunability over a vast range of frequencies. A key challenge in designing lattice structures is the trade-off between geometrical compactness and wideness of the bandgap, i.e. the frequency range in which wave propagation is not allowed. A possible solution to reduce the size of the structure while maintaining or improving its vibrational performances, is to incorporate different materials in the metamaterial design. In this paper, we present a compact metamaterial, whose design is driven by a multi-material approach, that exhibits extraordinary properties in terms of wide frequency bandgap and lower frequency threshold. The vibrational performance of the proposed metamaterial is validated both numerically and experimentally for a unit cell with a side length of 3 cm. The results show a bandgap opening frequency of 1257 Hz and a low pass filter behavior in the range 1.25–13.83 kHz. Therefore, the proposed solution represent a significant advancement in the field of periodic structures, as the structure exhibits low frequency isolation performances relative to unit cell compactness. The proposed solution can therefore be used in several applications, such as in compact hand-held vibration probes and dynamic vibration absorbers. • Multi-material approach allows for a compact metamaterial solution. • Vibration isolation performance is unchanged compared to single-material solution. • Static performances of the structure are evaluated using optical techniques. • The metamaterial is used as a decoupling element for a novel vibration probe. • The effectiveness of the solution is tested in laboratory in operating conditions.

title: A triple domain adversarial neural network for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: In actual production, rotating machines often operate in different operation conditions, which makes it challenging to guarantee the superior accuracy of bearing fault diagnosis based on traditional deep learning-based models. Aimed at improving the effectiveness of fault diagnosis for rolling bearings in different operation conditions, a triple domain adversarial neural network with multi-scale feature extractor, triple classifier, and adaptive back propagation coefficient is proposed. Specifically, a triple classifier consisting of source classifier, target classifier, and domain classifier is designed to achieve the classification loss. Meanwhile, a multi-scale feature extractor with convolutional module and self-attention module is considered to transfer samples and extract features. Furthermore, an adaptive backpropagation coefficient which allows changing its numerical value based on distribution difference is implemented to enhance training effectiveness. As a result, the integration of multi-scale feature extractor, triple classifier, and adaptive back propagation coefficient forms an effective transfer learning model for bearing fault diagnosis in different operation conditions, named TDANN. Finally, the viability and efficacy of the proposed TDANN model are verified using the CWRU bearing fault dataset from Case Western Reserve University and the PT bearing dataset from a PT500mini bearing fault test bed in our laboratory. The higher accuracy and better transfer ability of the proposed model compared to other intelligent models are demonstrated in variable transfer tasks and different noise environments.

title: Real-time structural response reconstruction via window cached attention and structured state-space layer
abstract: Deep learning methods have markedly advanced structural response reconstruction. However, most existing approaches rely on the sliding window strategy to process streaming measurements, introducing computational redundancy and latency that are incompatible with real-time requirements. This study proposes WincaS4, a neural network that integrates a novel Window Cached Attention mechanism with the structured state-space (S4) model for real-time response reconstruction. The Window Cached Attention maintains an incrementally updated key–value cache, enabling stepwise processing and reducing redundant computation over historical measurements. Evaluation on simulated and experimental datasets shows that WincaS4 achieves superior reconstruction accuracy while reducing the average inference latency to 0.003s, thereby meeting real-time constraints under sampling rates up to 90Hz. These results demonstrate the potential of WincaS4 as an effective solution for real-time structural health monitoring and other latency-sensitive applications.

title: Fusing model-based and data-driven prognostic methods for real-time model updating
abstract: Prognostic methods broadly fall into two categories—model-based and data-driven—both of which have shown effectiveness across a range of engineering applications. Model-based approaches require an explicit representation of the degradation process, defining failure as the point when the physical damage state exceeds a predetermined threshold. Data-driven methods, on the other hand, leverage sensor data to directly predict end-of-life (EOL) or related prognostic information. Although both approaches offer insights that could be complementary and potentially fused, most existing fusion methods either combine the outputs from multiple methods or adopt a data-driven method to assist the model-based method. To further enhance the prognostic performance, this study proposes a fusion-based prognostic approach in which the output of one method is actively used to update the model of the other through either the crossover operator or the likelihood function. The proposed approach is validated using both an aluminum fatigue dataset and the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) 2010 cutter wear dataset, demonstrating improved prognostic accuracy compared to either method used independently.

title: Simulation-experimental study on vibration control of elastic dual-beam system with coupled nonlinear energy sink under dual-source excitation
abstract: In practical engineering applications, structures often encounter complex and diverse excitation conditions, with multiple sources of excitation acting simultaneously. To effectively suppress vibrations in complex structures, coupled nonlinear energy sinks (CNES) have been proposed. However, current research primarily focuses on vibration control in coupled systems under single-source excitation, which limits the application of the CNES in multi-source excitation systems. To explore the vibration suppression effects of the CNES in complex multi-source excitation environments and its potential applications in vibration control of elastic coupled structures, this study establishes an analytical model of an elastic double-beam system (EDBS) with CNES under dual-source excitation. Based on the generalized Hamilton’s principle, the vibration control equations of the EDBS were derived and subsequently simplified into solvable ordinary differential equations using the Galerkin truncation method (GTM). After verifying the accuracy and reliability of the GTM calculation results, this paper conducts a comprehensive study on the effect of the CNES and its core parameters on the vibration characteristics of the EDBS. Additionally, the vibration suppression effect of the CNES on the EDBS under dual-source excitation is further verified by establishing an experimental platform. The results of the numerical analysis and experiment confirm that the CNES with reasonable parameters can effectively suppress the vibration of the EDBS under dual-source excitation. It is worth noting that under complex multi-source excitation, the CNES exhibits two working modes: vibration reduction mode and failure mode. The study demonstrates that the CNES has great potential as a beneficial control strategy for mitigating vibrations in practical applications similar to the EDBS.

title: A sensor array optimization approach towards non-pseudo-source acoustic emission damage location in orthotropic steel decks
abstract: Existing acoustic emission (AE) source location methods are primarily oriented toward two-dimensional plate-like structures. They confront challenges when applied to complex thin-walled spatial structures, like orthotropic steel decks (OSDs). Multiple wave propagation paths within OSDs precipitate the emergence of pseudo-source problems, leading to significant deviations in damage location results. For adaptive wave propagation shortest distance estimation and more accurate damage location in OSD, a novel sensor array optimization-based non-pseudo-source AE location method is presented. In detail, the OSD structure is represented through a hierarchical topology strategy that includes the fully connected sub-topologies and the integrated global topology. The geodesic distances for wave propagation are obtained by implementing Dijkstra’s algorithm in the global topology. Then, the criterion for valuing non-pseudo-source location capability and the objective function for autonomous optimization of the sensor array configuration are established. A genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to search for the sensor array with absolute non-pseudo-source location capability. Furthermore, a continuous wavelet transform-Akaike information criterion (CWT-AIC) picker is introduced for more accurate arrival time determination. A field experiment was conducted on a large-scale OSD segment in the operating status of the bridge under high operational noise. Results demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed method over the existing methods.

title: Phase CRLB performance of FMCW radar for large displacement estimation
abstract: Displacement measurement using FMCW radar is a topic of great interest. However, position variations during large displacement measurements significantly increases the displacement estimation errors, resulting in performance that falls short of the ideal phase Cramér–Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address it, this study proposes a joint positioning and displacement estimation method that compensates for pre-estimated reference displacements to reduce position variations. By iteratively optimizing these reference displacements until they converge to the target displacements, position variations and associated displacement errors are minimized. The convergence and phase CRLB performance of the proposed method are proved. Among them, phase CRLB performance is superior to any known methods based on radar displacement measurement. In addition, a fast implementation is presented, along with a theoretical analysis of computational complexity. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. In experiments, the achieved RMSE proves the engineering performance of the proposed method.

title: A unified framework for dynamic parameter identification of elastic joint robots with hysteresis and friction nonlinearities
abstract: The accuracy of dynamic parameter identification significantly affects the model-based control performance of elastic joint robots (EJRs). Currently, the modeling and identification of friction and hysteresis nonlinearities in EJRs are mostly treated as separate steps requiring specialized identification equipment. This complicates the identification process and makes parameter re-identification more difficult. Moreover, some parameter identification results could be invalid either because they violate physical constraints or contribute minimally to dynamics. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified dynamic parameter identification framework for EJRs that integrates nonlinear friction and hysteresis models without requiring additional processes or equipment. The framework introduces physical feasibility constraints and iterative reweighted least squares to obtain physically feasible dynamic parameter solutions and deal with heteroscedasticity. It also includes a parameter update strategy that addresses parameters with minimal contribution to dynamics. Verification experiments conducted on a 2-degree-of-freedom EJR validate that the proposed framework is reliable and accurate. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first physically constrained dynamic parameter identification framework for EJRs that integrates nonlinear friction and hysteresis models.

title: Federated learning with prototype learning for RUL prediction of engine turbine blade
abstract: Current life prediction methods of turbine blades have less interpretability analysis. Moreover, multi-stage degradation characteristics are rarely analyzed. Therefore, this paper proposes a new life prediction approach of engine turbine blades based on physical information fusion and federated learning with prototype learning. Sensor monitoring data from airlines and physical degradation data based on digital twin are integrated to get physical information fusion dataset. Then, a new federated learning model with prototype learning and interpretability analysis is studied. Its convergence theorem is proved. A detection algorithm is used to get real-time change points. Furthermore, an improved FedProx algorithm and a new global weight optimization algorithm for federated learning with knowledge distillation are developed. Experimental results demonstrate that: (1) Proposed approach achieves better prediction performance than state-of-the-arts methods. (2) Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) for federated learning provides a multi-dimensional correlated interpretability analysis; stress analysis and hotmap reveal critical correlation results for blade life. (3) Ablation study and sensitivity analysis validate the effectiveness of proposed method.

title: Hypothetical order test enhanced fault diagnosis architecture for rotating machinery under variable speed conditions
abstract: By getting rid of the tachometer dependency, tacholess order tracking (TLOT) is validated effective in rotating machinery fault diagnosis orienting the nonstationary operating condition. However, some issues remain to be further addressed in this method, e.g., the interpolation error and resonance frequency band distortion induced by the angular domain resampling, the heavy computational burden due to the chain-styled demodulation, etc. Aiming at these issues, a hypothetical order test enhanced fault diagnosis architecture for rotating machinery is contrapuntally proposed in this paper. Firstly, vibration response is subjected to low-pass filtering and down-sampling to enhance the computational efficiency. Instantaneous rotating frequency (IRF) of rotating machinery is then extracted by a designed time–frequency searching strategy. Afterwards, the vibration signal is resonance demodulated to obtain the envelope component. Combining the extracted IRF and the fault characteristic orders, target characteristic components (TCCs) can be therefore identified in the time–frequency plane of the obtained envelope signal. Finally, hypothetical surrogate data test is conducted for each TCC. With the hypothetical test results, diagnostic decision can be accordingly established. Experiments by using industrial aero-engine and wind turbine generator datasets indicates that different from the currently available order spectrum based fault diagnosis approach, the proposed method can achieve quantifiable diagnosis result with high computation efficiency. Meanwhile, this method also reduces the dependency on the domain expert knowledge and therefore provides a more adaptive and flexible solution for the rotating machinery fault diagnosis under variable speed conditions.

title: Hierarchical co-estimation of mass and slope for tractor–trailer systems: Pitch dynamics-integrated EKF and novel RLS with tire radius compensation
abstract: In tractor–trailer combinations, accurate estimation of both vehicle mass and road slope is crucial for optimizing performance under varying load conditions. However, existing dynamics-based slope and mass estimation algorithms suffer from limitations in robustness, accuracy, and convergence speed. Moreover, although data-driven methods can enhance estimation accuracy, they rely on large amounts of labeled data and expensive hardware. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel hierarchical estimation framework featuring two key innovations: (i) an adaptive road slope and pitch angle estimation method that robustly handles diverse driving scenarios—including acceleration, deceleration, and gear shifting; and (ii) a vehicle mass estimation approach comprising two distinct components. The first component is a tire radius-adaptive mass estimation algorithm that considers tire radius adaptation in the mass estimation task to effectively mitigate errors under high-load conditions. The second component incorporates an IMU bias-derived initial mass as the starting condition, which significantly enhances the convergence of the mass estimation process. Our approach integrates a dynamic model of the tractor’s pitching motion with an extended Kalman filter for joint estimation of road slope and pitch angle, and employs a longitudinal dynamic model based on the torque balance equation together with a recursive least squares strategy enhanced by damping and forgetting factors for mass estimation. Real-world experiments demonstrate that the proposed vehicle mass estimation approach achieves an average improvement of 84.45% in MAE under high-load conditions, ensuring fast convergence and high estimation accuracy across various load scenarios.

title: Attentive neural networks and meta-learning integration for revolutionary vehicular engine health monitoring
abstract: Modern transportation increasingly relies on vehicle reliability, with unexpected engine failures posing significant safety risks, operational downtime, and increased maintenance costs. Conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)-based vehicular engine health monitoring systems (VEHMS) decision models using the ADAM optimizer with ReLU activation function demonstrate significant generalization gaps, achieving 80.3% accuracy. This study addresses these limitations by employing a hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates Attentive Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU) with MLP and Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) techniques. Systematic evaluation of multiple optimizers and activation functions across TensorFlow/Keras and PyTorch platforms led to the development of an Attentive BiGRU-MLP with Meta-Learning model. The proposed architecture, implemented in PyTorch using a Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimizer and Leaky ReLU activation function, achieves remarkable performance metrics: 92.30% training accuracy and 92.18% testing accuracy, with a minimal generalization gap. Performance analysis reveals an outstanding classification capability, with a ROC score of 0.965, an R2 coefficient of 0.8435, and class-specific metrics for precision (0.9321), recall (0.9155), and F1-score (0.9208). The model effectively categorizes engine conditions as good, minor, moderate, or critical with high diagnostic precision. The model demonstrates superior computational efficiency, with reduced training time (61.70 s), rapid inference (0.0188 s), and 50% lower memory requirements compared to alternative approaches. The attention mechanism enhances feature selection, while Meta-Learning improves adaptation to different operational contexts. The proposed technique represents a substantial advancement for intelligent vehicle monitoring systems, with practical implications for automotive maintenance, cost reduction, and transportation efficiency through improved reliability in fault detection and condition classification.

title: Multi-channel neural blind deconvolution:A physically interpretable network for impulsive mode extraction
abstract: Pulse components widely exist in various signals, including vibration signals, acoustic signals, pressure signals, etc. The extraction of pulse components has received extensive attention in many domains, particularly in machinery fault diagnostics. In this paper, multi-channel blind deconvolution (MCBD) framework is tailored for impulsive mode extraction. MCBD designs multiple adaptive finite impulse response (FIR) filters by maximizing the sum of impulsive metrics for multiple sub-components to extract multiple impulsive modes (IMs) from the test signal. In order to ensure that multiple filters converge to different pulse components instead of the pulse component with the maximum impulsiveness, an orthogonality constraint of the pulse components is introduced into the filter design algorithm to encourage the filters to converge to different pulse components. MCBD focuses on all impulsive modes (including periodic pulses and random pulses), not just periodic impulsive modes, which makes it more comprehensive in capturing abnormal events in the test signal. MCBD is a non-recursive decomposition technique that can detect multiple IM components at once. A neural network-based MCBD algorithm implementation, called multi-channel neural blind deconvolution (MCNBD), is presented. MCNBD can be embedded as a standardized feature extraction module into other neural networks. Each network layer in MCNBD corresponds to a classical signal processing technique, making the neural network physically interpretable. The validity and superiority of MCNBD are verified using simulation signals containing multiple pulse components and bearing signals containing composite faults. Results demonstrate that proposed method can extract all IMs simultaneously in one signal processing progress.

title: A novel guided-mode separation method for array signals with low signal-to-interference ratio
abstract: Elastic guided waves serve as critical tools for characterizing multi-layered structures in near-surface exploration, borehole acoustic logging, as well as structural health monitoring. Their dispersive propagation and multimodal superposition, however, induce severe overlapping in the time–frequency domain that compromises mode separation fidelity. Conventional decomposition methods such as variational mode decomposition and spectral filtering suffer from the limitations of prior knowledge dependence and spectral leakage, respectively. To overcome these constraints, we propose a prior-free and truncation-robust array signal processing algorithm based on enhanced spectral estimation through two key innovations: (1) An iterative strategy optimization algorithm that jointly resolves slowness, amplitude, phase factor, and attenuation parameters without requiring prior mode counts; (2) The application of matched filtering suppresses spectral leakage in guided modes spectral estimation. Rigorous validation through synthetic waveforms in a cased-hole model demonstrates significant improvements over conventional frequency-wavenumber filtering, achieving signal-to-error ratios (SER) exceeding 15 dB for dominant modes and 9 dB for weak modes with signal-to-interference ratios (SIR) below −25 dB. Experimental tests in a dual-string cased-hole model confirm the method’s practicability, successfully extracting signals with SIR below −10 dB. This work advances guided-wave analysis by enabling precise weak-signal extraction in multimodal wavefields, offering a reliable tool for high-resolution subsurface imaging and structural integrity monitoring in multi-layered systems.

title: Fibertouch: A novel fiber-optic tactile sensor with deep learning demodulation for dexterous robotic hands
abstract: Soft tactile sensors play a crucial role in enhancing dexterous manipulation capabilities of robotic hands. Although various tactile sensing systems have been proposed for robotic applications, existing solutions of electromagnetic-based, vision-based, and traditional fiber Bragg gratings (FBG) sensors face electromagnetic interference, occlusion, and signal coupling challenges respectively. This article presents a novel soft tactile force sensor based on seven FBGs, introducing an innovative force sensing mechanism specifically designed for dexterous robotic fingers. The proposed tactile sensor is integrated with a deep learning-based Force Multi-information Estimation Model (FMEM) utilizing Transformer architecture for spectral data demodulation, demonstrating superior performance in simultaneously detecting force magnitude, position, and direction in a single demodulation framework. Experimental results show high accuracy of 98.4% in detecting contact position (5×5mm2 grid resolution) and 99.9% in direction detection (5-degree angular resolution), and tolerable mean absolute errors of 0.688N in force magnitude measurement. These results suggest promising potential in applications to dexterous robotic hands where precise manipulation and grasping capabilities are required.

title: Curvature-driven regionally sampling and machine learning for forming error measurement in composite manufacturing
abstract: Curing induced deformation (CID) often occurs in the forming process of composite materials. In complex geometric components, obtaining forming errors quickly and efficiently still faces challenges. This paper proposes a simple and efficient method for measuring and reconstructing surface errors of composite materials. This method is based on Curvature-driven Region Adaptive Sampling (CRAS), and combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) to achieve the optimal configuration of measurement points. In addition, the BP neural network is utilized for point cloud prediction, and the Lung Performance Optimization (LPO) algorithm is introduced to improve the model accuracy. Result, in the experiment, the proposed method only used 410 measurement points and achieved a reconstruction accuracy comparable to that of the High-precision 3D scanner (HP3D), with an average absolute error of 0.0531 mm and a 96.6 % reduction in computational complexity. This research provides an efficient and low-cost solution for the rapid measurement and error reconstruction of complex curved surface composite material components, with good engineering adaptability.

title: Blade micro-Doppler measurement: A novel non-contact rotor blade vibration measurement method compliant with the Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem
abstract: Accurate non-contact vibration measurement of rotating blades is critical for ensuring structural integrity and operational reliability in aero-engines and gas turbines. This paper introduces a novel Blade Micro-Doppler Measurement (BMM) technique, which fully utilizes the measurement data obtained as the blade approaches, arrives, and departs from the sensor, the sampling frequency of this technique is inversely proportional to the radar chirp period, ensuring full compliance with the Shannon sampling theorem. The study introduces the novel BMM technique from two aspects: micro-Doppler feature modeling and microwave signal processing. First, the rotating-vibrating coupled blade micro-Doppler models are established to describe the modulation effect of blade vibration on the phase of the radar received signal. The model reveals that the observed micro-Doppler features primarily originate from blade surface specular reflection, blade root reflection, blade tip flash, and rotor disk reflection. Additionally, it characterizes the micro-Doppler components under different blade-to-sensor angular positions. Second, a comprehensive rotor blade micro-Doppler feature extraction framework is proposed, incorporating Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Synchrosqueezing Transform (SST), ridge extraction, and sparse decomposition. This framework enables the effective extraction and identification of blade rotational and vibrational parameters from microwave signals. Finally, both simulations and experimental validations are conducted for single-blade and multi-blade rotor systems, under both pure rotation and forced vibration conditions. The results verify the accuracy of the proposed micro-Doppler model and the parameter identification process, demonstrating the feasibility of using the common low transmitted frequency and narrow band microwave radar for high-precision blade vibration measurement, we believe BMM will establish a new paradigm for non-contact blade health monitoring.

title: A novel method for recovering continuous missing data fusing time–space-frequency features of multichannel signals
abstract: Complex service environment and equipment aging induced continuous data loss is the common problem in bridge engineering monitoring activities, which will seriously affect the accuracy of structural state assessment and safety warning. Due to the masking of underlying trends and distribution patterns, the recovery of such missing problem becomes a challenge, especially for data with complex characteristics. To this end, this study proposes a novel method which is the combination of multivariate nonlinear chirp mode decomposition (MNCMD) based signal decomposition, dynamic time warping-Kmedoids clustering algorithm (DTW-KMD) based subseries reconstruction, and physics-aided temporal convolutional network (PATCN) based prediction. This method can resolve multi-scale features in the monitoring data from a systematic time–space-frequency perspective. Specifically, MNCMD is first employed to decompose the multi-channel data into a series of time–frequency consistent subseries where the spatio-temporal coupling relationship among multiple channels is also considered. Subsequently, those decomposed subseries are reconstructed by DTW-KMD based two-stage clustering for reducing the complexity and interference of irrelevant information. Finally, PATCN is designed to recover each subseries by interactively learning the frequency information derived from the physical prior knowledge and time-domain features. Case studies using the measured data from the experimental arch rib and bridge health monitoring system demonstrate the remarkable superiority and practicality of the proposed method. For example, this method can even reduce the root mean square error by more than 60% relative to other methods.

title: Extended theoretical model for water pipeline passive assessment using ambient noise correlation
abstract: Passive assessment technique, which leverages ambient noise within water pipeline systems, has emerged as a promising non-intrusive solution for effective monitoring and condition assessment of aging pipeline networks. However, simplified assumptions in the existing theoretical model of this technique limit the interpretation of measured correlation analysis results, particularly in complex pipeline network scenarios. In this paper, the theoretical model is extended under an analytical framework to account for varying wave speeds and damping coefficients across the pipe system, frequency-dependent reflection and transmission coefficients of pipe faults, and non-uniform spatial noise distributions, all of which are commonly found in real-world pipeline networks but are ignored in the existing model. The explicit expressions of both cross-correlation and auto-correlation functions of ambient noise can be predicted by the extended model, and the results were compared with numerical simulations under controlled scenarios to demonstrate their consistency. Using this extended model, the influence of the specified parameters on the correlation functions is comprehensively investigated.

title: Optimal placement of distributed optic fiber sensors with the modified Constitutive Relation Error
abstract: This paper presents a novel Optimal Sensor Placement strategy tailored to model updating problems based on the modified Constitutive Relation Error (mCRE) functional. It offers a credible alternative to classical functionals by optimizing structural parameters alongside mechanical fields, achieving the best trade-off between available measured data and physical knowledge without any additional a priori assumption. The proposed approach leverages the strong connection between mCRE and Bayesian inference to develop a new Fisher Information Matrix based on mCRE, incorporating the sensitivity of the mCRE mechanical fields to updated parameters. The mCRE-based optimization strategy leads to increased robustness with respect to measurement noise, deviation in the sensor placement, and modeling bias. While many of the developments in this work apply to various sensor types, additional constraints are included to focus on distributed optic fiber sensors (DOFS). The shape of the fiber is represented using B-Splines, making the control point coordinates the design variables. Constraints on maximum fiber length and minimum curvature radius are treated as penalty terms in the fitness function, optimized using a genetic algorithm. The proposed methodology is validated on isotropic and orthotropic elasticity using 2D and 3D geometries.

title: An upsampling framework for vehicle low-frequency sampling data based on human-machine-environment fusion
abstract: Vehicle reliability fundamentally governs transportation efficiency, energy utilization optimization, and public safety, where signal fidelity determines diagnostic accuracy in health management systems. Conventional vehicle-mounted recorders predominantly employ low-frequency sampling due to cost and power constraints, inevitably causing transient fault feature loss through aliasing and dynamic interference. This paper introduced a human-vehicle-environment fused framework for physics-consistent signal upsampling. The approach systematically combines a power flow-driven stacked autoencoder for hierarchical feature extraction, with tensor product-based fusion of driver behavior, road resistance, and vehicle state parameters as physical constraints. By establishing adversarial learning conditioned on the fusion feature coupled with progressive optimization of time–frequency reconstruction objectives, the framework effectively addresses spectral distortion in conventional methods. Experimental validation on heavy-duty hybrid vehicle data demonstrates statistically significant spectral recovery capabilities, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.766 and 0.783 with original high-frequency reference signal in fault progression scenarios, supported by Wilcoxon rank-sum test p-values of 0.209 and 0.217. The framework outperforms cubic spline interpolation, standard GAN, and advanced benchmarks (e.g., TCN and UR-CNN) in preserving transient signatures critical for incipient fault diagnosis, with RMSE reductions of up to 65.83% against interpolation and 29.33% against GAN variants. By reconstructing physically consistent high frequency signals from low frequency data, this methodology bridges the gap between constrained onboard recordings and diagnostic requirements.

title: Reinforcement learning-based fusion framework for vehicle sideslip angle estimators using physically guided neural networks
abstract: Accurate and robust estimation of the vehicle sideslip angle is crucial for maintaining safety under extreme and variable driving conditions. In this paper, we first propose a reinforcement learning-based framework for estimator fusion in vehicle sideslip angle estimation, where the estimator is constructed using physically guided neural networks incorporating gated recurrent unit (GRU) and self-attention mechanisms. First, the physical knowledge of vehicle kinematics and dynamics is analyzed to design the input configuration of the dynamically and kinematically guided neural network estimators. Second, a GRU-based neural network with self-attention is developed to capture both instantaneous and long-range dependencies in time-series signals, serving as the employed neural network estimator. Third, a reinforcement learning-based estimator fusion framework is proposed to integrate the dynamically and kinematically guided neural network estimators. The estimator fusion is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) and implemented using soft actor–critic with auto-entropy, extending reinforcement learning to estimation scenarios where actions do not affect state transitions. Finally, the accuracy and robustness of sideslip angle estimation, as well as the generalizability and adaptability of the reinforcement learning-based estimator fusion framework, are validated through diverse real vehicle experiments using both self-collected and public datasets under normal and extreme maneuvers.

title: Deep learning-based Generative Fixed-Filter Active Noise Control: Transferability and implementation
abstract: The deep learning-based Generative Fixed-Filter Active Noise Control (GFANC) method can generate suitable control filters for different noise types, achieving faster response and better noise reduction than conventional approaches. However, its transferability and practical performance have not yet been fully validated. In this paper, the deep learning-based GFANC method is implemented in an Active Noise Control (ANC) headphone using a dual-rate architecture: a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) on a co-processor works alongside the real-time controller to ensure delayless noise control. A theoretical explanation of GFANC’s transferability is also provided, demonstrating that the method can be adapted to different acoustic environments by using system-specific sub control filters while retaining the same trained CNN. Finally, both simulations and real-time experiments confirm that GFANC outperforms the Selective Fixed-Filter ANC (SFANC) method, the Filtered-x Least Mean Square (FxLMS) algorithm, and a commercial ANC algorithm.11The code will be available at https://github.com/Luo-Zhengding/GFANC-Headphone.

title: Adaptive directional extraction transform for analyzing mixtures of harmonic-like and impulsive-like signals
abstract: Many real-world signals are composed of both harmonic-like and impulsive-like components. Accurately characterizing such mixed signals poses a challenge for the conventional time–frequency (TF) analysis methods due to the limitations of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle and current post-processing techniques. In this paper, a novel TF analysis approach called the adaptive directional extracting transform (ADET), is developed. We begin with a theoretical analysis to define an instantaneous frequency (IF) equation for a time-varying model and a group delay (GD) equation for a frequency-varying model within the short-time Fourier transform framework. We then propose to adaptively extract the fixed points of the solutions of these two equations, guided by a novel discrimination criterion. This criterion uses the TF information at the solutions to determine which fixed points to select. Numerical simulations and real-life applications demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves high concentration in both time and frequency while maintaining strong resistance to noise in addressing noisy mixed signals.

title: Damage characterization of CFRP composites under compression using acoustic emission time–frequency analysis and unsupervised deep learning
abstract: In this work, the acoustic emission (AE) technique is combined with an unsupervised deep learning approach to investigate damage progression in multi-angular CFRP specimens under compressive loading. Unlike traditional clustering approaches based on AE signal parameters, this work utilizes time–frequency representations (TFRs) for direct analysis. Various TFR methods, including short-time Fourier transform (STFT), continuous wavelet transform (CWT), Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD), and smoothed pseudo-Wigner-Ville distribution (SPWVD) are compared using Normalized Rényi entropy (NRE) as a metric. Furthermore, the impact of different TFRs on the performance of the deep learning model is examined, demonstrating how the characteristics of the input data influence the effectiveness of the model. Based on these observations, SPWVD is used to transform AE waveforms into time-frequency representations, which serve as input for an unsupervised deep learning approach called Deep Convolutional Embedded Clustering (DCEC). Unlike supervised models that require extensive labeled datasets, DCEC autonomously extracts deep features from TFR images and clusters AE waveforms. By integrating feature extraction and clustering, DCEC generates well-separated clusters, enhancing efficiency, and eliminating sequential processing. Clustering AE signals based on damage modes enables a detailed analysis of damage progression and failure mechanisms under compressive loads. These findings offer confidence in the applicability of the data-driven approach to real-time structural health monitoring using AE techniques.

title: Marine cranes enable ship-to-ship payload transfer: Rapid swing control under input saturation and uncertainty constraints
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive fuzzy finite-time tracking control (AFFTC) based on a command filter for marine cranes is proposed to facilitate ship-to-ship payload transfer and swing suppression in open-sea environments. Specifically, an adaptive fuzzy logic structure is employed to approximate the system uncertainties, and a finite-time command filter backstepping controller is integrated with it. Finally, an auxiliary dynamic system is utilized to address the input saturation issue. This approach is implemented through the integration of a novel fused coordinate system in the marine ship-to-ship crane system. Meanwhile, it is rigorously proven via the Lyapunov method that the designed control method can converge to zero in finite-time, rather than a small neighborhood. Through comparisons with existing control methods, the experimental results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the designed controller.

title: Unexcited identification for all dynamic parameters of non-cooperative target in orbit using SDW
abstract: To address the challenge of identifying all dynamic parameters—including mass, centroid position, principal moments of inertia, and inertia products—of a non-cooperative target in orbit, this study proposes an unexcited identification method based on state perception using a Soft Docking Wrist (SDW). Once the target is captured and mechanically constrained by the SDW, a compound spacecraft is formed, comprising the chaser, the manipulator with the SDW, and the target. During the post-capture buffering phase, the SDW remains in a non-excited state, allowing for passive observation of system dynamics. The kinematics of the chaser-SDW assembly are first analyzed, followed by the formulation of compound momentum equations that embed the unknown target parameters. From these, the Absolute Momentum Increment Equations (AMIEs) are derived. By incrementally increasing the equation dimension and analyzing matrix condition numbers, the approach ensures singularity avoidance and defines a robust termination criterion. Using measurements of generalized coordinates and velocities from the chaser, the complete set of target dynamic parameters can be identified without requiring external excitation. Numerical simulations demonstrate the proposed method’s advantages in terms of computational efficiency, reduced identification time, high accuracy, and negligible disturbance to the chaser. The method’s feasibility is further validated through semi-physical experiments.

title: Bearing degradation indicator using cage speed: Extension of BeaFEM to nonstationary operating conditions
abstract: The well-known bearing characteristic frequencies (BPFO, BPFI, FTF and BSF) reflect the complex kinematics of operating bearings. Far from the idealised perfect rolling assumptions, the experimental frequencies deviate from their theoretical values. The deterioration of the bearing health is likely to induce changes in the cage rotating speed, materialised by a shift of the angle characteristic frequencies. Monitoring the cage speed using these frequencies can provide a valuable degradation indicator. However, nonstationary operating conditions are also known to influence the bearing motion. This work is a continuation of BeaFEM introduced by Bertoni and André (2023), and assess its potential for monitoring bearings operating under nonstationary conditions. To this end, BeaFEM is reformulated with an original interpretation using cage speed and a short-term adaptation is proposed. The possible causes of cage slip are reminded, and the influence of load is studied on two wind turbine bearings. Based on this knowledge, the influence of operating conditions is mitigated and a strategy to use the cage speed as a valuable degradation indicator is proposed.

title: DeFIANT: A degradation-aware large model paradigm for generalizable RUL prediction
abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings over long horizons in cross-domain settings remains a central challenge in predictive maintenance, owing to the compounded difficulties posed by complex degradation dynamics and distributional shifts across diverse operating environments. Conventional deep learning methods often prove inadequate in this context, as they are hindered by insufficient signal representation, limited model capacity, and fragile adaptation mechanisms. The recent emergence of large Foundation Models (FMs) offers unprecedented opportunities to address these challenges; however, directly applying language-pretrained FMs to noisy, high-frequency vibration signals remains non-trivial due to fundamental modality mismatches and severe domain shifts. In this work, we therefore propose a hierarchical FM adaptation framework comprising three complementary modules that systematically converts FMs into degradation-aware predictors. Central to our approach is an adaptive signal-representation module that transforms raw vibration signals into structured degradation tokens, enabling the FM to parse bearing degradation as a learnable “language” and thereby bridge the critical modality gap. Building on this representation, we retrofit the frozen FM backbone with a reversible instance-normalization front-end and a triple-scale embedding head. This architectural adaptation suppresses cross-domain covariate shifts before the model and fuses multi-scale degradation information after it, effectively converting the FM into a degradation-aware long-horizon forecaster. Crucially, our framework is guided by a unified domain generalization theory, we derived a generalization error bound for FM-based cross-domain adaptation and evidence that frozen self-attention acts as a PCA-like compressor—we introduce a progressive, integrity-preserving fine-tuning strategy. This strategy selectively activates and calibrates the pretrained FM’s generalization capacity while preserving the core integrity of its attention mechanism, thereby boosting cross-domain prediction accuracy without incurring additional parameter burden. Extensive experiments on benchmark bearing datasets confirm that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods by up to 33.5% in cross-domain long-horizon RUL prediction.

title: A subspace parallel monitoring triggered damage assessment based on guided wave and ultrasonic vibration for composite stiffened panels
abstract: Composite stiffened panels with high strength-to-weight ratio are widely applied in advanced engineering structures but are prone to damage or defects. The structural complexity limits the development of structural health monitoring (SHM) and non-destructive testing (NDT) methods for these structures. This paper proposes a novel baseline-free damage detection method combining guided waves and ultrasonic vibrations. Numerical simulation and experimental results prove that the proposed method serves as an SHM-informed NDT method triggered by subspace inspection, and can be applied to both debonding and delamination detection in composite stiffened panels without baseline. In addition, compared with traditional NDT methods, the proposed method has higher sensitivity to damage and promotes imaging quality to evaluate the damage location and size. Consequently, the proposed method provides a novel two-step NDT approach to thoroughly interrogate complex structures with high resolution and efficiency.

title: A finite element model-based two-level method incorporating recommendation algorithm for structural damage detection
abstract: Accurate and efficient assessment of structural damage is crucial for the safety and longevity of civil engineering structures. This paper presents a finite element model-based, two-level approach that combines pattern matching and model updating for hierarchical damage detection. The recommendation algorithm is utilized to enhance the pattern matching process. In the first level, elements are classified into several groups, and potentially damaged groups are identified using pattern matching principles and automatic clustering methods, reducing the dimensionality of subsequent problem. In the second level, the extent of the damage of the elements within these groups is assessed based on model updating principles, with iteration direction and step length determined by pattern matching, while a one-at-a-time updating strategy addresses the ill-posed challenges in model updating. Throughout both levels, the recommendation algorithm, functioning as a relaxed pattern matching method, guides the localization of damaged regions and the adjustment of damage parameters of elements based on maximum similarity, effectively reducing the computational costs and inefficiencies of traditional pattern matching operations. Validation through numerical simulations on the ASCE Benchmark model and laboratory experiments on a 6-meter span truss bridge model demonstrates that the method accurately identifies damaged regions and quantifies the extent of the damage with high precision using limited natural frequencies and mode shapes, enhancing efficiency and accuracy compared to conventional approaches.

title: Physics-guided neural network for infrared temperature reconstruction in friction stir welding
abstract: Accurate temperature monitoring is essential for ensuring weld quality and optimizing process control during welding. Infrared thermography has gained widespread attention due to its nondestructive nature and high temporal resolution. However, infrared temperature measurements are highly susceptible to interference from spindle radiation and welding fumes, resulting in significant degradation of thermal image fidelity. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents a multidomain feature fusion and physics-data dual-driven neural network model (MDF-PDNN) for robust infrared temperature correction in welding environments. First, the coupling interference between the spindle radiation and welding fumes is thoroughly analyzed, emphasizing its spatial and temporal effects on the thermal signals. Subsequently, multidimensional features from infrared thermal images are extracted and fused with process parameters, thermocouple measurements, and time sequences into a unified feature space, which serves as input to the proposed model. Furthermore, a physics-guided residual loss derived from a modified heat conduction equation incorporating core temperature compensation is introduced to enforce physical consistency. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed MDF-PDNN model effectively mitigates multisource interference and significantly increases temperature prediction accuracy. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, the proposed approach achieves superior accuracy, yielding at least a 7.26 % performance improvement at the 95 % confidence level, while consistently maintaining a temperature error below 9.32 % throughout the entire welding cycle. These results confirm the potential of MDF-PDNN as a reliable solution for infrared temperature measurement under complex industrial welding conditions.

title: Leak detection in pipelines based on a multilayer network of time–frequency domain cross-visibility graphs and graph convolutional networks
abstract: Pipeline leak detection is essential for maintaining operational integrity, reducing environmental risks, and minimizing financial losses. As artificial intelligence rapidly advances and demonstrates significant benefits in data analytics, the application of deep learning technology for identifying gas pipeline leaks has attracted growing research interest in recent years. As such, this study proposes a pipeline leak diagnosis technique based on a new feature extraction technique called as multilayer-network-of-time–frequency domain-based-cross visibility graph (MNet-TFCVG) in combination with graph convolutional networks (GCNs). The MNet-TFCVG first uses variational mode decomposition (VMD) method to decompose the localized segments of an acoustic emission (AE) signal acquired from pipeline into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). The time–frequency information contained in IMFs are then retained by computing the energy features from the corresponding IMF sections and forming multiple layers of energy sequences. Afterwards, the resulting energy layers are converted into a network of graphs based on an innovative concept called as cross-visibility, which measures horizontal visibility between any two distinct energy layers. Cross horizontal visibility in turn is evaluated by determining whether a data point from one time series can be connected to a data point from another time series through a horizontal line without intersecting any intermediate data points. Finally, these graph patterns are analyzed through a GCN to effectively detect and classify leaks. The proposed technique is experimentally evaluated under two pressure scenarios and four leak sizes and the results confirm that high classification accuracies of 98.6 % and 94.4 % are achieved. In addition, the proposed MNet-TFCVG + GCN outperforms the existing techniques, namely, continuous wavelet transform (CWT) + convolutional neural network (CNN), Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT) + CNN, and traditional horizontal visibility graph (HVG) + GCN in terms of classification accuracy and computational time.

title: Cyclostationarity of the noise radiated by a rotating acoustic source in a duct: Proof of concept
abstract: The fan of an aero-engine, as a classical rotating structure, is located in the culvert (duct) and is a significant source of noise. Cyclostationary theory is widely applied in signal processing for rotating machinery. Therefore, the main objective of this paper is to demonstrate that the noise radiated by a rotating source in a duct is cyclostationary. Firstly, the Wold–Cramer decomposition form of the propagation equation for a rotating point source in a duct is derived. This decomposition is then used to demonstrate the cyclostationarity of the sound field radiated by a rotating point source in a duct is explained. Next, the theory is extended to a rotating blade source. Then, the cyclic spectral characteristics of several rotating sound sources in a duct are derived. It is worth mentioning that the broadband noise radiated by a fan inside a duct is still cyclostationary. Finally, the correctness of the proposed theory is verified by using rotating monopoles inside a duct, and the SJTU 1.5-stage compressor.

title: Synchrosqueezed X-ray wavelet–chirplet transform for accurate chirp rate estimation and retrieval of modes from multicomponent signals with crossover instantaneous frequencies
abstract: Recent advances in the chirplet transform and wavelet–chirplet transform (WCT) have enabled the estimation of instantaneous frequencies (IFs) and chirprates, as well as mode retrieval from multicomponent signals with crossover IF curves. However, chirprate estimation via these approaches remains less accurate than IF estimation, primarily due to the slow decay of the chirplet transform or WCT along the chirprate direction. To address this, the synchrosqueezed chirplet transform (SCT) and multiple SCT methods were proposed, achieving moderate improvements in IF and chirprate estimation accuracy. Nevertheless, a novel approach is still needed to enhance the transform’s decay along the chirprate direction. This paper introduces an X-ray transform-based wavelet–chirprate transform, termed the X-ray wavelet–chirplet transform (XWCT), which exhibits superior decay along the chirprate direction compared to the WCT. Furthermore, third-order synchrosqueezed variants of the WCT and XWCT are developed to yield sharp time–frequency–chirprate representations of signals. Experimental results demonstrate that the XWCT achieves significantly faster decay along the chirprate axis, while the third-order synchrosqueezed XWCT enables accurate IF and chirprate estimation, as well as mode retrieval, without requiring multiple synchrosqueezing operations.

title: Novel capacitive measuring method to determine the complex impedance behavior of machine elements
abstract: This study presents a novel method for in situ monitoring of the condition of elastohydrodynamically (EHL) lubricated contacts, as occurring in rolling bearings and gears, using a capacitance-based evaluation of the electrical charging behavior. A nonlinear regression model is applied to segmented portions of the voltage response curve following a defined voltage pulse. This enables accurate extraction of the contact capacitance and parallel resistance, which reflect the thickness and electrical integrity of the EHL film. The method is validated against LCR meter readings on reference circuits, showing deviations below 5%. It is then applied to deep-groove ball bearings (6008 HSMB) under oil-air lubrication, varying temperatures (60°C and 100°C), and rotational speeds up to 30 000 1/min. Over 500 measurements per speed step confirm the method’s robustness and sensitivity to changes in lubrication regime, including detection of starvation effects. The extracted electrical parameters serve both for condition monitoring and for populating equivalent circuit models in the context of inverter-fed electric drive systems.
