The method thus contributes to improved understanding and monitoring of bearing durability, tribological film behavior, and electrical system integration. • Non-invasive evaluation of lubrication state via capacitive charging response. • Accurate extraction of capacitance and parallel resistance from time-domain signals. • Applicable to system monitoring, electrical modeling, and film thickness estimation. • Robust against noise and signal distortions through nonlinear segment fitting. • Enables identification of starvation and mixed lubrication in rolling bearings.

title: Deep learning-aided guided wavefield imaging of delaminations in composite laminates
abstract: Delaminations in composite laminates pose a critical challenge for civil aircraft structural health monitoring (SHM) due to their hidden progression and severe mechanical degradation effects. This study develops a novel deep learning framework FRCNet for automatic delamination imaging through wavefield analysis. The FRCNet adopts a configuration similar to fully convolutional network, while innovatively integrating a modified ResNet34. The modified ResNet34 is enhanced with two key innovations: (1) integration of a convolutional block attention module for adaptive feature refinement, and (2) strategic implementation of dilated convolutions to expand the receptive field while preserving spatial resolution. The FRCNet is trained and tested on a numerically generated wavefield dataset and its prediction results are compared against state-of-the-art deep learning models. The FRCNet demonstrates robust performance in both numerical simulations and experimental validations involving single-delamination scenarios, with successful extension to multi-delamination configurations. Comparative evaluations against state-of-the-art deep learning models reveal FRCNet’s superior accuracy in delamination imaging. The framework eliminates reliance on manual interpretation, offering a new paradigm for real-time intelligent SHM in aerospace composites.

title: Interfacial resistance-based multifunctional health monitoring on ultrasonic welding of carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites
abstract: Ultrasonic welding is a pivotal technique for joining carbon fiber reinforced thermoplastic polymers (CFRTP), with broad applications across various industries. Despite its importance, current methods for predicting the quality of ultrasonic welding joints are complex, and there is a pressing need for accurate, non-destructive, and cost-effective methods to detect damage during service. This study introduces an innovative, multifunctional health monitoring approach for CFRTP ultrasonic welded joints that leverages the conductivity of carbon fibers at the welding interface. By establishing a correlation between welding strength and post-weld interface resistance, we achieved a non-destructive method for predicting joint quality. The simultaneous monitoring of welding power and interface resistance during the process enabled a detailed analysis of the ultrasonic welding dynamics and melt conditions, allowing for real-time interface monitoring. Furthermore, during lap-shear tests, the method employed resistance monitoring to compare stress–strain curves with resistance variation curves, revealing insights into various damage stages and their associated resistance changes, thus enabling damage sensing during service. The proposed method not only holds promise for quality prediction and damage monitoring of complex connection structures but also has the potential to be integrated with neural network deep learning for real-time optimization of welding processes. This advancement is instrumental in promoting and expanding the application of CFRTP in industrial settings.

title: Upstream-monitoring-driven early warning for downstream bridge overloading: a mechanical-data-physical model coupling methodology
abstract: Studying bridge overloading warnings is crucial for structural integrity and safeguarding lives and property. However, current methods often fail to provide early alerts for overloaded vehicles. This paper introduces an innovative methodology for early bridge overloading warning utilizing a combination of mechanical, data and physical models. In this study, a bridge located upstream of a road (P-bridge) is used to implement overload warnings for a downstream bridge (T-bridge), with only the P-bridge equipped with a long-term load monitoring system. An established mechanical model is firstly employed to analyze strain data from the P-bridge, determining the distribution of vehicle loads on the T-bridge. After collecting enough load data, a GWO-GRU neural network is then utilized to create a spatial mapping model that can predict the load distribution on the T-bridge based on data from the P-bridge. Finally, the predicted vehicle loading modes are applied to a calibrated finite element model to detect any abnormal responses and issue early warnings. By analyzing two multi-girder bridges with varying spans and considering different traffic flows and noise levels, this study demonstrates that the proposed methodology can accurately predict vehicle load distribution and offers multi-tier early warning capabilities.

title: Model-based fault diagnosis and monitoring of induction machine bearing fault
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for the diagnosis of bearing faults in the presence of coexisting electrical anomalies. A simplified dq-model is developed to simulate localized spalling on the outer race, with torque disturbances explicitly incorporated to represent the mechanical defect. Unlike finite element and magnetic models, which are often too computationally intensive for real-time industrial use, the proposed approach captures bearing fault transmission to the stator current with reduced computational cost. This trade-off between accuracy and efficiency allows the model to be extended to multifault scenarios, including broken rotor bars and inter-turn short circuits. The system equations are numerically integrated using the fourth-order Runge–Kutta method to ensure both stability and computational precision. To address fault detection under multifault conditions, a diagnostic strategy based on stator current analysis is introduced. The method combines frequency-domain analysis, used to identify characteristic fault frequencies, with time-domain processing based on newly proposed features specifically designed for bearing fault identification. These features, not previously reported in the literature, provide a robust basis for the development of data-driven classification algorithms capable of distinguishing concurrent faults. Experimental validation is performed on a dynamic test bench equipped with an induction motor. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the approach for real-time condition monitoring, although further validation is required to fully assess its robustness and generalization across industrial operating conditions.

title: Mechanism of a novel parallel ultrasonic vibration-assisted cutting system for high performance machining
abstract: Titanium alloy slender shafts have wide application on the aerospace, automotive and medical devices. However, they are prone to bending deformation during cutting process due to their low rigidity, resulting in poor machining accuracy and efficiency. A novel parallel ultrasonic vibration-assisted cutting (PUVC) system is proposed using two tools to simultaneously cut the workpiece and applying tangential ultrasonic vibration contributing to overcome above challenges. The main concept, motion trajectory and separation characteristics of PUVC system are analyzed. An analytical model for PUVC that integrating cutting intersection mode, chip geometry model, cutting force model and workpiece deflection feedback model is established. On this basis, the influencing mechanism of cutting force, diameter error and temperature of PUVC is explored under different cutting modes, ultrasonic parameters, tool parameters and cutting parameters. Furthermore, an experimental validation is performed to verify the proposed model’s accuracy and methodological efficacy, thereby establishing a reliable foundation for implementing this approach in high-precision manufacturing industries applications.

title: Physics-informed AI and ML-based sparse system identification algorithm for discovery of PDE’s representing nonlinear dynamic systems
abstract: Sparse system identification of nonlinear dynamic systems is still challenging, especially for stiff and high-order differential equations for noisy measurement data. The use of highly correlated functions makes distinguishing between true and false functions difficult, which limits the choice of functions. In this study, an equation discovery method has been proposed to tackle these problems. The key elements include a) use of B-splines for data fitting to get analytical derivatives superior to numerical derivatives, b) sequentially regularized derivatives for denoising (SRDD) algorithm, highly effective in removing noise from signal without system information loss, c) uncorrelated component analysis (UCA) algorithm that identifies and eliminates highly correlated functions while retaining the true functions, and d) physics-informed spline fitting (PISF) where the spline fitting is updated gradually while satisfying the governing equation with a dictionary of candidate functions to converge to the correct equation sequentially. The complete framework is built on a unified deep-learning architecture that eases the optimization process. The proposed method is demonstrated to discover various differential equations at various noise levels, including three-dimensional, fourth-order, and stiff equations. The parameter estimation converges accurately to the true values with a small coefficient of variation, suggesting robustness to the noise.

title: A time-frequency dual-domain deep learning approach for high-speed pantograph-catenary dynamic performance prediction
abstract: The pantograph-catenary system’s dynamic train-grid coupling critically determines traction current transmission quality in electrified railway development. With high-speed railway operational targets reaching 400 km/h, experimental constraints necessitate complete reliance on computationally intensive numerical simulations for dynamic performance evaluation while existing intelligent contact force prediction methods fail to capture high-frequency interaction components required for 400 km/h operations. To address this challenge, this study proposes a deep neural network-based prediction method that efficiently and accurately maps system design parameters to composite dynamic performance metrics. The prediction model’s core architecture integrates LSTM networks with Transformer modules, effectively balancing global and local feature extraction from training data. A frequency-domain prediction branch combined with time–frequency fusion mechanisms establishes a dual-domain supervised training framework, enabling precise prediction of both high-frequency and low-frequency dynamic characteristics. Results demonstrate strong agreement between predicted dynamic performance metrics and numerical simulation outcomes, while achieving three orders of magnitude reduction in computational costs. Comparative evaluations with conventional neural networks confirm the model’s superior performance across frequency domains. Furthermore, parameter sensitivity analysis through the prediction model reveals significant potential for explainable pantograph-catenary system optimization across different speed levels.

title: Simulation of parameterized random fields, Part I: Gaussian cases
abstract: Parameterized random fields play an important role to simulate complex uncertain physical models. In this kind of random fields, statistical properties of the classical random fields, e.g. marginal distributions and covariance functions, may be also related to (random) parameters. In-depth analysis and efficient simulations of parameterized random fields still require further research. This paper presents efficient numerical simulations of parameterized Gaussian random fields (PGRFs). To this end, a stochastic Karhunen–Loève expansion (SKLE) is first proposed to approximate PGRFs and used to provide an explicit representation of PGRFs. The stochastic integral equation arising in SKLE is solved efficiently by a reduced-order method. In this method, stochastic eigenvectors are represented as stochastic linear combinations of deterministic vectors. The deterministic vectors are calculated efficiently using deterministic eigenequations. Corresponding random variable coefficients of deterministic vectors and stochastic eigenvalues are solved via a reduced-order stochastic eigenequation built by the deterministic vectors. With the obtained stochastic eigenvectors, the SKLE of PGRFs can be reformulated as classical Karhunen–Loève-like expansions and PGRFs are revisited from different parameterized perspectives. Three numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Identification and monitoring of stochastic linear subsystems with unknown local nonlinearities via output injection
abstract: Most civil and mechanical structures exhibit nonlinear stochastic behaviour, which is difficult to model accurately, but necessary for conventional model-based structural health monitoring techniques. Although various methods have been developed to estimate nonlinear systems, they require information about the external excitation and are susceptible to sensor noise and modelling inaccuracies. This knowledge is challenging to acquire in practice. Hence, this article presents a novel nonlinearity model-agnostic approach to detect damage in mechanical systems with localized nonlinearities. The proposed method utilises output injection to reject the unknown nonlinearities as if they were unknown disturbances. By applying an existing disturbance rejection technique, the need for a priori knowledge about the functional form of nonlinearities is avoided. Besides, a switching strategy is employed to determine the most probable location of the nonlinearities, thereby eliminating the need for a priori knowledge about their location. The method makes use of interacting particle Kalman filter, where the particle filter estimates the parameters (health indices) in order to detect possible damage while the Kalman filter simultaneously estimates the states. The efficiency of the proposed method is demonstrated with the help of numerical experiments on a spring-mass-damper oscillator chain with attached localized nonlinearity. The proposed approach is further validated against experimental data of jointed beams.

title: Dynamic model and boundary control for mechanical systems with inequality constraints: A generalized Udwadia–Kalaba approach
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for integrating equality constraints and inequality constraints is proposed for dynamic modeling of mechanical systems. The equality constraints are used to delineate the ideal trajectory of the actuator, while inequality constraints are applied to artificially set the error boundaries of the system states with uncertainty. Then, a robust control including two portions is designed based on the generalized Udwadia–Kalaba equation. The first portion implements constraint-following control by ensuring that the nominal system adheres to the desired trajectory according to the control force based on the equality constraints. The second portion utilizes the state transformation method, which enables the fluctuations of the system state error to be strictly limited to the inequality constraints. Based on the Lyapunov approach, the uncertainties can be compensated when both equality and inequality constraints are present. The uniform boundedness and uniform ultimate boundedness of the mechanical system can be guaranteed. At last, the feasibility of the model and control method based on the generalized Udwadia–Kalaba equation is proved by applying a robotic arm system. The verification are performed compared with other methods.

title: Linear cutting force model to predict battery runtime of jigsaws
abstract: This paper introduces a new linear cutting force model that targets explicitly battery-powered jigsaws, as existing models primarily focus on industrial-scale or CNC-controlled systems. The proposed method uses a basic yet realistic approach to model dynamic force behavior under reciprocating motion instead of previous nonlinear or empirical methods. The model combines the jigsaw’s Scotch yoke mechanism with its electrical drive system through MATLAB Simscape to create a coupled electromechanical simulation framework. The model achieves precise experimental runtime data matching through simulated annealing parameter optimization, resulting in only a 3.7% error in runtime prediction. The approach maintains low computational complexity, making it suitable for real-time energy-aware control in handheld tools. The innovation enables longer operation times while minimizing energy consumption and promoting sustainability in mobile construction and maintenance applications.

title: Continual anomaly detection with Cross-Condition feature contrast for nonstationary industrial data stream
abstract: Deep anomaly detection (AD) models have shown powerful capacity in exploring abnormal patterns of industrial equipment. However, traditional static learning paradigms confine their application scenarios to independent and identically distributed data, unable to handle nonstationary data streams under changing working conditions. Continual learning (CL) provides a solution for dynamic environments, but faces challenges in integrating with AD tasks due to tough unsupervised knowledge extraction and inter-condition knowledge transfer. To address this, a continual anomaly detection method via cross-condition feature contrast is proposed for nonstationary industrial data stream. Specifically, a self-supervised anomaly detector is constructed as the continual learner, capturing normal feature distributions under specific conditions and regarding them as condition-specific knowledge. Then, the learner is continuously updated by conducting cross-condition contrast between new features from current conditions, old features from the past conditions and their hybrid features, enhancing adaptability on new distribution while mitigating catastrophic forgetting of historical knowledge. Furthermore, a representativeness-aware rehearsal strategy is proposed to consolidate the learned knowledge. Finally, online AD is performed based on distance metrics with current features. Compared with offline and other online AD approaches, the superiority of the proposed method is verified on continual AD experiments in both detection performance and efficiency.

title: A statistical time series model-based method for robust detection of incipient faults in rotating machinery under different operating conditions
abstract: A statistical time series method for robust detection of incipient faults in rotating machinery under different operating conditions (OCs) is postulated. The method is of the unsupervised type in the sense that there is no need for measurements from the faulty machinery or any information about the fault characteristics for its training. Instead, it is trained using vibration signals from a single accelerometer acquired from a sample of the considered OCs with the healthy machinery. Based on these, the modeling of the healthy machinery dynamics within the continuous OCs (speed, load) range of interest is achieved for the first time through a single stochastic, data-driven, model. This may account for the pseudo-static effects on the dynamics of the considered OCs using data pooling from all OCs and a proper least squares estimator. To assess machinery health, the consistency of a vibration signal from machinery in an unknown health state with the data-driven model is examined using a simple hypothesis testing procedure, with an optimization framework applied if the operating condition is not measurable. The method’s fault detection performance is investigated through hundreds of experiments with two different rotating machinery setups, one under different operating speeds and another under different load conditions. Early-stage faults of different common types are implemented, leaving no imprints on the time domain signals, while their effects in the frequency domain are confounded with those caused by the different OCs, resulting thus in a highly challenging detection problem. Additionally, comparisons with three recently introduced methods for robust fault detection under different OCs are performed through both setups. The fault detection results, presented via plots of the methods’ metrics and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves, indicate the superiority of the postulated method that achieves excellent performance in both setups and across all considered fault scenarios.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of rolling-element bearings based on cumulative transformation and EResNet-KSLSTM network
abstract: As one of the key components of rotating machinery, the health status of rolling-element bearings directly determines whether the equipment can function properly. Due to the harsh working environment and the weak early degradation trends of rolling-element bearings, the extraction of degradation features and the accuracy of prediction are significantly challenged. To address this issue, a cumulative feature model is proposed—based on the degradation characteristics of bearings—that is more sensitive to degradation trends. The focus and feature-mining capabilities of residual networks and long short-term memory networks are specifically enhanced to achieve high-precision remaining useful life (RUL) prediction in a small-sample training environment. First, a feature enhancement method based on cumulative transformation is introduced, wherein the extracted features are converted into their corresponding cumulative forms to increase sensitivity to bearing degradation. Second, a new health indicator (HI) is constructed based on cumulative features, and a continuous triggering mechanism is applied to classify the HI states, allowing for the identification of the initial fault point. Finally, the skip connection module of the ResNet network is enhanced, and additional calibration channels are added to improve the network’s ability to focus on key degradation features. A stacked LSTM network with a KAN module is employed to capture full spatiotemporal features for precise RUL prediction. By constructing cumulative transformation features and optimizing the network structure, the prediction accuracy of bearing RUL in a small-sample training environment is improved. Both simulation and laboratory experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Sparsity-assisted energy decoupling model for fault detection of planetary ring gear in wind turbines
abstract: Fault detection for wind turbine gearboxes is the pivot to ensure the sustainable and stable development of wind power. The planetary ring gear is the core component in this type of equipment. However, the challenge of ring gear fault detection is the coupling of pass-through effect and failure impulses with the same period in the time and frequency domains. Traditional diagnostic methods lack the directional constraints, which leads to the incomplete decoupling. Therefore, a sparsity-assisted energy decoupling model is proposed to identify the different states of the planetary ring gear in wind turbines. Firstly, a sparse representation with a weight-modified generalized minimax concave penalty function is deduced to reduce the influence of background noise. Then, a hyperplane, defined by Gaussian distribution with an elastic parameter, is proposed to decouple the pass-through effect and failure impulses, which consists of the global–local fuzzy cost function and pseudo-gradient optimization. The proposed method is verified by simulation cases and on-site cases, which can be utilized to prove the effectiveness in the aspect of decoupling the states.

title: The train collision load identification method combining LSTM autoencoder network and optimization iteration
abstract: Train collisions can cause serious casualties and property damage, and collision testing is a key means of evaluating the crashworthiness of trains. However, due to the complexity of the test environment, it is extremely challenging to directly measure the collision force. To this end, this paper proposes a collision load identification method that combines deep learning and optimization iteration to achieve indirect reconstruction of the collision load. Specifically, a curve prediction network based on an LSTM autoencoder was established, taking collision force parameters as input and displacement responses as output. Then, by iteratively optimizing the input parameters, the predicted displacement responses were aligned with the test data, thereby achieving the identification of the actual collision force in the test. The simulation validation and experimental comparison results show that the method effectively solves the limitations of the traditional measurement method in the train collision process, and provides a new technical way for train collision safety research.

title: Real-time monitoring of laser welding porosity defect using optical coherence tomography
abstract: Real-time monitoring of porosity defect is crucial for quality assurance during aluminum (Al) alloys laser welding. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) offers precise keyhole depth measurement and can be utilized for porosity monitoring. This paper proposes a laser welding porosity defect monitoring method using OCT. A laser welding monitoring platform based on OCT is developed to measure the keyhole depth. The weld depth and porosity depth are extracted from the keyhole depth with different percentiles and processed using empirical mode decomposition (EMD). The porosity and non-porosity regions are separated from the porosity depth curve based on a threshold. The standard deviation features of the weld depth and porosity depth are processed using EMD to serve as inputs for an artificial neural network (ANN). Considering the welding thermal history, a feedback ANN model with dual depth input is constructed for porosity prediction. Results indicate that the model reduces RRMSE and RMAE by 77.69% and 64.26% with a high prediction accuracy, exhibiting strong generalization ability, thus validating the proposed approach.

title: Multi-dimension hybrid particle filter-based online damage prognosis
abstract: Particle filter (PF) integrated with structural health monitoring (SHM) has received increasing attention for evaluating structural remaining useful life, due to its advantages of fusing online SHM observation to correct results and parameters of the physical damage evolution model. To apply this technique for the situation under complex service conditions, a sophisticated damage evolution model is essential, bringing multiple model parameters to be estimated. However, few PF-SHM methods have considered the multiple parameters estimation problem for the sophisticated model. Typically, only 1–2 parameters are combined along with the damage state as an augmented state vector to be estimated, where the model parameters and damage state share the same weight calculated with the SHM observation. This is because only the SHM observation of the damage state can be obtained with the SHM system, while the model parameter is not directly observable. This would lead to unstable and unreliable parameter estimates when more parameters are considered. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-dimension hybrid particle filter-based damage prognosis method. In this method, a multi-dimension hybrid damage-parameter state space model is developed, where the model parameters have their own evolution equations and observation equations in addition to the damage state. Besides, a novel parameter virtual observation likelihood is proposed for each parameter to update its own weight for posterior estimation, based on the SHM observation of the damage state and the partial derivative of the damage evolution model on the parameter. The proposed method is validated with both simulation and fatigue tests on aircraft attachment lug structures under three operational loading conditions, resulting in an average 40% increase in life prognosis accuracy, demonstrating its efficacy.

title: Elastic ring squeeze film damper dynamics and influence of bulge fitting: numerical and experimental investigation
abstract: The Elastic Ring Squeeze Film Damper (ERSFD) is a compact damping structure designed to minimize rotor vibrations in high-speed rotating machinery. Comprising bulge contact interfaces and oil-filled chambers, the ERSFD exhibits complex dynamic behavior, making it difficult to model and analyze due to the interaction and mutual dependencies between contact nonlinearity and the constantly varying oil film regions. To address these limitations, a novel oil film modeling approach is developed that incorporates both hydrodynamic effects and motion-dependent static pressure effects. The latter part of the proposed model arises from chamber volume variations and captures the deformation-dependent oil film region influenced by bulge contact nonlinearity. A fluid–structure interaction numerical simulation framework, incorporating dynamic parameter identification techniques, is developed to determine the system’s stiffness and damping coefficients. Parametric studies reveal the nonlinear influence of bulge fitting parameters on dynamic stiffness, damping, and pressure distribution. Notably, motion-dependent static pressure effects are shown to significantly enhance damping predictions beyond those obtained using conventional Reynolds equation-based approaches. The accuracy of the proposed model is validated through experimental investigations, which confirm its superior capability in predicting oil film pressure distribution and dynamic coefficients. Results indicate that interference fit configurations yield higher stiffness and damping performance due to full-circumference bulge engagement and increased oil chamber volume change rates. In contrast, clearance fits lead to reduced stiffness and damping, primarily due to limited ring deformation and lower volume variation. The wider bulge gaps in such cases allow easier oil flow, reducing flow resistance. With larger rotor motion, bulge separation further decreases flow impedance, thereby reducing the damping of the ERSFD.

title: Multi-directional extended attractors, coexisting attractors, circuit implementation of grid-scroll memristive chaotic oscillator with application to underwater signal detection
abstract: The reasonable design of chaotic oscillators is related to the performance of underwater signal detection. This study proposes a new grid-scroll memristive chaotic oscillator with infinite equilibrium points, and applies it to underwater signal detection. First, based on a cubic nonlinear memristor and piecewise linear functions, a novel grid-scroll memristive chaotic oscillator is designed. The oscillator can generate n × n-scroll attractors that extend infinitely in two directions with similar dynamical structures. Notably, by adjusting the initial conditions, infinitely coexisting multi-scroll and single-scroll attractors can be obtained in different dimensions, while a chaotic parameter enabling global amplitude control is also verified. The circuit model of the grid-scroll chaotic oscillator is constructed to assess its authenticity. Final, based on the 3 × 1-scroll chaotic oscillator, combined with the regenerated phase-shifted sinusoid-assisted empirical mode decomposition, correlation analysis and Hilbert transform, a new underwater signal detection model is designed, which can detect periodic signals across all frequencies. This model exhibits higher robustness to noise and easier identification of attractor’s state transitions. Compared to other existing detection systems, the designed model can realize a detection signal-to-noise ratio of −28 dB for ship signals, and its frequency extraction precision is above 99.9 %. The accurate detection for ship signals proves the universality of the designed model in practical applications.

title: Simultaneous identification of time-varying suspension parameters and unknown road roughness in a nonlinear suspension system
abstract: Road roughness plays a significant role in vehicle vibrations, which directly affect passenger ride comfort. However, many existing estimation methods for road roughness rely on simplified linear suspension models and assume that suspension parameters remain constant, which significantly restricts their practical applicability. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a novel augmented square root unscented Kalman filter with forgetting factor matrix (ASRUKF-FFM) method. The proposed ASRUKF-FFM method integrates the forgetting factor matrix and optimization-based solutions into the augmented square root unscented Kalman filter (ASRUKF), treating both parameters and unknown road inputs as augmented state vectors. This enables the simultaneous estimation of time-varying suspension parameters and road roughness. Then, both the nonlinear suspension model and road profile model are established, providing a foundation for the application of the proposed algorithm. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, simulations are performed considering both constant and time-varying parameters. Specifically, the time-varying parameters account for changes in mass-related parameters and damping variations under different driving conditions. Finally, the performance of ASRUKF-FFM algorithm is evaluated under different initial conditions, sensor configurations, and noise levels. The results highlight its robustness and reliability in practical applications.

title: Physics-inspired data-driven modeling of complex mechanical components in mecha(tro)nic systems
abstract: We present a data-driven approach for modeling complex components in mechatronic systems using a physics-inspired neural network structure. This structure reflects the principles of classical first-principle modeling, particularly the separation of time and state-space variables. Gated recurrent units (GRUs) approximate the system’s ordinary differential equations (ODEs), while a deep feedforward network maps state variables to a target variable, approximating the measurement equation. Training data is limited to standard input–output measurements, avoiding the need to measure the full state vector—a challenging or impractical task in many cases. The trained network can be symbolically approximated to yield ODE expressions for the system’s latent states and a symbolic measurement equation for mapping states to the target variable. This enables seamless integration into variable time-step, system-level simulation software. It is illustrated that these networks can be constructed with a certain latent space that may be mapped to the physics-based states which are obtained from a reference simulation. The framework is demonstrated on measurement data of a rubber bushing, and on model-based simulation data serving as a reference. The results show that the network captures the challenging nonlinear dynamics and hysteresis behavior. Its physics-inspired design uses a minimal number of parameters, reducing overfitting, enhancing interpretability, and lowering data requirements. Additionally, the framework requires no expertise in specific components or materials, making it versatile and accessible. With high accuracy and low computational cost, the methodology is suitable for a broad range of nonlinear dynamic components and facilitates integration into existing workflows through its symbolic descriptions.

title: Design of the vibration damping structures for battery pack casing of an electric vehicle
abstract: Two battery pack casings with pack total energy of 12.432 kWh are 3D-printed using aluminum alloy (AlSi10Mg) and carbon fiber-reinforced composite filament based on Polyamide 6, 12 (PA12 CF+). The vibration and shock attenuation capabilities of the three mechanical metamaterials (auxetic, lattice and X-shaped structures) applied to battery pack casing’s walls are studied. Lattice structure shows better shock mitigation capability on the PA12 CF+ battery pack casing, reaching up to 59.82% reduction longitudinally. Auxetic structure demonstrates effective vibration attenuation capability on the AlSi10Mg battery pack casing, reducing vertical and longitudinal vibration levels by 14% and 18.94% averagely, respectively. In addition, two damping structures are designed based on quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) principle and three-dimensional double-arrow-head (3D DAH) auxetic structure. Thereafter, the vibration attenuation capabilities of the two damping structures are evaluated. The QZS isolator is suitable for all aluminum battery pack casings and the modified PA12 CF+ battery pack casings. While the 3D DAH auxetic structure is more suitable for battery pack casings with larger power spectra density (PSD). Furthermore, the combination of the auxetic structure and a QZS vibration isolator shows the best vertical vibration mitigation performance when applied to PA12 CF+ and AlSi10Mg solid battery pack casings.

title: A reliability modeling method for accelerated degradation process with memory effects based on artificial neural network supported fractional Brownian motion
abstract: For degradation prediction of high-reliability equipment, accelerated degradation test data is often used to extrapolate the degradation state under normal stress levels. Previous studies typically model degradation using memoryless Markovian processes. However, due to the inherent degradation mechanisms and external stress influences, the degradation process often exhibits varying levels of memory effects, which significantly impact modeling accuracy when using Markovian methods. fractional Brownian motion quantifies memory effects through the Hurst exponent, but existing research often fixes the time-scale function to basic forms, leading to potential errors. This paper proposes a hybrid model combining artificial neural networks with fractional Brownian motion to simultaneously capture memory effects and the time-scale function that best reflects the actual degradation trend. The hybrid model employs a unified loss function and a gradient-based optimization algorithm to iteratively update the parameters of both the neural network and fractional Brownian motion, ensuring optimal alignment. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations and real-world degradation datasets, and the results demonstrate that the approach more accurately captures global memory effects and global degradation trends, outperforming traditional models.

title: Energy-coupling-based adaptive control for quadrotor transportation systems with double-pendulum swing effects
abstract: Quadrotor transportation system face underactuation challenges compounded by double-pendulum dynamics and unknown payload masses. To tackle these issues, this paper develops a novel energy-coupling-based adaptive controller to address quadrotor transportation system with double-pendulum swing effects and unknown payload mass. First, a generalized payload signal is introduced to strengthen state coupling between the quadrotor and the double-pendulum system, explicitly incorporating swing dynamics into the energy shaping framework for improved transient performance. Building on this foundation, an adaptive law is designed to estimate the unknown payload mass in real time, ensuring robustness against parameter uncertainties without requiring prior payload information. These advancements collectively enable the construction of a new energy storage function, whose stability properties are rigorously proven via Lyapunov techniques and LaSalle’s invariance theorem, guaranteeing asymptotic convergence of both positioning and swing suppression. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed control scheme under external disturbances and parameter uncertainties.

title: T-BGA-CA: A Multi-Level Attention-Based BiGRU model for early fault warning in unmanned ocean platform electromechanical systems
abstract: Large unmanned ocean platforms have extensive applications in military reconnaissance, maritime rescue, and resource exploration. The electromechanical system, as the core component of these platforms, faces numerous challenges due to harsh sea conditions, spatial constraints, and multiple monitoring points. These challenges include frequent component failures, complex multi-source data coupling, unpredictable fault propagation paths, and difficulties in real-time fault monitoring and localization. Consequently, reliability analysis algorithms for these systems have become a critical research focus. This study investigates a 15-ton unmanned ocean platform comprising two diesel engines, two electric motors, transmission equipment, and auxiliary systems. The research develops early-warning algorithms using real data from 30 key monitoring points deployed by the platform’s monitoring system. 1) A novel intelligent fault prediction model named Transformer-BiGRU Global Attention-Cross Attention (T-BGA-CA) is proposed, which combines prediction errors with Savitzky-Golay convolutional smoothing and dynamic threshold methods to construct health indicators for the unmanned ocean platform; 2) To verify the effectiveness of the new method, actual operating data from 30 monitoring points covering the main engine, electric motor, and auxiliary equipment are used. The grouped Pearson correlation coefficient method is employed to screen multi-source parameters, and principal component analysis (PCA) is combined with the algorithm to achieve multi-feature fusion. The PCA parameters are then used to train and predict the early warning model, successfully achieving effective early warnings for main equipment flyaway faults 136 s in advance; 3) T-BGA-CA is compared with traditional algorithms, e.g., LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, BiGRU, Transformer, and fusion algorithms. The results show that T-BGA-CA provides the earliest fault warnings (20–25 sampling points ahead of traditional algorithms). It achieves the lowest false alarm rate and optimal warning threshold. In terms of basic algorithm metrics, the MAE metric of the T-BGA-CA model decreased by 57.1% and the MedAE metric decreased by 56.3% compared to suboptimal traditional warning algorithms. The proposed algorithm also reduces running time while ensuring accuracy compared to fusion algorithms. The new algorithm is expected to provide algorithmic support for the state prediction and early warning of the electromechanical systems of unmanned platforms.

title: A resonance demodulation method based on amplitude Z-score of envelope spectrum for weak bearing fault detection
abstract: Resonance demodulation has been extensively employed for fault diagnosis in rolling element bearings due to its effectiveness in extracting fault features. Achieving high diagnostic accuracy largely depends on a precise identification of the optimal resonant frequency band for demodulation. However, accuracy and robustness of existing methods still require further improvement. To address this issue, this study proposes a resonance demodulation algorithm, termed Z-score-gram (Zsgram), which aims to enhance fault feature extraction under low signal-to-noise conditions. The proposed method constructs a hierarchical representation of a signal by summing minimum-scale components through a level-wise decomposition structure, significantly improving computational efficiency by reducing required number of Fourier and inverse Fourier transforms. To incorporate physical fault characteristics into evaluation processes of frequency bands, the algorithm introduces an amplitude-based Z-scores at fault-related frequencies within envelope spectra. This integration improves both sensitivity and robustness of fault-component identification. Experiments on simulated data and public datasets demonstrate that the Zsgram outperforms benchmark methods including Fast-Kurtogram, Autogram, and improved envelope spectrum via candidate fault frequency optimization-gram, achieving superior accuracy and stability in detecting weak fault components. As a result, the proposed method facilitates early and accurate extraction of fault features, improves potential defects observable, and consequently enhances both timeliness of predictive maintenance and intrinsic operational safety of bearings.

title: Designing optimal controller for semi-active rotor dry friction damper based on frequency-domain states: An offline deep reinforcement learning approach
abstract: For various semi-active rotor dry friction dampers (SARDFD), how to effectively suppress rotor unbalance responses with minimum normal forces can be formulated as an optimal control problem. Classical optimal controllers were mostly developed in the time domain, which makes them unsuitable for the control of SARDFDs due to the high rotational speeds of rotor systems. In this paper, an offline deep reinforcement learning approach is proposed to perform online force optimization for SARDFDs based on slowly time-variant frequency-domain states. Firstly, by experimentally investigating the dynamics of a SARDFD-rotor system, it is found that the SARDFD’s working mechanism makes it feasible to design optimal SARDFD controllers by taking vibration amplitudes as inputs. Then, theoretical analysis is performed to validate this feasibility, and the frequency-domain states are designed according to analysis results. Subsequently, a novel offline deep reinforcement learning approach is proposed to design optimal SARDFD controllers based on these frequency-domain states. The reward functions and environment updating strategies are designed according to the results of dynamical analysis. The effectiveness of the designed controller is finally validated by comparing it with three state-of-the-art SARDFD controllers. Results suggest that, even if no system models are included during the training procedure, the vibration suppression capacities of the designed deep reinforcement learning controller are quite close to well-tuned model-based optimal controllers. It spends less energy than those optimum-damping-oriented controllers, and its vibration control performance is much more robust to changes in residual unbalances compared with typical proportional-integral controllers.

title: FD-MVLLM: Fault diagnosis based on multimodal vibration data and large language model for bearing system
abstract: Bearing system is critical components in rotating machinery, whose health directly impacts operational safety. To address faults arising from bearing wear—and to overcome the limitations of conventional deep-learning methods that struggle to exploit both time- and frequency-domain information simultaneously—we propose FD-MVLLM, a novel reprogramming framework that combines a large language model (LLM) with multimodal vibration data for fault diagnosis. First, raw vibration signals are preprocessed to produce three distinct modalities: the original time series and two time–frequency representations. Convolutional layer then extract features from the time–frequency images. Innovatively, we reprogram both the raw time series and the image features using carefully designed text prototypes, yielding patch embeddings. To fully leverage the LLM’s reasoning capabilities and boost diagnostic accuracy, we also integrate key time-domain and frequency-domain evaluation metrics into the prompt context, producing prompt embeddings. These patch and prompt embeddings are fed into an LLM fine-tuned via low-rank adaptation (LoRA); a final linear output layer translates the LLM’s output into precise fault diagnoses. We validate FD-MVLLM on simulated rolling bearing fault data—generated using Hertz contact theory and Runge-Kutta numerical integration—as well as on several public benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that FD-MVLLM substantially outperforms fault diagnosis methods based on single-modal vibration data and LLM., highlighting its promise as a new paradigm for multimodal data-driven fault diagnosis. This work is open-sourced at https://github.com/youngpy996/FD-MVLLM.

title: Visualization and identification of nonlinear structural dynamics via phase-based motion magnification
abstract: The identification and analysis of nonlinear dynamics in structural systems remain critical challenges in engineering, particularly when subtle vibrational phenomena are involved. Phase-Based Motion Magnification (PBMM) has emerged as a powerful non-contact technique for visualizing fine-scale motions in complex systems, yet its application to nonlinear structural behavior remains underexplored. This study investigates the dynamic response of a beam–spring system with intentional nonlinearities, focusing on the characterization of superharmonic components and mode shapes using PBMM. Experimental tests under force-controlled stepped-sine excitation reveal pronounced hardening effects at the first resonant frequency, attributed to the geometric nonlinearity of the spring, and minimal nonlinear behavior at the second resonant frequency. High-speed video recordings were processed with PBMM, enabling the visualization of subtle energy redistribution into higher harmonics and the extraction of mode shapes across multiple frequency ranges. To enhance structural boundary visualization, a novel Visualization of Edge Detection (VED) method combining DexiNed edge detection and bilateral filtering was employed. Comparisons between PBMM results and accelerometer data validated the effectiveness of this approach in capturing nonlinear responses. These findings highlight the potential of PBMM, combined with advanced post-processing techniques, to revolutionize non-contact modal analysis and provide new insights into the nonlinear dynamics of engineering structures.

title: Parameters identification of blade vibration based on dual-sensor full waveform and improved grey wolf optimizer algorithm
abstract: Monitoring rotating blade vibration is critical for turbomachinery safety, and blade tip timing (BTT) is one of the key non-contact measurement techniques. Conventional BTT methods, however, face significant limitations in accurately identifying complex multi-frequency vibrations. These methods frequently depend on sparse time-of-arrival (TOA) data, resulting in undersampling of the vibration signal and the subsequent neglect of the rich dynamic information contained within the complete sensor waveform. To overcome these problems, this paper proposes a novel vibration parameters identification method based on dual-sensor full-waveform analysis. Initially, the complete sensor voltage waveform in relation to the blade tip vibration is used to extract richer information than the TOA-based method. Subsequently, an adaptive noise weighting strategy fuses the sensor data by assessing the signal quality based on the fitting residuals of the waveform data within one revolution. The improved grey wolf optimizer (IGWO) algorithm efficiently addresses the mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) complexities inherent in parameters identification, accurately resolving key vibration parameters without reliance on prior information. The effects of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and number of revolutions on the parameters identification results are analyzed under five different vibration modes. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through experiments involving both single-mode and dual-mode vibrations. The results show that the parameters of single-mode vibration can be identified with single revolution of data, and the parameters of dual-mode vibration can be identified with four revolutions of data. This demonstrated efficacy with limited revolution data provides a robust foundation for developing online BTT monitoring systems.

title: An adaptive measurement-based substructure identification framework for dynamic response reconstruction
abstract: The finite element model (FEM) plays an important role in model-driven response reconstruction of mechanical structure. Unfortunately, modelling difficulty of certain complex mechanical substructures could lead to the unavailability of precise modelling, thus impairing the reliability of the full FEM. This paper presents a measurement-based adaptive framework for substructure identification to address the limitation of FEM used in response reconstruction. Experimental measurement and structural information of the designed interface-attaching device (IAD) are exploited to identify the desired substructure (DS). Specifically, the measured signal is obtained from IAD assembling DS at the desired interface and is then processed to extract reliable modal parameters adaptively by the Bayesian module. These modal parameters characterize the assembly, which can identify DS in modal representation by analytically subtracting the IAD model by coordinate transfer. The resulted DS model, with connectible interface to which IAD attaches before, is coupled to the rest components to form the full FEM. On this basis, the response mapping is built by structural mode shapes, and the response at inaccessible locations can be reconstructed by available measurement. Response reconstruction cases of a numerical beam structure and an experimental flange-tube assembly are applied to verify superiority and accuracy of the proposed method.

title: Phase-based crossline center detection for robust vibration monitoring under large motion and pose variations
abstract: Monitoring of a vibrating target undergoing large motion has been an interest in the field of industrial informatics, aerospace testing, etc. However, the large translation and the possible pose variation of target impose difficulties to a stable and accurate vibration monitoring using vision tracking techniques. Herein, this study proposes a phase-based crossline center detection technique capable of accurate and robust absolute image-plane displacement tracking (mean absolute error under 0.003 pxl) even under large motion and severe pose changes. The two orthogonal lines of crossline pattern remain as line patterns even after perspective transformation, providing a stable feature for lateral phase extraction and center detection. Each line position is determined by searching for the phase zero-crossings after phase extraction along two directions, without the requirement of constant phase assumption and phase pyramid as the conventional phase-based optical flow. The center is accurately detected by intersecting the two lines. This study provides a derivation of the phase-based crossline center detection process, demonstrating that the marker center can be precisely located using phase zero-crossing. An improved pixel-wise camera imaging simulation method is also proposed to validate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed technique with different filter parameters and crossline poses and sizes. Laboratory experiments are conducted on a movable shaker with constant-amplitude vibration output testing the accuracy and robustness of the proposed technique. Field experiment is performed by monitoring the vibration of a moving spindle on a hybrid machine tool with comparison with accelerometers. The results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed phase-based crossline center detection and its potential for vibration monitoring tasks even with large motion and pose changes. In this context, accuracy refers to image-plane displacement, which corresponds to physical motion under planar conditions, while under significant pose changes and large motion it primarily indicates the motion’s order of magnitude, trends, and frequency content.

title: Nonlinear fatigue analysis of onshore wind turbines with steel–concrete hybrid tower using a co-simulation method and enhanced kernel density estimation
abstract: Steel–Concrete Hybrid Towers (SCHTs) offer an economical and structurally efficient solution for tall onshore wind turbines. However, accurately assessing their fatigue performance remains challenging due to nonlinear responses to stochastic wind loads. This study presents a comprehensive framework for nonlinear fatigue life analysis of SCHTs. A high-fidelity co-simulation method is first introduced by coupling multibody and finite element dynamics via a MATLAB-based interface between Simpack and OpenSees, enabling the simulation of geometric and material nonlinearities. To better capture wind load uncertainty, the framework accounts for the joint variability of wind speed and direction. An enhanced kernel density estimation (KDE) strategy is proposed to reconstruct their joint distribution from real data, optimizing bandwidths by minimizing the Frobenius norm error between analytical and empirical joint characteristic functions. The probabilistic wind input data is then integrated with the nonlinear structural model to evaluate fatigue life using rainflow counting algorithm and S–N curves. Results reveal that nonlinear effects significantly increase tower-top displacements and stress fluctuations, shift fatigue-critical regions downward, and reduce fatigue life compared to linear models. Comparative analysis confirms that the proposed KDE bandwidth optimization improves fatigue life predictions over conventional KDE approaches.

title: Model order reduction and dynamic analysis of the complex series–parallel-branch pipe system: Numerical and experimental studies
abstract: Efficient and accurate prediction for the dynamics of series–parallel-branch pipe (SPBP) systems can guide the design and damage detection of pipe systems in practical engineering. This paper develops a super reduced-order modeling (ROM) method for SPBP systems by combining the finite element method (FEM), Craig-Bampton method (CBM), and an improved transfer matrix method for multibody systems (MSTMM), thus efficiently analyzing the corresponding dynamic behaviors. Specifically, the idea behind the super ROM method is as follows: a finite element model for each substructure is initially established, and a reduction in internal and modal degrees of freedom (DOFs) is conducted using the CBM and MSTMM, respectively. Subsequently, the transfer equations between state variables at the parallel connections are established, enabling the extension of the MSTMM to a parallel pipe. Next, the state variables of the slave branches are integrated into those of the master branch using continuity and equilibrium equations, which is equivalent to the master branch absorbing the DOFs in the slave branches, thus reducing DOFs in the slave branches. For the SPBP system composed of 8 pipes studied in this paper, the reduced-order model has only 24 DOFs. Finally, general frequency and response equations are formulated and solved, the computational accuracy and efficiency of the ROM method are analyzed, and the energy transmission behaviors of the pipe system under base and point excitations are examined, respectively.

title: Broadband ultrasonic lamb wave phased array imaging
abstract: Broadband Lamb wave phased array imaging by total focusing method (TFM) and pulse compression can effectively improve imaging performance with respect to narrowband excitation, attracting widespread attention. This paper proposes a broadband Lamb wave phased array imaging method based on time-reversal of long-time pulse echoes, where the damage index is derived from the combined contribution of all frequency components. The broadband delay and sum (DAS) beamforming formula is derived for broadband phased array beamforming analysis. Based on the strategy of time-reversal refocusing, the broadband Time-domain topological energy (TDTE) imaging method is developed for dispersion compensation and broadband imaging of long-time pulse echoes, breaking through the insufficient spatial resolution of TFM under long-time signal excitation. The validation experiments on aluminum alloy plate with multiple defects show that the proposed broadband imaging method can achieve great performance and robustness without prior selection of optimal imaging frequency, and can maintain the imaging quality by long-time excitation under low voltage and low scattering.

title: Machining parameters inversion and regularity analysis based on surface topography point cloud of GH4169 alloy
abstract: Machining parameters directly influence the formation of surface topography. However, the surface topography is susceptible to partial distortion due to the interaction of various external disturbances, making it challenging to establish the mapping relationship between surface topography and machining parameters. PointNet++ can be utilized to develop a model for inverting machining parameters from surface topography using preprocessed point cloud data, thereby providing a research foundation for intelligent manufacturing. The test results of this model can be analyzed for regularity to study the results of different machining parameters on the surface topography. The GH4169 alloy is used as the study object. The mechanisms of the cutting depth, feed per tooth, cutting speed, and their orthogonal combinations are systematically investigated to reveal the parameter interactions and characteristic regularity. The dynamic relationship among data dimensionality, data density, model accuracy, and convergence speed is investigated by comparing multiple training and testing results. The robustness of PointNet++ in capturing surface topographic features is demonstrated. The output of this research provides theoretical and technical support for machining parameter inversion and a data-driven basis for high-quality surface machining in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Analysis on the characteristics of dynamics and sound insulation for the stiffened multi-layered panels-cavity coupled system
abstract: The vibro-acoustic behavior of the stiffened multi-layered panels-cavity coupled system is analyzed by the energy principle combined with Rayleigh-Ritz method. Both the structural–acoustic coupling between the enclosed cavities and the stiffened multi-layered panels and the coupling between the stiffeners and adjacent panels are established in theoretical formulations. The improved Fourier series are adopted to describe the displacement of the stiffened multi-layered panels and the sound pressure inside the enclosed cavities. The characteristic equation of the coupled system could be derived by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz procedure for the energy function of the stiffened multi-layered panels-cavity coupled system. The effectiveness of the theoretical modelling is validated by the comparision of the vibro-acoustic behavior of the stiffened multi-layered panels-cavity coupled system obtained from the current method and finite element method. In numerical analysis, it is analyzed that the effect of the incident sound wave, the dimensions, the layer number, the coupling stiffness and boundary conditions of the stiffened panels on the sound transmission characteristics of the stiffened multi-layered panels-cavity coupled system.

title: A coupled approach and analysis to pantograph-rigid catenary system considering the contact pair wear and system dynamic interaction
abstract: The carbon contact strips of the pantograph collect current from the overhead contact wire to power the train, inevitably causing wear and changes in the wear profile on the contact surfaces, which leads to uneven distribution of the normal load and results in varying degrees of wear rate. This study introduces the influence of contact pair wear on the dynamic interaction of pantograph-catenary system (PCS). A PCS coupling model, considering the entire wear life cycle, was established based on the multibody dynamic theory and energy dissipation theory. The evolution of the PCS dynamic interaction and wear performance during this period is explored. Furthermore, this paper proposes the concept of lateral distribution of contact force to simplify wear profile calculations and enhance the accuracy of wear predictions, thus providing an indicator for determining dynamic and wear performance. The results show that the model demonstrates a strong agreement with the field-measured data in both the time domain and frequency domain. Compared to traditional models, its accuracy has been significantly improved and is applicable to different PCS structures. Additionally, due to the change in the contact pair wear profile, the PCS dynamic performance, wear performance, and electrical contact performance all deteriorate to varying degrees with increasing operating mileage. This deterioration manifests in three stages for dynamic performance: stable, slow degradation, and rapid degradation. However, during operation, there is a competitive situation where the reduction in mass may lead to performance optimization, while the worsening of the profile curve causes performance degradation. On the other hand, the wear performance shows three stages: run-in, stable, and deterioration, which align with field test results. Based on this model, the entire wear life cycle performance of the contact pair can be explored and understood, thereby enabling the development of corresponding performance improvement and abnormal wear prevention measures.

title: Resonance observation of pump-turbine runners from the stationary frame: analytical-numerical model for the natural mode splitting of submerged rotating disc-blades-disc structures
abstract: • Corrects existing misconceptions of pump-turbine runner mode shapes and advances in the resonance mechanism understanding. • Proposes an explanation and validates mode splitting in rotating disc-blades-disc (DBD) assemblies in water. • Analytical analysis reveals mode shape splitting rules in such structures similar to pump-turbine runners. • Unveils root causes of multi-frequency vibration phenomena observed on pump-turbine top covers. With the growing adoption of renewable energy sources such as wind and solar power, pumped storage technology is flourishing in several developing countries. Based on the widespread vibration issues faced by pumped storage units, particularly in their runners and top covers, this paper aims to investigate the natural mode splitting of complex rotating structures and the observation of this phenomenon from the stationary reference frame. The finite element method (FEM) is employed to analyze the characteristics of the diametrical mode shape of a disc-blades-disc (DBD) structure, which is representative of pumped turbine runners. An analytical approach is utilized to investigate the formation mechanism of these diametrical components, thereby predicting the rules governing the mode shape splitting of underwater rotating structures. The imposed modal motion method, based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD), is used to predict the natural frequency splitting and hydraulic damping splitting of the DBD structure. Building on these studies, a combined approach of analytical methods, CFD, and FEM is employed to predict the resonance characteristics of the rotating structure on the stationary reference frame, as well as the resulting pressure pulsations and the vibrations of the stationary casing. Results reveal that the relationship between the diametrical components of the natural modes of the DBD structure is strictly related to the number of blades. When the structure rotates in water, its diametrical modes split into two independent travelling wave modes, each containing multiple diametrical components (i.e., travelling wave components), with the difference between these components equaling the number of blades. The model predicts that if a travelling wave mode is excited, a ’multi-frequency’ feature, with frequency differences equal to the product of the number of blades and the rotational frequency, will be observed on the stationary frame. These findings are consistent with the multi-frequency vibration phenomena observed in some real cases, providing a foundation for further understanding the vibration mechanisms in pump-turbines and similar mechanical structures.

title: Research on residual attention-based mechanism autoencoder for microseismic denoising network model
abstract: Noise induced by dynamic changes in the deep engineering environment seriously reduces the accuracy of P- and S-waves arrival-time picking, which in turn affects the accuracy of seismic source localization and the effectiveness of disaster warnings. This study proposes a residual attention-based mechanism autoencoder for the microseismic signal denoising (RAA-MD) model. The model combines the skip connection mechanism of residual blocks with the dynamic squeeze-and-channel attention module, which significantly improves the transfer efficiency of feature information and the recognition of key features by adaptively adjusting the channel weights. Based on the monitoring data obtained from the Hanjiang-to-Weihe River Diversion Project, the RAA-MD model was systematically verified under varying initial signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and diverse noise environment conditions. The results demonstrate that compared to the autoencoder network with ordinary convolution alone (CNN-AE), autoencoder network combined with a residual module (RES-AE), and autoencoder network combined with attention mechanism (CDSCA-AE) models, the RAA-MD model demonstrates excellent denoised performance, especially when dealing with microseismic signals with low SNR and complex environments. Subsequently, to further validate the application potential of the RAA-MD model, P- and S-waves arrival-time picking networks were constructed based on the U-Net architecture. A quantitative analysis was conducted to compare the arrival-time picking accuracy of signals before and after denoising. The results show that after denoising, the P- and S-waves arrival-time pickup accuracies are improved by 85.94% and 70.81%, respectively. Finally, the effects of different network depth configurations, attention mechanisms and dataset sizes on the denoising performance are discussed, and the optimal model is compared and analyzed with U-shaped network (U-Net), residual network (ResNet), and recurrent neural network (RNN) models widely used in the field of one-dimensional data denoising. The significant advantages of the residual attention-based mechanism autoencoder for the microseismic signal denoising network model in microseismic signal processing and its important application value in the field of microseismic monitoring are verified.

title: Elastic boundary conditions-based iFEM for shape-sensing of complicated boundary constrained structures
abstract: Accurate deformation monitoring is crucial for on-orbit aerospace structures to ensure performance and security. The inverse finite element method (iFEM) is a versatile, robust, computationally efficient shape-sensing methodology that only involves strain measurement, structural geometry, and displacement boundary conditions. However, in practical engineering applications, it is difficult to accurately obtain the actual displacements at the boundary locations due to the complexity of the boundary constraints. Inaccurate definitions of structural displacement boundary conditions in iFEM will lead to poor shape-sensing accuracy since boundary constraint equations are key to solving the reconstruction matrix of iFEM. To address the problem, this paper proposes an elastic boundary conditions-based inverse finite element method (EBC-iFEM). Elastic boundary conditions based on spring elements are used to approximate complex boundary constraints. The boundary constraint equations based on spring elements can be assembled with reconstruction equations of all inverse finite elements to obtain the constrained global reconstruction equation of the structure. By optimizing the elastic parameters of spring elements, complex boundary constraints can be simulated without knowing displacements at boundary locations. The proposed method was validated by numerical and experimental experiments of a bolted honeycomb plate structure of large deployable space-borne antennas. The results indicate that the proposed EBC-iFEM can improve the shape-sensing accuracy of a bolted honeycomb structure with the maximum shape-sensing relative error reduced from 7.1% to 4.8% compared to iFEM with ideal boundary conditions definition.

title: Motor current analytical models and signature analysis for rotate vector reducer fault diagnosis
abstract: Rotate Vector (RV) reducers are usually driven by electric motors, and motor stator currents contain meaningful information about RV reducer health conditions. The stator current measurement is free of sensor placement issue, and the signal has relatively low complexity. Therefore, motor current analysis provides a promising approach to RV reducer fault diagnosis. In order to leverage the advantages of motor currents, it is essential to thoroughly understand the oscillation mechanism of currents and reveal their spectral characteristics in fault cases. Firstly, the current signal analytical models are derived through mechanical-magnetic-electrical interaction analysis, for gear faults in both the planetary and cycloidal gear stages, considering the modulation effects on power supply frequency due to gear fault, meshing and cycloid wobble. Such analytical models discover the multiple amplitude modulation and frequency modulation nature of motor currents, and inspire demodulation analysis idea for fault diagnosis. Then, the explicit equations of Fourier spectrum, amplitude and frequency demodulation spectra are derived based on the signal analytical model. Such theoretical derivations reveal the RV reducer fault spectral characteristics manifested in motor currents, in both power supply and gear meshing frequency regions, and advise what features to seek for fault diagnosis. Finally, inspired by the multiple modulation nature of motor currents, a synthesis methodology is proposed by exploiting the complementary information from Fourier spectrum, amplitude and frequency demodulation spectra. This methodology suggests how to identify fault features and provides more convincing evidences for fault diagnosis. The theoretical derivations are validated experimentally through data analysis of an RV reducer test rig, and gear localized faults on the sun, planet, cycloid and pinwheel are all successfully diagnosed, even though the planet and cycloid fault characteristic frequencies are identical.

title: Energy-based optimization of tuned mass damper parameters for vibration control of force-excited damped structures
abstract: An energy-based optimization procedure is proposed for the design of tuned mass dampers (TMDs) in force-excited systems. In this procedure, the optimal TMD parameters are determined by minimizing the energy dissipation demand on the primary system using an H∞ norm minimization technique. The optimal values of the design parameters (i.e., tuning frequency ratio and damping ratio of the TMD) are obtained and presented for different damping ratios of the primary system and mass ratios of the TMD. Subsequently, explicit formulae for the optimal parameters are derived using a nonlinear curve-fitting technique. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, the energy-based optimal parameters are used to design a TMD for a 76-story wind-excited benchmark building. Dynamic response analysis of the building model demonstrates that the proposed optimal TMD can effectively reduce the wind responses of the building, even in the presence of frequency and damping uncertainties. Furthermore, the method is shown to be very effective and promising for the dual purposes of vibration control and energy harvesting.

title: A novel stream computing engine for virtual dynamic response of bridge digital twins under real-time traffic load: Framework and experimental validation
abstract: In the context of real-time sensing of in-service bridge structural performance and working state, the digital twin-based direct method driven by real-time traffic load offer promising applications but also pose significant challenges. A critical prerequisite is establishing real-time interaction between the physical prototype bridge and its digital twin, driven by real-time traffic load and their induced dynamic responses. However, existing methods lack real-time computational capabilities to synchronize virtual responses in the digital domain with the evolving traffic load in the physical domain. To this end, this paper propose an online integrated stream computing engine, leveraging the stream-loading characteristics of real-time traffic load on the deck. The engine integrates a real-time digital twinning method for traffic loads with an advanced stream computing method for virtual dynamic response calculation, within a stream processing framework. Numerical studies based on potential application scenarios validate the proposed stream computing method, demonstrating its performance and robustness against initialization errors, while the proposed multi-level modal selection strategy provides a foundation for constructing efficient stream computing operators. The feasibility and applicability of this engine framework is further validated through experimental implementation on a test bridge, highlighting its potential for future applications on real-world bridges. The proposed stream computing engine enables accurate and efficient digital representation, real-time loading, and dynamic responses twinning for bridge under RTTL, providing a foundation for the future development of structural performance and working state sensing-oriented digital twin systems.

title: Propagation mechanism of 1/f noise in FTR system of micro hemispherical resonator gyroscopes
abstract: The 1/f noise in micro hemispherical resonator gyroscopes (mHRGs) induces bias instability (BI); however, theoretical understanding of 1/f noise propagation in force-to-rebalance (FTR) systems remains inadequate. For the first time, we have investigated the effect of 1/f noise attached to the amplitude of the AC signal on the instability of the output of the mHRG under constant angular velocity input in the FTR system, and propose a new model for the propagation of 1/f noise. We first demonstrate the fundamental dependence of 1/f noise Allan variance on low-frequency spectral components under large correlation time regimes. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, we prove that Allan variance is predominantly governed by low-frequency characteristics, with high-frequency components becoming negligible. We subsequently identify and characterize the flat amplitude-frequency response of FTR transfer functions within the low-frequency domain, establishing their critical role in noise amplification. Analytical expressions are derived for this flat gain characteristic, which directly governs propagation coefficients mapping various 1/f noise sources to gyroscope bias output.
