We further develop quantitative models describing regulatory mechanisms by which system parameters control noise propagation. The influence of drive mode amplitude, frequency splitting, and proportional-integral controller coefficients on low-frequency gain is systematically analyzed, revealing distinct regulatory effects on five identified noise sources: external angular velocity fluctuations, anchor voltage variations, mechanical parameter instabilities, demodulation artifacts, and feed-through interference. Experimental validation through FPGA-based implementation confirms theoretical predictions, providing a physics-based foundation for systematic noise optimization.

title: Estimating complex-valued material parameters of piezoceramic thin-walled tubes by finite element model updating
abstract: Accurate estimation of complex-valued material parameters (CMPs) is crucial for the design and analysis of piezoceramic thin-walled tube transducers, particularly in underwater acoustic applications. This study proposes an iterative finite element model updating-based (FEMU-based) parameter correction approach to determine four key CMPs – one dielectric permittivity, two elastic compliances, and one piezoelectric constant – using a measured impedance function (MIF). Unlike traditional impedance-based approaches, which often suffer from numerical instability and sensitivity to measurement noise, the proposed method employs a cross-model cross-mode-based updating strategy that utilizes complex-valued poles and zeros extracted from the MIF. This approach enhances computational efficiency by directly modifying system matrices without reconstructing the finite element model at each iteration. Numerical simulations and experimental validation demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method in estimating CMPs, even in cases where certain vibration modes are not present. The results show significant improvements in parameter estimation, highlighting the effectiveness of the FEMU framework for characterizing piezoceramic materials in practical engineering applications.

title: Ambient noise-based passive reconstruction of dispersion curve in a thin-plate with complex boundary interferences using sparse learning
abstract: The passive reconstruction of dispersion curve of a plate-like structure using ambient noise has been intensively studied and applied to various structural health monitoring problems. Its principle is to use the cross-correlation between the random guided wave signals measured by two receivers to approximate the impulse response between the two measurement points where the resolution is proportional to the wavelength. This methodology is powerful in many scenarios but problematic for structures with complex boundaries, because boundary reflections contaminate the desired direct propagation components in the cross-correlation such that the estimated impulse response is biased. To address this problem, this paper proposes a sparse learning scheme to decompose the cross-correlation and then to restore the robustness of passive impulse response estimation. First, an overcomplete dictionary considering the features of the cross-correlation components is proposed. We then perform the sparse decomposition on the cross-correlation, from which individual wave packets corresponding to different propagation paths are obtained and this enables a precise dispersion curve reconstruction. The efficiency of the proposed method is demonstrated via a passive experiment where the ambient noise is excited by spraying air-jet onto the surface of a plate. Additionally, the method is successfully applied to the passive detection of ice accretion on plates, which has the potential for passive online monitoring of aircraft structure icing.

title: Fault-induced intrinsic morphological signals in gear systems: theory and experiment
abstract: Although pitting and crack in gears exhibit distinct fault mechanisms and meshing characteristics, effectively distinguishing these faults in vibration signals remains challenging. Despite the application of numerous indicators and analytical methods for fault identification, these approaches are difficult to clearly capture the meshing characteristics of faulty gears or provide intuitive explanations of fault mechanisms. This study introduces the concept of Fault Intrinsic Morphological Signal (Fault IMS), designed to intuitively reflect the dynamic meshing behavior of faulty teeth, with waveform patterns explicitly revealing fault characteristics. The primary contributions of this work are threefold: (i) This study analyzes the underlying reasons for the difficulty in distinguishing different fault types and formally defines the concept of Fault IMS. (ii) A systematic theoretical framework for calculating Fault IMS is proposed, which constructs the signal by suppressing gear meshing components. (iii) Two experimental setups are designed and conducted to validate the patterns and characteristics of Fault IMS for pitting, crack, and multi-tooth pitting. This work addresses the challenge of distinguishing pitting and cracking in vibration signal, offering a novel perspective on gear fault vibration analysis. The findings provide a theoretical foundation for fault diagnosis and enhance the interpretability of fault mechanisms.

title: Simulation of stationary non-Gaussian stochastic process based on phase modulation and particle swarm optimization
abstract: Stationary non-Gaussian random process simulation can provide sufficient sample data, which is crucial for engineering research. Currently, the most commonly used method is to construct a conversion function between Gaussian random processes and non-Gaussian random processes, and then simulate non-Gaussian random processes based on Gaussian random process simulation methods. However, the statistical moments of the simulation results may match the preset statistical moments, but their power spectra may not match the target power spectra, which is a major problem faced by many methods. This paper presents a novel method for simulating non-Gaussian random processes by integrating phase modulation with particle swarm optimization (PSO). The proposed approach introduces optimization algorithms into the domain of non-Gaussian process simulation. By exploiting the strong global search capability of PSO, the method enables efficient and accurate phase modulation, thereby generating non-Gaussian random processes with prescribed skewness and kurtosis. Two different non-Gaussian scenarios are considered, simulating wind speed and earthquake acceleration, respectively. The results show that the simulated samples exhibit only minor deviations in skewness and kurtosis, while their power spectrum density is highly consistent with the target spectrum.

title: A predicted methodology of dynamic behavior of harmonic reducer considering the experimental signal of comprehensive transmission error
abstract: A dynamic analysis model considering the cumulative pitch deviation of the circular spline and flexspline in harmonic reducer has been developed, capable of prediction of geometry transmission error (GTE) and torsional vibration. The GTE components of the circular spline and flexspline is established by considering multi-tooth meshing effects of the harmonic reducer. Experimental validation has been conducted to investigate the impact of the total cumulative pitch deviation and accuracy grade on the GTE. Subsequently, the GTE is treated as the primary excitation to study the torsional vibration characteristics of the harmonic reducer. A vibration test rig has been constructed to verify the analytical results. The findings indicate that the beat frequency amplitude of the GTE correlates with the difference in the amplitude of the GTE components of the circular spline and flexspline. The GTE primarily consists of even harmonics, and its amplitude in the frequency domain maps to torsional vibration. The amplitude fluctuation phenomena observed in torsional vibration are consistent with those in the GTE. Experimental results validated the theoretical simulations, confirming the accuracy of the proposed analysis approach.

title: Sensor placement for sparse force reconstruction
abstract: The present study proposes a Gram-matrix-based sensor placement strategy for sparse force reconstruction in the frequency domain. A modal decomposition of the Gram matrix reveals that its structure is dominated by a few modes near the target frequency, and that each modal contribution reflects the spatial correlation of the corresponding mode shape. This suggests that placing sensors near nodal regions where spatial correlation is low can reduce coherence in the frequency response function (FRF) matrix and improve force reconstruction accuracy. To translate the physical insight into a practical design framework, a greedy algorithm is proposed to select sensor locations that minimize the off-diagonal energy of the Gram matrix. Numerical simulations and experimental validations demonstrate that the proposed method yields robust and accurate force estimation, outperforming heuristic sensor layouts.

title: Exploring a full latent space for Gaussian process modeling with qualitative and quantitative factors
abstract: This paper proposes a new latent variable Gaussian process modeling method for problems involving both qualitative and quantitative input variables. By exploring a full-dimensional latent space where the values of qualitative variables are appropriately represented by certain normalized points therein, we generalize the concept of distance to be applicable to qualitative variables and thereby adapt the mixed qualitative-quantitative inputs to any conventional quantitative-only correlation structures. Specifically, we present distinct treatments for ordinal and nominal qualitative variables. For each ordinal qualitative variable, the corresponding values are represented by intrinsically ordered points of a one-dimensional unit latent space. For each nominal qualitative variable, the corresponding values are represented by points residing in an axis-aligned latent space, with the dimensionality equal to the number of values, and each point anchored to a separate unit axis. The coordinates of the latent points, along with other hyperparameters of the Gaussian process model, are jointly estimated via maximum likelihood estimation. An experimental study was conducted to compare four representative Gaussian process modeling methods for mixed qualitative and quantitative factor problems and the proposed method, using twelve analytical test functions from relevant literature and a dataset of cooling system noise. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated by the results. We further demonstrated how to gain insights into the qualitative factors via the proposed LVGP-Full method.

title: Dynamic feedback control method considering cross-coupling effect of PMSM for multi-DoF forming robot under transient overload
abstract: Recently, a multi-DoF forming robot (MDFR) with the maximum forming load of 8000 kN is developed, which is driven by six permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). In order to obtain the maximum output power, the PMSM works under transient overload, which will result in the overload of current. However, the magnetic fields of q-axis and d-axis of PMSM affect each other under overload of current, which results in cross-coupling effect. The traditional torque compensation control method (TCCM) combining field-oriented control (FOC) method is ineffective for MDFR under cross-coupling effect. To solve this problem, a new coupling-field-oriented control (CFOC) method is proposed to compensate cross-coupling effect. On this basis, a new dynamic feedback control method for MDFR, which combines TCCM and CFOC method, is developed. Firstly, the structure of MDFR and the principle of cross-coupling effect of PMSM are described. Then, an electrical dynamic model of PMSM considering cross-coupling effect is developed, in which the cross-coupling angle is proposed to represent the cross-coupling effect. To determine cross-coupling angle, a cross-coupling angle identification method based on virtual-rotary-axis high-frequency signal injection (VHSI) is proposed. Further, the electromechanical coupling dynamic model (ECDM) of MDFR considering cross-coupling effect is developed. On such basis, a CFOC method is proposed to decouple the dynamic equation of PMSM. Finally, a dynamic feedback control method for MDFR is developed. Compared with TCCM combining FOC method, the experimental error variance reduces 87.8% under 8000 kN forming load, showing a better performance of the proposed method under transient overload.

title: Integrated approach to robotic grinding of curved parts with macro- and micro-actuators guaranteeing high-precision force and trajectory control
abstract: Complex curved parts have high requirements of contour accuracy and surface quality. Although compliant force control can alleviate the impact of the normal positioning error of the grinding trajectory, the tracking errors in the tangential and subnormal directions of the trajectory still limit the grinding accuracy. To address this problem, this paper proposes a high-precision force and trajectory control method for integrated macro- and micro-actuators of robotic grinding. Firstly, a grinding system consisting of a robot as a macro-actuator for tracking the planned grinding trajectory and an in house developed compliant end-effector as a micro-actuator for controlling the normal contact force and compensating the tangential and subnormal positioning errors is introduced. Secondly, the robot geometric parameters are calibrated, and the robot end positioning errors considering joint axis servo error and geometric error are calculated online and decoupled into the tangential and subnormal directions of the grinding trajectory. Thirdly, to improve the normal force control and the tangential and the subnormal positioning accuracy, a generalized predictive decoupling control (GPDC) algorithm is proposed by decentralizing the objective function and feedforward decoupling the interaction between inputs and outputs. Finally, grinding experiments show that the proposed GPDC method has higher force and position control accuracy than the traditional generalized predictive control (GPC), model predictive control (MPC), and proportional-integral–differential (PID) algorithms. Moreover, the proposed method for dynamic compensation of robotic geometric and servo errors by micro-actuator has better tangential and subnormal positioning accuracy of grinding trajectory and material removal accuracy of curved parts than the pre-compensation method of robotic geometric and servo errors.

title: Hysteresis constitutive model of metal rubber based on the lay-up manufacturing method
abstract: Metal rubber is an elastic porous metal material widely applied in vibration isolation due to its excellent damping properties. However, traditional manufacturing methods often lead to non-uniform internal structures, resulting in inconsistent hysteresis properties among samples with identical structural parameters. Although structural parameters play a crucial role in determining the hysteresis properties of metal rubber, the lack of a theoretical correlation between them has hindered further optimization. In this paper, a novel lay-up manufacturing method is proposed, in which a planar lay-up is adopted to replace the traditional layer-by-layer winding of spiral metal wires, thereby improving the consistency of hysteresis properties. Based on the structural parameters of this method, a metal wire microelement model is established to obtain the normal distribution of the equivalent orientation angles and the contact behavior of the microelements. A constitutive model of metal rubber is then developed accordingly. The reliability of this model is verified through quasi-static compression experiments. Furthermore, based on the hysteresis properties predicted by the constitutive model, a dynamic model of a metal rubber vibration isolation system is established. The reliability of this dynamic model is validated through vibration isolation experiments. The constitutive model developed in this study effectively links the structural parameters of the lay-up manufacturing method with the hysteresis properties of metal rubber, providing a theoretical basis for both the optimization of hysteresis performance and the prediction of the dynamic response of metal rubber vibration isolation systems.

title: A novel variable potential energy well bistable piezoelectric rotational energy harvester
abstract: The rapid development of Internet of Things (IoT) systems has led to an increased demand for wireless sensing devices, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable power supply solutions. This paper presents a variable potential energy well bistable piezoelectric rotational energy harvester (VPEW-BPREH) as a potential solution to this challenge. The VPEW-BPREH employs centrifugal force to compress a spring, which dynamically adjusts the distance between a magnetic tip located at the free end of a cantilever beam and a fixed magnet. This mechanism modulates the potential energy barrier between the magnets, facilitating the creation of variable potential energy wells. The theoretical model of the VPEW-BPREH is developed using the extended Hamiltonian energy method. The simulation results are in good agreement with the experimental results. Experimental results indicate that the VPEW-BPREH exhibits a 1:2 internal resonance under a low-frequency rotation range, as well as a nonlinear hardening effect under high-frequency conditions. The maximum root-mean-square (RMS) output power achieved is 330.6 μW. The operational bandwidth spans from 0 to 15 Hz when the VPEW-BPREH is operating under optimal parameters. Comparative analysis with a traditional bistable piezoelectric rotational energy harvester further demonstrates that the proposed VPEW-BPREH significantly improves energy harvesting efficiency and expands the operational frequency bandwidth.

title: Investigation of an elastic boundary coupled bistable vibration energy harvester under different types of stochastic excitation
abstract: This paper investigates the stochastic dynamics of a novel bistable vibrational energy harvester with an appended elastic nonlinear boundary (BENB). The BENB system has demonstrated excellent performance for energy harvesting in the case of deterministic excitation but has not been tested under stochastic excitation. The main challenge addressed in the paper is to reveal how BENB performance is affected by a wideband or narrowband stochastic excitation, and what are the key parameters influencing BENB’s performance in such an environment. The mathematical model of BENB is experimentally verified under stochastic excitation for the first time. The harvesting performance of BENB under stochastic excitations are carried out to established a theoretical stochastic response framework to guide the design. Subsequently, the comparative study demonstrates that the output power of BENB under a white Gaussian noise excitation and the band-limited white noise excitation is 46.57% and 17.83% higher than that of a linear elastic boundary coupled system under the same excitation levels. This advantage is more evident in comparison to monostable linear system. The results reveal that BENB has a wider operational bandwidth and higher output power due to the nonlinear elastic boundary coupling effect. It provides a new in-depth perspective of the elastic boundary coupled energy harvester and offers a feasible and effective approach to improve energy harvesting performance under different types of stochastic excitation.

title: Editorial Board
Broadband and low-frequency sound absorber by a rectangular sonic black hole combined with labyrinth metasurface
abstract: Noise control with low-frequency and broadband remains a critical challenge for engineering applications. As an exceptional broadband absorber, sonic black hole (SBH) has been received much attention in recent years. However, due to the limitations of the practical manufacturing and the system damping, the low-frequency performance of the SBH is unsatisfactory. To tackle this problem, this paper integrates a labyrinth metasurface at the termination of a rectangular SBH embedding with porous materials (PLRSBH), resulting in an additional low-frequency absorption mechanism. Taking the thermal-viscous losses into consideration, a transfer matrix method (TMM) is derived for the theoretical modeling, which is validated by the finite element method (FEM) and an impedance tube experiment. The theoretical and simulated results reveal that the PLRSBH retains the broadband characteristics of the SBH while properly inheriting the low-frequency absorption of the labyrinth metasurface. Furthermore, four coupled PLRSBHs based on coplanar principle are designed to achieve ultra-broadband and low-frequency absorption, reaching α=0.8 at 201 Hz and covering the broadband above 230 Hz, corresponding to the wavelength 13.13 and 11.47 times the structural length, respectively. Complex frequency plane analysis confirms that the LM units effectively compensate for the underdamped behavior of SBH at low frequencies. This work provides a prospective approach to advance the practical application of SBH in noise control.

title: Friction torque fluctuation mechanisms in precision ball screws: A dynamic modeling approach integrating geometric imperfections and system defects
abstract: Friction torque (FT) stability serves as one of the critical determinants in achieving micron-level positioning accuracy for ball screw transmission systems. This study elucidates the fundamental mechanisms behind friction torque fluctuations (FTF) through the development of a comprehensive dynamic model integrating lead errors and installation deviations. A systematic investigation is conducted through three primary advancements: (1) Analytical derivation of nonlinear load redistribution patterns under combined imperfections, establishing the time-varying ball load characteristics; (2) Formulation of a multi-degree-of-freedom dynamic model incorporating transient contact angle evolution and load-dependent friction coupling; (3) Synergistic integration of modified Coulomb-viscous friction theory with defect-modulated load variations for torque prediction. Experimental validation shows that the maximum error is reduced from 72.2 N·mm to 20.3 N·mm compared with the NSK model, and from 34.6 N·mm to 20.3 N·mm compared with the Oh’s model. Parametric analysis further reveals that lead errors dominate fluctuation pattern of the torque, while installation misalignment predominantly affects torque with low preload. The proposed model provides a theoretical foundation for dual-objective optimization of motion accuracy and friction stability, and significantly enhances the precision in reliability assessment and service life estimation for precision transmission systems.

title: Study on thrust energy attenuation mechanism and early blockage signal identification in water jet propulsion pumps under shallow water blockage conditions based on Hilbert-Huang Transform
abstract: During operation of water jet propulsion vessels (WJPV) in shallow water regions, environmental debris can lead to intake blockages. In severe cases, this may result in issues such as equipment vibration and cavitation, thereby compromising the stability and efficiency of the system. Timely identification of blockage fault signals is crucial for enhancing system reliability and reducing energy consumption. This study developed a direct thrust measurement system for Water jet propulsion pumps (WJPP), analyzing the energy attenuation mechanisms of the thrust signal under blockage conditions and capturing the thrust energy features during the progressive blockage process. Based on the Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT), the study found that thrust energy is predominantly concentrated within the frequency ranges of 50–200 Hz and 0–15 Hz. As the blockage develops, the dominant frequency shifts from 7.21 Hz to 0.31 Hz. The low-frequency components in HHT spectrum can be used to reflect the degree of blockage, while the high-frequency components are more sensitive to the occurrence of early-stage blockage events. Based on the energy threshold and duration of high-frequency instantaneous energy deficient zones, this study captured the thrust signals characteristic of early-stage blockage. By comparing the time–frequency spectra obtained from Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and Synchro-squeezed Wavelet Transform (SWT), the accuracy of early-stage blockage signal features captured by HHT was evaluated. The HHT method demonstrated high sensitivity, and the early blockage features captured through HHT effectively identified early blockage signals in WJPP operations. The findings provide valuable references for optimizing blockage detection algorithms and fault prediction.

title: CMSE-DGNet: A cutting mechanism-guided spatial-scale enhanced domain generalization network-based method for tool wear monitoring
abstract: The unclear mechanisms behind the data distribution discrepancies of monitoring signals during equipment operation hinder the development of specific strategies for improving model generalization. Therefore, this work proposed a cutting mechanism-guided spatial-scale enhanced domain generalization network (CMSE-DGNet) based tool wear monitoring method. Specifically, a mathematical model of monitoring signals’ spatial distribution at different cutting speeds is established based on the mechanical characteristics of the tool-cutting process. Based on this, inspired by spatial transformer networks (STN), a multi-parameter-guided STN structure configuration strategy is constructed to guide the spatial consistency transformation of monitoring signal semantic structures at different cutting speeds. This approach achieves common characteristic constraints across different domains. Additionally, domain-invariant knowledge is learned through global distribution alignment and local clustering, resulting in broader discriminative representations. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are further validated on both the SWUST dataset and the engineering dataset. The proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art domain generalization approaches across different working conditions. Furthermore, its interpretability is further analyzed through visualization.

title: Identification and modeling of 3-DoF mechanism with nonlinear friction effects by combination of LuGre and neural network modeling
abstract: Many mechanical systems suffer from strong passive effects due to presence of various imperfect kinematic joints and bearings. Such effects are more crucial for free oscillation systems or vibration absorbers since their ideal design should be as friction free as possible to work properly. To be able to deal with such inconveniences, it is first necessary to describe passive effects acting to moving bodies of the mechanism. However, such forces are usually far from linear function of velocity and incorporates hysteresis, backlash, stick–slip or nonlinear functions of velocity as well as of position. Therefore, state-full friction model is needed. This paper deals with passive effects identification present in multi degrees of freedom absorber demonstrator’s kinematic joints. Such absorbers are suitable for absorbing spatially complex unwanted vibrations of robots and other complex mechanisms. For such identification purpose, the well known LuGre dynamical model of dissipative forces is firstly tested. Finally the absorber mechanism model with optimized LuGre models is extended by trained neural network improving the whole mechanism modeling in order to reach sufficient simulation corresponding to measured behavior of absorber.

title: Chaotic characteristics of pressure fluctuations and operation state recognition in S-shaped region of a pump turbine
abstract: Strong pressure fluctuations in pump-turbine S-shaped regions threaten grid stability. This study investigates vaneless space (VS) and draft tube (DT) pressure fluctuations within the S-shaped region through tests, combining time and frequency domain analysis and chaos theory. Time and frequency domain analysis reveals that the root mean square of pressure fluctuations peaks at the runaway condition in VS and DT. When the operating condition enters the S-shaped region, the probability density function evolves from unimodal to multimodal. Low-frequency broadband fluctuations increase in both regions before zero-flow. Based on the improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN) denoising and phase space reconstruction, the minimum covering sphere theory was employed to quantify the apparent characteristics of the attractor trajectory. Three chaos indicators are extracted: Correlation Dimension, Largest Lyapunov Exponent, and Kolmogorov Entropy. The results demonstrate that VS pressure fluctuations are more sensitive to operating condition transitions, with significant changes observed in the chaos indicators. Conversely, DT pressure fluctuations maintain stable high-dimensional chaos but exhibit greater sensitivity to the emergence of the runaway condition. The constructed chaos feature space effectively identifies operating condition changes and delineates instability regions, providing theoretical support for monitoring, control optimization, and fault early warning in pumped storage systems.

title: Numerical estimation of generalized frequency response functions from time series data using NARX
abstract: Generalized Frequency Response Functions (GFRF) are a higher-order analog to the well-known frequency response functions and play a central role in understanding the behavior of nonlinear systems, such as the occurrence of intermodulation. Existing probing algorithms for estimating GFRFs from input-output time series data rely on lengthy manual derivations or the use of symbolic computation for setting up harmonic balances. However, these approaches become intractable for higher-order or multi-scale systems commonly found among engineering applications as the number of intermodulation terms grows substantially. Starting from a polynomial NARX model (Nonlinear AutoRegressive model with eXogenous input) trained on input-output data, this paper presents a probing algorithm for estimating the GFRFs, in which harmonic balances are computed in a numerical manner suitable for parallel computing. The new approach constructs the harmonic balances in the frequency domain by exploiting the linearity of the Volterra system response with respect to the GFRFs. Therefore, solving for the unknown GFRF reduces to solving a linear equation involving the spectral residual constructed with respect to the unknown GFRF. This new method is verified in two examples. The first one is the well-studied Duffing oscillator. The second one, of great interest for marine hydrodynamics, is the estimation of the quadratic transfer function linking incoming waves to the low-frequency wave loading on a floating structure.

title: Nonlinear triboelectric-driven smart toolholder for self-powered sensing of milling vibration and real-time tool wear monitoring in CNC machine tools
abstract: The real-time online monitoring of machining processes in computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools is essential for ensuring manufacturing accuracy and efficiency. However, the existing sensing technology faces the dual challenges of frequency band limitation and difficult capture of weak vibration characteristics in this high-speed rotating state monitoring. This study proposes a piecewise nonlinear triboelectric vibration sensor (PN-TES) through the synergistic integration of a CNC toolholder, a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), and a nonlinear cantilever beam mechanism with collision-induced stiffness modulation. By inducing the collision extension effect of the cantilever mechanism, the characteristics of broadband vibration sensing and tool wear state are decoupled. The designed triboelectric sensor is manufactured by 3d printing lightweight structure. After being integrated with the CNC tool shank, the total mass increase of the tool shank is less than 5 % of the weight of the tool shank. This design ensures negligible influence on spindle speed fluctuations. The system monitors the vibration state of milling process in real time through the wireless transmission of triboelectric signals. Based on the calibration experiment of preset tool wear (0.1 ∼ 0.4 mm), the mapping relationship between time–frequency characteristics of electrical signals and tool wear state is established. Only a lightweight convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) model is needed to accurately identify the tool wear state, with an average classification accuracy of 99.3 % under known cutting conditions. In addition, by introducing a cutting parameter feature normalization method, a classification accuracy of 92.92 % is also achieved under unknown conditions. Provide technical support for online monitoring of CNC machine tool machining status and tool wear.

title: Micro-mechanical mode-localized tunable wide-range band-pass filter
abstract: Micro-Electromechanical Systems (MEMS) micro-resonators devices are widely used in filtering applications, operating through resonant structures to selectively allow certain frequencies to pass while blocking others. The linear and nonlinear dynamic behaviors of these micro-resonators, including internal resonance and localization mode phenomena, have been extensively explored to enhance filter performance. In this study, we present a proof-of-concept for a high-performance bandpass filter with a highly tunable wide-range bandwidth and center frequency. The proposed filter is based on an electrostatically actuated mode-localized V-shaped clamped–clamped micro resonator. By taking advantage of its high initial rise, the proposed device exhibits linear coupling (localization mode) between the first symmetric and antisymmetric modes. Moreover, under electrostatic actuation configurations, these resonance frequencies can be widely tuned to achieve the desired narrow (∼18.82 kHz) to wide (∼30.1 kHz) bandwidth passband filter. We experimentally demonstrate a significant tuning range (∼5.36 %) of the filter’s center frequency by varying the electrostatic voltages applied to the micro-resonator, along with a passband ripple of ≤2 dB. The tuning range could be further extended to (∼11.7 %) by applying higher actuation voltages. Finite element analysis is conducted to validate the behavior of the filter and to investigate the effect of the microbeam’s geometrical parameters on the device performance. It showed that for a quarter value of air–gap, the driving voltage can be reduced by 94 %. Featuring a highly tunable center frequency, adjustable bandwidth, sharp roll-off rate, low ripple, and the potential for downscaling to the nanoscale, the proposed filter presents a strong candidate for a wide range of applications in RF communication systems, including Wi-Fi, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks.

title: Development and DMP-learning-based predictive control of a shoulder-hip assistive exoskeleton for muscular augmentation
abstract: Exoskeleton robots have promising applications in industrial production, military logistics and rehabilitation training. However, existing assistive exoskeletons still have challenges in accurate motion pattern recognition and effective human-robot cooperative control. This study develops a shoulder-hip assistive exoskeleton that integrates motion perception and learning control strategies to enhance load-carrying performance. Firstly, in structural optimization, the assistive structure of exoskeleton for shoulder and hip muscular strength augment is designed based on human biomechanics and gravity compensation. And then, in motion perception and control scheme, a K-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based motion pattern recognition method is proposed for human motion intention recognition. Additionally, a trajectory learning prediction control strategy based on dynamic movement primitives (DMP) is designed, utilizing motor current feedback to optimize exoskeleton motion trajectory control. Finally, three kinds of experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of proposed exoskeleton and control strategy, including the motion pattern recognition experiment, load-handling experiment and load-transferring experiment. Experimental results indicate that the KNN-based motion pattern recognition method can achieve a recognition accuracy of 92.4%. Moreover, with the exoskeleton and DMP-learning-based trajectory prediction control strategy, the oxygen consumption of human decreases significantly, with a 21.41% reduction in the load-handling experiment and a 19.42% reduction in the load-transferring experiment.

title: A self-adaptive physics-informed neural network for real-time prediction of structural damage
abstract: Rapid prediction of structural damage states using partially available response data is essential for ensuring structural safety and enabling timely intervention. This becomes more critical for lab test structures under complex loading conditions, e.g., real-time hybrid simulation, while stiffness reduction prediction is considered as an effective index. Although deep learning methods have shown promise due to their capability to approximate complex nonlinear relationships, their generalization performance is often limited when training data includes only healthy structures. This limitation persists even with the use of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), as conventional PINN constraints are applied only during training and are insufficient to bridge distributional gaps between healthy and damaged states. To address this, we propose a novel Self-Adaptive PINN (SAPINN) framework capable of predicting structural displacement and stiffness using only measurable forces and accelerations as inputs, even when trained exclusively on undamaged structural data. In contrast to traditional PINNs, SAPINN introduces an adaptive scaling mechanism that allows efficient and accurate parameter updates during inference, significantly enhancing its generalization across damage states. Additionally, we introduce MambaCrossNet, a Mamba-enhanced neural architecture that improves the prediction accuracy on time-series data. Validation is conducted on a 1-degree-of-freedom (1-DOF) real-time hybrid simulation (RTHS) benchmark and a 4-DOF shear frame benchmark. In the 1-DOF case, SAPINN achieves a displacement prediction MAE of 0.243 mm and a stiffness error below 50 kN/m under 50 % stiffness reduction. In the 4-DOF case, with two DOFs degraded, displacement errors remain below 0.4 mm error across all DOFs, with stiffness prediction errors under 15 kN/m. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SAPINN in generalizing structural damage scenarios without requiring damage-state training data.

title: Mechanical system cross-domain diagnostics based on signal fusion and cycle consistency domain adaptation network
abstract: In actual industrial situations, the operating conditions of mechanical systems usually change over time and the inconsistency of data distributions leads to poor generalization ability of intelligent diagnosis models. Therefore, this research proposes an intelligent cross-domain diagnostic method based on signal fusion and cycle consistency domain adaptation network (SF-CCDAN) for mechanical systems under time-varying conditions. Firstly, a multi-source signal fusion strategy using the weighted information entropy is designed to enhance the richness of fault information. Subsequently, a condition-immune feature extractor is constructed with residual networks and sparse regularization techniques, which aims to extract the time-varying condition-immune fault features. Simultaneously, a cycle consistency domain adaptation network is designed for the inter-transformation of source and target domain features, aiming at enhancing the domain-invariant features. Finally, the cross-domain diagnosis of mechanical systems is realized through the collaborative training of the feature extractor with label classifier, domain discriminator, and cycle consistency network. Experimental validations of the proposed SF-CCDAN method have been carried out on two machinery datasets considering various time-varying conditions, and diagnostic accuracies of 98.38% and 98.31% are yielded respectively, which adequately demonstrate the superior domain adaptation capability and transfer diagnostic performance of the proposed SF-CCDAN method over several mainstream comparison methods.

title: Delamination characterization in thick laminated composites with tapered profile and varying-angle fibers using ultrasonic through-transmission inspection with adaptive beam focusing
abstract: Thick laminated composites with tapered profile are prone to defects such as delamination, thick resin and fiber waviness. This study proposes a modified ultrasonic through transmission method that is capable of detecting and locating delamination defects in thick laminated composites with unknown material properties or fiber orientations. To investigate the influence of mixed-type defects and ply-drop layouts on the defect detection, three types of samples with constant thickness and straight fibers, constant thickness with wavy fibers, tapered thickness (ply-drop layouts) and wavy fibers were investigated via simulations and experiments. Time reversal method was used to generate an adaptive focusing beam. A sensing network built by two phased array probes, characterized by a modified ellipse algorithm, was generated to image the position of delamination defect. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed method for delamination imaging in the three samples was evaluated in comparison with traditional B-scans. The proposed method demonstrates potentials of delamination imaging, despite the existence of multi-defects (thick resin, fiber waviness) and ply-drop layouts, and is expected to contribute to in-situ quality verification of thick laminated composite structures.

title: Physics and geometry informed neural operator network with application to acoustic scattering
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a physics and geometry informed neural operator network with application to the forward simulation of acoustic scattering. The development of geometry informed deep learning models capable of learning a solution operator for different computational domains is a problem of general importance for a variety of engineering applications. To this end, we propose a physics-informed deep operator network (DeepONet) capable of predicting the scattered pressure field for arbitrarily shaped scatterers using a geometric parameterization approach based on non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS). This approach also results in parsimonious representations of non-trivial scatterer geometries. In contrast to existing physics-based approaches that require model re-evaluation when changing the computational domains, our trained model is capable of learning solution operator that can approximate physically-consistent scattered pressure field in just a few seconds for arbitrary rigid scatterer shapes; it follows that the computational time for forward simulations can improve (i.e. be reduced) by orders of magnitude in comparison to the traditional forward solvers. In addition, this approach can evaluate the scattered pressure field without the need for labeled training data. After presenting the theoretical approach, a comprehensive numerical study is also provided to illustrate the remarkable ability of this approach to simulate the acoustic pressure fields resulting from arbitrary combinations of arbitrary scatterer geometries. These results highlight the unique generalization capability of the proposed operator learning approach.

title: The role of finite element model updating in homogeneous transfer learning for damage classification in structural health monitoring
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of employing transfer learning (TL) for structural damage classification using synthetic data generated from un-updated finite element models (FEMs). While finite element model updating (FEMU) is commonly used to align FEM outputs with experimental data, it does not fully eliminate residual discrepancies between simulated and real measurements. These discrepancies can undermine the reliability of damage classification models trained on FEM-generated data, when used to classify experimental observations. Recent studies have addressed this issue by leveraging TL to align synthetic data from updated FEMs with real measurements. However, FEMU is time-consuming, prone to ill-conditioning, and its necessity in TL-based damage classification remains unclear. Motivated by these factors, this study investigates whether synthetic data from un-updated FEM can still enable effective damage classification through the Joint Domain Adaptation (JDA) method, a form of homogeneous TL where real and simulated domains share consistent labels and features. To this end, an investigation using both numerical and experimental case studies is conducted, along with a detailed discrepancy analysis to evaluate how domain mismatch affects classification performance. The results demonstrate that the TL-based approach achieves high classification accuracy and reliable damage characterization, even without an ad-hoc FEM calibration.

title: Real-time delamination reconstruction of composite panels based on ultrasonic C-scan and deep learning-assisted TOF algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a real-time delamination reconstruction method for aircraft composite panels using the proposed deep learning-based image segmentation-assisted time of flight (TOF) algorithm. A phased array ultrasonic (PAU) C-scan device with a roller probe is utilized to collect PAU data of delamination defects in the wing composite panels of 5 aircrafts under overhaul. First, a dataset comprising over 1100 B-scan images of actual aircraft structures is established, 61 % of which exhibit delamination signals, sourced from more than 100 delamination defects on the aircraft. Second, a deep learning-based B-scan image segmentation method with pixel positional embedding (PPE) technique, and a masked time-of-flight (masked-TOF) depth modeling algorithm are proposed for real-time defect reconstruction. Finally, the performances of various network architectures with different PPE methods are evaluated in terms of accuracy and efficiency after training on the dataset. The results show a depth modeling accuracy of 0.1 mm with a real-time reconstruction speed. The proposed method provides an automated, high-precise, real-time and visualized nondestructive evaluation approach for complex composite structures in service, which provides a novel insight for NDT 4.0.

title: Research on the influence of environmental variables on the natural frequency of concrete gravity dams via mechanism analysis and data-driven models
abstract: Contemporary vibration monitoring equipment incorporates highly sensitive, low-noise sensors, enabling the implementation of continuous dynamic monitoring systems in dams. This advancement facilitates the assessment of the suitability of such systems for monitoring large structures, with the ultimate goal of identifying potential damage. Concrete dams are subjected to prolonged exposure to environmental variables, including reservoir water, temperature fluctuations, and ageing. Establishing a correlation between these environmental variables and the structural modal parameters is crucial for the application of dynamic characteristic parameters in structural health monitoring (SHM). This paper presents the development of a safety monitoring statistical model for the natural vibration frequency of concrete dams, utilizing mechanism analysis and formula derivation. Additionally, it provides a quantitative analysis of the statistical components represented by environmental variables. This study initially employs the Hankel matrix joint approximate diagonalization (HJAD) method alongside stability diagram analysis utilizing the affinity propagation (AP) clustering algorithm to identify the modal parameters of structures subjected to ambient excitation autonomously. The influence of environmental variables on the natural frequency of gravity dams was subsequently investigated through theoretical analysis, culminating in the development of a multiple linear regression (MLR) model for monitoring natural frequency safety. Finally, by integrating Shapley additive explanations (SHAPs) theory with the light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) model, an interpretable quantitative analysis of the established natural vibration frequency safety monitoring model for concrete dams is conducted. The findings from numerical simulations and monitoring data analysis indicate that the proposed model for monitoring the natural vibration frequency of concrete gravity dams has high fitting and prediction accuracy, provides both global and local model interpretability, and has significant potential for engineering applications.

title: Bionic Issus-inspired gear-driven structure with adjustable stiffness and rotational inertia properties for low-frequency vibration isolation
abstract: The Issus is an insect renowned for its exceptional jumping ability. A unique gear-like structure within its legs ensures synchronized movement during jumping while facilitating energy transfer between the limbs. Inspired by this mechanism, this paper proposes a bionic vibration isolator designed for low-frequency vibration isolation by mimicking the leg motion of Issus. The design mimics the insect’s leg motion: springs emulate muscles to provide restoring force, rods represent legs, and a gear pair replaces rotational motion between trochanters. The governing equation of the isolator is established using Lagrange’s equations. The corresponding dynamic responses are derived via the Harmonic Balance Method. Results demonstrate that the vibration isolator possesses enhanced tunability of the isolation performance for different operating conditions. The rotational inertia provided by the gear system effectively reduces the isolator’s peak frequency and peak transmissibility, enabling low-frequency vibration isolation. The nonlinear inertial damping can effectively suppress the response within the resonance region while having negligible impact on the isolation performance in the isolation region. The designed isolator exhibits excellent low-frequency vibration isolation performance, achieving a peak frequency as low as 4 Hz and peak transmissibility below 0.38 dB.

title: Cavitation state recognition of centrifugal pumps across various working conditions by Multi-Adversarial Attention Network
abstract: Cavitation is a common issue in centrifugal pumps that significantly affects operational efficiency and stability, making accurate recognition crucial for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. While deep learning-based methods have shown promising recognition results, their performance is often limited by both the difficulty in extracting cavitation features and the data distribution discrepancy caused by varying pump conditions. To address this, the Multi-Adversarial Attention Network (MAAN) is proposed to improve cavitation recognition across diverse working conditions. The MAAN leverages Time-Frequency Maps (TFMs) of cavitation noise, generated by Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), as input. A novel residual convolutional attention feature extractor with a Multi-Scale Global Hybrid Attention Module (MSG-HAM) is introduced to capture discriminative cavitation features. The MSG-HAM enhances cavitation-relevant features through multi-scale pooling and global dependency modeling. Additionally, a multi-adversarial distribution alignment module is incorporated to align joint and conditional distributions using multiple domain discriminators and the adaptive weight factor. Evaluated on a cavitation simulation experiment, the MAAN demonstrates recognition accuracy exceeding 93%, surpassing that of the comparison methods. An ablation study and additional studies further highlight the contributions of each component.

title: Discrete wavelet convolutional network with cross-contrast perturbation for single domain generalization in fault diagnosis
abstract: Single-source domain generalization for fault diagnosis aims to train on a single-condition source domain and generalize to multiple unknown target domains, drawing widespread attention. Existing methods typically generate new domain features to expand data distribution and extract domain-invariant representations, but still face key challenges: (1) It is difficult for the model to extract robust features under noisy conditions, and feature perturbation may amplify the noise components, resulting in unreliable representation results; (2) Domain expansion often relies on random perturbations without proper constraints, leading to semantic distortion of the generated features; and (3) domain invariant feature learning overemphasizes semantic alignment while overlooking instance-level learning, failing to capture fine-grained inter-instance differences. To cope with these challenges, we propose a cross-contrast perturbation single-domain generalization architecture based on discrete wavelet convolutional networks. First, learnable discrete wavelet operators are employed to extract noise-robust features. Then, cross-contrast perturbation between the main and auxiliary networks enhances feature diversity while preserving semantic consistency, thereby improving the reliability of domain extension. Instance similarity learning is further introduced to ensure consistent feature space characterization and enhance model generalization. Finally, extensive experiments were conducted on gearbox and bearing datasets to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The code will be available at: https://github.com/JC952/DWCN-SDGFD.

title: A large-stroke and adjustable-load magnetic quasi-zero stiffness isolator
abstract: Unlike traditional parallel structures that combine magnetic negative stiffness and positive stiffness, this study employs the principle of Lorentz force acting on a current-carrying coil in a uniform magnetic field to design a novel magnetic quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) isolator. The proposed isolator achieves both a wide QZS range and continuously adjustable load capacity by integrating the mechanisms of magnetic constant-force and magnetic repulsion-force, with the QZS characteristics primarily realized through the constant-force. The constant‐force mechanism includes three magnets: two stator magnets generating a uniform magnetic field, and one moving magnet acting as a current-carrying coil. A constant Lorentz force is produced by placing one end of the moving magnet in the uniform magnetic field. The stroke and load capacity of the isolator depend on the field’s spatial extent and intensity. The intensity can be adjusted by altering the overlap area of the stators. The magnetic repulsion boundary provides a hardening restoring force beyond the constant force region. Then, the effects of magnet parameters are discussed, and a dynamic model of the isolator incorporating equivalent viscous damping is established. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed QZS isolator exhibits ultra-low resonant frequencies and large stroke, and verified the theoretical results.

title: A bistable electromagnetic energy harvester with cross-ring structure for ultra-low frequency applications
abstract: Ultra-low frequency energy harvesting technology offers an effective solution for capturing weak environmental vibrations, enabling the advancement of self-powered systems. This study presents a novel bistable electromagnetic energy harvester incorporating an optimized cross-ring structure designed for ultra-low frequency vibration environments. The nonlinear restoring force of the cross-ring configuration is analytically derived using a chained beam constraint model, enabling the determination of bistable structural parameters that produce the shallowest potential wells. The dynamic response of the harvester under a harmonic base excitation is modeled, and the steady-state displacement transmissibility and output voltage are analytically obtained via the harmonic balance method. The analytical outcomes are numerically validated through the direct integration of the governing dynamic equation. Experimental investigations, including the restoring force characterization and the energy harvesting performance tests, confirm the theoretical predictions. Results demonstrate that the proposed harvester achieves a peak output voltage of 1.74 V and a power output of 2.54 mW at an ultra-low frequency of 1.172 Hz. Furthermore, numerical simulations indicate that under optimal preload mass conditions, the device can generate 3.85 V at an even lower frequency of 0.502 Hz. Compared to equivalent linear harvesters, the cross-ring energy harvester exhibits a 2.18-fold wider operational bandwidth and 7.49-fold higher power output, attributed to its enhanced nonlinear characteristics. This work establishes both a practical prototype and a theoretical foundation for efficient ultra-low frequency energy harvesting via a cross-ring structure.

title: Delamination detection and quantification in composites using co-Kriging with Lamb wave data
abstract: Delamination is a typical form of damage in laminated composites that must be detected and quantified early to prevent severe consequences, such as total structural failure. However, experimental testing to investigate this kind of damage mechanism can be expensive and, in some cases, unfeasible. The main contribution of this paper is to detect and quantify delamination damage using a cost-effective regression technique called co-Kriging, which combines two datasets of distinct natures. By leveraging a second, simpler, and more affordable co-variable, co-Kriging improves the prediction accuracy of a target variable while reducing data acquisition costs. The method integrates Lamb wave datasets from low-cost numerical simulations with experimental laminate tests. Based on a simplified plate theory model, the numerical data includes a basic delamination model to capture its influence on signal features without requiring a complex or fully detailed model. This numerical data is then integrated with experimental results from a laminate with piezoceramics used for actuation and sensing. The combined datasets are utilized to develop a surrogate model that provides more accurate predictions of the size of the delamination area. The results showcased that co-Kriging, by fusing low-cost numerical data with experimental information, significantly enhances the ability to detect and quantify early damage in composite structures.

title: Mistuning identification of blisk based on antiresonance
abstract: Differences between blades in aero-engine blisks, known as mistuning, can lead to vibration localization and amplified dynamic response, ultimately resulting in high-cycle fatigue failure. Accurate mistuning identification is essential for predicting such vibration amplification but remains challenging due to blade-disc coupling effects in conventional resonance-based methods. Most existing identification methods rely on resonance measurements, yet they cannot fully eliminate the influence of blade-disc coupling. In this work, we propose a novel antiresonance-based mistuning identification method that leverages cyclic-metamaterial wave phenomena: by treating each blade as a local resonator, its blade-alone frequency is revealed as an antiresonance. A Measurement Point Correction strategy is introduced to ensure that the antiresonant frequencies approximate the blade-alone frequencies, thereby eliminating blade-disc coupling errors. The method incorporates a detuning strategy to isolate individual sector responses, enabling accurate blade-by-blade mistuning extraction. Validated both numerically (on a Rotor37 model) and experimentally (on a 12 blades dummy blisk), the approach achieves response amplification prediction errors below 1%. The proposed method is particularly effective for lightweight blisks with strong blade-disc coupling.

title: Less Can Be More: Dictionary-driven reconstruction of full-field measurements from optimally configured sensor network
abstract: Full-field online sensing with dense spatial vibration data can improve real-time structural monitoring. However, cost and feasibility constraints often make deploying numerous sensors impractical, while sensor malfunctions can create data gaps that further impede measurement availability. To address this challenge, we propose a framework for reconstructing full-field vibration responses from sparse sensor data using dictionary learning and compressive sensing. We first collect dense measurements under controlled excitation to learn spatial basis functions that can be leveraged to characterize structural responses. This process employs dictionary learning to extract an overcomplete basis that sparsely encodes the dense data. In the reconstruction phase, the learned dictionary is combined with sparse measurements from strategically placed sensors to regenerate the full-field response through compressive sensing, which is facilitated by solving an optimization problem enforcing sparsity constraints while minimizing reconstruction errors. Since reconstruction quality depends on limited sensors, determining their optimal number and placement is critical. We formulate this as a sparse binary multi-objective optimization problem balancing reconstruction accuracy and sensor sparsity via the L0 norm. This optimization yields multiple solutions trading off accuracy and efficiency, from which the users may conduct decision making in an adaptive manner. We validate our approach on a three-story laboratory structure under various loading conditions, demonstrating high-precision reconstruction while offering flexible sensor placement strategies for practical applications. The results demonstrate that high-accuracy reconstruction can be achieved using only 6 sensors. Additionally, the burst chirp excitation effectively reconstructs harmonic responses with nearly 100% accuracy, while reconstructing burst chirp responses using harmonic excitation performs poorly due to the monotonous characteristics of harmonic excitation. The capability of the framework to reconstruct full-field responses has promising applications for inverse analysis and fault identification through analyzing changes in dynamic characteristics of the reconstructed data.

title: Experimental research on the mechanism of self-excited vibration caused by structural interfaces in magnetic levitation system
abstract: The self-excited vibration induced by structural interfaces in magnetic levitation systems significantly compromises operational stability, making elucidating its underlying mechanisms crucial for engineering applications. This study innovatively incorporates interface characteristics into the magnetic levitation dynamic analysis framework, employing a combined theoretical–experimental approach to unravel the universal mechanisms of interface-induced self-excited vibration. Firstly, an experimental platform for simulating the interface of a structure with adjustable interface parameters was proposed, and a nonlinear dynamic model of the magnetic levitation-structure interface coupling system was established. Then, the system’s critical parameters were determined using the Routh criterion, and the influence law of interface parameters on the vibration characteristics of the system was analyzed through the fourth-order Runge-Kutta numerical method. Finally, the self-excited vibration phenomenon was verified through experiments, and the evolution mechanism of self-excited vibration was revealed. The research results show that changes in structural interface parameters will trigger the migration of the system’s dominant frequency, thereby causing changes in system stability, while the interface collision process reduces the vibration amplitude through energy dissipation, prompting the system to form an amplitude self-regulation mechanism.

title: Dynamic load identification based on dual sparse dictionary learning
abstract: In order to deal with the issue of low accuracy in the identification of complex dynamic loads in the presence of measurement noise, a novel load identification method based on dual sparse dictionary learning is proposed. In order to identify the dynamic loads, discrete cosine basis functions are selected as the base dictionary for sparse representation of the complex loads. Firstly, a load identification model is established using the dual sparse dictionary learning theory, and the effect of parameter settings on the load identification accuracy during dictionary updating is investigated. Secondly, a numerical simulation is used to investigate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. Ultimately, the GARTEUR model is utilized as the experimental subject to verify the proposed load identification method. The results of the numerical simulation and experimental verification demonstrate that the load identification method based on dual sparse dictionary learning exhibits high identification accuracy and robust performance in the presence of harmonic load and superposition load.

title: Low-frequency vibration attenuation and ensemble learning-based inverse design of vibro-acoustic metamaterials
abstract: Low-frequency vibration attenuation remains a critical challenge in electric vehicles, where conventional solutions face inherent limitations of excessive mass, bulky dimensions and narrow operational bandwidth. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel monolithic locally resonant vibro-acoustic metamaterial (LRVM) featuring a dual-resonance coupling architecture. By integrating parallel cantilever-mass subsystems within a single-material resonator, the LRVM generates a synergistic continuous bandgap below 50 Hz, validated through theoretical dynamic modeling, finite element simulations and experimental tests. A performant gradient-based inverse framework is further employed to tailor geometric parameters, achieving targeted bandgap with limited datasets. Meanwhile, experimental vehicle tests demonstrate an exceeding 9 dB attenuation at the first order of parcel shelf resonance, outperforming traditional asphalt dampers of equivalent mass by over 7 dB. The cavity-free, injection-moldable Nylon PA12 design eliminates multi-component assembly dependencies while ensuring lightweight, compact and scalable manufacturability. By bridging subwavelength resonance physics with data-driven inverse design, this work establishes a paradigm for practical low-frequency vibration control, offering valuable insights into NVH optimization for electric vehicles.

title: An improved informative frequency band selection method for early fault detection of rolling element bearings
abstract: Detecting rolling element bearing (REB) fault symptoms in real-world industrial settings is quite challenging due to external noise and interference from other components, especially in the early stages of fault. Therefore, enhancing the fault symptoms is crucial in practical applications. REBs usually exhibit two key characteristics: impulsiveness and cyclostationarity. However, most traditional band selection methods, which focus on maximizing these factors, are often ineffective due to impulsive noise and cyclostationary-type signal from other components, such as gears. This limitation arises from two sources: the demodulation technique and the chosen indicator for band selection. To address this limitation, first, an improved envelope spectrum with adaptive thresholding strategy is developed to extract the most pertinent bearing fault signatures. Building on this improved demodulation approach, a novel Multi-Harmonics Energy Index (MHEI) is then introduced to quantify the fault harmonic energy relative to background noise. This index facilitates the identification of the optimal demodulation band containing the most relevant fault information. A genetic algorithm optimization with a gridline-based initial population selection scheme is employed to select this optimal band automatically. The robustness and accuracy of the proposed method are validated through experimental tests incorporating inner race, outer race, roller, and compound faults in the presence of various noise types. The results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness even under challenging conditions with significant non-related impulsive and cyclostationary noise.

title: Concurrent topology optimization for energy flow control based on the poynting vector
abstract: Controlling the energy flow within structures enables directional energy transmission, focusing, and harvesting, offering significant application potential in fields such as aerospace. However, the dynamic response of structures is inherently complex and challenging to control, posing significant difficulties in achieving effective energy flow control. In this study, we propose an energy flow control concurrent topology optimization method, which controls the energy flow within a structure under dynamic excitation through designing the microstructures and their distribution on the plate. As a physical quantity that measures the magnitude and direction of energy flow, the integral of the Poynting vector is selected as the objective function of the optimization model. By specifying the direction of energy flow, it allows for more flexibility in controlling the energy flow. Three different optimization objectives based on the Poynting vector are constructed: energy flow focusing, energy flow barrier, and energy flow circulation. To reduce the impact of local optima, random morphology description functions (RMDFs) are adopted to provide the initial guesses. Numerical examples show that the intended objectives can be successfully achieved on the optimized design, proving the effectiveness of the proposed optimization method in accurately controlling energy flow. The optimization results also show that microstructures with maximized directional stiffness and strip-like macrostructural distributions are beneficial for guiding the flow of energy. Experimental validation is also conducted, and the results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method in manipulating energy flow. The findings demonstrate significant potential for engineering applications in fields such as structural energy management and dynamic dissipation system design.

title: Threshold variational mode decomposition cascade high concentrated time–frequency analysis algorithm
abstract: To further improve the concentration performance of the time–frequency analysis (TFA) method and accurately capture the time–frequency (TF) spectral anomaly, we propose a threshold Variational Mode Decomposition cascade high concentrated TFA algorithm, termed improved Local Maximum Synchrosqueezing Generalized S transform based on threshold Variational Mode Decomposition (ILMSSGST). The LMSSGST method, combining the frequency self-adaptability of the Generalized S transform (GST) and the iteration operation of the Local Maximum Synchronosqueezing (LMSST) algorithm, achieves a TF representation with higher energy concentration. Then, the threshold variational mode decomposition (TVMD) algorithm is presented, which can adaptively select the optimal number of mode decompositions and realize signal denoising. By combining the TVMD algorithm with the LMSSGST algorithm, the anti-noise performance of the algorithm can be improved while maintaining high concentration performance. The improved ILMSSGST integrates TVMD for adaptive denoising and mode selection, with GST serving as the kernel for LMSST. The “improvement” lies in the cascade architecture that enhances both TF concentration and noise resistance, rather than modifying LMSST itself. The novel contributions include: 1) an adaptive TVMD for automatic optimal mode selection; 2) a cascade framework integrating TVMD and LMSSGST to enhance both concentration and noise resistance; and 3) multi-metric validation of TFA performance. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, the simulated signal and experimental signal of the bearing fault are tested, respectively. Experiments demonstrate that ILMSSGST achieves higher concentration improvement than state-of-the-art methods. The ILMSSGST can clearly describe the precise TF characteristics of the vibration signal, which provides an effective technical solution for anomaly detection.

title: A novel bearing fault diagnosis method based on improved product envelope spectrum Gini coefficient ratio optimization gram
abstract: The spectrum analysis-based fault diagnosis method for rolling bearings is prone to noise and interference under complex working conditions, potentially obscuring the fault signals and reducing diagnostic accuracy. This paper proposes an improved product envelope spectrum Gini coefficient ratio optimization-gram (IPESGIRgram) based on adaptive spectrum segmentation and improved product envelope spectrum (IPES). Firstly, adaptive spectrum segmentation is achieved through power spectral density (PSD) and energy distribution, where Gaussian kernel function is iteratively convolved with PSD to generate diverse spectrum segmentation forms. Then, the optimal demodulation frequency band (ODFB) is determined by maximizing the IPESGIR index and demodulated, yielding the IPES for final analysis. Compared with the three typical methods, the quantitative analysis results showed that the significance of fault features of this method increased by 88.12%, 142.12% and 71.01% respectively, and the improvement magnitudes in the performance of fault information extraction 46.46%, 47.25% and 27.91% respectively. The results demonstrate that the IPESGIRgram method can effectively suppress the noise interference and significantly improve the accuracy of signal identification.

title: Corrigendum to “Mechanism of a novel parallel ultrasonic vibration-assisted cutting system for high performance machining”. [Mech. Syst. Signal Process. 238 (2025) 113213]
Research on the calculation method of acoustic radiation of underwater double-shell structures covered by acoustic coatings and its application
abstract: This study focuses on the problem of fine design and calculation of stereo protection for double-shell underwater vehicles with multi-layer acoustic coating configurations. We have innovatively developed a mathematical-physical model for coupled dual-fluid domains to characterize underwater structural acoustic radiation with arbitrarily configured acoustic coatings. Furthermore, a computationally efficient three-dimensional (3D) vibro-acoustic (sono-elastic) coupling computational methodology has been established to achieve high-precision numerical solutions. Impedance matrix is introduced to describe the vibro-acoustic transmission between inner and outer surfaces of the acoustic coating, the boundary condition on the interface between the acoustic coating and the fluid is skillfully derived. The method is given that can solve the modal generalized hydrodynamic coefficients induced separately by the outer and inner flow fields after applying acoustic coatings in any configuration. The vibro-acoustic coupling and underwater acoustic radiation solution of the “hull structure-acoustic coating- inner and outer flow fields” can be realized. The correctness of this method is verified by numerical examples. The engineering applicability of this method is verified by the underwater acoustic radiation test of the reinforced cylindrical shell with the acoustic coatings. Furthermore, a series of examples involving a double-layer flat plate structure and two underwater vehicles demonstrate the practical value of this method in engineering applications.

title: Finite-time tracking control for the ball and beam system based on a new fast terminal decoupled sliding mode control in the presence of matched and mismatched uncertainties
abstract: This paper presents a novel decoupled sliding mode controller for finite-time position tracking in ball-and-beam systems in the presence of matched and mismatched uncertainties. The proposed controller employs two fast terminal sliding surfaces and a novel coupling variable to ensure rapid and simultaneous convergence of all sliding surfaces to zero. A new reaching law is introduced to minimize chattering while ensuring finite-time asymptotic stability. Additionally, a finite-time extended state observer is employed to estimate disturbances and system states within a finite time frame, without requiring prior knowledge of uncertainty bounds. Furthermore, the finite-time convergence stability of the closed-loop system is proved in the Lyapunov framework. The control signal design is simplified, as it requires knowledge of only a small known portion of the system dynamics rather than the entire dynamics. The proposed method is validated through simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments, demonstrating enhanced robustness, faster convergence, and significantly reduced chattering compared to existing approaches.

title: Robust partial eigenvalue assignment problem of high order control system
abstract: In this paper, we consider the partial eigenvalue assignment problem of high order control systems (PEAP) by active feedback control. The real-valued spectral decomposition of the high order symmetric matrix polynomial is characterized, and some necessary and sufficient conditions that the no spill-over property can be preserved in the closed-loop, are provided. Using the measured receptances and system matrices, a new set of parametric solutions of the PEAP in the high order control system is characterized. In practice, the active feedback control should be robust, which means that the norms of the feedback matrices and the condition number of the closed-loop eigenvectors are as small as possible. We formulate the robust PEAP as an unconstrained minimization problem and propose a gradient-based optimization algorithm. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

title: Hammerstein structure based high-precision modeling and identification of piezoelectric fast steering mirror
abstract: Research on the hysteretic-coupling between dual piezoelectric actuators under uniaxial condition and electromechanical cross-coupling under biaxial condition of the complex piezoelectric fast steering mirror (PFSM) system remains insufficiently explored, resulting in persistent challenges to achieving high-precision modeling. In this paper, a comprehensive model of the PFSM is established based on the Hammerstein structure. An improved asymmetric Bouc–Wen model is proposed to characterize the nonlinear rate-independent hysteresis, while a biaxial coupling dynamic is derived to represent the linear rate-dependent physical behavior.
