Specifically, the GLUE strategy is employed to optimize the initial iteration population and narrow the parameter value range, subsequently facilitating efficient sampling by the DREAMKZS algorithm. This combined procedure is referred to as the DREAMKZS(G) approach. Efficient full-scale updating and posterior prediction of a long-span suspension bridge is carried out utilizing measured data, assisted with the radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) model to enhance computational efficiency. Results show that the inclusion of the GLUE strategy improved the convergence efficiency of Markov chains by 71.5%. The updated FE model shows a closer alignment with the actual structure behavior, confirming the high accuracy of the proposed Bayesian updating framework. Additionally, the DREAMKZS(G) approach achieves a narrower 95% confidence interval than the original DREAMKZS algorithm, highlighting the potential of the GLUE strategy to enhance prediction precision. Finally, uncertainties arising from the RBFNN surrogate model were explicitly incorporated into the Bayesian updating process, further demonstrating the robustness of the DREAMKZS(G) approach.

title: Improved rotation-excited energy harvester based on adaptive centrifugal force weakening mechanism
abstract: Energy harvesting has emerged as a promising solution to sustainably power wireless sensor networks in rotating machinery. Although rotational kinetic energy can be effectively converted through various energy harvesting systems, the energy harvesting bandwidth and power are constrained by the negative effect of the excessive centrifugal force produced from high-speed rotation. In this paper, an adaptive centrifugal force weakening mechanism (ACFW) is proposed to suppress the strong centrifugal force and to achieve broadband energy harvesting of rotating machinery. The ACFW employs a slider pulley mechanism to generate a counteracting tension force to suppress the adverse impact brought by the centrifugal force such that the high output power can be maintained for a wide range of rotational speed. The effects of the slider mass and the position of the pulley are theoretically investigated using a constructed system dynamics model. A prototype is fabricated and experimentally tested under various rotating speed excitations. According to the results, the ACFW can effectively harvest energy in a wide rotational speed range, generating a maximum power of 1.08mW and improving the bandwidth by up to 400 % compared to the one without the ACFW mechanism. Furthermore, such a significant enhancement can be validated and explained according to the derived theoretical model, indicating that the ACFW can increase the output power and broaden the bandwidth. As evidenced by the theoretical and experimental results, the ACFW exhibits superior performance in expanding the output power bandwidth and provides a novel strategy to enhance the performance of rotational energy harvester.

title: Nonlinear steady-state characteristics of thin, highly flexible cantilever beam having higher aspect ratio
abstract: The work uses experiments and numerical computations to study the nonlinear steady-state characteristics of a very thin, highly flexible cantilever beam with a high aspect ratio. Large rigid body rotations in the strain-description play a key feature in the deformations. The classical finite element formulations have a restriction on moderate rotations and are unsuitable for modeling large rigid body rotations due to the choice of nodal coordinates as infinitesimal rotations. The beam’s large deflection nature, including the rigid body rotations, is incorporated using the gradient-deficient Absolute Nodal Coordinate Formulation beam elements with curvature terms for bending. A semi-analytical solution approach, the time variational method, is proposed for evaluating the nonlinear steady-state response in conjunction with this modeling approach. An experimental harmonic response evaluation setup for a stepped sine sweep has been developed to support the vertical configuration of the long cantilever beam. The numerical and experimental results show good agreement with each other. The gravity has a stiffening effect on the beams’ vertical downward configuration and must be included in the computations. Sub- and super-harmonics of the fundamental frequency participate in the beam responses, and internal resonances are also observed. The higher bending modes show a softening behavior, while the first mode shows a slight hardening behavior in both experiments and computations. A mode-mixing behavior is observed for the fourth mode. The Floquet multipliers are used to determine the local stability of the periodic solutions.

title: A polar coordinates-based image processing for LPBF co-axis melt pool monitoring under high background noise
abstract: In the domain of Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing, melt pool monitoring plays a crucial role in ensuring process stability and part quality. In recent years, numerous melt pool monitoring systems and image processing methods have been designed to develop defect detection and quality control systems based on melt pool geometry. However, existing image processing methods lack robustness and accuracy under high background noise and are difficult to apply for different processing conditions, leading to false alarms and incorrect feedback signals. To mitigate this issue, an image processing method was proposed following an in-depth analysis of the co-axis melt pool images. An adaptive threshold algorithm based on grayscale difference and a spatter reduction algorithm based on spatial properties were designed to eliminate noise and determine the melt pool edge. Then a feature extraction algorithm was proposed to calculate the basic geometrical features, based on the assumption that the melt pool shape is symmetric. It is able to calculate the length and width of the melt pool without prior knowledge of the scanning strategy. The performance of the image processing method was validated using two datasets collected under different processing conditions. The validation results show that the method can correctly determine the melt pool edge under high background noise and accurately calculate the width of the melt pool generated under different materials and processing strategies. The root mean square error of the melt pool width is about 1 pixel. Finally, a detailed analysis was conducted on the impact of processing strategies on process stability and the differences in background noise patterns.

title: Monitoring of sparsely observed structures by time-lagged Bayesian smoothing
abstract: Utilizing model-based strategies for structural health monitoring (SHM) parallels the methods used in system identification. By contrasting the identified system to a pre-established healthy baseline, damage can be characterized. These methods demand comprehensive models and considerable instrumentation, resulting in significant computational and financial costs. Bayesian filtering techniques provide a comprehensive model-based framework for estimating unobserved response states and structural health parameters based on available data. Nevertheless, sparse measurements due to limited instrumentation may impair the system states' observability, leading to unrealistic or non-physical solutions. Taken's theorem postulates improving state observability for sparsely observed systems via delay-embedded measurement models. With these new virtual sensors, the dimensionality of the measurement vector is enhanced, supplementing real sensors with virtual sensors built from time-delayed measurements and thereby improving the observability aspect of dynamic systems' state space. This study embeds this approach within a Bayesian filtering-based SHM framework wherein the augmented (and delayed) measurements are posed as 'temporal' virtual sensor (VS) data. This necessitates formulating an applicable measurement model for observing states via future measurements and its integration to a standard interacting particle-Kalman filter (IPKF), which has been undertaken in this study. Notably, unlike conventional (spatial) virtual sensors that rely on model-based synthesis to predict responses at unmeasured locations, the proposed VS-IPKF method leverages the actual measurements, offering higher fidelity and reliability in virtual data. This approach has been numerically validated for state and joint state-parameter estimation in cantilever beam models. An extensive study across various estimation scenarios, considering different damage levels and sensor noise, shows that the proposed method substantially improves estimation reliability and accuracy, especially when the system is sparsely instrumented. Additional experiments on a physical cantilever beam validate these results, highlighting the method's efficacy in monitoring real-world systems with sparse instrumentation

title: Conditional simulation of spatially correlated nonstationary ground motions using a physics-informed machine learning approach
abstract: Simulating spatially correlated, nonstationary ground motions at multiple support points is essential for the seismic performance assessment of extended structures. Traditional conditional simulation schemes can approximate certain features of spatially varying ground motions but often struggle to fully capture the complex nonstationary characteristics observed in real earthquakes, such as evolving frequency content and energy accumulation. On the other hand, a purely data-driven approach can model sequential dependencies but may produce physically inconsistent outputs without explicit constraints. This paper introduces a physics-informed Long Short-Term Memory network (PhyLSTM) for conditional simulation of multi-point ground motions. The PhyLSTM-based simulation embeds three key constraints into the LSTM’s loss function, including spatial coherence function, power spectral density, and normalized Husid function. These constraints ensure that the generated accelerograms reproduce the phase correlation relationship, spectral content, energy buildup, and temporal nonstationarity. The simulation framework is validated using recordings from events in the SMART-1 and Chiba arrays. Across multiple stations and seismic events, the PhyLSTM-based method outperforms conventional wavelet packet transform–based conditional simulation in capturing both spatial and temporal characteristics. To demonstrate engineering relevance, the simulated multi-support ground motions are applied to a 735 m three-span suspension bridge. Compared with uniform excitation, spatially varying inputs result in up to a 50 % increase in peak mid-span vertical displacements and pier-base bending moments. These differences are primarily attributed to coherence loss and high-frequency phase variability between supports. By integrating deep learning with physical constraints, PhyLSTM provides a robust and physically consistent framework for generating multi-point ground motion inputs applicable to extended structural systems.

title: Nonlinear vibration analysis of fluid-conveying spatial pipes treated by CLD considering the combination dependence of amplitude and frequency
abstract: To achieve vibration suppression of pipes, a combined vibration reduction scheme for arbitrary fluid-conveying spatial pipes (FCSP) with constraints from both clamps and constrained layer damping (CLD) is proposed. Initially, a hysteretic frictional mechanical model is produced to represent the nonlinear mechanical behavior at the clamp interface, characterized by amplitude dependence. By integrating the three-dimensional Timoshenko beam theory with the Lagrange equation, a semi-analytical dynamic model of the FCSP treated by CLD is established, which comprehensively accounts for the combined nonlinear effects of CLD materials and clamp constraints. This model provides a universal scheme for spatial geometric transformation and coupling of pipe substructures to accommodate the centrifugal and Coriolis force effects induced by flow-induced actions in spatial configurations. Subsequently, a frequency-domain iterative algorithm is developed to solve the nonlinear vibration response under combined dependent effects. The accuracy of the model and the effectiveness of the CLD damping capability are verified by comparing the results with FE analysis, modal testing, and experimental testing of nonlinear vibration. Finally, the effects of clamp mechanical parameters, fluid parameters, and CLD material nonlinearity on the natural characteristics and nonlinear vibration characteristics of the FCSP are analyzed. The mechanism underlying the nonlinear mechanical behavior of clamps is revealed, as well as the interrelation mechanism between the nonlinearity of clamps and CLD materials. Additionally, the contribution of CLD material to the vibration suppression performance of FCSPs is expounded. This research provides scientific guidance for subsequent optimization studies focused on vibration suppression and avoidance for complex FCSP systems.

title: Deep spiking transfer learning for rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: Transfer learning is commonly used to find domain-invariant features between different domains. However, existing models may extract redundant and distorted features, which show poor interpretability and lead to poor performance in the target domain. To address this issue, a novel model named Multi-order Statistics Matching Gated Spiking Neural Network (MSM-HGSNN) is proposed for rotating machinery fault diagnosis. To better extract features and reduce noise in signals, an interpretable feature extraction module composed of sparse wavelet convolution and gated leaky integrate-and-fire module is proposed. Furthermore, to ensure better performance in the target domain, the multi-order statistical matching measure is proposed to align features from the source domain and target domain. Compared with traditional transfer learning methods, the proposed method demonstrates better diagnostic performance on bearing and gear datasets.

title: A new fail-safe active seat suspension system using magnetorheological technology for enhanced comfort and safety
abstract: Active seat suspensions have emerged as a widely adopted solution to address the growing demand for enhanced ride safety and comfort. However, current active seat suspension systems are significantly hindered by their inability to guarantee driver safety in the event of system failures, as well as delays in the change of active force direction, which ultimately compromise the vibration reduction performance. To address these challenges, this paper develops an innovative active seat suspension system based on magnetorheological (MR) technology. The core component of this new system is an MR joint which enables the new active seat suspension to possess fail-safe characteristic that ensures driver safety in the event of an active system failure, and facilitates the system with high-frequency active force commutation without altering the rotation direction of the motor, allowing the MR joint to more quickly follow the controller’s output and thereby enhancing vibration reduction performance. The performance of the novel seat suspension was evaluated experimentally in both fail-safe mode and active vibration reduction mode, focusing on vibration attenuation and suspension travel reduction. The test results indicate that the proposed active seat suspension achieves a 36.9% vibration reduction under fail-safe mode with a sky-hook controller and 52.9% vibration reduction with an H∞ controller when comparing to the uncontrolled suspension. Even comparing to some reported active seat suspension, these experimental data still demonstrate obvious superiority in vibration reduction. Therefore, this innovative active seat suspension with MR joint has been verified that it cannot only guarantee driver safety but also significantly enhance driver comfort, overcoming the key shortcomings faced by the existing active seat suspension systems.

title: A novel embedded deep learning framework for real-time online chatter detection in robotic milling
abstract: Chatter is a common issue during robotic milling processes and significantly degrades the quality of machined workpieces. To improve productivity, online chatter detection has been widely investigated. However, the characteristics of chatter vary with robot postures and machining parameters, presenting challenges for traditional detection methods. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel lightweight deep learning framework for real-time online chatter identification in robotic milling. A multi-band feature generation method is introduced to produce robot-modal dependent time–frequency maps with irrelevant frequency bands effectively removed. The feature maps are then fed into a specially designed lightweight deep learning network, which incorporates lightweight convolution to ensure accurate and efficient chatter identification. Finally, a cost-effective online chatter detection system is established, where the proposed analysis algorithm and deep learning network are implemented and tested on a microcontroller device. This system enables signal acquisition, processing, and communication with an upper-level monitoring system. To facilitate real-time data collection and chatter detection, a sliding window strategy is employed to acquire vibration signals. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for chatter identification across various robot postures and milling parameters. The designed model shows strong generalization capabilities, with minimal parameters and computational cost. Additionally, the monitoring system exhibits remarkable real-time performance, successfully detecting chatter at its early stages.

title: Hyper-viscoelastic dynamic modeling and analysis for soft dielectric elastomer actuators
abstract: For the dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs) with high-frequency excitations and large deformations, it is full of challenges to accurately describe their continuum dynamic responses due to the viscoelastic effect and geometric nonlinearity. The absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF) possesses notable advantages in precisely depicting the rigid-body motions and large deformations of the DEAs. In this paper, a novel ANCF hyper-viscoelastic solid element for arbitrary shaped DEAs is developed, where the accuracy of predicting viscoelasticity is improved by adding more viscoelastic units to a two-part constitutive viscoelastic model. The volumetric locking problem of incompressiblematerial is effectively avoided by using high-order interpolation functions. Firstly, the homogeneous deformations of a dielectric elastomer block are predicted with the proposed model and verified with the analytical solutions. Secondly, the proposed model is proved to be applicable to the DEAs with complex shapes by studying the dynamic response of a three-dimensional torsional DEA. Subsequently, the effectiveness of the proposed model under a wide frequency range is demonstrated through the experiments and dynamic simulations of a rolled DEA. The numerical results show that the hysteresis effect and creep of the rolled DEA are predicted more precisely with the proposed model than those obtained with only one viscoelastic unit. Finally, the effect of changing geometric parameters and applying different loading voltages on the actuation properties of a rolled DEA are further analyzed. The proposed viscoelastic dynamic model can be implemented effectively in the design of a complex DEA with fast responsiveness and high deformability.

title: Reciprocal control barrier function enhanced safe deep reinforcement learning control for maglev train–guideway coupling system
abstract: Ensuring the stability and safety of the air gap between the train and its guideway plays a crucial role in the operation of a magnetic levitation (maglev) train. This article proposes a safe deep reinforcement learning (SDRL) controller for the maglev system considering the deformation of the flexible guideway. Notably, a reciprocal control barrier function (RCBF) is augmented in the reward function of the DRL to ensure safety and optimality of the controller. Additionally, a damping coefficient is incorporated into the designed RCBF to specify the trade-off between safety and optimality. The improved performance of the proposed SDRL is verified by comparing to baseline twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3), deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), RCBF incorporated DDPG, and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) incorporated DDPG algorithms. The superiority of the proposed controller is validated through a comparative analysis with a traditional proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller and a genetic algorithm tuned super twisting sliding mode controller (GA–ST–SMC) via simulations. Additionally, the robustness of the proposed controller is assessed under conditions of changing train loads, load fluctuations, external disturbances, and track irregularities. Furthermore, experiments have also been conducted to validate the control performance of the proposed RCBF–SDRL controller in comparison to the PID controller and an adaptive model predictive controller (AMPC) on a magnetic levitation system.

title: Influence of contact constitutive equations on the vibro-impact response of structures
abstract: This paper investigates how different nonlinear constitutive equations for contact affect the dynamic response of a coupled structure composed of substructures with close dynamic characteristics. A general formulation based on nonlinear dynamic substructuring in the frequency domain is developed to analyze the vibro-impact behavior of three-dimensional structures. The substructure dynamics, which account for most degrees of freedom, are solved only once. Various constitutive equations representing the microscale interactions between surfaces are incorporated into the model through closed-form nonlinear equations without resolving the whole system. Two case studies are considered: first, a numerical evaluation of two rods separated by a small gap; second, an experimental and numerical analysis of 3D solid beams with clearance subjected to harmonic base excitation. This work focuses on modeling the contact behavior between small, lightweight plastic components, such as those used in hearing aids, wearable electronics, or acoustic sensor systems, where the vibrational response is crucial for device performance. The finite element method is used for the spatial discretization of each substructure, with node pairs in the contact region connected by nonlinear elements derived from six constitutive equations from contact theories. The multi-harmonic balance method, combined with nonlinear substructuring, is employed to obtain the system’s harmonic response efficiently. Experimental measurements validate the numerical results, and updating the macro-scale parameters of each model yields good agreement with the measurement. The findings emphasize the crucial role of damping, even in vibro-impact scenarios where friction effects are minimal. Moreover, the results highlight the influence of substructure dynamics in the nonlinear regime, where sequential contact and separation occur during vibration. • Nonlinear dynamic substructuring in the frequency domain is presented for vibro-impact. • Six contact constitutive equations are compared using the multi-harmonic balance method. • Measurements and numerical predictions are in good accordance for substructures with clearance. • Kelvin-Voigt contact model performs best for vibro-impact in small plastic assemblies.

title: Intelligent diagnosis of rolling bearings under cross-domain missing data: A lightweight complex domain imputation and unsupervised time–frequency alignment approach
abstract: Fault diagnosis of rolling bearings is essential for the safety of industrial equipment. However, the generalization and accuracy of existing methods are limited by discrepancies in cross-domain data distribution and issues related to missing monitoring data. Therefore, a novel framework is proposed to tackle these challenges: For data missing issues, a high-precision, lightweight Frequency-Domain Adaptive Imputation Method (FD-AIM) is developed via a generative adversarial network (GAN). It integrates spectrum-focused Fourier transform, adaptive threshold filtering, and complex-domain linear transformation modules to reconstruct non-uniform missing data robustly. For domain adaptation challenges, a Time–Frequency Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (TF-UDA) method that incorporates Sinkhorn divergence alignment is proposed. It enhances cross-domain adaptation performance through time–frequency feature joint encoding and dynamic distribution alignment. Experimental results indicate that the FD-AIM reduces imputation errors by 10% to 20% compared to the state-of-the-art Di-Informer, evaluated on both CWRU and self-collected datasets, with only 0.608M parameters. Meanwhile, the TF-UDA achieves an average accuracy of 99.30% in complicated transfer tasks, outperforming the JAN benchmark by 2.58%, with a 90% reduction in parameters. The efficiency and robustness of the proposed framework are verified.

title: Temperature drift Identification, modeling and combined structural self- and VCR/LSTM algorithm compensation in quartz resonant accelerometer
abstract: The thermal stability of an accelerometer is vital, whether it operates independently or in conjunction with gyroscopes and magnetometers as part of an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) in autonomous driving, navigation, and satellite in-orbit applications. Various methods can enhance this stability, including optimizing the structure, redesigning the readout circuit, and employing offline modeling to compensate for temperature drift. Quartz resonant accelerometer has gained widespread popularity due to their high quality factor, repeatability, and long-term stability. However, it is highly susceptible to fluctuation in ambient temperature. In this study, temperature drift of the quartz resonant accelerometer was identified based on the frequency-temperature characteristics of the α-quartz crystal and the z-cut α-quartz resonator through theoretical analysis and simulation, and experimental validation. Then, a novel isolation structure as a structural self-compensation method was proposed to improve the thermal stability of the accelerometer to an extent, and the static and dynamic temperature drifts were modeled by experiments. Subsequently, variational mode decomposition (VMD) and Kalman filter (KF) were utilized to denoise frequency output of the accelerometer, and a novel Variable Coefficients Regression /Long Short-term Memory (VCR/LSTM) algorithm was introduced to compensate for static and dynamic temperature drifts, respectively. Other content in this study include detailed comparisons among different mode decomposition techniques, Kalman-based filters, optimization methods for VMD parameters, and compensation strategies for both static and dynamic temperature drifts using VCR, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and LSTM modeling. Results demonstrated that the scale factor and zero bias temperature coefficients compensated by VCR were less than 1.25 ppm/°C and 5 μg/°C, respectively. Additionally, the temperature repeatability compensated by LSTM was improved by more than 55 % in environments with varying temperature rates. The thermal performance of the accelerometer along with stability at constant temperature are comparable or even better than state-of-the-art counterparts.

title: An interpretable cavitation recognition method for centrifugal pumps based on multiscale convolutional neural network
abstract: Cavitation in centrifugal pumps leads to performance degradation, excessive vibration and noise, and even corrosion damage. Therefore, it is imperative to timely and accurately recognize the cavitation state to ensure efficient, quiet, and safe operation. Despite the application of various signal processing techniques and intelligent models for cavitation state recognition, challenges remain in accurately identifying distinct cavitation states and elucidating their noise characteristics. This paper proposes an interpretable cavitation state recognition method. First, to comprehensively extract the crucial information of cavitation acoustic signals and precisely recognize different cavitation states, a multiscale convolutional neural network based on time-frequency information mining and wavelet feature fusion (TF-WFMSCNN) is innovatively developed, which consists of the time-frequency attention module (TFAM), the multiscale feature extraction module (MSFEM), and the discrete wavelet transform fusion module (DWTFM). Second, to explore the acoustic characteristics of cavitation, the frequency band-based Grad-CAM (FBG-CAM) is proposed, which integrates deep and shallow activation maps to visualize cavitation characteristic frequency bands. Additionally, the cavitation state division criteria are established based on the head drop rate, experimentally validated on a transparent-casing centrifugal pump for laboratory observation, and subsequently applied to an industrial-grade centrifugal pump. Finally, experiments are conducted on these two pumps under both single-condition and variable-condition tasks to validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. The results demonstrated that TF-WFMSCNN outperformed the other seven comparison methods, with average accuracy exceeding 95 %. Meanwhile, the FBG-CAM algorithm reveals that the models are all concentrated in the range of 1–3 kHz and use this frequency band as the main recognition criterion for the different cavitation states.

title: Time-dependent structural reliability analysis: A single-loop approximate Bayesian active learning quadrature approach
abstract: Time-dependent reliability analysis allows for assessing the performance and safety of an engineering structure over its entire lifespan, accounting for inherent randomness and time-varying factors in both structural properties and external loads. However, incorporating the time dimension dramatically increases the computational complexity. To address this challenge, we propose a novel method for computationally expensive time-dependent reliability analysis, which is called ‘single-loop approximate Bayesian active learning quadrature’ (SL-ABALQ). First of all, estimation of the time-dependent failure probability is treated as a Bayesian inference problem with the help of Gaussian process regression. To avoid the intractability of exact Bayesian inference, an approximate Bayesian inference approach is instead developed. In this context, the mean of an approximate posterior failure probability is given, which can serve as a failure probability estimator. Moreover, we also derive an upper bound on the mean absolute deviation of the approximate posterior failure probability, which provides a measure of uncertainty for the failure probability estimator. Second, leveraging the estimator and its associated uncertainty measure, a novel stopping criterion is proposed to determine when the iterative learning process should terminate. Third, two new learning functions are introduced to identity the next best time instant and the sample point given the time instant. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated by five numerical examples, with comparison to several existing methods. It is shown that our method can reduce the number of performance function evaluations without compromising accuracy.

title: A novel milling force prediction method based on the AI-empowered dynamic coupling model
abstract: Real-time prediction of milling force through servo signals of Computer Numerical Control Machine Tools (CNC) is a reliable and efficient dynamic monitoring method, which has demonstrated significant engineering application value in the field of intelligent manufacturing for state perception and adaptive machining. Within this research, a novel milling force prediction method based on the AI-empowered dynamic coupling model is proposed to address the challenge of dynamically and precisely predicting milling forces using CNC servo signals as input variables. This method quantitatively describes the key nonlinear dynamic characteristics in servo system by constructing a dynamic model of the CNC feed system. Subsequently, a deep neural network is introduced as function approximation model to capture these nonlinear dynamic characteristics of the servo feed system, which are based on the physical relationships between relevant parameters. Simultaneously, the time-varying dynamic information of each part for CNC is coupled by considering these independent weighting factors, and the Meta-Transformer method is introduced to accomplish this task of time series prediction about milling force by using a recursive strategy. This study background is established through finite element simulations and workshop experiments. And these prediction effects of the X and Y feed axis milling force signals are systematically evaluated using time-domain and frequency-domain analysis methods. The results indicate that this proposed method significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy, stability, and generalization ability, while ensuring physical interpretability. Specifically, comparing with other methods, this paper achieves a maximum reduction of 99.53 % in mean squared error, and a maximum reduction of 97.84 % in the absolute value of relative error after phase reconstruction.

title: Nonlinear stochastic dynamics of NES-based energy harvesters under random excitation via DPIM
abstract: Suppression and energy harvesting from structural vibration have become increasingly important in engineering, and systems are usually subjected to random excitation. Determining their stochastic dynamic responses and first-passage reliabilities is still a challenging task. This paper proposes a new versatile framework of stochastic dynamic analysis via direct probability integral method (DPIM) for nonlinear energy sinks (NES)-based energy harvesting systems under random excitation. For the first time, the unified framework efficiently evaluates probability density functions of dynamic responses, reliabilities, and stochastic stability simultaneously despite strong nonlinearity and uncertainties, breaking through the limitations of conventional approaches that typically address these aspects separately. Two typical two-degrees-of-freedom systems are examined, i.e., one combines an NES with giant magnetostrictive material under Gaussian white noise, and the other integrates an NES and piezoelectric harvester under colored noise. Notably, this paper bridges a significant research gap by rigorously analyzing NES energy harvesting systems under colored noise excitation, which has been rarely investigated due to computational complexity. Moreover, the results by DPIM are validated against those by Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) and quasi-MCS, confirming both high accuracy and efficiency. Maximum Lyapunov exponent is utilized to analyze stochastic stability of energy harvesting systems. Parametric investigations examine how excitation intensity, damping and nonlinear stiffness affect output power, NES dissipation and dynamic reliability. It is indicated that a balance between reducing structural vibration and maximizing energy output is reached, and the proposed DPIM-based framework offers a powerful tool for engineering design of NES energy harvesters in random environments.

title: Physical knowledge embedded sparse Bayesian regression model for contour error prediction and compensation of robotic surface milling
abstract: Monitoring machining errors in curved parts is crucial for optimizing process parameters and improving machining accuracy. Robotic machining errors are affected by the coupling of multiple factors, thereby complicating the development of an accurate machining error prediction model. This study proposes a prediction model that accounts for multiple error sources to realize accurate machining contour error prediction and compensation during robotic surface milling under variable workpiece placement. First, monitored acceleration and joint angles are combined with a transfer learning algorithm to accurately predict milling force under varying working conditions. The dynamic features extracted from the cutting force are then subjected to principal component analysis, effectively reducing the feature space complexity by 67.65%. Additionally, the influence of joint servo error, attributed to cutting force perturbation, on the end-effector’s tracking accuracy is incorporated into the model, and the unsupervised globally weighted tracking errors are taken as model input features. The final feature vectors, comprising machining parameters, robot stiffness, cutting force features, and weighted tracking errors are fused, and the machining error prediction model is trained grounded on the sparse Bayesian model using the structured dictionary matrix. Owing to the sparsity of the error prediction model, its computational complexity is reduced by 68.30%. Milling experiments are conducted on curved parts derived from the characteristic surfaces of an engine casing with different workpiece placements. The results indicate that the proposed method possesses high predictive accuracy, with an overall prediction R2 value of 0.9484 across different machining scenarios. In contrast to multiple baseline models trained on the same fusion features and sparse Bayesian model trained using ablation features, the proposed method achieves notably higher prediction accuracy. Furthermore, toolpath pre-compensation based on the machining error prediction model leads to substantial improvements in machining accuracy, reducing the peak, mean and standard deviation values of the contour error by 66.09%, 67.80% and 65.17%, respectively.

title: Development of an efficient, novel hybrid flutter-based wind energy harvester and identification of its delay characteristics and hysteretic behavior—Part Ⅰ: Design idea and experiments
abstract: The first of two parts, this paper presents the design and experimental evaluation of a novel, efficient hybrid flutter-based wind energy harvester. The proposed system simultaneously harnesses both the plunging and pitching motions of an airfoil and utilizes two types of energy transducers—piezoelectric and electromagnetic—to achieve enhanced energy-conversion efficiency. Through a systematic design process, including preliminary experiments, numerical simulations, and full-scale wind-tunnel testing, the optimal configuration and key parameters of the system are determined. To understand the system’s complex dynamic behavior under realistic operating conditions, particularly the observed hysteresis and jump phenomena, we perform computational fluid dynamics simulations. These simulations elucidate the unsteady flow field around the oscillating airfoil, revealing the importance of time-resolved flow characteristics in analyzing nonlinear responses. Accordingly, various system parameters are experimentally optimized in a systematic and rigorous manner. With the optimal configuration, the proposed harvester achieves average output powers of 2.41 mW and 4.36 mW from the plunging and pitching motions, respectively, under a wind velocity of 10 m/s, thereby delivering a total output power of 6.77 mW. These results confirm the system’s high efficiency and outstanding energy-harvesting performance compared with conventional flutter-based harvesters. Moreover, the findings from this part of the study provide critical empirical support for the mathematical modeling, analysis, and numerical simulations presented in the Part Ⅱ paper, thereby establishing a strong foundation for further understanding and optimizing the proposed hybrid wind energy–harvesting system.

title: Array-based ultrasonic characterization and mixed-modal TFM imaging of transversely isotropic materials
abstract: This paper presents a novel array-based ultrasonic testing method for transversely isotropic materials (TIMs), including optimized stiffness matrix measurement and mixed-modal total focusing method (TFM) imaging. The method improves the stiffness matrix measurement by introducing advanced wave extraction techniques based on the Apex-Shifted Radon Transform (ASRT), taking into account the propagation effects of the surface-skimming longitudinal wave and Rayleigh wave. In addition, based on wave propagation theory, the quasi-shear-vertical(qSV) wave is decoupled into three sub-waves to achieve time-of-flight(TOF) calculations for mixed-mode waves, thereby maximizing the consideration of wave-mode conversion combinations in TFM imaging. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by simulation and experiment, showing that the related error in stiffness matrix measurement is 2.54% when the selected curve is set as qSV3-qSV3 in the simulation, and that mixed-modal TFM imaging successfully detects and characterizes defects that are difficult to visualize using conventional methods with the single quasi-longitudinal (qL) mode. The method demonstrates potential for adaptive imaging applications in TIM with unknown elastic stiffness matrix, suggesting broad industrial application prospects.

title: Data-driven structural response prediction with limited RTHS data via a hybrid physics-aware GNN-Transformer framework
abstract: Accurate time-history response prediction is critical for evaluating structural performance, particularly in probabilistic performance-based earthquake engineering. While experimental data offer higher fidelity than phenomenological finite element models, large-scale testing is often cost-prohibitive. This study presents a hybrid training framework that leverages limited real-time hybrid simulation (RTHS) data alongside extensive low-fidelity (LF) simulations to train a physics-aware, data-driven neural network. A novel graph neural network (GNN)-Transformer fusion model is proposed, integrating structural topology through GNNs and capturing temporal dependencies via Transformer. This architecture effectively models spatial characteristics and time-varying seismic effects. The framework is validated on a two-story steel moment-resisting frame with self-centering viscous dampers (SC-VDs), under varying structural properties and ground motions. Results show that incorporating limited experimental data substantially improves prediction accuracy, enhances generalization, and embeds physical realism into data-driven structural response analysis.

title: Cavitation detection for water hydraulic axial piston pump based on physics-informed CNN data augmentation and XGBoost
abstract: As a core component of water hydraulic systems, water hydraulic axial piston pump (WHAPP) has been extensively applied in ocean engineering equipment, nuclear power plant cooling systems, food processing equipment, pharmaceutical manufacturing installations, and high-pressure industrial cleaning apparatuses. Compared with hydraulic oil, water’s relatively high vapor pressure leads to more pronounced flow velocity and pressure fluctuations, which significantly elevates cavitation risks, therefore induces component erosion, undesirable noise and vibration. To address the small-sample challenge in WHAPP cavitation detection, this study proposes a novel cavitation detection framework based on physics-informed data augmentation integrated with convolutional neural network (CNN) models. Firstly, through systematic analysis of cavitation mechanisms and CFD simulations, a three-stage cavitation classification system for WHAPP was established. Secondly, to overcome the experimental data scarcity, a CNN-based data augmentation methodology was developed for cavitation feature enrichment. By integrating numerical simulation data with generated data, a hybrid cavitation detection method was formulated. Finally, systematic validation using eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifiers demonstrated the accuracy improvement. This research provides an innovative data augmentation method for small sample cavitation detection in WHAPP.

title: Low-frequency energy harvesting from a nonlinear magnet-assisted bistable dielectric elastomer generator
abstract: Dielectric elastomer generators (DEG) have shown its particular and significant advantages in energy harvesting from environmental vibrations. Building on existing mechanical features of circular dielectric elastomer membranes (DEM), this paper proposes a magnet-assisted bistable dielectric elastomer generator (MBDEG) for high-performance low-frequency vibration energy harvesting. The dynamical model of the MBDEG is established first by using the Euler-Lagrange equations. The bistability of MBDEG is achieved by synergistically coupling the DEM’s inherent restoring force with nonlinear magnetic forces, where the nonlinear magnetic force interactions between magnets are analytically derived using the magnetizing current method. The electrical model of the MBDEG is then established to reveal the electrostatic energy harvesting mechanism. Subsequently, the unknown parameters of the theoretical models are identified through dynamical and electrical experiments, and the accuracy of the theoretical analyses is fully validated. Additionally, the influences of excitation and structural parameters on the MBDEG’s potential field, dynamical responses, and energy harvesting performance are studied through numerical simulations. It is found that the MBDEG significantly enhances the low-frequency vibration energy harvesting capabilities and broadens the operational frequency bandwidth. This study provides a possible approach to design a magnetic-assisted bistable system, and builds the theoretical bases for optimizing system parameters to boost the low-frequency vibration energy harvesting performance of the MBDEG.

title: A frequency diverse array (FDA) of dispersive lamb waves for grating lobes suppression
abstract: Governed by the spatial sampling theory, the element spacing of a phased array for damage imaging shall preferably be smaller than half the wavelength of the excitation signal. Otherwise, the grating lobes emerge, resulting in pseudo damage in the constructed damage images. The prevailing methods for grating lobe suppression often exhibit downgraded effectiveness when applied to dispersive Lamb waves. Drawing inspiration from the Frequency Diverse Array (FDA) technique, which originates from radar target detection, an FDA-based damage detection approach has been developed, which utilizes a specially designed zigzag frequency vector to address the challenges. Previous studies have demonstrated that multiple adjacent damage, which cannot be separated by conventional phased array, can be effectively identified by the FDA using Lamb waves. This is attributed to the ability of FDA to adjust the size of the focusing area (i.e., the in-phase gain area) by incorporating array signals of diverse frequencies. Similarly, the grating lobes, which result from the accidental in-phase gain of phased array signals, can be suppressed by the FDA. This is achieved by disrupting the in-phase gain through the introduction of signals with varying frequencies. By redesigning the anti-dispersive excitation with different frequencies, the dispersion compensation for Lamb waves and the frequency control of FDA can be integrated into a single step for damage imaging. The focusing capabilities of ordinary phased array and FDA are compared under various excitations and parameters. The ability of multiple damage identification and grating lobe suppression of FDA has been experimentally validated by characterizing damage under seven kinds of cases.

title: Broadband energy harvesting from high-speed railway bridge vibrations using piezoelectric energy harvester arrays
abstract: Energy harvesting from bridge vibrations has emerged as a promising approach to powering wireless sensors for structural health monitoring (SHM). The principles guiding the design of broadband piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) arrays for railway box-girder bridges and their performance under different high-speed train loadings remain largely unexplored. Addressing this gap, this study conducts in situ vibration measurements on a simply supported railway box-girder bridge during repeated passages of two types of high-speed trains. The measured signals are analyzed to identify train-specific dominant frequency bands, forming the basis for the theoretical design of two broadband PEH arrays. These designs are experimentally validated, and their energy harvesting performance is evaluated under varying electrical connection configurations. Results reveal that dominant bridge vibration frequencies lie within 25–70 Hz, comprising several sub-bands of 1.5–2.5 Hz, with marked variations between train types. These variations underscore the need for customized PEH array designs tailored to specific operational conditions. Electrical connection configuration strongly influenced harvesting efficiency, with independent operation of each PEH yielding the best performance. Under this configuration, the first array achieved 2.79 mJ per train crossing, about double that of the other three connections, and the second array produced 2.58 mJ. The findings establish practical design principles for broadband PEH arrays in bridge applications and provide guidance for integrating self-powered sensing into structural health monitoring systems.

title: Dynamic analysis of the lateral-torsional coupled vibration of a bolted joint rotor system considering the varying contact state at mating interface
abstract: As one of the most used types of mechanical connections, bolted joints are extensively employed in large-scale rotating machinery to fasten multiple components into an integrated structure. During normal operation, the mating interfaces exhibit complex multi-scale contact mechanical behavior, which can lead to intricate lateral-torsional coupling vibrations. This study develops a numerical model within the Iwan framework to capture the time-varying contact behavior at rough bolted interfaces. The model parameters are identified from load-displacement curves obtained via quasi-static finite element simulations, enabling accurate representation of nonlinear interface behavior under different preload conditions. After integrating this model into a lumped-mass rotor system, the effects of preload and eccentricity on coupled lateral-torsional dynamics are analyzed. Results demonstrate that higher preload suppresses vibration magnitude and raises the critical speed, whereas increased eccentricity amplifies interfacial sliding, augments friction-induced energy loss, and slightly weakens the equivalent stiffness. The developed modeling approach provides new insights into how interfacial slip and stiffness softening influence critical speeds, vibration amplitudes, and coupling mechanisms in practical rotor systems.

title: A simulation-enhanced deep learning framework for bearing fault diagnosis using an improved bearing force model
abstract: Timely detection of bearing defects is crucial, especially in industrial applications, where identifying a defect before it propagates can prevent financial losses or injury. Vibration measurements contain adequate information on the integrity of such components and are thus used in many condition monitoring applications which utilize traditional as well as novel damage detection methods, such as machine or deep learning algorithms. While powerful, these fault diagnosis methods are entirely dependent on the availability of training data, which can be scarce or inexistent, due to the prohibitive costs of data acquisition or inaccessibility of a structure. To address this challenge, this work proposes a novel condition monitoring framework which utilizes simulation data to train deep learning algorithms for bearing fault classification. First, high-fidelity labeled data is generated through simulations of multibody dynamics models that utilize an improved rolling element bearing model which facilitates the simulation of defects in the races of a bearing. An intelligent condition monitoring framework is then established using an ensemble of autoencoders and convolutional neural networks which are trained using this simulation data. The proposed modeling and condition monitoring methodology is validated on two experimental systems of different complexities, validating the robustness of the bearing model and the generalization capabilities of the condition monitoring method. This work aims to provide an efficient and robust condition monitoring method which can utilize simulation data for training, mitigating the issues emanating from the lack of physical measurements, thus allowing for accurate health state classification in real-world mechanical systems.

title: In-situ porosity monitoring in laser powder bed fusion through acoustic signal and interpretable multi-sensor fusion
abstract: Porosity is a harmful defect in alloys produced by the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process. Acoustic signals from the laser-material interaction can capture complex events such as pore formation. However, the defect-signal correlation mechanism and porosity monitoring in complex LPBF processes influenced by non-laser energy parameters have received limited attention. Existing research rarely considers the potential impact of sensor configuration on monitoring, and it lacks interpretable acoustic signal processing methods and multi-sensor fusion monitoring approaches. This paper proposed an interpretable multi-sensor acoustic monitoring framework. First, a multi-source acoustic monitoring system was developed, tailored to the LPBF acoustic characteristics. The complementarity and effectiveness of 20 kHz-40 kHz resonant multi-sensor monitoring were validated from signal and model perspectives. Next, the physics-informed frequency-scale texture image method was proposed to enhance the expression of acoustic defect features. Finally, an interpretable multi-sensor fusion model was established for in-situ porosity monitoring in the LPBF process. It embedded prior knowledge of sensor performance and acoustic defect features. Results show the method achieves 99.22 % accuracy in identifying LPBF porosity defects with eight different quantization labels. Visualization and interpretability analysis confirm that the model achieves reliable multi-sensor fusion and extracts the physically reasonable global or local key spectrum features from the acoustic signals. With a monitoring response time of 1.69 ms and interpretable multi-sensor fusion monitoring capabilities, this method offers significant potential for industrial deployment.

title: An end-to-end modeling and source separation solution for vibration signal analysis
abstract: Vibration analysis is a common tool for rotating (mechanical) system condition monitoring. The vibration is generated by the meshing excitation responses transmitted through a path from the excitation source to the sensor point. The desired health state information in vibration measurements is often modified by transfer function effects. In this paper, an end-to-end solution based on neural network (NN) with symbolic layers is proposed to identify a mathematical expression that describes the interactions (multi-modulation) between the force excitation responses and the rotating (gears) elements, taking into account the transmission path. Our NN architecture consists of three parts. Given the gearbox kinematic model and gear input speed, we estimate the excitation response and the source signals related to the gears. These signals feed into the second part, a so-called equation learner, which seeks a concise expression to fit the modulation sidebands of the vibration signal’s power spectrum. This signal is then passed through a convolutional layer to compensate for the transmission path and reconstruct the vibration signal. The end-to-end differentiable feedforward network is trained with sparsity regularization, which promotes an interpretable and concise expression for the vibration measurement and selects active harmonics of the elementary sources. Moreover, the input source signals are separated, and the convolution layer estimates the transfer function of the system. The proposed method is validated with simulated and experimental data from a test bench.

title: Effective generation of shear horizontal waves from Lamb waves by meta-converters
abstract: Shear horizontal (SH) waves in thin-walled structures exhibit many advantages that are conducive to structural health monitoring (SHM) applications. However, their effective excitation is challenging in practice due to the inefficiency of shear-type piezoelectric transducers or the installation inconvenience of electromagnetic transducers. In this study, embracing the concept of metamaterials, we propose an SH wave generation scheme based on the mode conversion from Lamb waves activated by piezoelectric transducers. To this end, a metamaterial-mediated converter (referred to as a meta-converter), mounted on the surface of a host structure, is designed to achieve high-efficiency energy conversion from Lamb waves to SH waves. Targeting different Lamb wave modes in specific frequency bands, a topology optimization approach is developed to design the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of the meta-converters. The efficiency of the conversion is further evaluated in terms of the magnitude of the converted SH waves with respect to the incident Lamb waves. Analyses of band structures and mode shapes elucidate the mechanisms of the mode conversion within the targeted frequency band. Time-domain responses are analyzed to verify the efficient generation of SH waves, which are further illustrated by the visualizations of wave fields and wavenumber-frequency Fourier transform spectra. The robustness of the designed meta-converters is evaluated by examining piezoelectric transducers of different sizes. Finally, representative meta-converters are 3D-printed using the selective laser melting technique and tested for validation. The proposed method offers an alternative and feasible route for SH wave generation and paves a novel way for further SH-wave-based SHM applications.

title: Seismic performance evaluation of isolated liquid storage tanks with passive variable damping and stiffness devices
abstract: Liquid storage tank (LST), as critical infrastructure in the petrochemical industry, is highly vulnerable to earthquake-induced damage, which may trigger secondary hazards such as fires and explosions. Seismic isolation has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to mitigate seismic impacts on LSTs. To achieve effective vibration control while preventing isolation system failure due to excessive displacement, a novel passive variable damping and stiffness device (PVDSD) was proposed. Performance testing verifies that the PVDSD delivers real-time variable damping forces responsive to velocity and provides stepwise stiffness activation upon excessive displacement within the isolation layer. Subsequently, the numerical model of PVDSD was developed and validated against test results. Integrated with lead-rubber bearings (LRBs), a new seismic isolation system was formulated and benchmarked against alternative isolation configurations under seismic excitations spanning four hazard levels. Five key engineering demand parameters (EDPs) including the isolation layer displacement, base shear, overturning moment, sloshing height and hydrodynamic force are evaluated and compared. Results demonstrate that the PVDSD isolation system exhibits a superior performance on energy dissipation under design-based earthquakes and effectively mitigates residual displacements under maximum considered and rare earthquake scenarios. Although marginal increases in base shear and sloshing height are observed, these remain significantly lower than those in non-isolated systems. In general, the PVDSD isolation system substantially enhances the seismic resilience of LSTs by providing robust energy dissipation ability at low- and middle-intensity earthquakes and improved overturning resistance at high-intensity.

title: Coupled dynamic characteristics of electric drivetrain system under vehicle-mounted environment
abstract: The electric drivetrain system, mounted directly on the drive axle near road excitation sources, experiences significant external loads, leading to complex dynamic behavior. This study establishes a coupled drivetrain system dynamic model under vehicle-mounted environment considering the vehicle vibration aroused by random road excitation and the equivalent time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) under Elastohydrodynamic lubrication conditions. Meanwhile, to improve the computational efficiency under various operating conditions, a prediction model for the equivalent TVMS based on neural network is developed and integrated. The coupled dynamic model is analyzed against conventional electric drivetrain system and further is validated through real vehicle testing. The vibration characteristics of the system under varying operating conditions, road excitation profiles, gear mesh stiffness and damping, and bearing support stiffness and damping are then studied. Finally, a multi-objective intelligent optimization method based on a meta-heuristic algorithm for collaborative optimization of drivetrain and vehicle vibrations is established, and the vibrations before and after optimization are analyzed. The results demonstrate that neglecting the vehicle-mounted environment will lead to the significant lack of low-frequency response of drivetrain system; operating conditions and system parameters induce highly nonlinear interactions, rendering simple linear analysis ineffective for achieving global vibration control; the developed metaheuristic optimization method effectively coordinates the coupled system vibration suppression.

title: Full-probabilistic reconstruction of unobserved system states under partial observations: A decoupled density evolution perspective
abstract: Accurate probabilistic characterization of unobserved responses in high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems remains a critical challenge due to sensing limitations, modeling complexity, and limited prior information. In this paper, a novel framework for full-probabilistic information reconstruction of unobservable system states is proposed based on partial observations of measurable responses. Unlike traditional methods that provide deterministic estimates or error bounds, the proposed approach directly reconstructs the conditional probability distribution of unobserved responses, providing engineers with a full-probabilistic interpretation of hidden system behavior under uncertainty. The framework is built upon three key elements: (i) a deterministic computational model capturing the system dynamics; (ii) an initial probabilistic description of the uncertainty sources; and (iii) monitoring data of observable responses. These components provide a basis for consistent probabilistic inference under both epistemic and aleatory uncertainties. By adapting the decoupled multi-probabilistic density evolution method (M-PDEM), the approach mitigates the curse of dimensionality by reducing the inference task to solving a one-dimensional generalized density evolution equation (GDEE), regardless of the system complexity or dimensionality. Through numerical examples featuring strong nonlinearity (e.g., hysteresis), non-Gaussian responses, and nonstationary excitation, the method demonstrates high accuracy and substantial computational efficiency relative to Monte Carlo simulations (MCS) and analytical benchmarks. This work establishes a pathway for reconstructing hidden probabilistic information from partial system observations, and for updating engineers’ understanding of complex dynamical systems under uncertainty.

title: Vibration signal analytical models and signature analysis for harmonic drive fault diagnosis
abstract: Harmonic drives involve rigid-flexible body coupling and multiple point contact excitations. This leads to highly complex dynamics, and therefore poses a tremendous challenge to harmonic drive fault diagnosis. To address this issue, it is essential to thoroughly understand the vibration characteristics of harmonic drives. To this end, the explicit equations of fault characteristic frequencies are derived. Furthermore, fault vibration signal analytical models are derived, considering the multiple modulation nature: (1) amplitude modulation and frequency modulation due to circular spline or flexspline fault; (2) extra amplitude modulations caused by time-varying vibration transfer path and time-varying angle between meshing force and vibration sensor measurement axis; and (3) the asymmetry of two meshing zones and resultant vibration superposition. Based on the proposed analytical models, the explicit equations of Fourier spectrum, amplitude demodulation spectrum and frequency demodulation spectrum are further derived, and thereby the spectral characteristics of harmonic drive fault vibrations are discovered analytically. The theoretical derivations are illustrated and validated by numerical simulation and lab experiments. The localized faults on both circular spline and flexspline are all successfully diagnosed.

title: Suppression of shock vibration by cellular nonlinear energy sinks
abstract: Research on nonlinear energy sinks (NESs) typically focuses on vibration suppression under periodic excitations. The influence of NES contact mode on the vibration control performance under shock excitation is studied through theoretical calculation, optimization and experimental verification in this paper. A method for evaluating the vibration control performance under shock excitation is proposed. Firstly, the mechanical model of shock excitation of the linear oscillator coupled with indirect contact NES cells is established. Numerical results show that the vibration control performance of indirect contact NES cells under shock excitation is affected by the natural frequency and excitation intensity. In addition, the additional mass and the layout of the NES will also affect the vibration control performance. The contact damping and contact stiffness under different working conditions can be optimized using the differential evolution algorithm. The experimental results verified the theoretical calculation results. In conclusion, the indirect contact NES cells have excellent vibration control performance under shock excitation with high natural frequency and large initial velocity. This paper provides new ideas for vibration control of shock excitation and evaluation of vibration control performance.

title: Deep clustering of rotating machinery faults based on cross-domain information guidance
abstract: Unsupervised clustering methods are becoming increasingly important in the field of fault diagnosis; however, existing deep clustering methods suffer from poor interpretability, unstable clustering performance, and training difficulties. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a deep clustering method for the diagnosis of rotating machinery faults. Firstly, an adaptive wavelet convolution neural network is proposed, which enables the model to capture high-quality, physically meaningful fault features by combining a wavelet convolution kernel that can change its size with frequency with a cross-dimensional attention module. Second, the use of source domain classification loss instead of traditional reconstruction loss guides the model to capture more discriminative fault features and improves the clustering performance of the model in the target domain. Finally, a deep clustering training strategy using offline clustering results to initialize the parameters of the online clustering model is proposed to improve the training stability of the model. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the motor fault dataset and the bearing fault dataset.

title: Design and characterization of a magnetically-coupled excitation-direction-switching piezoelectric vibration energy harvester
abstract: Energy harvesting from vibration environments has been considered as an alternative solution to replace conventional electrochemical batteries because of their limited lifespan, periodical replacement and environmental pollution. To improve the environmental adaptability of existing piezoelectric vibration energy harvesters (PVEHs), this paper proposes a magnetically-coupled excitation-direction-switching piezoelectric vibration energy harvester (ME-PVEH). It is promising to enable excitation-direction-switching between two components by magnetically-coupling, thereby enhancing environmental adaptability of PVEHs. Through theoretical analysis and experiments, the frequency response properties of ME-PVEH were investigated. Experimental results showed that there were two resonant frequencies to maximize the output voltage. Both the resonant frequency and output voltage could be modified by adjusting stiffness of spring and proof mass of the system. The maximum power of 1.82 mW was achieved at an excitation frequency of 15 Hz and an optimal load resistance of 160 kΩ. Moreover, the ME-PVEH could successfully illuminate up to 60 LEDs, power a wireless transmitter module and charge a capacitor via the excitation of the bicycle and electrical bike. It further demonstrates the potential applications of ME-PVEH in practice. This work confirmed the potential of the ME-PVEH as a robust and available micro power source for low-power electric devices in realistic vibration scenarios.

title: CITDG: A causality and information-theory inspired domain generalization method for machine remaining useful life prediction in unseen domains
abstract: Domain generalization (DG)-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction aims to train predictive models solely on multiple observed source domains while ensuring robust generalization to unseen target domains. Existing DG methods predominantly focus on extracting domain-invariant features to enhance model transferability. However, they often overlook domain-specific label-relevant cues that can be critical for cross-domain generalization. Additionally, relying on statistical correlations for invariant representation learning can lead to the inclusion of spurious, label-irrelevant features, ultimately impairing performance in previously unseen operating conditions. To address these challenges, a causality and information-theory inspired domain generalization (CITDG) method is proposed. Specifically, CITDG employs a learnable binary mask to explicitly disentangle latent representations into label-relevant causal features and label-irrelevant non-causal features. To guarantee the sufficiency of information captured in each part, an information-theoretic causal sufficiency loss is introduced. Furthermore, a causal intervention purification module is proposed to remove domain-invariant label-irrelevant redundancy from the causal subspace while redirecting domain-specific label-relevant information into the causal features, mitigating potential competition or redundancy between causal and non-causal representations. To enhance the degradation characterization ability and generalizability of causal features, a causal feature factorization and alignment module is designed to enforce joint independence across the causal feature dimensions and align causal representations of the same subdomain across different source domains. Extensive experiments conducted on one real-world industrial dataset and two publicly available datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the CITDG.

title: Multi-bandwidth fusion based damage imaging using ultrasonic zero-frequency waves
abstract: When primary ultrasonic pulse waves propagate in solid media, a wave component with a carrier frequency of zero (referred to as zero-frequency wave), also known as the quasi-static component, will generate because of material nonlinearity. Due to its carrier frequency being zero, zero-frequency wave has the ability to propagate a long distance in highly attenuative materials. Therefore, zero-frequency wave has been utilized to locate defects in highly attenuative materials. Imaging methods relying exclusively on single-bandwidth response signals exhibit inherent limitations due to the wavelength-dependent scattering interactions between ultrasonic waves and defects, where the restricted bandwidth inherently constrains the obtainable defect information and characterization accuracy. A novel multi-bandwidth fusion imaging method for defect localization in highly attenuative materials is proposed, which combines synthetic aperture focusing technique and multi-bandwidth zero-frequency waves. The pixel values of reconstructed images obtained from several zero-frequency waves with different bandwidths are fused. Numerical simulations and experiments on silicone rubber blocks are carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results indicate that compared with single-bandwidth zero-frequency waves imaging method, the proposed multi-bandwidth fusion method through mixed mean technique is able to provide better resolution and significantly suppress the background noise and sidelobe magnitude.

title: Bayesian model updating and nonlinear response estimation of structures subjected to unknown loads via FE-aided Kalman Filtering
abstract: This paper proposes a novel methodology for updating the parameters and estimating the full response of a nonlinear structural system subjected to unknown loads and with sparsely measured responses. The proposed methodology is based on the combination of an FE-aided Kalman Filter framework for nonlinear joint input-state estimation with a Bayesian model updating. A new explicit formulation of the Newmark-beta method in state space form is introduced for the joint input-state estimation in the Kalman Filter-based estimation, which avoids the need for an invertible mass matrix and the computation of the matrix exponential. The unknown parameters are updated on the basis of the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate combined with Laplace's approximation to obtain a probability distribution. The optimization problem to find the MAP estimate is performed by means of a surrogate-based optimization. The methodology is illustrated through a numerical example consisting of a 2D steel frame subjected to a strong ground motion and responding in the nonlinear regime. The obtained results are compared with a state-of-the-art method, showing a clear superiority in terms of computational efficiency and equally accurate results.

title: Out-of-distribution fault detection in multi-sensor systems using spatio-temporal dynamic graph neural networks
abstract: Mechanical equipment fault diagnosis often faces the challenge of detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) faults that differ from known failure patterns. Traditional methods, due to their reliance on predefined structures and static modeling approaches, struggle to adapt to unseen faults. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a spatio-temporal dynamic graph neural network architecture for multi-sensor data fusion, called STDG-AS. The framework employs a temporal subgraph partitioning strategy with learnable embedding matrices to enable dynamic adjacency relationships, thereby effectively modeling spatio-temporal correlations. At the network level, a spatio-temporal gated aggregation mechanism is introduced. This mechanism regulates information propagation across time steps through gating units, capturing dependencies between consecutive subgraphs. Furthermore, an edge attention-based adaptive propagation algorithm dynamically adjusts edge weights based on node feature similarity. Coupled with feature smoothing regularization constraints, these innovations significantly enhance the model’s sensitivity to OOD data. Experimental results on a diesel generator set dataset from an Antarctic simulation cabin and a public bearing fault dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. It can accurately recognize known fault types and successfully detect novel faults. Significantly, under diverse conditions, the average OOD detection rates across the two datasets reach 90.08% and 98.70%, respectively. These results strongly demonstrate the robustness of the STDG-AS architecture in mechanical equipment fault diagnosis, particularly in handling OOD faults.

title: Intelligent tire force estimation with dynamic domain adaptation for varying wear states
abstract: This work introduces a comprehensive framework for reliable tire–force estimation under real-world wear conditions, combining a newly assembled wireless acceleration dataset with a dynamic domain-adaptation model. The dataset, collected across multiple wear depths and load levels under longitudinal free rolling conditions, does not consider slip, cornering, or tire-pressure variations. It reveals systematic shifts in signal distributions induced by progressive abrasion. To address these distributional changes, we design a feature-alignment network that jointly aligns mean and variance statistics through a learnable weighting mechanism, while a residual-attention encoder captures the non-stationary dynamics of worn tires. Our approach learns a domain-invariant representation that adapts continuously to varying wear states, enabling accurate cross-condition predictions. In cross-wear evaluations, the proposed model cuts relative error by nearly forty percent versus traditional regressors. These results demonstrate that coupling targeted data collection with adaptive alignment strategies can substantially enhance the generalization of force-prediction models across evolving mechanical conditions, offering a powerful tool for tire health monitoring.

title: Enhancing stability and convergence of offline real-time hybrid simulation via global model-based numerical substructuring approach
abstract: Real-Time Hybrid Simulation (RTHS) is an efficient structural dynamic testing technique that models the well-understood components as numerical substructures, while obtaining the response of the unknown dynamic characteristics through physical testing. Offline RTHS, a recently introduced iterative substructure interaction method, decouples numerical simulation from physical loading over time, enhancing the flexibility of solving complex models and performing multi-specimen tests. However, this method faces challenges in iteration stability and convergence speed, limiting its application in certain dynamic systems. To address these issues, this study proposes a Global Model-based Numerical Substructuring (GMNS) approach, which integrates known information from the physical specimen with the rest of the system into the numerical substructure, retaining only the uncertainties of the physical specimen as the physical substructure. Simulation results demonstrate that GMNS effectively enhances iteration stability and convergence speed in both actuator-based and shake-table-based offline RTHS systems.
