Further validation was performed through a Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) seismic mitigation test. The experimental results indicate that GMNS significantly enhances the critical stability mass ratio, increasing it from less than 2.7% to over 10%. Furthermore, under a TMD mass ratio of 2.5%, it reduces the number of iterations required to achieve a relative iteration error below 0.1 from more than 7 to only 2.

title: Smart adaptive trigger sensing powered by edge intelligence and digital twin for energy-efficient wireless Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: Capturing structural transient responses under sudden events, e.g., earthquakes, is a critical challenge for wireless Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems deployed on resource-constrained edge devices. To address it, researchers are developing event-triggered sensing to detect events while enhancing energy efficiency. However, this technology is fundamentally constrained by the selection of triggering conditions, e.g., vibration threshold, which are mostly based on empirical values and lack the adaptability required to handle dynamic and unpredictable environments. Such limitations give rise to an inherent trade-off between missed triggers and false triggers, hence possibly failing to satisfy practical application demands. To achieve the optimal triggering conditions that may vary under changing environments, this study introduces an adaptive triggering mechanism powered by edge intelligence and accelerated by Digital Twin (DT). By embedding adaptivity into the sensing process, the proposed approach dynamically optimizes critical parameters to achieve both detection accuracy and energy efficiency. In particular, anchored in a Feedback Control (FC) framework, the proposed mechanism leverages Bayesian Optimization (BO) and lightweight neural networks to address the challenges of data scarcity, data imbalance, partial observability, and high observation costs. Experimental validation on LiftNode, a low-power IoT sensor node, demonstrates the framework’s capability to enhance detection performance (Fβ) by approximately 30% compared to conservative manual parameter setting methods, while achieving similar or higher precision with computational overhead reduced by 2–3 orders of magnitude compared to batch exhaustive processing methods, marking a transformative step toward more reliable and sustainable SHM deployments.

title: Inter-turbine modelling of wind-farm power using multi-task learning
abstract: Because of the global need to increase power production from renewable energy resources, developments in the online monitoring of the associated infrastructure is of interest to reduce operation and maintenance costs. However, challenges exist for data-driven approaches to this problem, such as incomplete or limited histories of labelled damage-state data, operational and environmental variability, or the desire for the quantification of uncertainty to support risk management. This work first introduces a probabilistic regression model for predicting wind-turbine power, which adjusts for wake effects learnt from data. Spatial correlations in the learned model parameters for different tasks (turbines) are then leveraged in a hierarchical Bayesian model (an approach to multi-task learning) to develop a "metamodel", which can be used to make power-predictions which adjust for turbine location - including on previously unobserved turbines not included in the training data. The results show that the metamodel is able to outperform a series of benchmark models, and demonstrates a novel strategy for making efficient use of data for inference in populations of structures, in particular where correlations exist in the variable(s) of interest (such as those from wind-turbine wake-effects).

title: Adaptive modeling and parameter identification of piezoelectric structures under system uncertainty and nonlinear effects
abstract: A novel robust synchronization-based computational strategy is developed capable of identifying material and system parameters of active flexible smart structures and modeling the nonlinear response due to faults and system reconfiguration even in the presence of noise in the experimental data and uncertainties. The sensitivity problem, resulting from the gradient-based algorithm, is addressed with a novel hybrid technique that exploits the advantages of both frequency and time-domain procedures. This hybrid approach ensures robust parameter identification and accurate modeling under challenging conditions making it highly suitable for real-time applications. Extensive numerical results confirm the intrinsic benefits of the proposed computational strategy, demonstrating its effectiveness for simulating the response of nonlinear electromechanical vibration-based devices. The proposed approach is validated through its application to parameter identification and damage diagnosis of a sandwich laminate, showcasing its practical relevance and versatility. These advancements represent a significant step forward in the modeling and control of piezoelectric smart structures, offering a robust solution for applications ranging from structural health monitoring to energy harvesting.

title: Complete Stribeck curve prediction by applying machine learning to acoustic emission data from a lubricated sliding contact
abstract: The Stribeck curve for a sliding contact characterizes its lubrication behavior and enables friction to be predicted across various regimes. It is crucial for optimizing the energy efficiency and durability of mechanical systems. However, current methods of obtaining Stribeck curves are confined to laboratory settings and often involve destructive testing, which precludes real-time monitoring. This study shows how to predict the Stribeck curve for a reciprocating, sliding contact between a steel ball and flat by applying machine learning (ML) models to recorded acoustic emission (AE) signals. These models were trained and validated against experimental Stribeck curves obtained by directly measuring the coefficient of friction while varying the Stribeck number through temperature-induced viscosity adjustments. AE signals were captured at a high sampling rate and processed using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and Short-Time Histogram (STHG) techniques to compress the data and extract relevant features. Machine learning models, consisting of artificial neural networks (ANNs) optimized with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) or Genetic Algorithm (GA), were utilized to predict both the Stribeck Number and the Coefficient of Friction. The STFT＋GA-ANN combination provided the highest accuracy in predicting the Stribeck Number (MSE = 2.60, MAPE = 28.84%), while the STFT＋PSO-ANN combination excelled in predicting the Coefficient of Friction (MSE = 0.0001, MAPE = 4.94%). Combining these methods enables the complete Stribeck curve to be successfully predicted based only on the emitted sound. This demonstration of in-situ, non-destructive AE-ML-based prediction of comprehensive tribological behavior paves the way for real-time lubrication monitoring in machine applications without disrupting system operation.

title: Advanced self-tuning vibration modeling strategy for rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: Fault diagnosis of planetary gearboxes under non-stationary operating conditions faces significant challenges from complex modulation effects and strong noise interference. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a novel self-tuning vibration modeling strategy to enhance the interpretability of fault features. The key innovations include: (1) An angular domain modulation informed non-stationary model is developed to generally interpret fault related signatures; (2) A hybrid signal processing framework combining variational mode decomposition (VMD) and order tracking for precise instantaneous order component under speed fluctuations; (3) An adaptive parameter determination strategy employing loss function constrained gradient descent between proposed model and monitored data, enabling model parameters self-tuning without noise interference. Experimental validation under varying speed conditions demonstrates that the key parameters of the proposed model achieving 91.30% and 93.61% classification accuracy for acceleration and deceleration conditions, over 20% improvements than the comparative vibration model. The developed strategy not only advances rotating machinery fault diagnosis in non-stationary environments but also establishes a new paradigm for self-tuning vibration modeling in condition monitoring applications.

title: Equi-Euler GraphNet: An equivariant, temporal-dynamics informed graph neural network for dual force and trajectory prediction in multi-body systems
abstract: Accurate real-time modeling of multi-body dynamical systems is essential for enabling digital twin applications across industries. While many data-driven approaches aim to learn system dynamics, jointly predicting internal loads and system trajectories remains a key challenge. This dual prediction is especially important for fault detection and predictive maintenance, where internal loads-such as contact forces-act as early indicators of faults, reflecting wear or misalignment before affecting motion. These forces also serve as inputs to degradation models (e.g., crack growth), enabling damage prediction and remaining useful life estimation. We propose Equi-Euler GraphNet, a physics-informed graph neural network (GNN) that simultaneously predicts internal forces and global trajectories in multi-body systems. In this mesh-free framework, nodes represent system components and edges encode interactions. Equi-Euler GraphNet introduces two inductive biases: (1) an equivariant message-passing scheme, interpreting edge messages as interaction forces consistent under Euclidean transformations; and (2) a temporal-aware iterative node update mechanism, based on Euler integration, to capture influence of distant interactions over time. Tailored for cylindrical roller bearings, it decouples ring dynamics from constrained motion of rolling elements. Trained on high-fidelity multiphysics simulations, Equi-Euler GraphNet generalizes beyond the training distribution, accurately predicting loads and trajectories under unseen speeds, loads, and configurations. It outperforms state-of-the-art GNNs focused on trajectory prediction, delivering stable rollouts over thousands of time steps with minimal error accumulation. Achieving up to a 200x speedup over conventional solvers while maintaining comparable accuracy, it serves as an efficient reduced-order model for digital twins, design, and maintenance.

title: Data-driven temperature compensation of strain measurements using particle filters: Sensitivity study and application for event-driven structural health monitoring of a bio-composite pedestrian bridge
abstract: This paper introduces a novel temperature compensation methodology for strain measurements based on the Particle Filter (PF), integrated into the event-driven Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) of a bio-composite pedestrian bridge, namely the Smart Circular Bridge (SCB). The adoption of fiber Bragg grating strain sensors, such as those embedded in the SCB, has led to a significant increase in the number of strain sensors used in SHM. However, these measurements are highly sensitive to temperature variations, particularly the local heating induced by solar radiation. Traditional temperature compensation methods involving dedicated sensors become impractical as sensor numbers grow, and real-time compensation for detecting anomalous events, such as misuse, is often required for effective SHM. Therefore, a particle filter-based temperature compensation method is proposed, enabling real-time compensation without the need for dedicated temperature sensors. A comparison between different filters highlights the added value of the PF’s built-in knowledge of the expected loads for isolating short-lived strain events from temperature-induced variations. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis using synthetic data provides guidelines for selecting PF control parameters and shows that PF-based temperature compensation works best for short, high-amplitude events, while underestimating longer, low-amplitude events. Application of this method to SCB’s strain data reveals insights into bridge usage patterns, including unintended vehicular use, demonstrating the PF-based approach’s potential for real-time event detection in complex SHM scenarios.

title: Active transfer learning for structural health monitoring
abstract: Data for training structural health monitoring (SHM) systems are often expensive and/or impractical to obtain, particularly for labelled data. Population-based SHM (PBSHM) aims to address this limitation by leveraging data from multiple structures. However, data from different structures will follow distinct distributions, potentially leading to large generalisation errors for models learnt via conventional machine learning methods. To address this issue, transfer learning -- in the form of domain adaptation (DA) -- can be used to align the data distributions. Most previous approaches have only considered \emph{unsupervised} DA, where no labelled target data are available; they do not consider how to incorporate these technologies in an online framework -- updating as labels are obtained throughout the monitoring campaign. This paper proposes a Bayesian framework for DA in PBSHM, that can improve unsupervised DA mappings using a limited quantity of labelled target data. In addition, this model is integrated into an active sampling strategy to guide inspections to select the most informative observations to label -- leading to further reductions in the required labelled data to learn a target classifier. The effectiveness of this methodology is evaluated on a population of experimental bridges. Specifically, this population includes data corresponding to several damage states, as well as, a comprehensive set of environmental conditions. It is found that combining transfer learning and active learning can improve data efficiency when learning classification models in label-scarce scenarios. This result has implications for data-informed operation and maintenance of structures, suggesting a reduction in inspections over the operational lifetime of a structure -- and therefore a reduction in operational costs -- can be achieved.

title: Nonlinear vibrations of collagen hydrogel cylindrical shells under radial harmonic excitation
abstract: Owing to their excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility, collagen hydrogels have recently attracted intensive attention. We simplify the collagen hydrogel artificial blood vessels as thin-walled hyperelastic cylindrical shells and, for the first time, investigate their nonlinear resonant and chaotic responses under radial harmonic excitation. Employing Donnell’s nonlinear shell theory, hyperelastic constitutive relation and Lagrange equation, the governing equations of motion are established for the hydrogel cylindrical shells under the radial harmonic excitation. The incompressible hyperelastic Mooney-Rivlin model is used to describe the material behaviors, and the boundary condition of the cylindrical shell is simply-supported at both ends. The amplitude-frequency and force-amplitude response curves are obtained via the multi-scale method. The 2:1 internal resonance condition is identified and the validity of the dynamic model is confirmed. The effects of various parameters on the resonant and chaotic responses of the hydrogel cylindrical shells are discussed. The results indicate that the ultraviolet (UV) cross-linking energy significantly affects the linear frequencies and chaotic responses of the hydrogel shells. However, its influences on the amplitude-frequency and force-amplitude responses are almost negligible. Changes in structural parameters and external excitation enrich the vibration behaviors observed in both resonant and chaotic responses.

title: An adaptive phase feedback algorithm for displacement tracking from video frames
abstract: Computer vision-based non-contact displacement measurement techniques have demonstrated significant potential for structural health monitoring. A new category of Phase Motion Estimation (PME) method has been developed recently extracting spatial motion information of structures by analyzing the phase information in image sequences. It has sub-pixel accuracy without the need of artificial markers. However, conventional PME methods suffer from a subjectively selected wavelength parameter that may lead to limited computation efficiency if it is too large, or wrapping of phase information if it is too small. This study proposes an adaptive wavelength for the phase-feedback to address this issue. It adaptively adjusts the wavelength of Gabor wavelet in the PME method in real time to ensure non-wrapping phase information. The proposed algorithm is systematically evaluated with numerical simulations and experiment in the laboratory. Simulation results demonstrate that it can effectively eliminate phase wrapping, with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of less than 0.06 pixels and Root Mean Squares Error (RMSE) of less than 0.08 pixels in the estimated displacement which is similar to that from conventional PME. The computation time is also reduced by 38.5 %. Experiment with a steel beam shows that the displacement extracted is closely matching that from a laser displacement sensor with a correlation coefficient of 0.998 and a MAE and RMSE of 0.17 mm and 0.27 mm, respectively. The computational time has been significantly improved by 65 % compared to that from the traditional PME approach.

title: Large displacement measurement using deep learning-based RAFT and KLT optical flow
abstract: In the field of visual measurement, displacement scales usually include both pixel and sub-pixel levels, particularly evident in vibration measurements of large displacements (pixel displacement between consecutive frames significantly exceeds one pixel). A single recognition method often performs inconsistently at different accuracy levels. For example, RAFT optical flow excels at pixel-level accuracy but is less effective at sub-pixel accuracy, whereas KLT optical flow exhibits the opposite behavior. Therefore, this paper proposes a deep learning-based Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transform (RAFT) and Kanade-Lucas-Tomasi (KLT) optical flow method to identify structural motions involving both pixel-level and sub-pixel-level displacements, thereby improving the accuracy of large displacement measurements. The proposed method aims to improve optical flow techniques by leveraging the complementary strengths of RAFT and KLT. First, a vibration video of the structure was captured using a camera and preprocessed to obtain the initial region of interest (IROI) vibration data. RAFT was then applied to calculate the full-field optical flow, predict the ROI, and extract the pixel displacement within the ROI. Next, a translation transformation was performed on the ROI image based on integer pixel displacement between consecutive frames to reconstruct the video. Subsequently, the KLT optical flow was used to calculate the sub-pixel displacement of the ROI in the reconstructed video. Finally, the integer pixel and sub-pixel displacements were added to obtain accurate pixel displacement, which was then converted into physical displacement for structural vibration. The proposed method was validated through both laboratory and field tests. The proposed method applied image translation transformation, which limited pixel-level motion to the sub-pixel level, to achieve large displacement measurement of structures. This process preserves pixel integrity, avoids distortion, and guarantees the recognition performance for large displacement motion. The proposed method effectively overcomes the accuracy limitations of a single method in identifying different pixel displacement levels and significantly improves the accuracy of large displacement measurements.

title: A probabilistic machine learning method for predicting nonlinear vibrations of marine helical gear transmission system
abstract: The dynamic performance of the marine helical gear transmission system (MHGTS) is a critical indicator of its health status, directly affecting the stability and safety of the ship. However, the coupling of multiple factors such as load disturbances and main engine vibrations results in significant nonlinearity and uncertainty in the system’s dynamic characteristics, making it difficult to accurately identify the nonlinear vibration response of MHGTSs. This study proposes a probabilistic machine learning (PML) method for accurately characterizing and predicting the nonlinear vibration response of MHGTS. Specifically, the proposed method replaces traditional point estimation approaches by developing an improved sparse Bayesian learning framework to achieve interval estimation of the uncertainty in vibration responses. Additionally, it employs a piecewise spike and slab prior to adaptively separate the sparse and fidelity components of the vibration response, effectively enhancing the prediction accuracy of the proposed method. To evaluate the generalization performance of the PML method, the training data comprises simulated data generated through dynamic simulations as well as experimental data acquired from full-scale ship experiments. These datasets jointly validate the robustness and accuracy of the proposed method under various loads, rotational speeds, ship speeds, and wave heights. Compared to GPR, SINDy, and LSTM, the PML method achieved higher R-squared values, ranging from 0.83 to 0.98, coupled with lower root mean square error.

title: A state-of-the-art constrained variational Bayesian method based on posterior projection for matrix completion in non-synchronous measurements
abstract: The Non-Synchronous Measurements techniques have garnered attention for their ability to enhance the performance of a single microphone array by translating the array to scan the acoustic source. However, existing non-synchronous measurement methods often perform poorly at low signal-to-noise ratios and are highly sensitive to parameter settings. To address these challenges, we propose a variational Bayesian method based on posterior projection. This innovative method models non-synchronous measurements as a low-rank matrix completion problem and solves it using a variational Bayesian method, embedding the properties of spatial continuity and Hermitian semi-definiteness into the posterior through posterior projection and correction. This method avoids the difficulties in modeling and solving caused by multiple constraints in the non-synchronous measurements model, while achieving high-precision adaptive parameter estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through extensive simulations under various conditions, including different signal-to-noise ratios, frequencies, measurement distances, and numbers of measurements. The results from these simulations and experiments demonstrate that the proposed method generally outperforms conventional non-synchronous measurements methods in terms of accuracy and noise robustness, without requiring parameter adjustment, particularly under conditions where the imaging algorithm has sufficient spatial resolution.

title: Bridge modal frequency estimation and uncertainty analysis using Vehicle-Independent coherence filtering
abstract: This study presents a novel, model-free spectral filtering framework for extracting modal frequencies of bridges using drive-by (indirect) vehicle data. Acceleration signals collected over a 45-minute period from a passenger vehicle driving over a short, multi-span bridge are segmented into road-only and bridge-crossing segments. Power Spectral Density shapes of the road segments are then normalized and used to construct a frequency-dependent filter, informed by three data coherence measures: road-road, bridge-bridge, and bridge-road. This approach enhances bridge response by suppressing road and vehicle noise without requiring explicit knowledge of vehicle dynamics. The methodology was able to identify up to 8 modal frequencies of the bridge, validated through portable Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) sensor measurements. Specifically, the drive-by data improved the mode identification results due to exposure to a broader spatial and temporal coverage of structural responses under a wider range of traffic-induced excitations, improving peak estimations and revealing unclear modes in stationary data. To quantify reliability, an uncertainty analysis was conducted across 455 three-run combinations (totaling 45 min) to compute the 95 % percentile range, the Coefficient of Variation (CV), bias metrics, and statistical tests. The validation against the portable SHM estimation demonstrates high accuracy (bias ≤ 0.5 Hz) and precision (CV < 4.07 %), with stable frequency estimates achieved after as few as 100 three-run combinations. This study establishes a robust foundation for vehicle-agnostic bridge modal frequency identification and rigorous uncertainty quantification using extensive indirect vehicle data, which holds critical importance for the practical monitoring of bridge networks.

title: Robust finite-time super-twisting control for magnetic field manipulation system with abrupt disturbance
abstract: Accurate measurement and analysis of physiological magnetic field signals enable early and precise diagnosis, thereby facilitating targeted interventions for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. Nevertheless, establishing an ultra-low noise environment and detecting subtle magnetic signals under abrupt disturbance remain formidable challenges. This article reformulates the dynamic model of the magnetic field manipulation system (MFMS) and proposes a robust finite-time super-twisting control (RFTSTC) strategy. A finite-time extended state observer (FTESO) is designed to estimate unmeasurable system state and disturbance, thereby enabling real-time system uncertainty quantification. Based on this, a fast super-twisting algorithm is developed on a nonsingular terminal sliding mode surface, incorporating additional linear and fractional-order terms. This operation effectively mitigates singularities, enhances convergence speed, significantly reduces oscillations, and suppresses system noise in the presence of abrupt disturbance. The finite-time convergence of the estimation errors and system states is rigorously proven using the Lyapunov method. Numerical simulations and experiment results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed strategy over existing approaches.

title: Dynamic modelling and vibration analysis of parallel misaligned shaft system considering the spline time-varying meshing point
abstract: Involute spline couplings see extensive use in shaft system connections. In reality, parallel misalignment can cause changes in the meshing point positions of spline teeth. However, most previous works assume that parallel misalignment will not notably change the spline tooth meshing point position. This is unreasonable because the time-varying meshing position (TVMP) will alter the spline meshing force (SMF) and significantly affect the shaft system vibrations. Thus, a TVMP calculation model is derived in this paper. The spline tooth time-varying backlash and pressure angle models considering the TVMP are proposed. Moreover, the spline meshing stiffness (SMS) and deformation models considering TVMP are given. Furthermore, a shaft system dynamic model considering the TVMP is established. Spline meshing characteristics and shaft system vibrations verification experiments are carried out. A comparison of SMFs obtained by the methods with and without considering TVMP is conducted to highlight the importance of considering TVMP. Finally, the influence of parallel misalignment and rotating speed on the shaft system vibrations is evaluated. This paper can provide parallel misalignment control insights for the shaft system.

title: Second harmonic coupling mechanism analysis and compensation of leaf-spring-type tri-axial standard vibrator
abstract: Tri-axial dynamic calibration technology and systems are recently used to effectively calibrate tri-axial vibration sensors by accurately simulating application environments. Achieving high-precision decoupling control as well as minimizing harmonic distortion of the tri-axial vibrator are essential for accurate sensor calibration. In this paper, a harmonic compensation method for a leaf-spring-type tri-axial standard vibrator (LS-TAV) is proposed to effectively suppress harmonic distortion and enhance the accuracy of the output signal. The second harmonic coupling mechanism of the LS-TAV is first analyzed based on cantilever beam equivalent model. Considering the nonlinear stiffness of the flexible restoring and decoupling structures, the coupling characteristics of the LS-TAV are further calculated using simplified simulation models. Then, the amplitudes and phases of the corresponding second harmonic compensation quantities are calculated and incorporated into the input excitation signals to verify the feasibility of the harmonic compensation method. The results show that the accuracy of the output signals is significantly improved after harmonic compensation in theoretical and simulation analyses, with the corresponding second harmonic distortions (SHDs) reduced from over 3.27% to below 0.33%. Finally, the correctness of the harmonic coupling mechanism and the effectiveness of the harmonic compensation method are verified through experimental test. Across the entire test frequency range, the SHDs of the experimental output displacement waveforms along each axis decrease from over 3.52% to below 0.29%.

title: Data-driven sparse coding for onboard condition monitoring of railway tracks
abstract: Continuous monitoring of the rail condition plays an important role in railway maintenance and the planning of noise- and vibration-reducing measures. Rail monitoring can be carried out efficiently using vibro-acoustic measurements with onboard sensors. However, this approach generates large amounts of acoustic and vibration data, which makes real-time transmission, processing and storage a challenge. This paper presents a sparse coding framework applied in the time-frequency domain that aims to overcome these challenges by significantly reducing the amount of data while preserving important information for rail defect detection and diagnosis. The Short-Time Fourier Transform is used as a preprocessing step to transform raw signals into a time-frequency representation, capturing the non-stationary characteristics of the signals. The spectrum at each time window is then represented by a sparse linear combination of basis spectra, which form a dictionary. Online sparse dictionary learning is used to create a data-driven, adaptive representation tailored to the frequency characteristics of vibro-acoustic signals related to rail defects. Experimental data acquired with a microphone and an accelerometer mounted on the wheelset of a tram are used to evaluate the framework. The experimental results show that the framework is able to achieve high compression rates and reduce noise. A reduction in data size of 98% was obtained without loss of relevant information. The proposed approach offers significant advantages for modern railway condition monitoring systems. It is scalable for large amounts of data, energy efficient and suitable for real-time implementation. By reducing data bottlenecks, it enables efficient track monitoring with on-board sensors. This work thus contributes to the development of intelligent and cost-effective solutions for infrastructure management.

title: Analysis and application of fractional coupled Duffing oscillator with damping
abstract: This paper introduces a signal detection model based on fractional coupled Duffing oscillator with damping and use it to detect the ship-radiated noise signal (S-RNS) under the background of noise interference. Firstly, we introduce a nonlinear dissipative damping term into the fractional coupled Duffing oscillator, named fractional coupled Duffing oscillator with damping (FCDOD). The system structure of FCDOD is analyzed in detail. By analyzing the damping term of FCDOD, it is proved that the system has a faster energy dissipation rate, which means that the interference of external disturbances (e.g., noise) can be attenuated faster. Then, the critical chaotic state threshold of the system is determined by Lyapunov exponent, bifurcation behavior and fluctuation-based dispersion entropy. Next, the detection experiment of the simulated signal proves that the signal-to-noise ratio threshold of the system can reach −76.02 dB. Finally, to detect S-RNS when the signal prior information is unknown, a differential fractional coupled Duffing oscillator with damping (DFCDOD) is constructed by combining two FCDOD in the form of difference. Combining oscillator train and intermittent chaos method, the S-RNS is detected by using DFCDOD, and the accuracy rate can reach 99.86 %. The results show that the proposed detection model can provide effective technical support for weak signal frequency measurement of maritime targets.

title: Closed-form solution for vibration analysis of structures with localized features via Metaheuristic-enhanced Homotopy Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel closed-form analytical methodology for predicting the global modal parameters, specifically natural frequencies and corresponding mode shapes, of one- and two-dimensional (1D/2D) structures containing localized features. These features are defined as discrete irregularities, such as cracks, bolted joints, or abrupt stiffness changes, which introduce concentrated changes to the system’s properties. The core of the approach is an integrated framework combining Homotopy Mapping with Metaheuristic Optimization. Homotopy Mapping constructs a continuous transformation from the known linear modal properties of the intact structure to those of the structure with localized features. Metaheuristic Optimization is then employed to determine a set of auxiliary convergence-control parameters for each mode order in this transformation. Based on the transformation along with pre-computed auxiliary parameters, an explicit closed-form expression is derived, linking the physical parameters (e.g., location and stiffness) of the localized features to the global modal behavior of the structure. A key advantage is that the derived explicit closed-form expression naturally avoids the iterative numerical re-modeling inherent in traditional methods, leading to substantially improved computational efficiency. The accuracy of the proposed method is validated through experimental tests. When benchmarked against semi-analytical, data-driven, and numerical approaches, the method exhibits natural frequency prediction errors below 1.5 % for both fundamental and higher-order modes, across the full range of variations in localized features. Moreover, the method offers physical interpretability by explicitly revealing how feature parameters influence global modal behavior. This work provides a computationally efficient and robust analytical tool for the forward analysis of structures with localized features, effectively balancing theoretical innovation with engineering applicability.

title: Python open-source signal processing and modeling/simulation for scientific research in structural dynamics—A review
abstract: Open-source scientific research has become indispensable, because it fosters a global collaborative environment in which knowledge is freely shared, accelerating the pace of discovery. Emphasizing transparency and reproducibility ensures the credibility of scientific findings, while democratizing access to research gives a wider community the opportunity to contribute to progress. Avoiding duplication of effort leads to faster progress and greater societal benefit. The Python programming language provides readable code and is highly collaborative, leading to a large user community. Libraries such as NumPy (i.e. numerical Python) and SciPy (i.e. scientific computing) have been developed for scientific research. The latter was crucial, for example, in the discovery of gravitational waves and the first imaging of a black hole. This review focuses on selected open-source Python libraries that support scientific development in the field of signal processing and mechanical systems. In particular, the article focuses on packages related to signal processing, experimental and operational modal analysis, vibration fatigue, image-based identification of structural dynamics, vibration control, substructuring, rotor dynamics, vibrations in pipeline systems, and machine-learning. A basic theoretical overview of the presented topics and some typical use cases for selected open-source packages are given. Finally, this review article proposes a strategy to increase collaboration among many researchers resulting in highly-related future scientific packages. The purpose of this review is to help new researchers get started in open-source-based signal processing, while those already active can learn the development principles for better and interconnected scientific packages.

title: Advancements in detecting combustion events through vibration analysis in internal combustion engines: a literature review
abstract: Accurate combustion characterization is very important for the reliability, efficiency, and emissions of internal combustion engines (ICEs). Standard in-cylinder pressure sensors are costly, obtrusive, and have a short lifespan under harsh environments. This research examines vibration-based analysis as a non-intrusive method for identifying and reconstructing combustion events in compression ignition (CI) and homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) engines. We examine the correlation between engine block vibrations and combustion parameters, including start of combustion (SOC), peak pressure (PP), pressure rise rate (PPRR), maximum heat release rate (HRRmax), and mass fraction burned (MFB), while assessing signal decomposition techniques such as Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD). Advanced signal processing is also combined with machine learning (ML) models to improve real-time estimation and nonlinear mapping. Our study shows that vibration signals can be used as reliable indicators of combustion, with timing precision of less than 1 CAD and pressure reconstruction error of less than 5%. Nonetheless, difficulties persist in adaptive parameter tuning, signal decoupling during transient situations, and the comprehensibility of machine learning models. Hybrid and explainable ML frameworks, multi-sensor data fusion, and the creation of virtual combustion noise sensors for onboard diagnostics are some promising areas of research. In the end, vibration-based combustion analysis provides a cheap and scalable means to get to real-time, non-intrusive monitoring, which will help the shift to cleaner, quieter, and more efficient engines.

title: Study on the coupling vibration mechanism and amplitude-frequency modulation characteristics of electromechanical composite transmission system used in HEV
abstract: With the automotive industry transitioning toward electrification, electromechanical composite transmission (EMT) system have emerged as a new-generation powertrain solution for heavy-duty vehicles. The incorporation of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) in EMT system not only significantly enhances off-road mobility, fuel efficiency, and dynamic response performance but also introduces novel electro-mechanical-magnetic coupling characteristics. And the electro-mechanical-magnetic coupling characteristics may induce coupled vibrations, thereby affecting the overall operational performance of the EMT system. Therefore, it is crucial to elucidate this coupling mechanism in EMT system. This study develops an EMT dynamic model based on Lagrange-Maxwell equations that incorporates multiple nonlinear factors including current harmonics, time-varying mesh stiffness, gear backlash, and transmission errors. Furthermore, a characterization method for the machine-electricity-magnet coupling interface is innovatively proposed. Subsequently analytical expressions for coupled vibration signals are derived by integrating coupling interface model and Amplitude-Frequency Modulation (AFM) analysis, thereby elucidating the underlying electro-mechanical-magnetic coupling mechanisms among multiple physical fields. Ultimately, the AFM laws are validated by numerical simulations and experimental tests based on the developed model and derived expressions. The results demonstrate that coupled vibration signals from the mechanical subsystem and electrical subsystem exhibit asymmetric sidebands around their respective carrier frequencies—gear meshing frequency and electrical frequency—modulated by component rotational frequencies. The revealed AFM mechanism provides a theoretical foundation for excitation source decoupling, vibration suppression strategy formulation, and EMT system optimization.

title: Experimental and computational-fluid-dynamic thermal model analysis on oil-flood angular contact ball bearing
abstract: Angular contact ball bearings (ACBBs) in high-speed rotating machinery demand precise thermo-fluidic modeling to prevent skidding-induced failures and optimize lubrication efficiency. This study addresses this need through a novel coupled computational-Fluid-dynamic thermal (CFD-T) model integrating fluid dynamics, bearing kinematics, and thermal effects for ACBBs with integral cages. The 3D CFD framework simulates full fluid-domain behavior in a 220 mm bore bearing, incorporating skidding dynamics and replacing empirical drag formulations with first-principles fluid solutions. Experimental validation using triboelectric cage-speed sensors and infrared thermometry confirms the model’s accuracy across skidding regimes. Key results demonstrate that cage presence increases maximum oil pressure by 80 kPa (+90 %) and flow velocity by 19.6 % versus cage-free models. Skidding causes 52.6 % and 13.6 % variations in maximum pressure and velocity, respectively. Neglecting thermal-viscosity effects overestimates drag torque by nearly 100 %. The CFD-T model reduces cage-speed prediction errors by up to 6.05 % versus conventional dynamic-thermal models and maintains temperature deviations below 2 °C at 1500 rpm. Parametric studies reveal oil supply pressure critically balances lubrication performance and power loss, with high-pressure supply increasing drag torque by 50 % but improving thermal management. This work provides a validated high-fidelity tool for ACBB reliability enhancement and anti-skidding design.

title: Improved waveform command shaping anti-sway control for arbitrary initial and terminal conditions
abstract: In crane operations, the payload may not always be directly beneath the trolley, leading to varying initial load states. To address the challenges of load swing suppression and precise trolley positioning under uncertain initial conditions, this paper proposes an improved waveform command shaping anti-sway control method applicable to arbitrary initial and terminal conditions. By introducing constraints on trolley acceleration, the maximum speed of the whole process, and maximum swing of the load, the method effectively suppresses load sway and ensures precise motion control. Unlike conventional approaches, it systematically determines acceleration and deceleration times based on constraints rather than manual selection, enhancing engineering applicability. The proposed method is validated through simulations and experiments on a scaled crane platform. Results demonstrate its effectiveness in suppressing load swing for both zero and nonzero initial conditions while achieving precise trolley positioning within motion constraints.

title: A novel multimodal fusion knowledge graph embedding method for remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is an important guarantee for preventing major accidents and formulating reasonable maintenance strategies. Multimodal data can provide more comprehensive information for equipment RUL prediction from different perspectives. However, existing methods treat all modal data as the same attributes and ignore the complex coupling relationships among heterogeneous information, which will fail to collaboratively construct accurate degradation patterns. To this end, this paper proposes a multimodal fusion knowledge graph embedding (MFKGE) method to utilize multimodal data in the degradation process for RUL prediction. Firstly, a multimodal knowledge graph (MKG) describing the information association between multiple modalities is constructed, which combines data structures and prior knowledge to emphasize the relations between different types of entities. Subsequently, a relational heterogeneous graph neural network (RHGNN) is proposed to represent the interactions between multiple different types of entities. In particular, intra-modal and inter-modal message passing mechanisms are designed for the aggregation of relations and attributes of entities. Third, to solve the problem of inconsistent description of the degradation process by heterogeneous information, a knowledge embedding-based method is used to align multiple modal features. Finally, a relational information-guided multimodal fusion method is proposed, which effectively fuses the attributes of entities with relations to determine the final estimate of RUL. The effectiveness and advancement of the proposed method are verified by two public datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed method performs better than other methods and has the accuracy of long-range prediction.

title: Latent deep-kernel filtering for lightweight and robust industrial sound source localization
abstract: Sound source localization (SSL) in industrial environments faces significant challenges due to complex acoustic conditions and resource constraints of edge devices. Current approaches either lack robustness (model-based methods) or demand excessive computational resources (learning-based methods), creating a gap for solutions that balance accuracy, efficiency, and robustness in real-world industrial IoT applications. This paper introduces Latent Space Kernel Adaptive Filtering (LS-KAF), a novel framework that synergistically combines deep representation learning with kernel adaptive filtering. LS-KAF employs an encoder-filter-decoder paradigm where: An audio encoder projects high-dimensional audio features into a compact, task-driven latent space; a lightweight kernel filter performs efficient localization in this space; and a reconstruction decoder regularizes the latent representation to preserve critical spatial information. We develop three variants each addressing different efficiency-accuracy trade-offs. Extensive evaluations against both conventional methods (GCC-PHAT, SRP-PHAT, MUSIC) and deep learning approaches (CNN, CRNN, MTIT, U-Net) demonstrate LS-KAF’s superior performance in synthetic and real-world industrial settings. Our best-performing variant achieves significant improvements in localization accuracy while maintaining robustness to reverberation and noise, all while retaining a lightweight structure suitable for resource-constrained hardware. LS-KAF bridges the gap between model-based and learning-based approaches, offering an optimal balance of interpretability, computational efficiency, and localization accuracy for practical deployment in challenging industrial environments.

title: Ultrasonic synchronous identification method of wear and water film thickness in water-lubricated bearings
abstract: Wear depth and water film thickness represent crucial parameters for water-lubricated bearings, elucidating the wear evolution mechanisms, guiding material and structural design, and implementing health monitoring strategies. In this paper, a four-layer ultrasonic propagation model is developed, and a novel bearing-water layer reflection coefficient integrating wear and lubrication film thickness is derived mathematically. Furthermore, a synchronous identification method is proposed. The water film thickness is precisely determined utilizing the residual reflection coefficient phase. Based on this, a fitness function is constructed that effectively eliminates interference arising from phase and amplitude variations within the water film layer in the frequency domain. Consequently, an intelligent optimization algorithm is employed to invert the wear depth accurately. Finite element simulation and experiment are conducted to verify the proposed method. Results demonstrate that when the water film thickness ranges from 5 to 200 μm, the relative error remains below 12.4 %. Compared with existing methods, the proposed method achieves higher wear identification accuracy across various water film thicknesses, with absolute errors reduced to approximately 50 μm.

title: A sparse extended Kalman filtering based on Laplace prior for real-time state-parameter identification of time-varying structural systems
abstract: Due to severe external loads and material degradation, structural parameters of engineering structures often vary during service. However, it is still a challenging task to identify time-varying structural physical parameters, especially in real time. In this paper, a sparse extended Kalman filtering based on Laplace prior (SEKF-L) is proposed for the real-time state-parameter identification of time-varying structures using only partial structural response observations. First, a set of pseudo-observation equations with a sparse prior is constructed to introduce spatial sparsity of time-varying structural parameters. Specifically, a Laplace prior is employed as the sparse prior to enhance the real-time tracking capability of time-varying parameters in the proposed SEKF-L. Furthermore, the Laplace prior is decomposed into a Gaussian and a Gamma distribution via a hierarchical Bayesian model to address the non-Gaussian noise in the pseudo-observation equations. Then, the pseudo-observation equations are combined with observation equations based on partially observed structural responses to form extended observation equations, which are then integrated into the EKF for state and parameter joint identification of time-varying structural systems. Finally, sparse Bayesian learning is integrated with the EKF to estimate noise parameters and the hyperparameters of the sparsity-inducing prior in pseudo-observation equations at each time step. To validate the proposed method, the real time identification of both numerical models of linear and nonlinear structures with time-varying stiffness and an experimental frame with abrupt stiffness are used in this paper. The results demonstrate that the proposed SEKF-L can accurately estimate the states and parameters of time-varying structural systems in real time using only partial structural response observations.

title: Optimal sensor placement for bridge weigh-in-motion using an augmented Kalman filter
abstract: Bridge Weigh-in-Motion (B-WIM) systems, which estimate crossing vehicle weights from instrumented bridge responses, are critical for enhancing design practices, ensuring structural safety, and informing maintenance. However, optimizing sensor placement for B-WIM presents challenges: existing studies often explore limited positions and primarily homogeneous sensor types, neglecting the inherent heterogeneity and complexity of practical deployments where multiple sensor types might be beneficial. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel multi-objective optimization framework for heterogeneous sensor placement in B-WIM systems. The framework integrates an augmented Kalman filter (AKF), capable of estimating system states and unknown inputs (vehicle loads) from diverse sensor data (displacement, velocity, acceleration, and strain) and known input locations, with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to identify optimal sensor configurations. The primary goal is to identify Pareto-optimal solutions balancing high load identification accuracy against minimal monitoring deployment cost, evaluated by either sensor count or total price. Sensor configurations, encompassing count, location, and type, are encoded as variable-length chromosomes within NSGA-II. The AKF provides the fitness evaluation, assessing the identification accuracy for each candidate placement to guide the evolutionary search. Numerical investigations using a three-span continuous bridge model demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed framework, under the assumption that axle counts and traveling positions are known for AKF matrix construction. The investigation explores various individual and mixed sensor configurations, yielding comprehensive cost-error trade-off curves. The results reveal an effective cost range where optimized placements reduce the identification error by approximately 2% compared to random or experience-based sensor layouts, while achieving equivalent high accuracy with up to 32% in cost savings.

title: Adaptive waveguide control based on graphene-reinforced phase-change phononic crystals
abstract: Advancing phononic crystal-based waveguides with tunable band structures is crucial for effective waveguide design and control in practical engineering applications. While the tunability of band structures, driven by phase transitions and graphene reinforcement, has shown great promise, it requires further in-depth investigation to fully realize its potential. This study introduces two different phase-change materials (PCMs), paraffin wax/oil and ice/water, into two-dimensional phononic crystals with graphene-reinforced composites (GRCs), resulting in phase-change graphene-reinforced phononic crystals (PGPCs), to design highly tunable waveguides. Initially, temperature-dependent dispersion characteristics of waves in PGPCs are obtained and analyzed using the finite element method. The results demonstrate that thermally induced phase transitions of PCMs can switch on or off the first bandgaps, enabling effective control of wave propagation. The introduction of GRC cores significantly enhances bandgap formation, with the first bandgap width expanding by up to 71.243 kHz as the core size increases. Additionally, varying the graphene content within the GRCs allows further tuning of the bandgap characteristics, yielding bandwidth and central frequency increases of up to 13.75 % and 8.53 %, respectively, in the examined cases. Based on these findings, a temperature-controlled waveguide design is proposed, exhibiting distinct frequency-dependent and temperature-controlled characteristics. This research provides an innovative strategy for developing highly tunable temperature-controlled acoustic devices through the combined use of phase-change materials and graphene-enhanced inclusions.

title: Transducer configurations for enhanced power density in cylindrical electromagnetic vibration energy harvesters
abstract: • A systematic comparison of cylindrical electromagnetic VEH transducers is presented. • A novel fully enclosed back iron design is proposed to concentrate the magnetic flux. • Simulations show the novel transducer improves magnetic flux density by 74 percent. • The magnetic flux leakage is reduced by over 99 percent for the novel transducer. • Tests show a max power of 44.50 mW and 4.25m W/cm 3 power density in 1 g vibrations. Vibration energy harvesters (VEHs) convert the mechanical energy of vibrations into electrical energy and can power wireless sensor networks. However, there are challenges to overcome in the development of practical VEHs that include maximizing the converted energy and energy density. This work presents a systematic comparison of cylindrical electromagnetic VEH transducers and a novel transducer configuration to address these challenges. An enclosure and spring system was designed, and a basic single cylindrical magnet transducer was established as a baseline. Multiple transducers were developed to investigate the use of opposing magnets and back irons to concentrate the magnetic flux. A novel transducer was introduced that incorporates a fully enclosed back iron. The transducers were simulated, fabricated, and tested experimentally. Simulations showed that the novel transducer enhanced the magnetic flux density by 74 percent from 0.23 T to 0.40 T over the coil and reduced the magnetic flux leakage by over 99 percent from 0.15 T to 3.6 × 10 −5 T below the transducer. These results show that the novel transducer effectively channels the magnetic flux over the coil and nearly eliminates magnetic flux leakage. Experimental tests in vibrations of 60 Hz and 1 g RMS demonstrated a maximum power generation of 44.50 mW and a power density of 4.25 mW/cm 3 for the novel design, representing an improvement in power density of 103 percent over the basic transducer. This study demonstrates that opposing magnets and back irons can be used to enhance the power density of electromagnetic VEH transducers and improve the overall practicality of VEHs.

title: ACWIgram: An adaptive composite weighted indexgram based on acoustic signals for rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: The spectral components of acoustic signals generated by rotating machinery are complex, requiring the identification of frequency bands that capture fault-related information while suppressing irrelevant components. Traditionally, sensitive frequency bands are selected using statistical indices. However, many of these indices rely on absolute values and are also susceptible to interference from non-Gaussian noise (e.g., sporadic impulse) and periodic signals (e.g., rotational frequency), which limits their ability to reflect fault characteristics accurately. To address these limitations, this paper introduces an ACWIgram. Two preprocessing methods—subband trimmed averaging and comb filtering—are proposed to enhance metrics based on impulsiveness and cyclostationarity, enabling better representation of fault characteristics. Additionally, a framework integrates impulsiveness, cyclostationarity, and health reference signals, leading to the construction of a novel relative index called the Adaptive Composite Weighted Index (ACWI). Furthermore, an adaptive spectral segmentation methodology is proposed, leveraging variations between fault and health signals and the proportionality of fault characteristic frequency to rotational frequency. The approach is validated using simulation data and experimental data of rolling bearings and gears with weak faults implanted. Results show a strong correlation between the ACWI and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) based on fault characteristic frequency, confirming the index’s validity. The method adaptively identifies the optimal demodulation band with appropriate center frequency and bandwidth. The ACWIgram delivers accurate detection results and improves the SNR of filtered signals by at least 15% compared to the original signals, demonstrating its effectiveness for diagnosing faults in rotating machinery.

title: Mode-based energy transfer modulation for DBD-PA controlled cavity buffeting noise
abstract: This study establishes a novel energy-pathway regulation paradigm for suppressing cavity buffeting noise using dielectric barrier discharge plasma actuators (DBD-PAs). Through systematic multiparameter experiments and high-fidelity simulations, we demonstrate that plasma actuation achieves control by reconstructing turbulent energy transport paths. A non-probabilistic sensitivity analysis first identified the actuator’s excitation angle as the dominant spatial parameter, with an orientation of 180° delivering a maximum noise reduction of 4.5 dB. To unravel the underlying physics, we developed a phase-conditioned proper orthogonal decomposition (PC-POD) method, which successfully isolated three key spatiotemporally evolving energy structures from the quasiperiodic flow. Quantitative analysis of the fluctuating kinetic energy equation revealed a dual-path regulation mechanism: the actuator enhances dissipation in the dominant modes while simultaneously suppressing the energy cascade to higher modes. This is achieved by reducing the efficiency of intermodal energy transfer by 50 % and promoting spectral broadening, which significantly increases dissipation. The findings provide a new energy-based framework for the active control of flow-induced noise.

title: Structural modification and active vibration control by the receptance method: Review and tutorial
abstract: The problem of eigenvalue assignment, both generally and in terms of vibration suppression, has a long history, as indeed does the use of measured receptance data in understanding the dynamic behaviour of compound systems made up of a number of component subsystems. It is often the case that there is a need to change the undesirable dynamics of an existing system, perhaps to move a natural frequency sufficiently far away from a frequency of excitation or to change a mode shape to tailor the dynamic response. This may be achieved either by a suitably designed structural modification or by active control.Now the two previously separate disciplines of structural modification and active control for vibration suppression have been brought together in what has become known as the receptance method, developed principally in the first two and a half decades of the twenty-first century. The purpose of this article is to explain in depth the details of the receptance method, covering systematically all its recent developments and applications, supported by example problems to illustrate the most important principles and reveal its advantages and limitations.

title: MFAformer: A novel framework for milling chatter detection via multi-source signal fusion
abstract: Milling chatter is a self-excited vibration in machining operations that leads to poor surface quality, tool wear, and potential damage to the machine. It arises from the interaction between the cutting forces and the dynamic characteristics of the machine-tool system, often producing excessive noise and instability. Thus, timely and accurate chatter detection is crucial for ensuring workpiece surface quality, improving machining efficiency, and extending tool life. Although artificial intelligence methods have been developed for milling chatter detection, several key challenges still remain, including over-reliance on artificial feature extraction, limitations of single-source signal information, and interference from environmental noises. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes the multi-source signal fusion anti-noise Transformer (MFAformer), a novel framework for milling chatter detection via multi-source signal fusion. Firstly, a strategy is introduced to process multi-source signals to filter out most noises and eliminate the influence of milling parameters. Then, the correlation kurtosis and the energy ratio weights are constructed to effectively fuse multi-source signals at the data level. Subsequently, an anti-noise Transformer encoder is built for chatter feature extraction, with strong feature learning and noise resistance capabilities. Extensive experiments were carried out to validate the superiority and robustness of the proposed MFAformer.

title: A novel method for testing inertial parameters of large-scale structures
abstract: Accurate identification of the inertial parameters of railway vehicle car bodies is essential for analyzing and predicting the dynamic behavior of vehicle systems. However, existing testing methods are limited by low accuracy and poor generalizability when applied to car bodies, due to their diverse structural configurations and substantial mass. This paper proposes a novel method for testing these inertial parameters using a dual parallel six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) test rig. In contrast to conventional testing approaches, we introduce a variable-frequency loading technique and a moment differentiation-based data processing method, which simplify both the testing procedure and the computational workflow. Furthermore, a signal reconstruction technique is proposed to recover true inertial loads from friction-corrupted measurement signals. Together, these methods contribute to improved testing efficiency and accuracy. The relative errors between the major inertial parameters of the car body obtained from both virtual and field tests and their theoretical values were all below 5%. This study provides a comprehensive and effective method for determining the inertial parameters of large-scale structures such as railway vehicle car bodies.

title: A neural network based on stochastic subspace theory for dynamic parameters recognition of the curved thin-walled parts milling process
abstract: The system dynamics parameters are crucial for predicting chatter in the milling of thin-walled components, and machine learning offers a new paradigm for traditional structural modal parameter identification. In this study, a novel machine learning-based method is proposed for identifying dynamic parameters in the milling process of the curved thin-walled parts. This method, based on stochastic subspace theory, integrates subspace decomposition techniques and modal eigenvalue extraction into neural networks, achieving relatively autonomous parameter optimization and reducing manual intervention. Initially, the state space model of the curved thin-walled milling system is established, the continuous system is discretized, and the stochastic state space equation of the generalized milling system discretized is derived. Subsequently, the Hankel matrix of measured response data is constructed, and the singular value decomposition of the output projection matrix is performed. The high-dimensional complex mapping relationship between the singular values of the projection matrix and the system modal order is developed through the established modal order determination neural network, and the modal order is automatically determined through the designed loss function. In the modal parameter identification neural network, the determined modal order and extracted signal features are taken as inputs, and the functional relationship between the input features and modal parameters is constructed through the modal parameter identification neural network to realize the online modal parameter identification of curved thin-walled parts. Finally, a series of milling experiments are carried out to verify the accuracy of the proposed method by taking an S-shaped standard sample as an example.

title: Corrigendum to “Vibration mode identification method for structures using image correlation and compressed sensing”. [Mech. Syst. Signal Process. 199 (2023) 110495]
Erratum to “A novel data-driven K-SVD transferrable baseline method for multi-damage identification for composite fuselage panels.” [Mech. Syst. Signal Process. 232 (2025) 112702]
A lightweight and fully-expandable piezoelectric sensor network with shared signal transmission wires for aircraft smart skin
abstract: Aircraft smart skin for structural health monitoring (SHM) plays an important role in the design and maintenance of advanced aircraft. To ensure its large-area monitoring function, large-scale and lightweight sensor networks are required, but they are difficult to implement due to limitations in structural design, manufacturing process and additional weight from cables. To solve this problem, the design method of lightweight and fully expandable piezoelectric (PZT) sensor networks (EPSNs) for aircraft smart skin is proposed. An EPSN includes a PZT array, a signal interface, and expandable signal transmission cables between them. The PZT array adopts both the stretchable island-bridge structural design and shared signal transmission wires design, thus can be designed and manufactured on a small scale and then deployed to a large area for applications with only a few signal wires and monitoring channels. To secure the electrical connections after deployment, signal transmission cables are also expandable. Based on this method, a 6 × 9 EPSN is designed and manufactured by the flexible printed circuit (FPC) process, ensuring its flexibility, light weight and high reliability. It can be fully expanded to 5894 % of its original size and integrated with a composite skin structure for impact and damage monitoring validation. The monitoring area reaches more than 2 m2, but the additional weight introduced is only about 8 g/m2. Results demonstrate that it achieves impact monitoring with 95 % accuracy and damage monitoring with 100 % accuracy for simulated damage. Moreover, a real and complex aircraft smart skin for SHM is realized and validated based on a 7 × 7 EPSN and a T800 wing-box panel. Results show that even on complex structures, the EPSN still has an impact monitoring accuracy of 82.5 % for 20 typical impact positions and a damage monitoring accuracy of 100 % for simulated damage as small as 10 mm × 10 mm × 0.5 mm and real impact-induced damage. This demonstrates the feasibility of EPSNs in large-scale and lightweight aircraft smart skin.

title: A method for determining the high-frequency in-cylinder pressure of an internal combustion engine using a pressure sensor dynamically calibrated with a shock tube
abstract: A key parameter for determining the different dynamic parameters of an internal combustion engine (ICE) is the high-frequency pressure in the combustion chamber. The uncertainty of these parameters is dominated by the dynamic accuracy of pressure sensors (PSs). However, PSs used in dynamic applications are typically calibrated quasi-statically with conventional static standards, which limits their accuracy. To address this limitation, this paper proposes and evaluates a method for determining the high-frequency in-cylinder pressure of an ICE using a PS dynamically calibrated with a shock tube (ST). The method reconstructs the in-cylinder pressure by applying an inverse discrete Fourier transform to the ratio of the frequency spectrum of the PS voltage output response and the complex frequency response function of the PS obtained with a dynamic calibration using a ST. The method was tested on a diesel ICE over a wide range of operating conditions using a piezoelectric PS calibrated in a diaphragmless ST. The Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis shows that the proposed method improves the accuracy of high-frequency in-cylinder pressure determination. Consequently, it significantly improves the accuracy of other dynamic ICE parameters, such as the rate of pressure rise, the average in-cylinder gas temperature and the rate of heat release.

title: Dimension-reduction representations for stationary and non-stationary stochastic processes in time domain
abstract: Accurate modeling of stochastic dynamic actions in engineering serves as the basis for assessing the disaster-resilient reliability of structural systems. The time-domain analysis methods facilitate simulation by directly modeling stochastic processes, eliminating frequency decomposition. However, within the conventional Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) framework, the time-domain methods encounter the challenges of handling high-dimensional random variables and capturing comprehensive probabilistic details. To this end, this study proposes a time-domain dimension-reduction (DR) representation for simulating both stationary and non-stationary stochastic processes. The core concept is to construct random orthogonal functions, including Legendre polynomials, Gaussian Hartley orthogonal basis, and Trigonometric orthogonal basis, as constraints upon the orthogonal random variables, thereby reducing the number of required random variables form thousands to merely one or two. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations of both stationary and non-stationary stochastic earthquake ground motions. Analytical results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and efficiency compared to the conventional MCS. Moreover, in simulating non-stationary stochastic seismic processes, the time-domain DR method is more capable of capturing the non-stationary characteristics in real seismic scenarios than the frequency-domain DR method. It’s also noteworthy that the probabilistic information of representative seismic samples generated through the DR method is complete, which allows for integration with the third-generation structural design theories, such as the probability density evolution method, to conduct refined stochastic dynamic response analysis and reliability assessment of complex engineering structures.

title: An adaptive time–frequency fusion framework for real-time sound monitoring in CVD roller dressing
abstract: To address the challenge of real-time monitoring in CVD roller dressing, we propose a lightweight and adaptive acoustic analysis framework. Our approach first applies a two-stage noise suppression technique combining spectral subtraction and dynamic Bayesian thresholding, designed for harsh industrial noise conditions. Then, we introduce a time–frequency fusion network that combines residual temporal convolutions and frequency-domain attention to capture transient dressing anomalies. Finally, a multi-class classifier identifies eight distinct dressing states for fine-grained anomaly detection. Experimental results on both public and real-world datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with 99.12% classification accuracy (for the eight dressing states) and 79.63% pAUC under low false-positive rates, all while achieving real-time inference (3.012 ms running time). The implementation of our framework is publicly available to facilitate reproducibility and further research at https://github.com/meihuoAI/ATFF-CVD-Dressing.

title: Machinery multimodal heterogeneous-aware RUL prediction: A spatial-temporal graph network for cross-temporal information propagation and dynamic fusion
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as a promising technology in the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. Despite the substantial progress achieved by GNN-based approaches, several limitations remain: 1) Existing methods fail to adequately account for the multi-attribute heterogeneous associations inherent in multi-sensor data, thereby constraining effective feature extraction from diverse sources. 2) Conventional methods generally construct graph structures based solely on single-timepoint sensor associations, thereby limiting the exploitation of rich temporal information. To address the above challenges, a heterogeneous graph convolutional network with cross-temporal information propagation, termed HGCN-CIP, is proposed to implement the RUL prediction for mechanical systems. First, a cross-temporal heterogeneous graph architecture is proposed to enable the joint modeling of sensor synchronization and interaction relationships across time steps. Two types of heterogeneous meta-paths are introduced to explicitly capture the diverse dependencies within the sensor network. Second, a multi-scale heterogeneous graph convolutional network (MSHGCN) incorporating the information propagation operation is proposed, which generates heterogeneous sub-features by temporally aggregating node features from temporal graphs under different meta-paths. A dynamic feature fusion layer is then employed to integrate the sub-features, enabling effective feature fusion and accurate RUL prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses multiple state-of-the-art approaches in RUL prediction tasks.

title: Breathing crack detection in rotating blades via blade tip timing and envelope diagram image classification with an optimized CNN architecture
abstract: High-cycle fatigue cracks in rotating blades of large turbo-machinery are induced by repeated loading and harsh operating conditions. These cracks lead to nonlinear tip vibration responses due to the blade’s “breathing effect”. As a promising non-contact monitoring technique, blade tip timing (BTT) enables blade condition assessment by recording tip vibration signals. The main challenge in identifying breathing cracks using the BTT measurement method lies in the difficulty of establishing an analytical relationship between tip displacement and blade damage state. Additionally, due to limitations on the sampling principle of BTT measurement, the useful information gathered by the BTT method is further constrained. In this paper, BTT signals from two probes of testing blades are transformed into envelope diagram images, and an optimized convolutional neural network (CNN) model called BladeNet model with an attention mechanism (BladeNet-AM) is utilized to extract implicit nonlinear dynamic information from these images, enabling the identification of breathing cracks. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through both simulation and experimental studies, and its superior identification capability is demonstrated in comparison with existing BTT-based crack detection methods. The advantage of this method lies in its ability to exploit a richer set of blade dynamics information by converting BTT test data into image format, providing a more comprehensive understanding than analyzing digital signals. By utilizing a limited number of probes, this method exhibits high accuracy and robustness against measurement uncertainties, presenting a novel approach specifically tailored for diagnosing breathing cracks in rotating blades.

title: Identification of bridge curvature profiles from dynamic responses induced by moving vehicles using autoregressive models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology for structural damage localization in beam-like single- and multi-span bridge structures based on curvature profiles extracted from acceleration measurements. The approach builds on the rationale that autoregressive models, when trained on ambient vibration data, fail to reconstruct the quasi-static response induced by moving loads. This limitation produces a reconstruction residual that, under suitable conditions, corresponds to a shifted and scaled version of the curvature profile of the structure generated by a point load applied at the sensor location. The proposed method enables the calculation of this residual with extremely sparse sensor networks that do not require synchronization. A damage index is then defined from variations in the estimated curvature profile, enabling localization of stiffness reductions. To eliminate the need for manual parameter tuning, a model order selection criterion is proposed, which makes the method fully automated, unlike existing approaches that rely on prior knowledge of the monitored structure. The methodology is validated through numerical simulations that incorporate vehicle–bridge interaction phenomena and road roughness, as well as experimental data from a full-scale truss bridge.
