The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves damage localization performance comparable to established filter-based techniques, while offering improved spatial resolution and requiring no tuning parameters.

title: Identification of vibration and noise sources in EHA internal gear pumps under variable operating conditions and noise reduction design
abstract: Hydraulic pump serves as the primary noise source in Electro-Hydraulic Actuator (EHA), with complex variable speed and pressure conditions leading to intricate evolution of EHA pump excitation. This study establishes a fluid–structure-acoustics-coupled prediction model for an EHA internal gear pump, incorporating the effects of mechanical excitations, to accurately identify these vibration and noise excitations under such variable conditions. The model is validated through tests conducted in a semi-anechoic chamber. Results demonstrate a radiated noise prediction error of less than 1.5 dB(A), representing a 28.6 % improvement in accuracy compared to traditional prediction models. The evolution laws and contribution of excitations under variable conditions are also evaluated, and a housing noise reduction design is implemented. The results show that the fluid surface source consistently contributes the most to radiated noise across all operating conditions. Moreover, mechanical excitations contribute significantly at the peak sound pressure frequencies. The fluid volume source is considerably influenced by rotational speed, and under high-speed conditions, pronounced turbulence, cavitation, and trapped oil phenomena make the contribution of the volume source non-negligible. Structural optimization yields a reduction of 3.7 dB(A) in the predicted overall sound pressure level (SPL) of the EHA pump under the rated operating condition, and the average total SPLs under variable pressure and speed working conditions decrease by 1.2 and 2.2 dB(A), respectively. These findings are significant for guiding the noise reduction design of EHA internal gear pumps under variable operating conditions.

title: A novel approach to forward design elastic ring squeeze film dampers by decoupling stiffness and damping parameters in aerospace engines
abstract: In order to solve the problem of iterative design of support structures for aerospace engines, this study proposes a structural parameter decoupling method and establishes a systematic forward design process of elastic ring squeeze film damper (ERSFD) aiming at rotor vibration control. In order to study the dynamic characteristics considering boss slip and separation, a ERSFD fluid–structure coupling dynamic model is established, which passes the experimental verification of ERSFD components. Then the idea of decoupling key parameters into stiffness-related parameters and damping-related parameters is proposed for the first time. On this basis, the forward design process of ERSFD with the goal of vibration reduction for ERSFD-rotor system is put forward, and simulating test rig is established. The results show that the calculating modes and responses are in good agreement with the experimental ones, which verifies the accuracy of the calculating method. The amplitude of the rotor system does not exceed 47.2 μm with the ERSFDs lubricated, and the vibration reduction ratio is not less than 42.5 %, which shows the obvious damping effect of ERSFDs. Long-time resonance experiments are carried out at two orders of critical speeds with additional unbalance respectively. The resonance duration of the ERSFD-rotor system for each mode is no less than 3561 s, during which both the vibration displacement and vibration velocity signals remained consistently low and stable. The experiment verifies that the designed ERSFDs have the ability to tolerate long-time resonance. This study can provide theoretical and technical support for improving the design efficiency of ERSFDs, enhancing structural reliability and strengthening vibration resistance.

title: An iterative dual Craig–Bampton method
abstract: The dual Craig–Bampton (DCB) is one of the most well-known component mode synthesis (CMS) methods. In this paper, we propose an iterative dual Craig–Bampton (I-DCB) method that enhances the accuracy of the original DCB method without adding more retained modes. The key idea is to iteratively use higher-order corrections to substructural residual flexibility to capture the substructural modes that were truncated. Ill-conditioning is then typically encountered through the iterative process. To mitigate this problem, the original DCB formulation is modified by condensing the Lagrange multipliers, thereby eliminating the indefinite matrix block that causes spurious modes. This condensation yields a displacement-based reduced-order system, and it can offer better numerical stability and a smaller size of the system matrices. The I-DCB method is developed by using this well-conditioned modified DCB formulation. The performance of the proposed I-DCB method is evaluated through numerical examples.

title: A novel PINN algorithm for a bridge weigh in motion system without prior knowledge of axle location
abstract: Bridge Weigh-in-Motion (BWIM) is an effective method of using instrumented bridges to find the weights of passing vehicles. Traditional BWIM systems rely on axle detectors to determine axle locations/spacings, which are used to formulate the system of equations and calculate axle loads. However, commonly used Free of Axle Detector (FAD) systems exhibit reduced accuracy when vehicle speeds are high or when multiple vehicles cross the bridge simultaneously. Similarly, computer vision-based detectors are highly sensitive to environmental conditions (e.g. rain), which can degrade video quality and affect detection accuracy. Inaccurate axle location data introduces significant errors in vehicle load estimation. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel BWIM system that does not require prior knowledge of vehicle locations. Since the relationship between vehicle axle information and bridge response is inherently non-linear, we introduce a Gaussian-based neural network layer as a function approximator to model this complex mapping. Furthermore, the physical principles governing time, location, axle spacing, axle loads, and bridge responses are embedded directly into the network structure, ensuring that the model predictions remain physically consistent. Once the network is trained, the error between theoretical and measured responses can be minimized to find axle loads from the neural network parameters, which correspond to the magnitudes of vehicle loads. Numerical results indicate that, for cases where two- and three-axle vehicles traverse different lanes simultaneously, the 99.9% confidence level error for GVW is 1.2%. Field test results further validate the approach, demonstrating that the 99.9% confidence interval error for GVW is 8.9%.

title: Torsional deformation-transferring waveguide for generating perfectly omnidirectional shear-horizontal waves in plate structures
abstract: Omnidirectional SH waves offer distinct advantages for the structural health monitoring of large-scale infrastructures by enabling rapid and wide-area scanning without signal distortion. Despite their potential, conventional omnidirectional SH wave transducers inherently limit their directional uniformity, due to their reliance on complex and segmented excitation sources. As a result, no transducer to date has achieved truly ideal omnidirectional SH wave excitation. Here, we propose a novel waveguide-type omnidirectional SH wave transducer (WG-OSHT) that achieves perfect omnidirectionality by leveraging torsional deformation transfer through a cylindrical waveguide. By developing a theoretical model for the frequency response of the waveguide-installed plate system, three key design parameters are identified, enabling tunable design to maximize SH wave energy generation at the desired target frequency. Experiments and finite element analyses confirm the generation of high-purity SH0 mode with nearly perfect omnidirectionality with no unwanted mode interference, and showing good agreement with the proposed theoretical model. This waveguide-based approach not only achieves ideal omnidirectional SH wave source for the first time but also enhances its applicability by simplifying fabrication through a significant reduction in segmented components. Furthermore, it expands the inspection capabilities to curved surfaces and extreme environments, including high-temperature and chemically hazardous conditions.

title: Model-based controller assisted domain randomization for transient vibration suppression of nonlinear powertrain system with parametric uncertainty
abstract: Complex mechanical systems such as vehicle powertrains are inherently subject to multiple nonlinearities and uncertainties arising from parametric variations. Modeling errors are therefore unavoidable, making the transfer of control systems from simulation to real-world systems a critical challenge. Traditional robust controls have limitations in handling certain types of nonlinearities and uncertainties, requiring a more practical approach capable of comprehensively compensating for these various constraints. This study proposes a new robust control approach using the framework of deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The key strategy lies in the synergy among domain randomization-based DRL, long short-term memory (LSTM)-based actor and critic networks, and model-based control (MBC). The problem setup is modeled via the latent Markov decision process (LMDP), a set of vanilla MDPs, for a controlled system subject to uncertainties and nonlinearities. In LMDP, the dynamics of an environment simulator is randomized during training to improve the robustness of the control system to real testing environments. The randomization increases training difficulties as well as conservativeness of the resultant control system; therefore, progress is assisted by concurrent use of a model-based controller based on a physics-based system model. Compared to traditional DRL-based controls, the proposed approach is smarter in that we can achieve a high level of generalization ability with a more compact neural network architecture and a smaller amount of training data. The controller is verified via practical application to active damping for a complex powertrain system with nonlinearities and parametric variations. Comparative tests demonstrate the high robustness of the proposed approach.

title: Nonlinear modal identification through a nonlinear frequency response surface
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for nonlinear modal identification using a nonlinear frequency response surface (NFRS). The approach involves sampling an experimental NFRS through constant-excitation voltage stepped sine testing, eliminating the need for a dedicated controller for testing. By extracting quasi-linear constant-response frequency response functions from the NFRS, linear modal techniques can be employed to determine equivalent modal parameters for various response amplitudes. The method’s performance is evaluated against existing techniques using two experimental benchmark structures, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying nonlinear modal parameters.

title: Reliability analysis of a high-rise benchmark building with novel self-powered active mass damper under random wind excitations
abstract: This study investigates the reliability of a benchmark high-rise building subjected to random wind excitations, incorporating a novel self-powered active control system. Owing to their height and flexibility, high-rise buildings are vulnerable to dynamic wind effects, which can compromise serviceability and structural safety. Conventional active control systems depend on external power sources, which may fail during extreme events. The proposed self-powered system overcomes this limitation by harvesting energy from structural vibrations to power its control mechanisms, achieving autonomous and sustainable operation. A dynamic model of the building and stochastic wind loads is developed, and extensive simulations are carried out to evaluate the performance of the control system under various wind scenarios and design parameters. Reliability is quantified using the probability density evolution method combined with the equivalent extreme-value event principle, enabling accurate assessment of structural responses under uncertainty. The results reveal that the self-powered control system effectively reduces peak displacements and response variability, thereby enhancing the building’s reliability and performance. Comparative analysis with the uncontrolled case highlights its advantages in mitigating wind-induced effects. This research demonstrates the potential of integrating energy harvesting with active control to improve the resilience, safety, and sustainability of high-rise structures under wind excitations.

title: Tunable bandgaps and programmable wave propagation of magnetically actuated metamaterial plates
abstract: Active acoustic metamaterials offer tunable control over elastic waves through external stimuli. Among various actuation strategies, magnetic actuation has attracted considerable attention due to its contactless nature and fast response time. However, most magnetically actuated metamaterials achieve wave manipulation only in non-standard structures, with limited focus on programmable propagation in engineering-relevant structures, thereby limiting their practical applicability. Here, we propose a magnetically actuated metamaterial plate that enables tunable bandgaps and programmable wave propagation. Programmable units, consisting of support blocks, resonant beams, and magnets, are mounted onto the surface of the host plate to preserve its structural integrity. An external magnetic field switches the programmable units between pull-in and released states. The tunable bandgap is validated through theoretical, numerical, and experimental analyses. Programmable wave propagation paths, including cross-shaped, T-shaped, and inverted U-shaped configurations, are demonstrated. The proposed design expands the application potential of magnetically actuated metamaterials and improves their suitability for real-world engineering scenarios.

title: A Volterra-series-based semi-analytical method for fractionally damped nonlinear systems under stochastic excitation
abstract: This paper presents an approximate analytical method for evaluating the response of fractionally damped nonlinear systems under stochastic excitation using the Volterra series. Traditional statistical linearization methods provide satisfactory statistical moments but fail to accurately estimate the power spectral density (PSD), as they cannot capture harmonic resonances by linearizing nonlinear terms. The Volterra series, effective for integer-order nonlinear systems, is adapted here for fractional-order systems by utilizing an approximate expression for the fractional derivative of exponential functions in a stationary state. Key steps include deriving generalized frequency response functions and transforming the high-dimensional excitation spectrum into the physical spectrum. The method’s validity is confirmed through Monte Carlo simulations, and it demonstrates the significant impact of fractional derivative order on the peak and shape of the output PSD and probability density function (PDF).

title: Bayesian operational modal analysis considering the coupling effect of both structural responses and temperature variations
abstract: Operational modal analysis aims to identify the modal properties of structures, including natural frequency, damping ratio, and mode shape based on the measured vibration response data only with structures under working conditions. However, the performance of structures is gradually deteriorating or being compromised due to factors such as environmental and operational variations, which cannot be directly controlled in this case. Modal properties of structures estimated by conventional operational modal analysis techniques based solely on the structural dynamic model without considering such effect can be biased. To address this problem, this paper proposes an operational modal analysis method that integrates a data-driven model into the conventional structural dynamic model. Specifically, Gaussian process model is used to account for the coupling effect of structural responses and temperature variations. A Bayesian modal identification framework is then deployed for parameter inference to account for data uncertainties and efficient modal identification algorithm is proposed. Two examples are presented in this study to illustrate the proposed method. The proposed method is firstly validated by a synthetic ambient vibration dataset. A full-scale bridge example is also presented in this work to illustrate the applicability of the method to real implementations. The results show that the proposed method can capture the nonlinear relationship between environment effects and structural responses, and can efficiently identify the modal parameters under different environmental and operational conditions.

title: Signal processing and feature engineering for automated Multi-Type damage assessment of wind turbine blades via Machine vision
abstract: Ensuring the structural integrity of wind turbine blades (WTBs) is paramount for operational safety and optimal energy generation, yet diagnosing the diverse range of potential damages incurred during service presents significant challenges for conventional inspection techniques. Reliable and automated damage assessment is crucial for effective condition monitoring. This paper presents an automated diagnostic approach leveraging machine vision, focusing specifically on robust signal processing and tailored feature engineering to address these challenges. The proposed pipeline integrates several key stages: (i) optimized image segmentation employing a combination of K-Means clustering and OTSU thresholding to effectively isolate potential damage regions even against variable backgrounds found in field images; (ii) refined morphological closing operations, incorporating a minimum connected domain area threshold ( α ), specifically designed to suppress imaging noise and artifacts common in UAV-captured WTB imagery while preserving true damage contours; and (iii) extraction of a carefully selected set of geometric and grayscale features, engineered to capture the distinct morphological and textural characteristics of different damage types. Based on these engineered features, a rule-based classifier achieves accurate localization and subsequent classification of five critical WTB damage types: sand holes, excoriations, cracks, oil stains, and breakage. Experimental validation performed on a comprehensive dataset of 1250 blade images, including samples augmented to simulate challenging real-world conditions, demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach, achieving an average detection and classification accuracy of 91.00%. This integrated machine vision system offers a valuable tool for automated WTB condition monitoring, facilitating more efficient, objective, and potentially earlier identification of various damage modes, thereby supporting informed maintenance strategies and enhancing wind farm reliability.

title: Adaptive focusing imaging method for flexible ultrasonic arrays on complex curved structures
abstract: Flexible ultrasonic array transducers offer significant potential for the conformal and shape-adaptive inspection of complex surface structures. However, since the array geometry directly governs the time-delay calculation in delay-and-sum beamforming, inaccurate shape estimation can significantly degrade image reconstruction quality. This study proposes a method to estimate the shape of a flexible array transducer solely from full matrix capture data, without relying on any external device. The method formulates the problem as a multi-objective optimization task, simultaneously minimizing the image entropy and the average phase variance within the region of interest. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method across arrays conforming to various surface contours. The reconstructed images achieve structural similarity index values exceeding 0.8, and the average positioning error of the array elements remains well below the ultrasonic wavelength. These results verify the accuracy of the proposed shape estimation approach and highlight its potential for enabling high-fidelity ultrasonic imaging with flexible array transducers.

title: Two-stage physics-guided deep learning framework for impact force identification and source localization using a single sensor
abstract: Accurate identification of time-varying impact forces from noisy structural responses is critical for ensuring the operational safety of composite structures. Conventional physics-driven methods typically suffer from high computational complexity and sensitivity to system identification errors, whereas purely data-driven methods lack sufficient physical interpretability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel two-stage physics-data hybrid-driven deep learning framework, termed the Physics-guided Impulse Response Dictionary Method (PG-IRDM). In the first stage, a Physics-guided Impulse Response Temporal Convolutional Network (PG-IRTCN) is constructed by integrating L1 sparsity constraints, frequency-domain consistency, and Tikhonov regularization to effectively predict impulse response functions and reconstruct impact forces across the structural surface. In the second stage, an expanded multi-sample dictionary built from impulse response similarities enables accurate impact localization with a single sensor, overcoming the limitations of conventional “localization-then-inversion” paradigms. Experimental results demonstrate that PG-IRDM achieves peak force prediction accuracies exceeding 95.41 % on both a composite flat plate and a foam-core blade, surpassing GTCN, DPH-TrLSTM, and NSC-Net by 6.93 %, 12.32 %, and 35.67 %, respectively, with impact timing errors below 1.2602 ms. Under sufficient data conditions, PG-IRDM also successfully accomplishes localization tasks that remain challenging for other methods, achieving a localization accuracy exceeding 91.57 %. Moreover, systematic sensor-position analysis indicates that central arrangement contributes to accurate force reconstruction, and edge arrangement enhances localization performance. Overall, PG-IRDM demonstrates excellent physical interpretability and superior noise resistance, offering a practical and scalable solution for intelligent monitoring and structural integrity assessment in complex composite systems.

title: Research on the vibration mechanism of TBM main bearing considering surface shape error
abstract: Main bearing plays a very important role in the TBM main driving system. Since the main bearing belongs to three-row cylindrical roller bearing, both the radial side and the thrust side will be affected by surface shape error. These shape error will induce abnormal vibration of the main bearing, resulting in degradation of the performance of the main bearing and reduction of service life. Aiming at the time-varying excitation and dynamic model of TBM main bearing excited by surface shape error on the radial and thrust side, a dynamics model of TBM main bearing considering surface shape error is established in this paper. The model takes into full consideration of the comprehensive influence of shape error of radial side raceway, thrust side raceway and rollers, and systematically analyzes the influence of key parameters such as order, amplitude, and wave number on the vibration response characteristics of the main bearing. The results show that the vibration degree of the main bearing is gradually enhanced with the increase of the surface shape error order. With the increase of the radial side raceway waviness amplitude, the vibration level of the main bearing rises first and then tends to stabilize the fluctuation interval. The change in the thrust side raceway waviness amplitude first makes the vibration level of the main bearing fluctuate within a certain range, and then shows an increasing trend. In contrast, the increase of the radial side raceway roundness amplitude will cause the vibration of the main bearing to intensify, but its effect is smaller than the waviness. The effect of the thrust side raceway flatness amplitude is also relatively small. In terms of the wave number of shape error, when the wave number of the radial side raceway waviness is 0.5 times the number of radial rollers, the vibration level of the main bearing will peak, and the integer multiple relationship has the most significant impact. The vibration level of the main bearing will also peak when the wave number of thrust side raceway waviness is an integer multiple of the number of thrust rollers. In addition, surface shape errors have no effect on bearing defect characteristic frequencies. This paper further discusses the influence of uneven load condition on the vibration characteristics of the main bearing.

title: Influence of static deflection and fatigue on the characteristics and reproducibility of additively-manufactured systems
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables novices to create complex geometries, but the limited research on the dynamical properties of these parts hinders their widespread use. To help fill this gap, three “identically” printed PLA beams are fabricated and tested, with a particular focus on the influence a static position has on the dynamical responses and repeatability of the results. In the first setup, the beam is orientated in such a way to enhance the initial static deflection created by the accelerometer whereas in the second setup the initial static deflection is negligible. By utilizing free, random, and harmonic vibration tests, the vibratory profile of each beam is generated so that “identically” printed beams can be compared to one another with the only dissimilarity being the initial static deflection. In the free vibration tests, it is shown that the existence of an initial static deflection creates a higher fundamental frequency, which has a more dominant nonlinear softening backbone. Also, the presence of an initial static deflection leads to a larger instantaneous damping ratio. To quantitively characterize the nonlinear dynamical responses and repeatability of the manufactured systems, three different levels of input excitations are considered in the harmonic vibration testing. The results verify the trends in the free vibration, allowing the claim to be made that the initial static deflection creates a stronger nonlinear softening backbone to all beams tested. Finally, to examine the reproducibility of these systems’ results under fatigue effect, the harmonic excitation tests are identically replicated three times. It is observed that even when the same exact beam is tested, its behavioral characteristics tend to vary. In addition, both setups indicate that the multi-stable solutions are most prominent directly after the manufacturing process, which decreases substantially as the beam gains fatigue due to experimental testing.

title: Intelligent chatter detection and identification method integrating GSA-FE and DB-SMRN oriented robotic milling under variable machining conditions and postures
abstract: Chatter detection is essential for achieving stable robotic milling of large and complex components. However, detecting chatter under varying machining conditions and robot postures remains a challenge due to the limited training data. Additionally, the broadband nature of chatter, influenced by multiple chatter types, complicates the feature extraction process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel chatter detection method based on few-shot learning. Initially, the milling statuses are categorized into stable, tool-mode-dominated high-frequency chatter (TMDHC), and robot-structural-dominated low-frequency chatter (RSDLC). The proposed method comprises four key components: an adaptive Short-time Fourier transform (ASTFT) for time–frequency map transformation, a global spatial attention feature extractor (GSA-FE), a dual-branch similarity metric relational network (DB-SMRN), and a classification module. The GSA-FE module consists of the deformable residual large kernel attention (DRLKA) and global grouped coordinate attention (GGCA) components. It utilizes deformable convolutional kernels and spatial channel attention to adjust weights according to changes in chatter frequency. The DB-SMRN comprises two branches: a Global Transformer branch with cross-attention to capture global context and assess correlations between the query and support sets and a Local Mahalanobis branch to isolate local features from the support sets. The outputs of both branches are integrated for classification purposes. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through a series of milling tests conducted under varying postures and with different size milling tools. This framework provides a robust solution for chatter detection in robotic milling, particularly in environments with limited training data and varying machining conditions.

title: Designing likelihood function under nuisance components in block particle filter
abstract: Particle filter (PF) has proven effective for nonlinear identification scenarios; however, its performance in high-dimensional problems is often limited by the curse of dimensionality. To overcome this challenge, block particle filter (BPF) is proposed to reformulate a high-dimensional model into several blocks, so the identification of one high-dimensional system can be simplified into that for many lower-dimensional blocks. However, due to the coupling between blocks, the likelihood function for each state subgroup depends not only on its own state components (components of interest) but also on the components of its neighboring subgroups (nuisance components)—a dependency that BPF does not address. In order to extend BPF to coupled systems, we design likelihood functions, including plug-in, profile, and marginal likelihoods, that can incorporate nuisance components within each block. We demonstrate the state and parameter estimation performance of BPF with each likelihood through a numerical example of a forty-story Bouc-Wen frame structure under ground motion. We also design the BPF in a differentiable manner, integrate it into a deep learning architecture, and evaluate its performance on three datasets: the open-source Electricity Transformer Temperature (ETT) dataset, an open-source cutter wear dataset, and the AstraZeneca bearing dataset. The code is available at https://github.com/TianZLi/Likelihood-in-BPF .

title: Adaptive Ramanujan collaborative decomposition: An intelligent band boundary fusion strategy
abstract: As an important auxiliary technology for feature extraction, spectrum segmentation is confronted with two fundamental challenges: the difficulty of boundary determination and poor noise robustness. To address these issues, an adaptive Ramanujan collaborative decomposition (ARCD) algorithm based on boundary fusion is proposed in this paper. On the one hand, the ARCD method employs an order statistics filter (OSF) to smooth the power spectral density, followed by moving average processing to derive an initial segmentation, thereby establishing a robust foundation for accurate frequency band division. On the other hand, to mitigate over-segmentation, a novel boundary fusion strategy based on the Ramanujan spectrum signal-to-noise ratio (RSSNR) is proposed, which iteratively merges adjacent segments by evaluating their RSSNR values, thereby adaptively determining both the optimal segmentation boundaries and the number of decomposition modes. Comparative tests involving both simulated bearing fault signals and real-world measured data demonstrate that ARCD method outperforms most traditional approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy, validating its effectiveness and strong robustness.

title: Modal decomposition and identification for a population of structures using physics-informed graph neural networks and transformers
abstract: Modal identification is key to structural health monitoring and control, offering vital insights into dynamic behavior. This study proposes a novel deep learning framework that combines graph neural networks (GNNs), transformers, and a physics-informed loss to perform modal decomposition and identification among a population of structures. The transformer extracts single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF)-equivalent modal response estimates from multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) measurements, enabling the identification of natural frequencies and damping ratios. The GNN encodes structural topology to infer the corresponding mode shapes. Trained in a fully unsupervised, physics-informed manner, the model leverages modal decomposition theory and mode independence, requiring no labeled data. Validation through simulations and lab experiments demonstrates accurate recovery of modal properties from sparse measurements under varying loading and structural conditions. Comparisons with conventional modal identification methods highlight the framework’s effectiveness, robustness, and superior performance, establishing it as a powerful tool for population-level structural monitoring.
